# LockPlus Native: technical design

Status: draft 10.11, 2026-11-12 (draft 10.11 folds in the 2.0.2 round 7 review fixes; draft 10.10 folds in the 2.0.2 round 6 review fixes; draft 10.9 removes the user-stop notice and folds in the 2.0.2 round 5 review fixes; draft 10.8 folds in the 2.0.2 round 4 review fixes; draft 10.7 folds in the 2.0.2 round 3 review fixes; draft 10.6 folds in the 2.0.2 round 2 review fixes; draft 10.5 folds in the 2.0.2 round 1 review fixes; draft 10.4 folds in 2.0.2, build 200026: profile checks and zip reads in a sandboxed validator service, the minimum app build in the peer requirement, owner-authorised starts, opening profile files from Finder and the connection self-test; drafts 10.1–10.3 folded in the 2.0.0 fix rounds and the 2.0.1 start guard; draft 10, 2026-10-29, folds in E2E-1, the first end-to-end run of the notarized 2.0.0 (200001) on the test VMs, and PENDING-FOLD 50–55; draft 9.2 moved the build output off the backed-up volume; draft 9.1 records owner decisions and adopts ZIPFoundation; draft 7 added the results of P1 spike waves 1 and 2; draft 7.1 raised the minimum OS to macOS 26.0; draft 7.3 folded in the engine spikes S11, S6, S7 and S4 on macOS 27; draft 8 folded in the P2 implementation, its reviews and the app root as built; draft 9 folds in the S2 VM results (`includeAllNetworks` semantics), S4/S5 on 26, the relay-free S11 run and the lead decisions on them; see the revision log, §17.1 and §18). Implements the decision in [`../NATIVE-REWRITE.md`](../NATIVE-REWRITE.md) (cited below as **NR**). Every `L-*` requirement in NR §3 is addressed by name; §19 maps each one to the section that satisfies it and to its test.

Component detail lives in the verified references under [`reference/`](reference/) (cited as **ref/<file> §n**). This document states decisions and rules; where it says "see ref/…", the reference is normative for the detail. If a reference and this document disagree, the revision log's "Conflicts resolved" table decides; anything not listed there is a bug in this document.

This document is written for one developer working with AI coding agents. Every section ends in something implementable: a type, a sequence, a rule, or a test. Where Apple behaviour is uncertain, the text states the **assumption**, the **spike** that validates it (§17), and the **fallback**.

Conventions:
- `MUST`/`MUST NOT` are hard rules. Reviewers reject code that breaks them.
- **Decision** marks a choice this document makes that NR leaves open.
- Team ID: `M53GHX9FAY`. App bundle ID: `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac`. Extension: `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel`.
- **TBD-by-Sn** marks an expected outcome that spike Sn must confirm before code depends on it. Every TBD has a designed response for each possible result.
- **SAFETY** marks an unsafe concurrency escape (`@unchecked Sendable`, `nonisolated(unsafe)`, `MainActor.assumeIsolated`, `@preconcurrency`, `DispatchSemaphore`). Each one carries a `// SAFETY:` comment citing its contract and is listed for the Fable pass (§0, ref/swift-concurrency §0 rule 10).

## Revision log

### Draft 10.11

Draft 10.11 folds in the 2.0.2 round 7 review (Fable round 7: GO, L1, L2, N1–N6; Codex round 7: #1–#3) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026).
- **D10.11-1 NE's restart of a signable hold stays signable while it is `.connecting` (§10.4; Fable r7 L1).** A new attempt this app didn't issue clears `resumableSession` (D10.9-2) unless the profile was, just before that status, the hold a Pause could sign (`signableHold`: a crash gap or a verified network-restart hold of a session this run started or saw connected). So NE's own restart of such a session after a crash or after a "No network available" refusal, paused while it is still `.connecting`, is signed and reconnected at the pause's end, exactly as a Pause an instant earlier (in the gap or the hold) would have been. Nothing is signed that such a Pause would not sign; D10.10-4's sequences (no hold, or a hold that is not signable) still clear the set.
- **D10.11-2 The agent writes a change of the debt before `spend()` returns (§10.4; Codex r7 #2 = Fable r7 N1).** Every spend in the resume agent writes `pauseValueOwed` at once when it changes, over what that run last wrote (so the early on-demand write is never taken back), so no later return (`.networkRestartPending`, `.armUnavailable`, `.keychainUnavailable`) and no watchdog exit loses a failed spend.
- **D10.11-3 The launch's agent reconcile waits for the launch's spend (§10.4; Codex r7 #3 = Fable r7 N2).** `reconcileResumeAgent` doesn't unregister while a spend chain is pending; every chain ends with a reconcile on its result (spent: an agent kept for it goes when nothing is paused; owed: it stays). So the debt that arises at a launch keeps the agent registered as well.
- **D10.11-4 Extending a pause while a value is owed carries no profile (§10.4; Fable r7 N3).** With `pauseValueOwed` set, the earlier record's profile is not carried into the extended pause (a genuine record written back would verify against the surviving value); the extended pause signs only what it stops itself.
- **D10.11-5 After-Connected Save at the current revision is tested (Fable r7 N4); `AppEnvironment.init(mode:)` has no default (Fable r7 N5).** No call builds the live backends by leaving the mode out; `AppDelegate` passes it explicitly.
- **D10.11-6 Residual: a whole-file rollback of settings.json resets the owed flag (§20 risk 31 (b); Codex r7 #1 = Fable r7 L2). Documented, no new mechanism.** `pauseValueOwed` lives in unauthenticated settings.json. Same-user code that copied the whole file during a genuine pause and writes that copy back after the value became owed restores `pausedState`, `pausedUntil` and `pauseValueOwed: false` together; the pause's end (GUI, or the agent if still registered) then checks the genuine record against the surviving value, and it holds. Precondition: a data-protection keychain delete that fails through a whole GUI run (the launch's spend, five retries 30 s apart, every `load()` and wake), which same-user code is not known to be able to cause. Gain: at most one unattended start of the owner's own verified profile, within `ResumeIntent.maxAge` (7 days) of the pause's end. No full cure without storage the same user can't write (signing the flag would not stop a rollback). The test `documentedResidualAWholeSettingsRollbackClearsTheDebtAndThePauseResumes` asserts today's behaviour. N6 (two concurrent provisions of one profile could interleave the revision check and the payload write in `EngineServiceBackend.provision`) is outside this round and noted for 2.0.3.
- **D10.11-7 Corrections.** D10.10-3 (the owed flag closes a quit or crash while owed and a surgical edit, not a whole-file rollback, D10.11-6; the agent writes it at once, D10.11-2; the launch's reconcile waits, D10.11-3), D10.10-4 (NE's restart of a signable hold, D10.11-1) and risk 31 (b) are corrected in place.

### Draft 10.10

Draft 10.10 folds in the 2.0.2 round 6 review (Fable round 6: GO, L1, L2, N1–N4; Codex round 6: #1–#3) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026).
- **D10.10-1 An answer belongs to its prompt's payload revision (§5.2; Codex r6 #1).** Each live prompt carries the payload revision of the attempt that prompted (`LivePrompt.revision`); its stashed answer keeps it (`Session.answerRevision`; a prepared answer has none). The next attempt reads the payload bytes and their revision in ONE store read (`ExtensionSecretStore.load`) and drops an answer of another revision (its response, challenge cookie and carried credentials belong to that server; the server prompts again). So an attempt that loaded revision 2 before revision 2's commit reached the controller never sends revision 1's answer.
- **D10.10-2 The save's revision check and its write are one store operation (§5.2, §6.3; Codex r6 #2 = Fable r6 N1).** `saveAnswer` writes through `ExtensionSecretStore.putCredential(_:ownerUID:ifPayloadRevision:)`: inside the store actor, synchronously, the stored payload's revision is compared with the answer's and the credential written only if they match (both stores; nothing can provision between the check and the write). The second, separate revision read after the credential read is gone. A revision provisioned at any point before the write keeps its own credentials.
- **D10.10-3 The pause's one-time value stays owed until it is spent (§10.4; Codex r6 #3, Fable r6 N4b).** Every spend of `.pause` that fails (the launch's spend with nothing paused, both spends at a pause's end, every spend in the resume agent) sets `AppSettings.pauseValueOwed` (written durably). GUI: retried `maxResumeIntentRetries` times `resumeIntentRetryDelay` apart, then at each `ProfilesStore.load()`, each wake and the next launch, while no pause holds a value of its own and none is being made; a pause's end spends an owed value BEFORE it checks its record (if it can't, the end is retried like an unreadable keychain); a pause that seals a value clears the debt (the seal replaces the value). `resume()` no longer ignores a failed `consumeRecord`. The agent is not unregistered while the value is owed (GUI end of a pause, launch reconcile); the agent spends an owed value first in every run and stays registered until a run spends it. `pauseValueOwed` is not authenticated (same-user code can clear it, as it can delete settings.json); it bridges a quit or crash while the keychain is unavailable. *(Draft 10.11: it does not survive a whole-file rollback of settings.json, a documented residual, D10.11-6; the agent writes it before any return, D10.11-2; the launch's reconcile waits for the launch's spend, D10.11-3; an extension while owed carries no profile, D10.11-4.)*
- **D10.10-4 Pause signs a live session only if this run started it or saw it connected (§10.4; Fable r6 L1).** The `resumableSession` rule of D10.9-2 now applies to the live session too, at both places Pause picks its target (before and after its durable write): a start made elsewhere while it is `.connecting` (a refused `scutil --nc start` whose `.connecting` NE delivers) is stopped by the Pause like every live session, never signed. At launch a session found `.reasserting` (it was connected) is inserted like one found `.connected`. *(Draft 10.11, D10.11-1: NE's restart of a signable hold, a crash gap or a verified network-restart hold, stays signable while `.connecting`; until then this rule cost that legitimate Pause, Fable r7 L1.)*
- **D10.10-5 A start without a kill switch compares a commit with the revision NE started it under (§5.2; Fable r6 L2).** D10.9-4's comparison with `loadedRevision` is kept for kill-switch starts only. A start without a kill switch is ended by any commit above its configuration's revision again (round 6 Codex M2), so a same-revision retry after a failed credential write ends a start of the old configuration that already loaded the new payload beside the old revision's credentials.
- **D10.10-6 The real keychains are never a default argument (Fable r6 N3).** `HeadlessResume.perform(keychain:)`, `SystemKeychainSecretStore.init(backend:)` and `TunnelSecretStore.make(backend:)` take their keychain with no default; the production call sites pass `DataProtectionKeychain()` / `SecItemBackend()` explicitly and every test passes a fake, so a test that forgets one doesn't compile instead of reaching a real keychain.
- **D10.10-7 Corrections.** D10.9-2 (live sessions follow the same rule from D10.10-4), D10.9-4 (the `loadedRevision` comparison is for kill-switch starts, D10.10-5; the save's re-check is replaced by D10.10-2), risk 29 (1) (rules withdrawn while the session is down leave the same record, Fable r6 N4a) and risk 31 (b) are corrected in place.

### Draft 10.9

Draft 10.9 folds in the 2.0.2 round 5 review (Fable round 5: GO, L1, L2, N1–N4; Codex round 5: #1–#7) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026). Coordinator decision: the user-stop notice for sessions that are already down (D10.7-3, D10.8-3, D10.8-4) kept producing timing findings in every round (Codex r4 #2, r5 #1, #3, #4); it is **removed**, not patched again.
- **D10.9-1 No user-stop notice (§7.2, §10.4; Codex r5 #1, #3, #4; Fable r5 L1, N1, N3).** Removed end to end: `RevokeUnattendedRequest.userStops`, the stop-only request (`keepProfileIDs` is required again), `UserStopNotice`, the extension's `userStopped` and the guard's refusal by notice (`replayOf`, `endedByUserStop`), the app's `noteUserStop`, `pendingUserStops` in `settings.json` and its delivery (capabilities, busy retry, next launch), the voiding at Connect and Connected, and the resume agent's notices. App and extension ship together and the peer floor admits only the same build, so the fields are simply gone. A user stop that reaches a LIVE session ends its record through NE's `stopTunnel` (`stop(.userInitiated)`), as before round 3. Kept from rounds 3–4: kill-switch starts that survive a commit (D10.7-1, D10.8-1), capacity and schema salvage (D10.8-6), sealed Auto-Connect, holds and pauses, one-time values, paged revoke batches, the private read queue, the validator's exit window, the hello retry (it also gates reconcile), and round 3's N1 marks (a replay waiting in the guard across a LIVE user act: the user's stop of the running session, a removed configuration, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets`, is refused and its record never put back). Fable r5 L1 (a `.replay` admission keeping the old `at`) is moot: `AuthorisedStart.at` now only orders capacity eviction, so a replay refreshes nothing that matters. Residual: §20 risk 29 (1).
- **D10.9-2 Pause signs only a hold of a session this run started or saw connected (§10.4; Fable r5 L2 = Codex r5 #2).** Pause still stops a crash gap (`.awaitingRestart`, the session down) and a network-restart hold, so the pause holds. It signs such a hold as its resume target only if this run issued that session's start or saw it `.connected` (`resumableSession`: set at an issued start, at `.connected`, and for a session already connected at launch; cleared by a new attempt this app didn't issue and by the never-active end of a start made elsewhere). A refused outside start (held 1–10 s online, or as the network-restart hold offline) and a hold re-entered at launch are stopped unsigned (`pausedState.profileID == nil`): the pause's end arms and starts nothing. *(Draft 10.10, D10.10-4: the same rule now also decides whether a LIVE session is signed; until then a start made elsewhere was signed while `.connecting`, Fable r6 L1.)*
- **D10.9-3 "Nothing paused" spends the pause's one-time value (§10.4; Codex r5 #5).** The resume agent with no `pausedUntil` consumes `.pause` before it unregisters; if the delete fails it returns `.keychainUnavailable` and stays registered for the next run. The GUI launch with no `pausedUntil` consumes it too, retried (`maxResumeIntentRetries`, `resumeIntentRetryDelay` apart) while nothing is paused; the user's Pause first ends that spend (cancel, then wait), so it never deletes the new pause's value. A genuine record whose expiry was removed, written back later with it, never verifies.
- **D10.9-4 Answers and commits are bound to the loaded revision (§5.2; Codex r5 #6, Fable r5 N2).** `Session.loadedRevision` is the payload revision the current attempt loaded (the configuration's until the first load). A commit restarts a kept kill-switch start's prompt only above it, so a same-revision commit (a retry, a reconcile) leaves the new prompt alone. A before-Connected answer is marked in flight across its credential save (`answerInFlight`); a commit meanwhile drops it and starts the fresh attempt, and the answer is stale after the await. Its save is bound to the revision the prompt's attempt loaded and checked again after the credential read, so it never overwrites a newer revision's credentials. *(Draft 10.10: the comparison with `loadedRevision` applies to kill-switch starts only, a start without a kill switch compares with its configuration's revision again, D10.10-5 (Fable r6 L2); the re-check after the read was not atomic with the write and is replaced by the store's conditional write, D10.10-2; an answer is also bound to its prompt's revision, D10.10-1.)*
- **D10.9-5 An unchecked "off" is sealed (§10.4; Codex r5 #7).** A disabled Auto-Connect choice whose check is `.unavailable` at load is sealed like an invalid one (owed and retried, at the latest at the next `load()`), so an "off" whose seal a quit cut short never stands beside an older enabled tag's one-time value.
- **D10.9-6 Corrections.** D10.7-3, D10.8-3 and D10.8-4's notice, and D10.8-4's "Pause … signed as the pause's target" without condition, no longer hold (struck through in place). Risks 29 (1), 30 (1) and 31 are rewritten as one entry (risk 29 (1)); risk 31 lists the refusal paths that remain.

### Draft 10.8

Draft 10.8 folds in the 2.0.2 round 4 review fixes (Fable round 4: L1–L3, N1–N6; Codex round 4: #1–#4) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026).
- **D10.8-1 A commit never ends a kill-switch start in the guard (§7.2; Fable L1 = Codex r4 #1).** Narrows D10.7-1's exception for guarded starts. `GuardedStart` records the start's kill switch (`includeAllNetworks` or the profile's `policy.killSwitch`); `payloadCommitted` invalidates only guarded starts WITHOUT one, in every wait (a duplicate beside its running profile, a `.stopping` incumbent of any profile, a stale session's teardown after NE stopped the old instance). A kept start is admitted when its wait ends and loads the committed payload (`runStarting` accepts a configuration older than the payload), as NE's restart after a Save Only does. The round 7 `staleRevision` rule for a reservation holder is gone (a holder is always a kill-switch start). D10.7-1's "starts still in the guard keep the round 5 rule" no longer holds for kill-switch starts.
- **D10.8-2 A kept kill-switch start at a live prompt (§5.2; Fable N2).** On a commit, a kill-switch start before Connected whose prompt is live (or whose answer is stashed) gets a fresh attempt on the committed payload: the prompt is resolved (`promptResolved`), the stash dropped, the adapter torn down; the server prompts again if it asks. The old revision's carried credentials and challenge cookie are never sent to the next attempt.
- **D10.8-3 User-stop notices are bound to the stopped generation (§7.2; Codex r4 #2, Fable N1).** *(Draft 10.9, D10.9-1: removed with the notice; its "never ends a newer session's record" claim did not hold for a replay-admitted session, Fable r5 L1, nor for a stop task that ran late, Codex r5 #1.)* `RevokeUnattendedRequest.userStops` (`[UserStopNotice]`: profile + `stoppedAt`, the app's wall clock, whole seconds rounded down) replaces `userStoppedProfileIDs`. The extension clears a record only if it was admitted at or before `stoppedAt` (and its session isn't running there), and refuses only a guarded replay whose matched record is that old; a notice delivered late never ends a NEWER session's record (on-demand, System Settings, NE's own restart of it). A request with `keepProfileIDs == nil` is a stop-only notice (no revoke, never paginated): the app sends its stops that way, apart from the keep set's pages, so a failed later page never resends a delivered stop and a keep set over the cap never holds one back (Fable N6). The app also voids a pending notice when a session of that profile reaches Connected.
- **D10.8-4 User stops are queued, durable and sent from the agent too (§7.2, §10.4; Codex r4 #3, Fable L2).** *(Draft 10.9: the queue, its delivery and the agent's notices are removed, D10.9-1; Pause in a crash gap stays, signed only under D10.9-2.)* Every user stop is recorded at once in `settings.json` (`pendingUserStops`, one per profile with the latest time, ≤ 64), written durably, and delivered when the extension's capabilities are known: at once, after the first successful hello (the hello is now retried, 10 s … 300 s, five times), after a busy answer's retry, at the next launch. Not sealed, by design: a forged entry can only end the record of a session admitted before its time that is not running, which same-user code can already do with `scutil --nc stop`, and it starts nothing. The resume agent's two stops of a held restart send the notice (capped by its 5 s budget) or leave it in `settings.json` for the GUI. Pause in a crash gap (`.awaitingRestart`, the session down): the session is stopped like a running one (cancelling NE's restart), told to the extension, and signed as the pause's target.
- **D10.8-5 The pause's one-time value is spent at every end (§10.4; Codex r4 #4).** The GUI's end of a pause and the resume agent consume `.pause` whatever the record says: a known target (as before), an unknown profile, no profile (`profileID` removed) or no record at all. Only the retryable "keychain unavailable" outcome keeps it.
- **D10.8-6 Records survive capacity and schema (§7.2; Codex r4 on FIX3 refusal path 2).** Past the 256-record cap the record that goes is the oldest without a kill switch, then the oldest kill-switch record of the ADMITTING owner, another owner's kill-switch record only when nothing else is left; never the one just admitted nor the running session's. A `state.plist` that doesn't decode as a whole or carries another schema starts empty except for its start authorisations, salvaged record by record (a damaged pair skipped; kill-switch records first if over the cap); records of another boot are still dropped at load.
- **D10.8-7 Smaller fixes (Fable N3–N6).** The user-clear marks a guarded replay checks exist only while a start is in the guard (none recorded otherwise, all dropped when the last guarded start ends). An "off" Auto-Connect choice whose seal failed is owed and resealed (30 s later, and at every `load()`; never an untrusted enabled choice). Reconcile never removes the extension copy of a profile whose NE configuration still exists, and the orphan sweep keeps an orphaned kill-switch configuration (`includeAllNetworks` or `enforceRoutes`) for 120 s after this run first saw it orphaned (NE's restart gap this run may not track), except one the user deleted in this run. The hold record's consume joins the seal/consume chain synchronously.

### Draft 10.7

Draft 10.7 folds in the 2.0.2 round 3 review fixes (Fable round 3: M1, L1–L4, N1–N7, and its verdict that a kill-switch record is never revoked; Codex round 3: #1–#9) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026).
- **D10.7-1 A profile change never fails a kill-switch start (§7.2; Codex r3 #1, HIGH).** `payloadCommitted` (every provision of a higher revision) no longer ends the waiting start of a session protected by its start-time or live flags (`includeAllNetworks` or `enforceRoutes`). Such a start may be NE's authorised replay that nothing else would start again (a Save Only revision verified and provisioned in the background while NE restarts the old one), and a failed protected start is open. It goes on: an attempt in flight finishes on the payload it loaded; a hold stays held (closed) and its next attempt (its own timer, or the new credentials of the same provision) loads the committed payload under the configuration NE started with, exactly as NE's restart after a Save Only does. A start without a kill switch still ends (the app starts the new revision). Starts still in the guard keep the round 5 rule (a duplicate of an older revision ends): each waits beside a live session of its own profile, which goes on protecting. *(Draft 10.8, D10.8-1: wrong for a `.stopping` incumbent and a stale session's teardown; no kill-switch start in the guard is ended by a commit any more.)* This narrows D9-20's "never the new payload under the old configuration" to starts without a kill switch.
- **D10.7-2 The Auto-Connect choice is sealed in every state (§10.4; Fable M1, Codex r3 #2).** The tag covers `enabled` and the profile (`autoconnect-choice.v2\n<0|1>\n<profile>`); "off" is sealed too, so every change replaces the one-time value and a copy of an earlier enabled choice stops verifying once the user turned it off. The first 2.0.2 launch seals whatever the choice is (a disabled choice whose tag doesn't verify is re-sealed; it gives no plan either way): from then on the keychain item exists, which same-user code can't reset, so the trust-once migration (`.neverSealed` with an enabled choice) happens at most on the first launch after the update. A disabled choice that can't be sealed drops its tag silently.
- **D10.7-3 User stops reach the extension (§7.2; Fable L1, N1; Codex r3 #3).** *(Draft 10.9, D10.9-1: the notice is removed; only the counting of LIVE user acts below, round 3 N1, remains.)* Every user stop in the app (Disconnect, Cancel of a recovery or of NE's awaited restart, Pause, Delete, a switch) also sends `RevokeUnattendedRequest.userStoppedProfileIDs` (≤ 16; delivered with the next revoke, retried with it when busy; a later Connect of the same profile voids an undelivered one). The extension ends that profile's whole record, a kill-switch session's included, unless that profile's session is running there (its own `stop(.userInitiated)` clears it, and a session the user started again before the notice arrived keeps its record); pending arms stay. This is the authority of a user stop that reaches a live session, distinct from the passive revoke, which still never touches a kill-switch record. Every user act that ends a record (the user's stop, a removed configuration, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets`, the notice) is counted; a replay decided before such an act and still waiting in the guard is refused (225) once it is seen, and the record is put back at admission only after a non-user removal.
- **D10.7-4 Records (§7.2; Fable N2, N3; Codex r3 #8).** A fresh controller that can't read `kern.bootsessionuuid` drops no record. A running session's record gets `killSwitch` as soon as its live flags (or start-time flags) say so, saved at once (at Connected and at every flag change the provider seat reports), not only at an orderly end. A keep set larger than 500 is sent as up to 20 pages of one batch (`batch`, `page`, `pageCount`); the extension applies the union only once every page of the newest batch arrived, never one page's complement on its own; a request of an older app decodes as one page. Over 10,000 kept profiles the app sends nothing (fault log).
- **D10.7-5 Recovery holds and one-shot values (§10.4; Codex r3 #4, Fable L2).** `networkRestartHold` is a settings record (`network-restart-hold`, `networkRestartHoldTag`): sealed when the hold is recorded, its one-time value consumed when the hold ends (seals and consumes run in order). At launch the hold is re-entered as before (it holds the restore back) but stays *unverified* until its tag verifies; invalid, `.neverSealed` (forged, a copy of an ended hold, one written before 2.0.2): dropped; keychain unavailable: kept, unverified. An unverified hold is stopped by a pause like any other but is never the pause's signed target. *(Draft 10.9, D10.9-2: a verified hold is signed only if this run started that session or saw it connected; a hold re-entered at launch never is.)* `revocationHeld` no longer reads the record from settings.json (the app's own hold is a pending entry). Every end of a pause (GUI and headless agent, a refused check, a failed start, a record naming no known profile) and of `resumeAfterUpdate` consumes the kind's one-time value whatever the check says, except `.unavailable` (retried).
- **D10.7-6 Reconcile and quarantine (§6.4; Fable L3).** Corrects D10.6-7, which held for a quarantined profile only until the next `load()`: `ProfileRepository.list()` now reports every ID with a `<id>.json.tampered.<stamp>` file and no `<id>.json` as quarantined, at every load, so it keeps its extension copy and its VPN configuration until the user deletes it (Delete removes the quarantined copies too). Independently, reconcile never removes the extension copy of a profile whose session is live, starting, or awaiting NE's restart: such a removal is queued in `pendingRemovals` until a reconcile finds it idle.
- **D10.7-7 Opened files (§11.1; Fable L4, N5; Codex r3 #7).** Reads run on a private concurrent dispatch queue, never on Swift's cooperative pool; a read given up after 10 s stays counted until it returns, and with 4 such reads outstanding a new read is refused at once. The first failed or timed-out read ends its import (the event's remaining files are not read). The import slot is taken synchronously before an import's task exists (a burst of open events queues against the cap). An opened import presents only when no sheet is up and no other import (the user's own, begun during its analysis) is still being analysed; its sheet watch is re-armed on every pass.
- **D10.7-8 Self-test evidence (§10.2; Codex r3 #5, #6).** `ProbeEvidence` tracks attempts: a `.preparing` after a `.waiting`, or on a usable path, clears the waiting evidence and marks the connection as attempted; a later wait, timeout or "no path" failure of an attempted connection is never a local refusal and never "no IPv6 here" (inconclusive). "No IPv6 here" needs the default route to prove absence (`RouteProbe.defaultRouteLookup`: none, or into a utun or lo0) and no contrary destination evidence (the attempted address routed out a physical interface, or a failed lookup: uncertainty); a failed default-route lookup is uncertainty, not absence.
- **D10.7-9 Validator client (§8.1; Codex r3 #9, Fable N7).** After the service's own `.timeout` answer the client drops the connection and waits the exit grace before it retries or throws, on the final timeout too, so the next request never meets the dying process early. The expected-exit window (1 s, was 2 s) is kept across requests: an interruption inside it is the earlier request's watchdog exit, retried without spending the next request's crash retry. A real crash inside that window is misread as the exit (the profile stays "Not yet verified", never refused).
- **D10.7-10 Smaller fixes (Fable N4, N6).** An unknown-connection trigger suppressed by the quiet period, or arriving while a reload is under way, is made up by one reload when the quiet (or that reload) ends: at most one reload per quiet period. A profile verified by a pass that ran before provisioning was allowed (the launch's un-awaited pass) is provisioned by the first reconcile's own pass, not at the next reconcile.

### Draft 10.6

Draft 10.6 folds in the 2.0.2 round 2 review fixes (Fable round 2: M1, M2, L1–L8, N1–N5; Codex round 2) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026).
- **D10.6-1 Authenticated settings records (§10.4, §12.3; Fable M1, L5, N3).** Every settings.json record that can make the app start a profile or give one unattended-start consent carries a tag: HMAC-SHA256 with the record kind's own HKDF key (`"lockplus.record-mac.<kind>.v1"` from the keychain master key; no longer the metadata key) over a one-time value and the record's message. The one-time value is a keychain item of the app's access group (`…record-nonce`, account = kind), replaced at every seal (older copies stop verifying) and deleted when the record is acted on (one shot). Kinds: `pause` (`PausedState.intent`, message `resume-intent.v2\n<profile>\n<end>`), `pending-resume` (`PendingResume.intent`, `<profile>\n<reason>`) and `autoconnect-choice` (`AutoConnectRules.choiceTag`, the enabled choice's profile). A record that fails restores on-demand only. The Auto-Connect choice read at launch gives a plan only once verified; in-process changes (the pane, the Go migration, a delete) are trusted and sealed (`SettingsStore.onAutoConnectChoiceChange`); a failing choice is turned off with a Problems line; a choice from before 2.0.2 (no record of the kind ever sealed) is trusted once and sealed; an unreadable keychain leaves it unverified (no plan) until a later load. The keychain being unavailable is retryable everywhere (`RecordCheck.unavailable`): the agent returns `.keychainUnavailable` with nothing changed; the GUI keeps the pause and retries every 30 s (5×). A pause that can't seal its intent doesn't happen (Problems line). Extending a pause carries the earlier profile only if the earlier intent verifies. The GUI's note names the real reason (changed outside, older than 7 days, earlier version, keychain).
- **D10.6-2 Unknown connection objects (§3.4; Fable M2).** A status change of an unknown connection object reloads only when it is connecting, connected or reasserting; at most one such reload per second, and one that finds no new configuration silences the trigger for 10 s; it never moves the settle clock (`waitUntilSettled`). A stray that goes live while its profile's addressable copy is idle reloads the same way (the F8 tie-break then sees its status).
- **D10.6-3 Records NE may still need (§7.2; Fable L1–L4, Codex r2 #2, #8).** `AuthorisedStart` keeps the last armed nonce and an `unattended` flag side by side (neither overwrites the other), its boot session (`kern.bootsessionuuid`; a record of another boot is dropped when the controller loads) and `killSwitch` (the session's protection at admission, or its live flags at its end). **A kill-switch session's record is never revoked** (Codex r2 #2, the plan's stop condition): NE restarts such a session by itself after a crash, `noNetwork` or `providerFailed`, and in that gap there is no session the extension could check; only the user's stop, a removed configuration, the profile's removal, a wipe or the next boot end it. Consent for NEW unattended sessions is the configuration's on-demand rules (row 3), which go with the plan. `revokeUnattended` now names the profiles that KEEP consent (`RevokeUnattendedRequest.keepProfileIDs ≤ 500`, request cap 32 KiB, a maximal request test-asserted to fit): the app sends the profiles with a plan plus every profile that is live, has a pending entry or is the recorded network-restart hold; the extension clears the `unattended` fact of every other record of the caller whose session NE never restarts (no kill switch: a leftover of a process that died before the session's end could drop it), never the running session's or one with a start in the guard (a record left with no nonce goes). A replay that waited in the guard puts its matched record back at admission. The app also sends a revoke each time everything has settled after being busy. An `.extensionBusy` answer is retried once after 25 s.
- **D10.6-4 Legacy extension (§7.2; Fable L6).** On `.legacyExtension` a kill-switch start is refused in the GUI and the headless agent, whatever the update marker says.
- **D10.6-5 Opened files (§11.1; Fable L7, N4).** Every import (chosen, dropped, pasted, opened) counts as analysing from its first read to its sheet; an open event starts only when nothing is analysing and no sheet is up, and its sheet is presented only when no sheet is up. At most 5 open events wait (more: one "Too many files" message). A read that takes over 10 s is given up as unreadable. "Opened from" is never truncated, and a folder whose name starts with "~" is quoted.
- **D10.6-7 Reconcile never removes an existing profile (§6.4; Codex r2 #1).** Only verified profiles are provisioned, but the removal set is "no local profile at all" (plus the user's Delete queue): a profile whose current revision is "Not yet verified" (a Save Only while the check is unavailable) or that is quarantined keeps its extension copy, i.e. the approved payload, its credentials and a connected session's start authorisation, until an approved replacement is provisioned or the user deletes it.
- **D10.6-8 Self-test evidence (§10.2; Codex r2 #5–#7).** `ProbeEvidence`: readiness on an interface clears an earlier `.waiting`, and a timeout after readiness reports the readiness and the interface (packets left), never a stale "no path". An IPv6 unreachable failure is route-checked against the address the connection attempted (from its path), with `RouteProbe.routeLookup` telling "no route" (`ESRCH`) from a failed lookup; unknown address or failed lookup: inconclusive. Split DNS: the profile's own servers are route-checked (via the tunnel, else mismatch; servers unknown: inconclusive), and the row says only that those servers are reached through the tunnel. The validator client also treats an interruption within 2 s of the service's own `.timeout` as its watchdog exit (still a timeout, never "crashed", Codex r2 #9).
- **D10.6-6 File checks that don't finish (§8.1; Fable L8, N1, N2).** `reconcile` runs `verifyPending` last (after provisioning, removals and the revoke), and `verifyPending` provisions what it verifies; the launch doesn't await it. At most 3 timeouts per run in total; `verifyTimeoutRuns` (settings.json) counts the launches in which a profile timed out, and after 3 only "Check Again" (profile hero) retries it. The validator client waits 300 ms after the service's own `.timeout` before reconnecting. The 2.0.1 payload migration checks each stored revision once per run.

### Draft 10.5

Draft 10.5 folds in the 2.0.2 round 1 review fixes (Fable, Sonnet, Codex round 1; the 2.0.1 VM E2E findings F6–F8) into 2.0.2 (still build 200026). The plan's stop condition (NE's restart of a live kill-switch session must never get 225) was violated by D10.4-5 as written and is fixed here.
- **D10.5-1 Start authorisation belongs to the session (§7.2; Fable H1, Sonnet M2, Codex 2).** A provision, of a higher revision or not, no longer clears the record ("Save Only" keeps a connected session up on the old payload). Unattended admissions are recorded too (`AuthorisedStart.nonce == nil`) and admit a non-manual restart of that profile after its on-demand rules went away; an armed record never admits a non-manual start and an unattended record never a manual one. The record of a session without a kill switch goes when it ends (NE never restarts those); the 256 cap never evicts the record just admitted or the running session's; a failed `state.plist` write or a discarded file is a fault log.
- **D10.5-2 Unattended consent is explicit and revocable (§7.2, §10.4; Codex 4).** A profile picked for Auto-Connect while the toggle is off has no plan (so `providerConfiguration.onDemand == false`); a pause keeps the plan. New XPC method `revokeUnattended` (`RevokeUnattendedRequest {profileIDs ≤ 500}`, error-only, 2 s, gated on `.startAuthorisation`): the app sends every profile without a plan after each on-demand re-save and each reconcile; the extension drops their unattended records except the running session's.
- **D10.5-3 Resume intent (§10.4; Codex 3).** `PausedState.intent`: HMAC-SHA256 with the metadata key over `"lockplus.resume-intent.v1\n<profileID>\n<pause end, whole seconds>"`. The headless agent and the GUI's resume arm and start the record's profile only with a valid intent for a pause end at most 7 days old; otherwise they restore on-demand as recorded and start nothing (the GUI notes it). The pause end is stored in whole seconds.
- **D10.5-4 Validator outcomes (§5.4, §8.1; Fable M1, Sonnet M1/L2/L5).** Per-method watchdogs in the service (evaluate 10 s, readArchive 25 s) that answer `.timeout` ("watchdog") before the exit; client timeouts = watchdog + 2 s; hello 5 s. A timeout drops the connection and is retried once on a fresh process, then is `.timeout`; a hello timeout is retried once, then `.extensionUnavailable`. Only `.profileCheckCrashed` is a verdict (`OVPNEngineEvaluation.Verdict.checkCrashed`, no category string); every timeout or unavailability is "Not yet verified" (import, editor, migrator) and `verifyPending` persists only verdicts, retrying a timed-out profile at most twice per run.
- **D10.5-5 The engine-check boundary (§8.1; Fable L1, N1, N2, N5; Codex 1, 5, 8; Sonnet L3, L4).** `ProfilesStore.provision` refuses an unverified profile for every caller (the 221 retry included), `OnDemandPlan` is nil for one; verdicts commit only for the checked revision and digest; Duplicate takes one snapshot; import floors follow the emitted directives (a `link-mtu` profile now gets the mssfix floor, so every canonical text is a fixed point) and reconcile migrates a stored 2.0.1 payload that isn't one (new unverified revision, checked before provisioning). Reply entry names are leaf names; `ValidateProfileReply` caps its strings; `.nameTooLong` and `.moreSkipped(n)` issues; `ZipCaps()` defaults are the shipped caps. New SPM target `LPOptionsParser` (`ShimOptionsParser`, `ProfileCheckRules`): the extension links it instead of `LPEngineCheck` (lint and `verify.sh static` enforce it).
- **D10.5-6 Opened files (§11.1; Fable L2, L3; Codex 11).** An open event's import queues behind a shown sheet or a running analysis, names its source ("Opened from …"), has no default button and enables Import after 1 s. Every chosen or opened path is read off the main actor: `open(O_NONBLOCK)`, `fstat` S_IFREG, size cap before the read.
- **D10.5-7 Connection self-test proof (§10.2; Fable M2, M3; Sonnet M3, L9; Codex 6, 7, 9, 10).** The interface is the one the connection's `NWPath` used and must be the session's utun (found by its addresses only when exactly one utun owns them; any other owner makes the result inconclusive). "Blocked" only for a proven local refusal (path unsatisfied with no interface, or an unreachable error whose route lookup for the probe host's IPv6 address is no route, lo0 or the session's utun); refused/reset/TLS mean packets left. `.waiting` no longer ends a probe at once. The headline claims only what the rows proved; Copy Results redacts every row and detail.
- **D10.5-8 Duplicates and refusals as they happen (§7.2, §11.7; E2E F6–F8).** Equal-revision copies of a profile's configuration are told apart deterministically (live first, then the more protective, then the first), never by NE's list order; a status change of an unknown connection object reloads; a never-connected end with no error yet is read again (0.5/1/1.5 s). While the old extension runs and its replacement awaits approval, a kill-switch profile isn't started without a nonce (Fable L4).
- **D10.5-9 Tooling.** `assert-test-count.sh` counts passed tests and caps skips per plan; `release.sh` requires `LP_PREV_APP` and `verify.sh pre` fails without it in a release run (Fable N4).

### Draft 10.4

Draft 10.4 folds in 2.0.2 (version 2.0.2, build 200026; commits `73920bb1`..`4f0480e6`), built from `PLAN-2.0.2.md` with the owner's decisions D-1 to D-6 all taken as recommended (2026-11-11). Outcomes: D-1 System Settings/`scutil` starts of profiles without Auto-Connect are refused (D10.4-5); D-2 another user's armed kill-switch start keeps priority (D10.4-5); D-3 QR entry points removed (D10.4-9); D-4 `.ovpn` Default, `.conf`/`.zip` Alternate (D10.4-7); D-5 no exit-address check (D10.4-8); D-6 shipped as 2.0.2, with item 3 (start authorisation) the cut candidate for 2.0.3 if E2E-8 S6/S8 fail and the fix isn't trivial (items 1 and 2 aren't cuttable). Unit- and package-tested on the dev Mac; the VM rows (E2E-8: V1–V7, R1–R3, S1–S11, O1–O9, T1–T7) are still open. Where the plan and the code differ, this document follows the code and says so.
- **D10.4-1 Profile checks out of the root extension (§1.3 A3, §1.4 inv. 2, §2.2–§2.4, §2.7, §8.1; 2.0.2 item 1).** Every openvpn3/OpenSSL check of a profile that isn't yet a running session moved into **`LockPlusValidator.xpc`**, an XPC service embedded at `LockPlus.app/Contents/XPCServices/` (bundle ID `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.validator`): it runs as the user, launched per app connection, with `com.apple.security.app-sandbox` as its only entitlement (no network, no files beyond its empty container, no keychain or app group). New package `Packages/ProfileValidator`: `LPEngineCheck` (`ShimOptionsParser`, `OpenVPNEngineCheck`, `WireGuardEngineCheck`; the [1]–[7] body of 2.0.1's `ExtensionPayloadValidator.evaluate`, moved; no ZIPFoundation; linked by the service and the extension) and `LPValidatorService` (exported object, zip reader, ZIPFoundation; the service only). The extension's `PayloadValidator` is now `validateForProvision` ([1]–[5] + the new canonical fixed point, no C++) and `validateForStart` (+ [6] on the payload bytes); `evaluateBytes` is gone from `Tunnel/` (lint rule) and `validateProfile` answers `.extensionBusy` without decoding. The app's import, editor, Go migrator and launch re-verify use `ServiceProfileValidator`; `OpenVPN3Options` is no longer linked into the app (it was unused, plan F3). *Deviation:* `LPEngineCheck` carries its own copy of `hasCertAndKey` (TunnelEngine's `CanonicalProfileFacts` logic), because it must not depend on TunnelEngine. Parity: a golden file of 1218 verdicts from the 2.0.1 code.
- **D10.4-2 Validator wire and client (§5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §8.1).** `LPWire/ValidatorWire.swift`: `LPValidatorXPC` (`hello`, `evaluateProfile`, `readArchive`), `LPValidatorWireVersion = 1`, `ValidatorHello {wire, build}`, `ReadArchiveRequest/Reply`, `LPValidatorMethod` with caps and timeouts. *Deviations (Phase 0):* `ReadArchiveReply` carries `archiveError: ZipArchiveError?` (no entries beside it), because the planned struct couldn't express an archive-level refusal; the `readArchive` limits are request 100 MiB + 1 KiB and reply 64 MiB + 256 KiB (plist framing, names, issues); the safe-name rule moved to `LPModel.ZipNames.isSafePath` (LPWire can't see `ZipStructure`). `ValidatorClient` (`LPXPCClient`) runs one request at a time (so an innocent request is never blamed for a crash), retries once on a fresh process after an interruption during a call and maps a second death to `.profileCheckCrashed` (105); a build mismatch in `hello` is `.versionMismatch`. *Deviation:* `evaluateProfile`'s client timeout is 8 s, below the service's 10 s watchdog, so a hanging file surfaces as `.timeout`; `ServiceProfileValidator` maps `.timeout` and `.profileCheckCrashed` to a refusal (report reason `.checkCrashed`, "LockPlus couldn't check this file safely."), every other error to "Not yet verified". A file marked `checkCrashed` is not re-fed to the service by the re-verify.
- **D10.4-3 Zip read in the service, new caps (§3.5, §8.1).** `ZipStructure` and `ProfileZipReader` moved to `LPValidatorService/ArchiveReader.swift`; the app keeps `ProfileZipWriter` (export, diagnostics bundle), which now reads its output back with ZIPFoundation (names, sizes, CRC) instead of `ZipStructure`. *Deviation:* in the service an entry over 1 MiB is an issue without bytes (`.tooLarge`) and the reply's entries total ≤ 64 MiB (`.totalTooLarge` beyond); issues are clipped to 500 and names to 255 bytes so every reply passes `isWireValid`. User-visible limits: 1 MB per profile entry, 64 MB unpacked (2.0.1: 10 MB, 100 MB). An unavailable or crashed service is `ZipArchiveError.checkUnavailable` ("couldn't be checked safely and wasn't imported").
- **D10.4-4 Minimum app build in the peer requirement (§5.3; 2.0.2 item 2).** `APP_REQ` (extension and validator listeners) gains `info [CFBundleVersion] >= "<floor>"` before the team clause; the value is quoted and compared numerically (plan F1: unquoted is a syntax error; `1000000` sorts above `200022`). *Deviation (Phase 0):* the floor is **this build, always**: `SigningRequirements.minimumAppBuild` = `common.sh` `MIN_APP_BUILD` = `LP_BUILD_NUMBER` (200026 for 2.0.2), and `version-check.sh` enforces equality in sources mode on every run, not only for Release. New `VALIDATOR_REQ`, applied by the app's `ValidatorClient`.
- **D10.4-5 Owner-authorised starts (§1.3 A2, §5.2, §7.2, §20 risk 23; 2.0.2 item 3).** New `armStart` (request `ArmStartRequest {profileID, nonce}`, reply `ArmStartReply {expiresAt}`, capability `.startAuthorisation`, start option `lp.startNonce`, refusal `.startNotAuthorised` = 225). `TunnelController.start` decides first (before the latch, the guard, any suspension and any secret read): an armed manual start, NE's replay of an authorised session, or an unattended start of an on-demand profile is honoured; everything else is refused 225. *Deviations:* the authorisation is written when the start is **admitted**, not at the decision, so an armed duplicate that the 2.0.1 guard refuses or holds never overwrites the record NE's replay of the running session needs; arms are in memory, live 15 s by the extension's wall clock (a clock set back invalidates), one pending arm per profile, at most 8 per uid, consumed by the first start carrying the nonce. Clearing rules and the decision table: §7.2. D-1 (as recommended): a System Settings or `scutil` start of a profile without Auto-Connect is refused, also for the owner. D-2 (as recommended): another user's armed kill-switch start still ends a split session (223).
- **D10.4-6 App side of start authorisation (§7.2, §11.2, §11.7).** Every GUI start arms right before `managers.start` (after the settle, network and active-session checks; `gone()` and the network re-checked after the await); a failed arm fails the start. *Deviation:* against an **older extension** (a non-definite, non-timeout arm failure whose own `hello` succeeds without `.startAuthorisation`) the app starts without a nonce, since that extension enforces nothing; definite answers (`profileNotProvisioned`, `profileRevisionStale`, `malformedRequest`, `unauthorizedPeer`, `notOwner`) and timeouts always fail. `HeadlessResume` gets a live `XPCTunnelService` and arms after the held-session handling and **before** any settings or on-demand mutation (cap min(2 s, remaining)): on failure an on-demand profile starts with `crashRestart` options (unattended), a definite refusal takes the existing fail-closed path, otherwise the new outcome `.armUnavailable` changes nothing and keeps the agent registered. The crash restart stays `[:]` (unattended). 225 is read like 222; a Diagnostics line is posted once per profile per 5 min unless the app armed that profile within 15 s.
- **D10.4-7 Open documents (§2.5, §11.1; 2.0.2 item 4).** `CFBundleDocumentTypes`: `net.openvpn.ovpn` Default, `com.wireguard.config.quick` and `public.zip-archive` Alternate (D-4), all Viewer; both types imported, nothing exported. `OpenDocumentRouter` queues open events until the environment is ready, drops non-file URLs, dedupes, caps 20 files per open over all queued events ("Open at most 20 files at a time.") and keeps at most 1000 queued URLs; a flush opens the main window, then runs the ordinary import (preview or batch sheet, nothing saved before Confirm). The "Edit Profile" window group has `.handlesExternalEvents(matching: [])`. Tunnelblick declares `.ovpn` by extension only, so no third-party identifier was added; Viscosity and OpenVPN Connect were not inspected.
- **D10.4-8 Connection self-test (§10.2, §11.5, §14.2; 2.0.2 item 5).** `ConnectionSelfTest` (app) proves the IPv4, IPv6 and DNS paths of the connected profile with at most two TLS fetches of `OnDemandPlan.ownProbeURL` (forced family, 6 s, no proxies) and a route check of the default resolver's servers; no exit-address check (D-5). It runs only on a user's button press. The last report goes into the diagnostics bundle as `selftest.txt`.
- **D10.4-9 QR import removed (§3.5, §11.1, §21; D-3).** QR import never existed (plan F2); its four entry points (two menu items, the onboarding button, the drop-overlay text) are removed and a dropped image says "Images aren't supported." QR decoding is a later item, built inside the validator service.
- **D10.4-10 Carried-over fixes (§20 risk 27; D10.3-9 residual (b), Fable final spot check LOW).** An automatic retry never mutates a manager during another start: `prepareForStart(_:admissible:)` and the pause take the attempt token, and inside each serialized mutation `ConnectionStore.startMutationAllowed` rejects a stale attempt and, for an automatic retry, requires `!othersBusy(except:)`; a refused retry ends with `abandonAutomaticRetry` (Diagnostics "didn't retry …"). The rollback marker records the manager's revision (`pendingRollbacks[id] = {metaRevision, managerRevision}`, memory only), so a second failed edit no longer quarantines the profile. Fable r9 L2 stays a 2.1 item.
- **D10.4-11 Tests and tooling (§15).** New suites: `LPEngineCheckTests` (parity golden), `LPValidatorServiceTests` (archive corpus moved from the app, handler, XPC round trip, watchdog, busy, reply-once), `ValidatorClientTests`, `CanonicalFixedPointTests`, `StartAuthorisationTests`, `StartGuardOrderTests`, `ProvisionValidationTests`, app `ImportPipelineServiceTests`, `StartAuthorisationAppTests`, `OpenDocumentRouterTests`, `InfoPlistTests`, `ConnectionSelfTestTests`, `RouteProbe` lookups. CI runs `swift test` for `Packages/ProfileValidator`; `fuzz_zip_import` compiles `ArchiveReader.swift`; `build-unsigned.sh`, `sign-inside-out.sh` and `verify.sh` know the third bundle. No `fuzz_engine_check` target (no ASan driver for the shim; the parity golden covers the move).

### Draft 10.3

- **D10.3-1 Start guard for a second configuration (§5.1, §7.2; 2.0.1).** Phase 0 (2026-11-10, VM measurement on 26.6.2 and 27.2) measured that macOS starts a second LockPlus configuration while one runs (System Settings, `scutil --nc start`; an on-demand start of the other configuration is not measured but takes the same path), with both providers in the one extension process; the old "NE never starts while a session runs" assumption let the second start displace the first session while NE kept reporting it Connected (a black hole under the kill switch; no leak). The controller now refuses a start beside a session another **live** provider instance owns (`.anotherTunnelActive`, 222), leaving that session, its host binding and its packet flow untouched; a stale session (same instance, one whose `stopTunnel` began, a freed one) is still replaced, and a `stopTunnel` ends only its own instance's session.
- **D10.3-2 Start guard, Fable review fold (§1.3 A2, §7.2, §20 risk 27; Fable review of 91a0c318, 2026-11-10).** (H1) Kill-switch priority: a start with `includeAllNetworks` is not refused by a session without it; that session ends visibly (`.supersededByKillSwitch`, 223: a pending start fails with it, a started session is torn down and its **own** provider cancelled) and the kill-switch start goes on. Kill switch against kill switch stays first-wins, a start without the flag beside a kill-switch session stays refused, and a refused kill-switch profile gets a notification. (M1) `cancelTunnelWithError` goes to the ended session's own provider (`ProcessProviderHost` keeps each bound instance's host until it unbinds). (M2) A start of the running session's own profile from a new instance replaces it (fault logged). (M3) A start whose instance was stopped meanwhile, or whose provider is gone at `bind`, ends with `.startCancelled`; leases carry a generation so a reused instance's late stop can't end its newer session. (L1–L3) The app trusts a 222 only when the snapshot dates it to this attempt and never after a connected session, says so when the blocking session isn't one it sees, and posts one Diagnostics line per profile per 5 min; the extension writes repeated refusals to disk at most once a minute. (L4) `sleep`/`wake` are owner-scoped. The provider's wiring lives in TunnelEngine's `ProviderSeat` (tested).
- **D10.3-3 Start guard, Fable re-check fold (§7.2, §20 risk 27).** The same-profile replacement follows the kill-switch rule (a same-key start without `includeAllNetworks` doesn't replace a kill-switch session) and cancels the replaced session's own provider when it lacks the flag; a start whose lease is no longer current preempts or replaces nothing (checked before every step of the loop); the process host's bindings carry the lease, so a late cancel or a stop's unbind never reaches a reused instance's newer start (`ProviderBindings`, tested); `RealProviderHost` holds its provider `weak`; teardown tasks stay listed until each finishes, so an ignored late stop waits for its engine; the start carries the NE protocol's `includeAllNetworks`/`enforceRoutes` beside the optional configuration; the app re-says a refusal beside a different set of active profiles and reads a 223 only when the snapshot dates it to this disconnect.
- **D10.3-4 Codex review fold (§7.2, §20 risk 27).** No same-profile exception: a live lease is never overridden by `ProfileKey` equality (duplicate configurations); the incumbent of the same profile is replaced only once NE stopped or freed it. The router that dispatches host calls by lease is TunnelEngine's `ProviderHostRouter` (the extension's `ProcessProviderHost.shared`), tested with the controller for a reused instance's late cancel and unbind and a delayed generation-1 start. The app reads a refusal's kill-switch flag from the configuration as it is now, applies the refusal's own freshness rule instead of the 1 s M8 filter, and throttles the kill-switch notice on both paths.
- **D10.3-5 Final reviews fold (§7.2, §20 risk 27).** A duplicate kill-switch configuration of the running kill-switch profile waits, pending and closed, instead of failing open; the preemption decides on the incumbent's effective protection (its provider's live `protocolConfiguration`; U7: a flag save on a connected session is enforced at once) and re-reads it before the cancel; an accepted kill-switch start reserves the slot across the teardown; a `startTunnel` retires the instance's older starts from cancel dispatch at once; the app drops an error read that a newer attempt overtook, reads a 223 on the never-active path, and dates an app-issued start's refusal against the issue. The abandoned-instance case is recorded as an open, accepted risk.
- **D10.3-6 VM E2E of 200023 (§11.2, §11.3, §10.2).** The network side passed all seven guard scenarios on 26.6.2 and 27.2; the app's display didn't. (F1) A start made elsewhere never takes the hero (`currentID`) from a profile NE still reports active: it becomes current once it is `.connected` itself or nothing else is active, and its refusal goes to Diagnostics and to its own detail. (F2) A non-current profile's last 222/223 end is shown in its own detail pane (`ConnectionStore.endNotes`) until it runs again; a 223 also gets a Diagnostics line. (F3) The sidebar's "Protected · h:mm" is re-read every 30 s and a newly current profile never inherits the previous one's session time. (F4) A WireGuard split tunnel without a DNS server sets no DNS and is not DNS-verified (no "overridden" false alarm). (F5) Onboarding step 4's import preview and import errors are presented on top of the onboarding sheet (they were queued behind it, invisible). The first launch of a build (first launch, update) opens the main window, as UI-CONCEPT §11.3 says.
- **D10.3-7 Round 3 structure (§7.2, §20 risk 27). (stray stop removed in D10.3-9).** One source of effective protection (`effectiveProtection`, live provider flags by lease, start-time fallback) for every hold-vs-cancel and guard decision; sessions ended visibly stay tracked through the teardown and are held if protected by then; one lifecycle gate per provider instance (publication, retirement, watermark, bind acceptance and cancel validation) with pinned dispatch outside the bindings lock; waiting starts re-check on a provider's protection change. App: an active successor becomes current when the current profile ends; an app-issued start's time is scoped to its attempt; this user's stray duplicate of an active profile is stopped (then swept at idle).
- **D10.3-8 Round 4 (§7.2, §20 risk 27). (stray stop removed in D10.3-9).** Two protection reads: the guard's verdict and the preemption's keep-or-cancel read the live flags (else the start-time flags), the same read for both; every other hold-vs-cancel, withhold, latch and reconnect-budget decision counts a session as protected when the live OR the start-time flags say so (a flag the system weakened never turns a hold into a cancel). `finishEnding` keeps the session tracked through the summary's plist I/O and reads the protection again right before the cancel; 223 is recorded only for a session that ends; a preempted session's prompt is resolved. Binding takes the lifecycle gate; a freed instance's watermark is dropped. App: only a pending stray duplicate is stopped, once the addressable configuration of its profile is `.connected` (never a connected or reasserting stray), once per attempt; the protective flag heal re-checks `.connected` when its save is issued; a late `.disconnected` keeps the new attempt's issue time.
- **D10.3-9 Round 5 (§7.2, §20 risk 27).** The app no longer stops a stray duplicate (it can't tell a waiter from a protective replacement): Diagnostics names a pending duplicate of an active profile once per attempt, and a duplicate's status change runs the shared recovery (deferred heal and on-demand restore). Extension: every start inside the guard (waiting, holding a reservation, or tearing a stale session down) is tracked by lease, key and revision; `profileRemoved`, `secretsWiped` and a higher revision's provision invalidate it (`.startCancelled`) before admission. The start latch is read again at admission, after every wait (credentials updated meanwhile clear it; one installed meanwhile counts). A preempted session kept because it became protected is held as `.sessionInterrupted` (224), not 223; the rollback after the summary save restores the ring as it was (an entry the append trimmed included). Round 6: a removal or wipe of the preempting start's profile during the preempted session's teardown ends that start, and the preempted session stays down (cancelled with 223: its teardown can't be undone); a higher revision then doesn't end the preempting start (it proceeds on the new payload). Invalidation is committed with the payload: `payloadCommitted` runs right after the payload write (a same-revision retry after a partial failure ends the starts of an older revision too), and a removal invalidates right after the payload delete, before the credential delete. App: every idle-path mutation (the on-demand restore, `load()`'s removals and syncs, `resaveOnDemand`) re-checks its deferral inside the serialization (a skipped restore keeps the pause record); the stray note is keyed by owner and profile (stable across reloads) and posted only beside a `.connected` addressable configuration whose manager carries `includeAllNetworks` (round 7: and only for a duplicate that itself carries `includeAllNetworks`). Round 7: a pending incumbent preempted by a kill-switch start is read again after its 223 is written and kept (the 223 withdrawn) if it became protected meanwhile; an exempted reservation holder that would wait (its preemption vetoed) ends `.startCancelled` instead of waiting as the old revision. Accepted: a same-revision provision (a retry after a partial failure, or the app's re-provision after `profileNotProvisioned`) ends a pending start whose configuration is older than the stored payload, as a higher revision would. App, round 7: one predicate for a start's own configuration work (`otherStartPending`: another configuration, any user's or a stray, in a pending `.connecting` start, or another entry of ours; a connected one doesn't count) re-checked inside the serialization for its own on-demand restore (also bound to its attempt and to its own session not having begun), `prepareForStart`'s saves (skipped: the start fails, it would be refused beside that start anyway) and the pause of the others (this user's own profiles excluded: their pending start is switched out); the on-demand plan itself still holds a profile's on-demand back beside any live session (E2E-3). Every save or removal re-checks its deferral inside the serialization, "behind" recomputed there (user saves, Delete's removal, the rollback, the idle path). The automatic retry after re-provisioning is bound to its attempt and entry and never switches away from (stops) another session; skipped, Diagnostics says so. A failed provision is retried by the next reconcile (the list is in memory only: after a relaunch the next credential update or re-provision brings a partial one up to date). A skipped rollback in `updateMetadata` (the metadata write failed after the manager save, and a start began meanwhile) is remembered IN MEMORY only (round 8: a durable record in settings.json would let same-user code exempt an older, authentic metadata file from replay detection and downgrade the kill switch, N6). While the manager is exactly one metadata revision ahead with the same payload revision, `load()` doesn't read it as a replay and treats it as behind, so the idle sync (or the next start's `prepareForStart`) saves the rollback; the marker is forgotten only on positive confirmation (the manager seen at the metadata revision, a later metadata commit, a Delete), never because one reload missed the manager. After a relaunch in that state the profile is quarantined as any replay (fail closed). Round 8 also: a background retry carries its origin on its pending entry through a wait for a network and ends (Diagnostics) instead of switching away from another session; a vetoed preemptor gives its reservation back; the app's own `.anotherTunnelActive` names another user's or an unseen connection when no profile of this user is active; a 223 of an attempt that never connected has only its own freshness window (round 9: a connected session's sticky 223 still goes through the generic filter). Round 9: the copy's "Disconnect it first" needs one of this user's own (listed) profiles active, else the unseen-blocker copy; the extension answers a `tunnelSnapshot` of an unprovisioned profile with the caller's own recorded error only (the refusal's time for the freshness check); an edit while a rollback is pending skips the burned metadata revision. **Accepted residuals for 2.0.1:** (a) Fable r9 L2, pre-existing: a metadata revision can be reused after a failed write across a relaunch, so an authentic same-revision file with other content can exist and would be healed as drift (a durable, same-user-unwritable high-water mark is a 2.1 design item); (b) Codex r9 MEDIUM, pre-existing: an automatic retry's manager mutation (`prepareForStart`, the pause) can land inside another start of this user's own profile (availability, not a leak; scheduled for 2.0.2, `PLAN-2.0.2.md`).

### Draft 10.1

Draft 10.1 records the fixes for the Fable review of PF 50–53 and the uninstall fix ([`reviews/2026-10-29-fable-pf50-52.md`](reviews/2026-10-29-fable-pf50-52.md), commits `fix(PF-R1…R6)`). - **PF-R1 (medium) A sticky `pluginFailed` is not a crash (§10.4, D10-6, D10-7).** `fetchLastDisconnectError` keeps returning an old 12, so a clean on-demand Disconnect, a stop from System Settings or `scutil`, or another user's stop after an earlier crash was restarted against the user's intent. PF 52 and PF 53 now act only on a **fresh** crash: the session reached `.connected`, and the app's XPC link to the extension was interrupted (the process died) within 10 s before this `.disconnected` (+ 1 s slack) and after the last `.connected` (`CrashRestartPolicy.isFreshCrash`; `TunnelServiceClient.lastInterruption`). Otherwise the 12 is ignored for both.
- **PF-R2 A push never replaces a prompt or an answered attempt (§5.2, §7.2).** `inStartAuth` clears the hold reason; `pushEndpoints` answers `.notHeld` while a prompt is live or the attempt in flight carries an answer (an OTP would be lost and a rejection would count toward the hard latch).
- **PF-R3 A push respects a `.backoff` latch (§7.2).** "Unchanged" compares with the map the start would use now (cache ∪ options ∪ earlier pushes), so a push of the cached IPs doesn't start before `notBefore`.

- **PF-R5 Proxy credentials follow an unauthenticated IP (§9.3, §20 risk 26).** Documented, no code change.
- **PF-R6 `endAttachedSheets` is one bounded loop (§4.4).** At most 8 steps, logged when the cap is hit; termination proceeds.

Draft 10 folds in E2E-1 ([`native/e2e/RESULTS-E2E-1.md`](../../native/e2e/RESULTS-E2E-1.md): the notarized 2.0.0 (200000) and (200001) on LP-macOS-26 26.6.2 and LP-macOS-27 27.0.1, 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-29) and PENDING-FOLD 50–55 with their "Built / Decision" notes (lead, P3). Each item below was checked against the code in `native/` (commits 150df23, d55f291, f6980aa, de36626, 146f0cd, 2040a49, cfeee49, a06412a). **E2E-1 is GO on both OSes** for import, connect/disconnect, the split-tunnel subnet, the kill switch (connected and provider `kill -9`), auth, auto-connect, Sparkle "Check for Updates" and uninstall (bug 3 fixed, not yet re-checked in a notarized build); sleep/wake is N/A in VZ guests.

**Product bugs found by E2E-1 and fixed.**
- **D10-1 Protocol-flag drift is healed, not quarantined; kill-switch starts fail closed (§3.4, §11.2, §5.5; PF 55; de36626; Conflicts bn).** On both VMs the first imported kill-switch profile was moved aside as "tampered" seconds after import. About 50 ms after our first `saveToPreferences`, nehelper logs "SCPreferences signature … does not match saved signature ((null))", re-derives the configuration "from the corresponding SCNetworkService" and posts a new generation with `includeAllNetworks = NO`; the §3.4 rule "equal `metaRevision`, different flags → tampering" then quarantined the authentic metadata and left the weakened configuration. Now equal revisions with different flags are **drift**, healed by re-saving from the metadata (once per profile revision per run; a repeat is a user-visible problem); a lower revision stays replay. Before every start `prepareForStart` settles, re-reads, verifies, makes one repair and otherwise refuses the start with `.killSwitchNotApplied` (104, app-only). Every save is read back and a discrepancy is logged at `.fault`. While drifted, the derived state never claims the kill switch and the profile shows "Restoring this profile's protection settings…". Observed healing on 26 and 27 with 200001.
- **D10-2 A split tunnel routes its own subnet (§8.5; 146f0cd).** On 27 an OpenVPN `topology subnet` profile without pushed routes connected as 10.81.0.2/24 and couldn't reach 10.81.0.1: only the host route existed. `NetworkSettingsBuilder` now adds the connected v4/v6 subnets of the tunnel addresses when that family has no redirect-gateway.
- **D10-3 Uninstall quits, and says when the app can't trash itself (§4.4; cfeee49).** AppKit refused `terminate` while the Settings uninstall sheet was attached ("App termination blocked by modal sheet"), so the uninstalled app kept running. `finishUninstall` now ends every attached sheet before `terminate`. When moving the bundle to the Trash fails (26: the bundle belonged to another administrator, so the move needed authentication), the app says so instead of nothing; a §4.4 residual. **Not yet in a notarized build:** re-check in the next one (§18).

**P3 lead items built (PF 50–53).**
- **D10-4 Fresh endpoint IPs pushed into a held start (§5.2, §5.4, §7.2, §9.3, §20 risk 25; PF 50; Conflicts bp).** New owner-scoped method `pushEndpoints` (`PushEndpointsRequest {profileID, endpoints}` → `PushEndpointsReply {retrying | unchanged | notHeld}`; 2 s, 16 KiB, not secret-bearing; additive, so `LPWireVersion` stays 1). The app pushes on a network change (2 s settle) or wake when the snapshot shows a recoverable before-Connected hold; the held start, or its retry in flight, takes the IPs and re-runs the start sequence. **Limit:** under the flag the app's own DNS is blocked too, so a push mostly helps from mDNSResponder's cache or with a LAN resolver (`allowLAN` on).

The draft 9 residual is gone.

Only while the app runs.

### Draft 9.1

Draft 9.1 records the owner's decisions of 2026-10-27 and the code that follows from them. Everything below is built and unit-tested on the dev Mac; nothing new has run signed.

- **D91-1 German register: du (owner, final; §11.6, UI-CONCEPT §8.3).** The catalog already used du; every new string is du. The open item is closed everywhere (D8-33, §11.6, §18, UI-CONCEPT).
- **D91-2 ZIPFoundation approved and adopted (owner; §2.2, §3.5, §9.2, §14.2, §15.4).** Pinned **0.9.20** exactly (commit `22787ffb`; ≥ 0.9.18 for CVE-2023-39138), app target only, `Package.resolved` committed, `pins.sh` `ZIPFOUNDATION_*`. The pre-adoption review ([`reviews/2026-10-27-zipfoundation.md`](reviews/2026-10-27-zipfoundation.md)) found that the library alone is unsafe for untrusted in-memory input: a 22-byte archive traps `MemoryFile` (F1), ZIP64 values trap `off_t` conversions (F2), the end-record scan covers the whole file (F3), an encrypted entry silently ends the iteration (F4), CRCs are never compared (F6), and inflation is unbounded (F7). Verdict: adopt, behind our own validator. As built (`App/Services/ProfileZip.swift`, the only file that may import it, by lint):
  - **Pass 1, `ZipStructure.validate`:** our own strict parse of the end record, the central directory and every local header. Every offset and range must lie inside the archive. Refused outright: ZIP64, encryption, multi-disk, methods other than stored/deflate, unknown flags, malformed extra fields, local/central disagreement, data descriptors that disagree, overlapping entries, duplicate names (raw or NFC), more than 1000 records or 500 profile entries, more than 100 MiB declared over the profile entries.
  - **Pass 2, ZIPFoundation:** its iteration must match pass 1 exactly (count, order, names, sizes). Only profile entries are inflated, in memory; the consumer stops at the declared size and the CRC must match the central directory.
  - **Per-entry error rows, never silent:** unsafe paths, symlinks, special files, entries over 10 MiB, ratio above 100:1 (for entries over 64 KiB), damaged entries.
  - Directories, `__MACOSX/` and `._*` entries are ignored; nested profiles import under their file name. Imported profiles record `ProfileOrigin.zip(<archive>)`.
  - Export All and the diagnostics bundle are built in memory with ZIPFoundation (`ProfileZipWriter`: deflate, 0600 entries, re-validated by pass 1) and written with `AtomicFile.writeUserFile`; `/usr/bin/ditto` and its scratch directory are gone. Export All is now **one zip** as UI-CONCEPT §6.15 specifies (it wrote loose files into a folder before).
  - `verify.sh static` and `check-symbols.sh` fail on any ZIPFoundation symbol, string or resource in the extension (the `otool -L` check can't see a static library), and `verify.sh` requires it in the app.
  - Fuzz target `fuzz_zip_import` (ASan + coverage, standalone mutation driver) with seeds in `Tools/fuzz/corpus/zip/`; a crafted corpus in `ZipImportTests`.
- **D91-3 64-bit-block ciphers stay unsupported (owner, final; §8.6, §21).** The import rejects every 64-bit-block cipher and `enableLegacyAlgorithms` is never set; re-enabling them needs a new owner decision.
- **D91-4 Update feed and key final (owner; §2.5, §12.1, APP-ROOT).** The appcast is hosted by the public repo `steiale/lockplus-updates` on GitHub Pages: `SUFeedURL = https://steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates/appcast.xml` (committed, fda5159). Update archives go to the GitHub Releases of that repo. `SUPublicEDKey` is real (a75c1f8): generated 2026-10-27 with `generate_keys --account lockplus-native`; the private key is in the owner's login keychain plus an offline backup, and agents never read or touch it. CI no longer sets `LP_ALLOW_SPARKLE_PLACEHOLDERS`; the placeholder gate stays in `verify.sh` and `UpdateController` as a safeguard. The `pages-host.invalid` literal in `UpdateTests` is a test fixture. The §10.4 probe and §22 `security.txt` share this host.
