- ~~**Decision:** the app links `OpenVPN3Options`, the header-only `OptionList` parser, so it can run the openvpn3 differential check at import time without the extension (§8.1).~~ *2.0.2 (D10.4-1):* never used by any app source; unlinked. The import-time differential [6] and [7] run in the validator service.
- **Decision (2.0.2):** profile checks that need openvpn3 or OpenSSL run in `LockPlusValidator.xpc` (sandboxed, as the user), not in the unsandboxed app (it holds the sealing key and every credential) and not in the root extension. Its `main.swift` only calls `ValidatorProcess.run()` (no closure literals, `lp_main_swift_closure`), which calls `LPOpenVPN3Core.initializeCrypto()` first, then `NSXPCListener.service()`, `setConnectionCodeSigningRequirement(APP_REQ)` and `resume()`. Target settings (`Config/Validator.xcconfig`): `ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX`, `ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME`, `SKIP_INSTALL`, `ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB = NO`, `ENABLE_PREVIEWS = NO`, `ENABLE_POINTER_AUTHENTICATION = NO` (arm64-only OpenSSL, as the extension), `LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS = @executable_path/../Frameworks`; Debug and FaultInjection sign manually with Apple Development and no profile (§2.7). Its `CFBundleVersion` is the app's (`verify.sh`); `ValidatorClient` compares builds in `hello`.
- **Decision:** ZIPFoundation (MIT) is the one new dependency, for in-memory zip read and write. Minimum 0.9.18 (CVE-2023-39138, path traversal); it is on the §9.2 watch list. *Draft 9.1:* approved by the owner, reviewed before adoption ([`reviews/2026-10-27-zipfoundation.md`](reviews/2026-10-27-zipfoundation.md)) and pinned at 0.9.20, app target only. *2.0.2:* the read side (with the structural validator) runs in the validator service; the app keeps the writer, which reads its own output back with ZIPFoundation (names, sizes, CRC). Zip import (§3.5), Export All and the diagnostics bundle (§14.2) use it in memory; `/usr/bin/ditto` is no longer used. Every read goes through our structural validator first (the library traps on malformed in-memory archives, review F1/F2); `verify.sh static` and `check-symbols.sh` fail if any of it reaches the extension.
- **Decision (confirmed by S14):** OpenSSL is built **before** Xcode by `Tools/bootstrap/openssl.sh` (`darwin64-arm64-cc no-shared no-module no-tests no-docs no-autoload-config`, `-mmacosx-version-min=26.0`, `-ffile-prefix-map`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the submodule; `make build_libs install_dev`; `libtool -static` merges libssl and libcrypto into one `libOpenSSL.a`; `xcodebuild -create-xcframework -library … -headers`) into `Vendor/build/OpenSSL.xcframework` and consumed as a local binary target: a local package cannot consume an External Build System target's output at compile time, and openvpn3 needs OpenSSL's generated headers. SPM puts the XCFramework's headers on the dependent C++ target's include path both in `swift build` and in Xcode; the `unsafeFlags` fallback is not needed. The build takes ~17 s, so CI caching (keyed on the submodule SHA and the script hash) is optional (ref/toolchain T11). `no-autoload-config` is new in draft 7: S13 found that OpenSSL's default config auto-load reads `openssl.cnf` from `--openssldir` on first use, which is file I/O in [7b] and in every connect (§8.1).
- **Pins recorded by S14:** OpenSSL 3.5.9 (tarball SHA-256 `603f5602…eb859a`), openvpn3 `release/3.11.8` = `4f3bdef7`, asio `asio-1-24-0` (tarball SHA-256 = openvpn3 `ASIO_CSUM`, asserted by the bootstrap script), lz4 1.11.0, wireguard-go `v0.0.0-20261024220952-b3bc704ef0ee` (bridge go.mod, patch W14: x/sys v0.50.0, x/crypto v0.58.0, x/net v0.62.0, `go 1.26.0`), Go 1.27.3, Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Swift 6.4. Build outputs were not yet checked for reproducibility (§12.4 `repro`).
- **`-showBuildSettings` does not work on package targets in Xcode 27.1** (it returns `[]`/`{}`; S14). Checks of package build settings therefore grep the build log's `swiftc`/`clang` lines (`-D…`, `-O…`) or use a compiled probe target that reports what it saw at compile time (the S14 `ProbePkg` pattern). `-showBuildSettings` on project targets (the `LP_DEV_SIGNING` Release check, §5.3) works.
- **Deployment target (O1, draft 7.1):** Xcode targets use `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0` (`Base.xcconfig`). Every LockPlus SPM package (tools 6.2+) declares `platforms: [.macOS(.v26)]`. The vendored wireguard-apple package (tools 6.0) uses the string form `.macOS("26.0")` (W0, §9.2). OpenSSL and the cgo objects get `-mmacosx-version-min=26.0` (above; W1).
- SPM packages enable `NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault`, `InferIsolatedConformances` and `MemberImportVisibility` in every target (SC1, Conflicts z). They define **no** configuration-dependent conditions: SwiftPM knows only debug and release, so package code built for a configuration not named Debug (such as `FaultInjection`) does not see `DEBUG`; every configuration-specific switch (`LP_DEV_SIGNING`, `LP_FAULT_INJECTION`) lives in the Xcode targets' `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS` (§5.3, §15.2).
- **Consequence (draft 6):** package code cannot see target-level globals either. `APP_REQ` and `EXT_REQ` (defined in the targets' `ActiveRequirements.swift`, §5.3) therefore reach package code only as **init parameters**: `TunnelServiceListener(peerRequirement: APP_REQ)` (TunnelEngine, created by the extension's `main.swift`) and `TunnelServiceClient(machServiceName:peerRequirement: EXT_REQ)` (`LPXPCClient`, created by the app's `AppEnvironment`). Neither type has a default value for the parameter, and neither package references `SigningRequirements.releaseSigner` at a call site that sets a requirement.
- **Xcode builds package targets as release for a custom configuration such as `FaultInjection`** (forum 45506; **confirmed by S14**: `-O`, no `DEBUG`, asserts off, and package C targets get no `NDEBUG` in Release either): package code there has no `DEBUG`, so its `#if DEBUG` paths (for example `CompletionOnce`'s `assertionFailure`, which is a no-op under `-O`) are off in FaultInjection builds. Project xcconfig conditions (`LP_DEV_SIGNING`, `LP_FAULT_INJECTION`) never reach packages. Nothing security-relevant depends on package `DEBUG` (§15.2).
- **`-xcconfig` reaches package targets (S14):** a setting passed with `xcodebuild -xcconfig` lands in every SPM package target (Swift and C), with `$(inherited)` keeping each target's own conditions. `Repro.xcconfig` therefore covers package code without `Package.swift` `unsafeFlags`, and must never set compilation conditions.

Frameworks and rpaths (NR §4 pitfall 3):
- OpenVPN3Shim and `libwg-go.a` are static and linked into the extension binary. There are no nested frameworks today.
- The Tunnel target sets `LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS = @executable_path/../Frameworks` **without** `$(inherited)`: Xcode's system-extension template inherits the app-extension rpath `@executable_path/../../../../Frameworks`, which does not exist after activation copies the extension to a protected location. CI asserts with `otool -l` that the extension's `LC_RPATH` entries are exactly `@executable_path/../Frameworks`, ± `/usr/lib/swift` (ref/toolchain T6). *Draft 8 (Conflicts bf, PF 19):* at the 26.0 target the Swift driver no longer adds `/usr/lib/swift` (the 15.1-target skeleton had it). Debug builds add `@loader_path` and `PackageFrameworks`, so `verify.sh static` checks Release only.
- No back-deployment dylib is needed. Drafts 4–7 expected `libswiftCompatibilitySpan.dylib` (Span back-deployment for macOS 15) as the likely first one. With the 26.0 target (draft 7.1), `Span` comes from the OS runtime, so it can't appear. The P1 skeleton (27.1 SDK, 15.1 target) already linked only `/System` and `/usr/lib/swift` libraries. The CI `otool -L` check stays and fails on any non-system dylib. If one ever appears, the extension embeds it in its own `Contents/Frameworks`, and S9 starts the extension on the 26 VM (§15.7).
- Tunnel target settings: `SKIP_INSTALL = YES` (otherwise a "Generic Xcode Archive"), `ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB = NO`, `ENABLE_POINTER_AUTHENTICATION = NO` and `ARCHS = arm64`, `ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX = YES`; the app embeds the extension with a Copy Files phase to Wrapper › `Contents/Library/SystemExtensions` (ref/toolchain T9).
- **ASan builds (draft 7.3, S7; test builds only, never archived for release):** built with `xcodebuild -xcconfig Config/ASan.xcconfig`, which reaches every package target (S14). `libwg-go.a` is Go and stays uninstrumented.
  1. **The ASan runtime goes into the extension's own `Contents/Frameworks`.** Xcode embeds `libclang_rt.asan_osx_dynamic.dylib` only in the app, and activation copies the extension out to `/Library/SystemExtensions/…`, so without its own copy the extension can't launch. The signing script copies and signs it whenever the extension links it. This is the only non-system dylib allowed, and only in ASan builds: `verify.sh static` exempts it there and fails on it anywhere else.
  2. **`__asan_default_options` is compiled in**, because a sysex has no environment. It is exported `__attribute__((used, visibility("default")))`, because dead stripping removes it otherwise. It returns `use_sigaltstack=0:handle_segv=0:handle_sigbus=0:allow_user_segv_handler=1:detect_leaks=0` (plus `abort_on_error=1` for test runs), because the Go runtime is in-process. **ASan/Go runtime clash:** Go installs its own `sigaltstack` on C threads that call into Go, and ASan then fails a CHECK while unmapping "its" alt stack at thread exit (`UnsetAlternateSignalStack`; 1 abort in ~280 sessions). This is not a memory error in our code, and `use_sigaltstack=0` avoids it.
  3. The hook that routes ASan reports to OSLog (a sysex has no usable stderr) is a `nonisolated` function, never a closure at the top level of `main.swift` (§0, draft 7.3).
  - Fixes 2 and 3 are in the spike source and **held in the v7 ASan re-run on 26** (draft 9, D9-16: ~453 sessions + 46 in-session restarts, no report, no `sigaltstack` CHECK, the report hook ran on a worker thread without trapping). ASan reports from the sysex need **offline symbolication** from the dSYM: `atos` can't run in the sandbox (§17.1).
  - **Pointer authentication (S14):** with `ARCHS = arm64`, `PAC = YES` is a no-op for the product; with `arm64e` the Go c-archive build fails and the arm64-only `libOpenSSL.a` is dropped by the linker. Enhanced Security (arm64e) on the extension is therefore impossible while it links wireguard-go and OpenSSL. If the app ever enables it, the app must not link either library (it doesn't, per the table above).

### 2.3 Bundle layout

```
LockPlus.app/Contents/
  Info.plist
  MacOS/LockPlus
  embedded.provisionprofile                                   ← LockPlus Developer ID (Release)
  Frameworks/Sparkle.framework/Versions/B/{Sparkle, Autoupdate, Updater.app}   ← XPCServices/ stripped
  Library/LaunchAgents/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.resume.plist             ← §10.4 (plist only)
  XPCServices/LockPlusValidator.xpc/Contents/{Info.plist, MacOS/LockPlusValidator}  ← 2.0.2, §2.2; no profile
  Library/SystemExtensions/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel.systemextension/Contents/
    Info.plist
    MacOS/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel
    embedded.provisionprofile                                 ← LockPlus Tunnel Developer ID (Release)
    Frameworks/   (only if something must ever be dynamic; nothing is today, §2.2)
```

- Sparkle's `XPCServices/` (Installer, Downloader) are for sandboxed apps; a non-sandboxed app must not enable them, and the 2.7.2/2.7.3 local exploits were in exactly these services. **Draft 8 (Conflicts ba):** `Tools/build/build-unsigned.sh` removes `Versions/B/XPCServices` from the archived app and fails if it is still there. Draft 4's Run Script phase (ref/sparkle C10) ran before SPM embedding and its output paths collided with the embed step ("Multiple commands produce Sparkle.framework"). The archive is unsigned at that point and `sign-inside-out.sh` signs the framework afterwards, so no re-sign is needed. The golden bundle layout check (§12.4) expects no `XPCServices` **inside Sparkle**. *2.0.2:* the app's own `Contents/XPCServices` holds exactly `LockPlusValidator.xpc`, copied by the LockPlus target's "Embed XPC Services" phase (`dstSubfolderSpec = 16`, `$(CONTENTS_FOLDER_PATH)/XPCServices`; the target depends on `LockPlusValidator`); `build-unsigned.sh` and `sign-inside-out.sh` fail on anything else there. macOS creates an empty container `~/Library/Containers/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.validator` on first use, which outlives an uninstall (§4.4).
- Only code lives in `Contents/MacOS`, `Contents/Frameworks`, `Contents/XPCServices` (2.0.2) and `Contents/Library/SystemExtensions`; scripts and data go in `Contents/Resources`.

### 2.4 Entitlements

Two sets of files (full XML in ref/toolchain §3.5):
- **Development sources** (`Config/Entitlements/*.entitlements`), used by Xcode's automatic signing with **Apple Development** for builds in the **Debug configuration** (and FaultInjection, which includes it), wherever they are built: the NE value **without** the suffix, `packet-tunnel-provider`.
- **Golden Release files** (`Config/Entitlements/Release/*.entitlements`), exactly what `sign-inside-out.sh` signs with (§12.4): the NE value **with** `-systemextension` on **both** targets, plus the profile-derived identity keys that an unsigned archive does not carry. *2.0.2:* a third pair for the validator service (below), identical in both sets.

App (Release golden):
```xml
<key>com.apple.application-identifier</key><string>M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac</string>
<key>com.apple.developer.team-identifier</key><string>M53GHX9FAY</string>
<key>com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension</key>
<array><string>packet-tunnel-provider-systemextension</string></array>
<key>com.apple.developer.system-extension.install</key><true/>
<key>com.apple.security.application-groups</key>
<array><string>M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac</string></array>
<key>keychain-access-groups</key>
<array><string>M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac</string></array>
<key>com.apple.security.personal-information.location</key><true/>
```

The app is hardened-runtime with no exceptions. It is not sandboxed, because it reads user-chosen files, the legacy Go data and the helper socket. `com.apple.security.personal-information.location` is the Hardened Runtime resource-access entitlement for Core Location ("Add current network" and the S1 fallback; ref/toolchain T5). Sparkle needs no entitlements in a non-sandboxed app (ref/sparkle C10).

Extension (Release golden):
```xml
<key>com.apple.application-identifier</key><string>M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel</string>
<key>com.apple.developer.team-identifier</key><string>M53GHX9FAY</string>
<key>com.apple.security.app-sandbox</key><true/>
<key>com.apple.security.network.client</key><true/>
<key>com.apple.security.network.server</key><true/>
<key>com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension</key>
<array><string>packet-tunnel-provider-systemextension</string></array>
<key>com.apple.security.application-groups</key>
<array><string>M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac</string></array>
```

Validator service (2.0.2; development source and Release golden are identical, `Config/Entitlements/{,Release/}LockPlusValidator.entitlements`):
```xml
<key>com.apple.security.app-sandbox</key><true/>
```
- Nothing else, by rule: **not** `network.client`/`network.server`, `files.*`, `application-groups`, `keychain-access-groups`, `com.apple.security.inherit` (that is for child processes, not XPC services), `get-task-allow`, `cs.*`. Xcode injects `get-task-allow` into Debug builds only; the Release golden is exactly `{app-sandbox}`, and `verify.sh pre` diffs the signed service against it and rejects any `com.apple.security.network.*`. No restricted entitlement, so no NE value, no suffix and no provisioning profile (§2.7). `sign-inside-out.sh` signs it after Sparkle and before the extension: `-o runtime --entitlements "$GOLD/LockPlusValidator.entitlements"`, no `--embed-profiles`. `check-entitlement-sources.sh` covers the pair.

- **Decision (O7, ref/toolchain T1, Conflicts b):** Debug-configuration builds are Apple Development-signed with the unsuffixed value; only `release.sh` signs with Developer ID and `-systemextension`. "Local" is not the criterion: a local **Release**-configuration build signed Apple Development carries the Developer ID-only requirement and fails its own peer check, so local Release builds are only useful unsigned (CI) or through `release.sh`/the P1 spike signing script (§18). A Developer ID system extension must be notarized before it activates, an Apple Development one need not be (forum 705582), and development signing uses unsuffixed values (forum 800887). L-EXT-6 is reworded accordingly in NR.
- Rules enforced by `verify.sh` (ref/toolchain §3.5): suffixed value only in Developer ID builds and on both targets; golden files are XML, LF, no BOM, `plutil -lint` clean; only `true` Booleans; no `com.apple.security.cs.*` and no `get-task-allow` on the extension (invariant 9); entitlements only on main executables.
- `keychain-access-groups`, the NE and the system-extension entitlements are **restricted**: each must be in the target's provisioning profile, otherwise the launch fails (AMFI). -34018 (`errSecMissingEntitlement`) is the separate, data-protection-keychain-only symptom of a keychain access group the signature isn't authorised for (ref/security §2, C7; Conflicts ad).
- The app group exists to satisfy the `NEMachServiceName` prefix rule. Quinn ties that rule to a sandboxed container app; ours isn't, but the prefix costs nothing and matches Xcode's template (ref/toolchain T23). The macOS-style `TEAMID.` form needs no portal registration and passes the group-container protection that macOS 15 introduced (still enforced on 26 and 27).
  - **No files are shared through it:** root's and the user's group containers are different directories. It is **not** a keychain access group (only registered groups are).

### 2.5 Info.plist keys

Extension:
```xml
<key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>$(PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER)</string>
<key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>$(PRODUCT_BUNDLE_PACKAGE_TYPE)</string>   <!-- SYSX -->
<key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>$(MARKETING_VERSION)</string>
<key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)</string>
<key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>$(EXECUTABLE_NAME)</string>
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>$(MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET)</string>
<key>NSSystemExtensionUsageDescription</key>
<string>LockPlus installs this network extension to run WireGuard and OpenVPN tunnels.</string>
<key>NetworkExtension</key><dict>
  <key>NEMachServiceName</key>
  <string>$(LP_APP_GROUP).tunnel.v$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)</string>
  <key>NEProviderClasses</key><dict>
    <key>com.apple.networkextension.packet-tunnel</key>
    <string>$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).PacketTunnelProvider</string>
  </dict>
</dict>
```

- `NSSystemExtensionUsageDescription` is **required**: "Failure to include this key results in an error at activation time." It is localized through the extension's `InfoPlist.xcstrings`, and `version-check.sh` asserts it (ref/networkextension C1, ref/toolchain T3).
- `$(LP_APP_GROUP)` (= `M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac`, defined in `Base.xcconfig`) replaces `$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)`, which comes from the signing setup and **does** expand to an empty string with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` (P1 skeleton: the unsigned build's Mach name lost its team prefix and stopped being a child of the app group; ref/toolchain T8 settled). The Mach name stays a dot-descendant of the group, which CI asserts (§2.6).

App:
- `SUFeedURL`: the **permanent** HTTPS appcast URL. GitHub does not redirect Pages URLs after a repo rename, so the host is a dedicated repo (ref/sparkle C8). **Final (owner, draft 9.1): `https://steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates/appcast.xml`**, served from the public repo `steiale/lockplus-updates` on GitHub Pages; update archives go to that repo's GitHub Releases. This document writes `<pages-host>` for `steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates`. The §10.4 probe and §22's `security.txt` share the host; gh-pages carries `.nojekyll`.
- `SUPublicEDKey`: a **new** key from `generate_keys --account lockplus-native`; the Go app's Ed25519 key is not reused. **Final (draft 9.1):** generated 2026-10-27; the private key is in the owner's login keychain plus an offline backup (agents never read or touch it).
- **Placeholder gate (draft 8, kept as a safeguard in draft 9.1):** the pre-decision builds carried `https://pages-host.invalid/appcast.xml` and a placeholder key (the literal survives only as an `UpdateTests` fixture). `UpdateController` never starts the updater while either is a placeholder (an `https` URL with a non-`.invalid` host, and a key that decodes to 32 bytes), so "Check for Updates…" stays disabled, and `verify.sh static` refuses to pass a build with them (`LP_ALLOW_SPARKLE_PLACEHOLDERS=1` was for pre-decision CI only; CI no longer sets it, draft 9.1). Both use one shared rule (Fable app review M3).
- `SUVerifyUpdateBeforeExtraction = YES`, `SURequireSignedFeed = YES`, and `SUSignedFeedFailureExpirationInterval = 1728000` (20 days) stated explicitly: it is the lost-key recovery path, and `0` would disable it (ref/sparkle C9).
- `SUEnableAutomaticChecks = YES`, `SUAutomaticallyUpdate = NO`, `SUEnableSystemProfiling = NO` (§22 privacy).
- `SUAllowsAutomaticUpdates = NO` (**decision**, owner may revisit): if allowed, install-on-quit happens silently, which is safe (the §4.2 preflight handles it) but hides the "Updating tunnel component" moment from the user.
- No `SUEnable*Service` keys and no `NSUpdateSecurityPolicy` (a custom policy breaks Sparkle's implicit same-team policy).
- `CFBundleVersion` is the integer `LP_BUILD_NUMBER` in Release; Sparkle compares it with `sparkle:version`.
- `LSApplicationCategoryType = public.app-category.utilities`
- `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, used only by the optional "Add current network" button and by the app-assisted fallback if S1 fails (§10.4)
- `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`: **not** present. The app never connects to LAN addresses itself (`measureLatency` runs in the extension, which as a root process is exempt from local network privacy, TN3179). If that ever changes, the key is added (ref/networkextension C24). **S6 confirmed the exemption on 27 (draft 7.3):** the root sysex got no prompt, and its sends to a LAN host on en0 succeeded. The extension's Info.plist doesn't carry the key either. LAN servers on a **non-primary** interface are a separate, routing limitation (§9.3).
- `LSMinimumSystemVersion = $(MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET)` (26.0)
- `LPTunnelBundleIdentifier = $(LP_EXT_ID)`
- *2.0.2 (D10.4-7, D-4):* `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, all role `Viewer`: "OpenVPN Profile" `net.openvpn.ovpn` rank **Default**; "WireGuard or OpenVPN Configuration" `com.wireguard.config.quick` rank **Alternate**; "Zip Archive" `public.zip-archive` rank **Alternate** (LockPlus never becomes the default app for nginx configs or zips; Default doesn't override a user's explicit choice). `UTImportedTypeDeclarations` for `net.openvpn.ovpn` (`.ovpn`, conforms to `public.text`, `public.data`) and `com.wireguard.config.quick` (`.conf`, `public.text`); no `UTExportedTypeDeclarations` (we own neither format). `.ovpn` has no system UTI (a dynamic type); Tunnelblick declares it by extension only, so there is no third-party identifier to add. LaunchServices registers the types on the first launch of an installed build. `InfoPlistTests` asserts the ranks.
- Validator service (2.0.2, `Config/Info/LockPlusValidator-Info.plist`): `CFBundlePackageType = XPC!`, `CFBundleVersion = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` (equal to the app's, `verify.sh`), `XPCService = { ServiceType = Application }`.
- No `LSUIElement`: the app starts `.accessory` from `applicationWillFinishLaunching` and switches policy at runtime (§11.1).

The app **reads `NEMachServiceName` from the embedded extension's Info.plist at runtime**. There is no duplicated constant.

### 2.6 Version: a single source (L-EXT-2, NR §2, NR §7)

`Config/Version.xcconfig`:
```
LP_MARKETING_VERSION = 2.0.0
LP_BUILD_NUMBER = 200000          // integer, strictly increasing per release
MARKETING_VERSION = $(LP_MARKETING_VERSION)
CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = $(LP_BUILD_NUMBER)
```
`Config/Debug.xcconfig` (project level, Debug only):
```
#include "Base.xcconfig"
LP_DEV_STAMP = 0
#include? "DevStamp.xcconfig"     // LP_DEV_STAMP = <unix minutes>
CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = $(LP_BUILD_NUMBER).$(LP_DEV_STAMP)
```

- Only `CFBundleVersion` carries the dev stamp (`200000.<stamp>`, which sorts above release 200000 and below 200001). `CFBundleShortVersionString` must be three integers, so `MARKETING_VERSION` is never stamped (ref/toolchain T7, Conflicts n). The replacement callback fires when **either** string differs (ref/networkextension §2.4), so the system still sees a new extension on every dev build.
- `DevStamp.xcconfig` is written by a **scheme Build pre-action** (or `LP_DEV_STAMP=…` on the `Tools/dev/build.sh` command line). A build-phase script would apply one build late and is blocked by `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING`. **Resolved in P2a (draft 8, PF 20):** the pre-action's file is read in the same build; the first Debug build carried that minute's stamp, and every later build a new one.
- Release never includes `DevStamp.xcconfig`.
- `Tools/release/version-check.sh` runs in CI on every build and before the appcast is generated. It fails if:
  - the app and extension `CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` disagree;
  - the `NEMachServiceName` suffix differs from `CFBundleVersion`, or the name is not a dot-descendant of `LP_APP_GROUP` (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C18);
  - the Sparkle appcast `sparkle:version`/`shortVersionString` or the git tag disagree;
  - a Release `CFBundleVersion` contains a period, or is not **strictly greater** than the previous release tag's (equal versions never reach the replacement callback, so users would silently keep the old extension; ref/networkextension C6);
  - the extension Info.plist lacks `NSSystemExtensionUsageDescription`;
  - `codesign --verify -R "=$APP_REQ"` on the app or `-R "=$EXT_REQ"` on the embedded extension fails (draft 10: two words; the `-R=` form is a syntax error, Conflicts bq) (signed builds only, so on the dev Mac: `release.sh` with the Release strings, `Tools/dev/build.sh` with the dev strings; CI's builds are unsigned and skip this check; ref/xpc-servicemanagement C18);
  - either binary's entitlements lack `packet-tunnel-provider-systemextension` (Release) or carry it (Debug) (ref/networkextension C27).
  - *2.0.2:* `SigningRequirements.minimumAppBuild` or `common.sh` `MIN_APP_BUILD` isn't decimal digits or differs from `LP_BUILD_NUMBER` (sources mode, on every run, not only for Release: the floor tracks `Version.xcconfig` at all times, §5.3). The version commit bumps `LP_MARKETING_VERSION`, `LP_BUILD_NUMBER`, both floor constants and the floor literals in `RequirementTests` and `LPWireTests` together.

### 2.7 Provisioning

**Four profiles (O7, ref/toolchain §4):**

| Profile | Type | Created by | Lives | Authorises |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| App, development | macOS App Development | Xcode automatic signing | Xcode-managed | NE (unsuffixed), system-extension install, `TEAMID.*` keychain groups |
| Tunnel, development | macOS App Development | Xcode automatic signing | Xcode-managed | NE (unsuffixed) |
| `LockPlus Developer ID` | Developer ID | Account Holder, portal | dev Mac only, `~/Library/Developer/LockPlus/profiles/` | NE (`-systemextension`), system-extension install, `TEAMID.*` keychain groups |
| `LockPlus Tunnel Developer ID` | Developer ID | Account Holder, portal | dev Mac only | NE (`-systemextension`) |

- **The validator service (2.0.2) needs no profile and no portal App ID**, in any configuration: its only entitlement, `app-sandbox`, isn't restricted. Debug and FaultInjection sign it with `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Manual`, Apple Development and an empty `PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER` (`Config/Validator.xcconfig`), so automatic signing never tries to register an App ID for it; the first signed Debug build on the dev Mac needed no owner step (WS-V). Release: Developer ID, hardened runtime, secure timestamp, inside the app, no `--embed-profiles`; notarized with the app (`syspolicy_check notary-submission` in `release.sh` covers it; untested on a Developer ID build until the 2.0.2 RC). Fallback only if Xcode ever asks for a profile: the **owner** opens the project in the Xcode GUI once and lets it fix signing for `LockPlusValidator`; agents never run `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.
- Development profiles list devices: dev builds run only on Alex's registered Macs. **Decision (draft 5): VMs never run Apple Development builds.** Every VM-based test, from P1 on (S2, S4, S5 on 26/27, S9, S10, §15.5, M2), uses **notarized Developer ID builds**. Reasons: registering a UTM VM's provisioning UDID is unverified (ref/toolchain §4.1 left it to P2a, with "test VMs use notarized builds only" as the fallback); S4(a) needs a Release-signed extension anyway (Release → Release replacement); a Developer ID system extension must be notarized to activate, which is exactly the shipping path; and a notarization round trip (about 5 min, 75 per day) is affordable for the few VM builds a spike needs. Fast iteration (S7, S8, S11, S13, S14) stays on the dev Mac with Apple Development builds.
- Developer ID profiles never reach CI (N1, §12.4). They list the certificates allowed to sign: **a new Developer ID certificate means regenerating both Developer ID profiles.** An expired Developer ID profile stops the app from launching; profiles made after 2017-02-22 last 18 years.
- **Developer ID certificate (F-5; corrected in draft 7, Conflicts al):** the team's **existing** Developer ID Application certificate ("Developer ID Application: Alexander Steiner (M53GHX9FAY)", expires **2031-05-04**) already chains to **"Developer ID Certification Authority, OU=G2"**, and that intermediate carries OID `1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6`, which `releaseSigner` pins (P1 skeleton, `codesign --verify -R` on a notarized dry-run bundle). There is no separate G2 certificate to request and no S9b; draft 5's "G1 CA expires 2027-02-01, G2 certificates last about a year" plan is void for this team. Keep the identity backed up as a `.p12` from Keychain Access (Xcode 16+ no longer exports identities). `release.sh` refuses to sign when the identity expires within 30 days, and every signature carries a secure timestamp (`--timestamp`), so releases stay valid after the certificate expires.
- `check-profile.sh` runs before signing: App ID, `ProvisionsAllDevices`, the `-systemextension` value, expiry > 1 year, and the certificate (ref/toolchain §4.3; **draft 10, E2E-1: by certificate SHA-1 hash, not by name**: two Developer ID certificates of the team share the subject, the first product profiles listed the other one, and a name check passed them; `syspolicy_check notary-submission` caught it as a Certificate Mismatch). It is a **required gate**, not a formality: notarization **accepts** a bundle whose restricted NE entitlements have no profile, `syspolicy_check distribution` passes it after stapling, and it then fails to launch (AMFI "No matching profile found", `RBSRequestErrorDomain 5`, POSIX 163). Only `check-profile.sh` and `syspolicy_check notary-submission` (before stapling) catch it (P1 skeleton §3).
- **Provisioning runs only from Terminal.app by the owner, never from an agent** (P1 skeleton §1): an agent-run `xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates` could not reach the account token and removed the Xcode account entry. `native/scripts/provision-product.sh` (draft 8; drafts 5–7 called it `provision.sh`) registers the App IDs and creates the Developer ID profiles; the manual portal steps are its fallback. ~~**Not run yet (draft 8):** the product App IDs and profiles don't exist, which blocks every signed run of the product (§18).~~ *Draft 10: done; E2E-1 ran notarized product builds, after the owner regenerated both Developer ID profiles against the keychain's certificate.*
- **Iteration without notarization (P1 skeleton §4):** once a notarized extension of a given version is activated, an app-only change with the **same** extension version can be installed un-notarized (local `ditto`, no quarantine): activation completes in ~10 ms with no prompt and no replacement. Useful on the VMs while notarization is unavailable; any extension change still needs a notarized build.

---

## 3. Domain model and storage

### 3.1 Profile

```swift
// LPModel
public enum VPNProtocolKind: String, Codable, Sendable { case wireGuard = "wg", openVPN = "ovpn" }

public struct Profile: Codable, Identifiable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public let id: UUID                    // stable forever; keys every store
    public var name: ProfileName           // display only
    public let kind: VPNProtocolKind
    public var policy: NetworkPolicy
    public var auth: AuthPolicy?           // OpenVPN only
    public var notes: String               // ≤ 4 KiB
    public var summary: ProfileSummary     // derived, non-secret, for list/detail
    public var payloadRevision: UInt64     // +1 on every payload change
    public var payloadDigest: String       // hex SHA-256 of canonical payload
    public var metaRevision: UInt64        // +1 on every metadata write; mirrored to providerConfiguration "metaRev" (§3.4, N6)
    public var ownerUID: uid_t
    public var createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date
    public var origin: ProfileOrigin       // .file(name), .zip, .qr, .editor, .migratedGo(oldName)
    public var importReport: ImportReport? // directives ignored/warned at import (§8.3)
}

public struct ProfileName: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
    // 1…64 grapheme clusters, no C0/C1 control chars, no leading/trailing whitespace,
    // NFC-normalized; uniqueness is case- and diacritic-insensitive within the owner's profiles.
    public init(validating: String) throws
}

public struct ProfileSummary: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var endpoints: [String]        // "host:port" as written (first is primary)
    public var transport: String          // "udp" | "tcp"
    public var addresses: [String]        // WG Address / OVPN unknown until connect
    public var isFullTunnel: Bool         // WG 0/0 or ::/0; OVPN redirect-gateway in profile
    public var dnsServers: [String]
    public var usesLegacyCrypto: Bool     // §8.6
    public var proxyEndpoint: String?     // draft 10 (PF 51): the accepted `http-proxy` "host:port" (set by OVPNNormalizer);
                                          // optional and additive: older metadata decodes as nil until re-import or edit
    public var resolvableEndpoints: [String] { endpoints + (proxyEndpoint.map { [$0] } ?? []) }  // what the app resolves (§9.3)
}

public struct NetworkPolicy: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var killSwitch: Bool            // full: includeAllNetworks; split: enforceRoutes
    public var allowLAN: Bool = false      // excludeLocalNetworks (effective with includeAllNetworks or enforceRoutes); default OFF (LocalNet)
    public var excludeAPNs: Bool = true
    public var excludeCellularServices: Bool = true
    public var excludeDeviceCommunication: Bool = true
    public var dnsMode: DNSMode            // .tunnelOnly | .split
    public var mtuOverride: Int?           // 576…9000
    public var stayConnected: Bool         // on-demand "always" rule (replaces Go AutoReconnect)
    public var blockIPv6WithoutKillSwitch: Bool = false // v4-only full tunnels: §10.5 blackhole even with killSwitch off
}

public enum DNSMode: String, Codable, Sendable { case tunnelOnly, split }

public struct AuthPolicy: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var needsUserPass: Bool         // bare auth-user-pass
    public var appendOTP: Bool             // UI collects base password + OTP, concatenated
    public var saveCredentials: Bool       // false when profile has auth-nocache
    public var staticChallenge: StaticChallenge? // text, echo, concat
    public var needsKeyPassphrase: Bool
}
```

- *Draft 8 (PF 25):* `VPNProtocolKind` raw values are `"wg"`/`"ovpn"` as above. `ImportReport`, `ProfileSummary`, `AuthPolicy`, `StaticChallenge` and `OVPNImportLimits` live in `LPModel`, so the app, the parsers and the extension share them. Display names keep Unicode (PF 15; §3.5, §13.1).

**Decision:** default policy for new imports (and the shipped `newProfileDefaults`, shown the same way in UI-CONCEPT §6.4, §6.8 and §6.13):
- `killSwitch = isFullTunnel`
- `allowLAN = false` for every profile (TunnelCrack LocalNet; F-1)
- the three exclude flags `true`
- `dnsMode = .tunnelOnly`
- `stayConnected = false`
- `blockIPv6WithoutKillSwitch = false` (the IPv6 blackhole follows the kill switch, §10.5)

Migrated profiles take the Go app's global settings instead (§13).

### 3.2 Settings and history

```swift
public struct AppSettings: Codable, Sendable {
    public var schema = 1
    public var language: AppLanguage = .system          // .system | .en | .de (draft 8; an older "ko"/"ja" decodes as .system)
    public var appearance: AppAppearance = .system      // .system | .light | .dark (owner request 2026-11-10; applied live through NSApp.appearance, UI-CONCEPT §6.14)
    public var menuBarRateLabel: RateLabelMode = .both   // .off | .download | .both  (UI-CONCEPT §6.1)
    public var menuBarIconStyle: MenuBarIconStyle = .monochrome   // .monochrome (template) | .color (tile, navy glyph)
    public var openWindowAtLogin = false
    public var notifications: NotificationMode = .problemsOnly    // .problemsOnly | .connectDisconnect | .off (§11.7)
    public var receiveReleaseCandidates = false         // Sparkle `rc` channel (§12.1)
    public var logLevel: LogLevel = .info               // the APP's log level (draft 8: setLogLevel is gone; the extension's level is a startup setting, §14.1)
    public var onboardingComplete = false
    public var supportNoteShown = false                 // the one-time Ko-fi note (UI-CONCEPT §10)
    public var menuOpenedLaunches: [Date] = []          // last N launches in which the menu was opened (§11.3 visibility policy)
    public var autoConnect: AutoConnectRules = .init()
    public var newProfileDefaults: NetworkPolicy        // killSwitch for full tunnels on, allowLAN off
    // draft 8, as built (App/Model/AppSettings.swift): lastQuitAt (§5.5), lastUsedProfileID, pausedState, pendingResume,
    // expectedUpdate (§4.2, §12.3), onDemandSuspended: [UUID] + onDemandSuspendedNetwork (§10.4 "until the next network
    // change"), pendingRemovals (§6.4), profileOrder, launches (§11.3 visibility policy)
}
public enum RateLabelMode: String, Codable, Sendable { case off, download, both }
public enum MenuBarIconStyle: String, Codable, Sendable { case monochrome, color }
public enum NotificationMode: String, Codable, Sendable { case problemsOnly, connectDisconnect, off }
public struct AutoConnectRules: Codable, Sendable {
    public var enabled = false
    public var profileID: UUID?                  // the one on-demand profile
    public var trustedSSIDs: [String] = []       // ≤ 64 entries, each ≤ 32 bytes UTF-8
    public var connectOnEthernet = false
    public var pausedUntil: Date?                // "Pause protection" (§10.4); nil = not paused
    // ssidProfileMap (SSID → specific profile) is cut from v2.0 (§21)
}
public struct HistoryEntry: Codable, Sendable, Identifiable {
    public let id: UUID                          // session ID minted by the extension
    public var profileID: UUID?, profileName: String
    public var start: Date, end: Date?
    public var rxBytes: UInt64, txBytes: UInt64
    public var endReason: SessionEndReason       // .user, .error(code), .sleep, .onDemand, .replaced
}
```

- Launch-at-login is **not** stored. It is read from `SMAppService.mainApp.status` every time Settings appears (§11.1 `LoginItemController`).
- The status item's visibility is **not** stored by us: `NSStatusItem.isVisible` persists itself under its `autosaveName` (§11.3).
- The Go settings `health_check` and `pin_interface` are dropped: the watchdog is always on and pf/-ifscope is gone. The Go `tray_icon_style` maps to `menuBarIconStyle` at migration (§13.1); the Go `theme` ("system" | "light" | "dark") carries over to the Appearance setting (§13.1), applied live.
- History is capped at 500 entries.

### 3.3 Where everything lives

| Data | Location | Format | Secret? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile metadata | `~/Library/Application Support/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac/profiles/<uuid>.json` (0600, dir 0700) | JSON `{"profile": Profile, "mac": hex HMAC-SHA256}` over the canonical (sorted-keys) encoding of `profile`; key = `macKey` (below); verified with `HMAC<SHA256>.isValidAuthenticationCode` (constant time) | no (integrity-protected) |
| Profile payload, app copy (canonical `.conf` / canonical `.ovpn` text) | `…/profiles/<uuid>.<revision>.sealed` (0600; draft 8: one file per revision, older revisions pruned only after the metadata commit, so a crash never leaves the committed metadata pointing at an overwritten file; a legacy `<uuid>.sealed` is still read) | `AES.GCM.SealedBox.combined` under `payloadKey`; AAD = `"lp.v1" ‖ kind(1 B: 0x01 payload) ‖ uuid(16 raw bytes) ‖ revision(UInt64 big-endian)` | **yes**, sealed |
| Master sealing key | data-protection keychain, service `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.payload-key`, account `v1`, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`; a generic-password item (draft 8: `kSecClassKey` declined: no gain without the Secure Enclave, and it would need a second keychain path and a migration). A missing key with profile files present is the §6.8 locked state; a wrong-size key is an error and is never replaced | 32 random bytes. Never used directly: `payloadKey = HKDF<SHA256>(master, info "lockplus.payload-seal.v1")`, `macKey = HKDF<SHA256>(master, info "lockplus.metadata-mac.v1")`, 32 bytes each (key separation, ref/security C15) | yes |
| OVPN credentials, app copy | DP keychain, service `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.credentials`, account `<uuid>`, `…AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` | `CredentialRecord` binary plist | yes |
| Settings, auto-connect, history, migration marker | `…/settings.json`, `history.json`, `migration.json` (0600) | JSON | no |
| Credential facts (draft 8, Fable app review L3) | `…/credential-facts.json` (0600) | JSON: per profile, the username (not secret) and whether a password and a key passphrase are saved, never a secret. The UI reads this; secrets are read only for show, change and provision | no |
| GUI instance lock | `…/instance.lock` (0600), `flock`ed by every GUI instance for its lifetime (§10.4) | empty | no |
| NE configuration | NE preferences, one `NETunnelProviderManager` per profile | see below | **no** |
| Payload and credentials, extension copy (**primary, S4**) | System keychain (root's default and only keychain in the system context), generic-password items created by the extension: service `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel.payload` / `….cred` (Debug: `….tunnel.dev.…`); **draft 8:** account = hex HMAC-SHA256(account key, `"lp.acct.v1" ‖ kind ‖ ownerUID (BE) ‖ uuid`); `kSecAttrLabel` = "LockPlus tunnel secret" and no other attribute | item data = `"LPK1" ‖ UInt32 BE metaLength ‖ SecretMeta plist {id, kind, ownerUID, revision, digest} ‖ secret` (the provision index lives inside the root-only value, never in readable attributes; §6.3) | yes (root; item ACL = the extension's designated requirement) |
| Extension account key (draft 8) | System keychain item service `<prefix>key`, account `account-hmac`, 32 random bytes, created on first `put` | binary | yes (root) |
| Payload and credentials, extension copy (**fallback, S4**) | extension sandbox container `Data/Library/Application Support/secrets/<ownerUID>.<uuid>.payload` / `….cred` (draft 8; root, 0600, dir 0700) | `"LPS2" ‖ UInt32 BE metaLength ‖ SecretMeta plist ‖ AES.GCM.SealedBox.combined` under the extension file key; AAD = `"lp.v2" ‖ kind(1 B: 0x01 payload, 0x02 cred) ‖ ownerUID (UInt32 BE) ‖ uuid(16) ‖ revision(UInt64 BE)`, so a file swapped between uids, profiles, kinds or revisions fails authentication | yes, sealed |
| Extension file key (fallback only) | `secrets/filekey.wrapped` = `0x01 ‖ HPKE.Sender.encapsulatedKey (65 B) ‖ seal(fileKey) (48 B)`, ciphersuite `.P256_SHA256_AES_GCM_256`, `info = "lockplus.filekey.v1"`, sealed to a CryptoKit Secure Enclave P-256 key whose `dataRepresentation` is `secrets/se.key`. When `SecureEnclave.isAvailable` is false (VMs) or the SE path fails: `secrets/filekey.raw` (32 bytes) | binary | yes (root 0600) |
| Extension runtime state (session ring, auth backoff and the 60 s AUTH_FAILED guard, start latches, last errors, last good resolved endpoint IPs) | extension sandbox container `Data/Library/Application Support/state.plist` (root, 0600) | plist, with a `schema` field; **schema 2 (draft 8)** keys every entry by `ProfileKey(ownerUID, profileID)`; a newer schema than the running build understands, or an older one, is discarded and rebuilt by reconcile (needed for §4.6 rollbacks). The provision index is no longer here: it is the store's own metadata (§6.3) | no |

The container is `/private/var/root/Library/Containers/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel/`. It is created by the sandbox for the root extension, so no other path or entitlement is involved.

**Device-bound data (Time Machine / Migration Assistant).** The master key is `…ThisDeviceOnly`, so it is not restored to a new Mac. The extension's copy does not rescue anything: it is a cache that reconcile rebuilds from the app's copy (§6.4), and the fallback's file key has a device-bound SE wrap. Whether System keychain items travel with a migration is therefore irrelevant and not claimed (the macOS 26.4+ `/var/db/SystemKeys` entropy file concerns hand-copied file keychains and is "irrelevant to our stores", ref/security fact 11; Conflicts ac). After a restore to a new Mac the profiles are **unrecoverable from the sealed files**. This is deliberate (a backup must not carry usable VPN keys) and handled in §6.8.

- The app data directory is named after the **bundle ID**, never `lockplus`.
  - So no Go-app cask `zap` stanza can ever match it (L-DIST-1, the bb50f10 incident).
- `providerConfiguration` (≤ 2 KiB, enforced):
  ```swift
  ["v": 1, "profileID": "<uuid>", "kind": "wg"|"ovpn", "revision": 7, "metaRev": 12, "ownerUID": 501,
   "dnsMode": "tunnelOnly", "mtu": 1420?, "blockIPv6": false, "onDemand": true,
   "auth": ["interactive": true, "kind": "userPass"|"staticChallenge"|"keyPassphrase"]?]
  ```
  - `metaRev` is `Profile.metaRevision` at the last manager save; it is the replay reference for §3.4 (N6).
  - **`onDemand` and `auth.kind` (draft 8, PF 1):** the provider can't read the manager's on-demand rules, and the §7.2 C16 rows need to know whether the system could restart the session; `auth.kind` tells the controller which known-interactive prompt a start expects.
  - **`ownerUID` is app-asserted** (§1.3 A2, draft 8): the extension uses it to pick the uid namespace, and nothing in NE binds it to the saving user.
- Other `NETunnelProviderProtocol` fields:
  - `providerBundleIdentifier` is the extension ID;
  - `serverAddress` is the primary endpoint, for System Settings display;
  - `passwordReference` and `username` stay `nil`, because the extension cannot read `passwordReference` (L-CRED-1).
- `includeAllNetworks`, `enforceRoutes`, `excludeLocalNetworks` and the other exclude flags are set from `NetworkPolicy` (§10), explicitly, every time (macOS defaults differ from iOS: `excludeLocalNetworks` defaults to false on macOS).
- `disconnectOnSleep = false`.
- `localizedDescription` is `profile.name`.

### 3.4 ProfileStore (app)

```swift
public protocol ProfileStore: Sendable {
    func list() async throws(LPError) -> [Profile]                       // owner's profiles only
    func payload(for id: UUID, gate: RevealToken) async throws(LPError) -> SecretBytes  // unseals; only via RevealGate (§1.3 A6)
    func create(_ draft: ProfileDraft) async throws(LPError) -> Profile  // validates, seals, saves NE manager, provisions ext
    func updatePayload(_ id: UUID, _ text: SecretBytes) async throws(LPError) -> Profile
    func updatePolicy(_ id: UUID, _ policy: NetworkPolicy) async throws(LPError) // throws .mustBeDisconnected (L-KS-2)
    func rename(_ id: UUID, to: ProfileName) async throws(LPError)       // metadata + localizedDescription only
    func delete(_ id: UUID) async throws(LPError)
    func reconcile() async                                               // see 6.4
}

/// The only owner of NETunnelProviderManager objects (non-Sendable; their completions run on main).
@MainActor final class ManagerStore {
    private var managers: [UUID: NETunnelProviderManager] = [:]   // loaded once at launch, reloaded on NEVPNConfigurationChange
    func loadAll() async throws(LPError)                          // must run before the first saveToPreferences after launch
    func save(_ id: UUID, protocolFlags: ProtocolFlags, providerConfiguration: ProviderConfiguration,
              name: String, onDemand: OnDemandPlan?) async throws(LPError)   // Sendable inputs only
    func status(_ id: UUID) -> NEVPNStatus
    func start(_ id: UUID) throws(LPError)                        // startVPNTunnel(options:) (§9.3 resolved-endpoint options)
    func stop(_ id: UUID)
}
```

- `FileProfileStore` is an `actor` for files, crypto and the DP keychain. All I/O is off the main actor (L-CRED-1). It talks to `ManagerStore` only with `Sendable` values (`NetworkPolicy`, revisions, a `ProviderConfiguration` struct encoded to `[String: Any]` on the main actor) (ref/networkextension C4, SC11).
- `loadAllFromPreferences` must run once before the first `saveToPreferences` after launch, or the save fails with `NEVPNError.configurationStale (4)`; with no configurations it may return `nil` or `[]` with no error, and both mean "none".
- Writes are atomic: temp file in the same dir, `F_FULLFSYNC`, `rename`.
- Corrupt JSON is moved to `*.corrupt.<UTC>` and logged, never fatal. This is ported from Go `SettingsStore.Load`.
- **Metadata integrity (A1):** every metadata write recomputes the HMAC (§3.3); every load verifies it with `HMAC<SHA256>.isValidAuthenticationCode` (constant time; no hex compare). On mismatch, the file is moved to `*.tampered.<UTC>`. The profile is shown as "Settings were changed outside LockPlus", and its NE manager is **not** re-saved and reconcile skips it. The user can restore the policy from the NE manager (the system's copy), re-import, or delete. The HMAC covers `policy`, `auth`, `ownerUID`, `payloadRevision`, `payloadDigest` and `metaRevision`, i.e. the whole `Profile`.
- **Replay (N6):** an HMAC alone does not stop same-user code from restoring an **older, validly MAC'd** metadata file (and its matching `.sealed` file), e.g. one from before the user turned the kill switch on. The reference copy is the NE manager, which same-user code cannot write: every manager save writes `providerConfiguration.metaRev = metaRevision` and `revision = payloadRevision`. Before reconcile or any save writes NE preferences or provisions the extension from metadata:
  - metadata `metaRevision` **lower** than the manager's `metaRev`, or `payloadRevision` lower than the manager's `revision` → replay: handled exactly like an HMAC mismatch (`*.tampered.<UTC>`, NE manager untouched, nothing provisioned);
  - ~~equal `metaRevision` but a policy that differs from the manager's protocol flags → also treated as tampering~~ **Draft 10 (E2E-1, PF 55; Conflicts bn): equal `metaRevision` and `payloadRevision` with different flags is drift, not replay.** HMAC-valid metadata at the manager's own revision is the copy we wrote; only the NE side can have moved. `ProfilesStore.load` logs the drift at `.fault` and re-saves the manager from the metadata, **once per profile revision per run**; a repeat is a user-visible problem ("The system changed the protection settings of <name> and they couldn't be restored. Turn the kill switch off and on again."), never a loop;
  - higher → a legitimate write whose manager save didn't complete; reconcile saves it.
  - No manager exists (e.g. the user removed the VPN in System Settings) → no reference, so the profile is shown as "Not installed" and re-created only by an explicit user action that shows the policy being saved.
  - The extension also refuses a `provisionProfile` with a revision lower than the one it holds for that uid (`.profileRevisionStale`; draft 8: from the store's per-uid metadata, §6.3), except after `wipeAllSecrets` or a §4.6 reinstall.
- `ManagerStore` keeps the **single cached `[UUID: NETunnelProviderManager]`**. `loadAllFromPreferences` is called once at launch and again after a `NEVPNConfigurationChange` notification; managers are never reloaded per call (NR §4 practices).
- **As built (draft 8, app-root review H3, M1, M3; APP-ROOT.md).** `ManagerStore` is the `VPNManaging` seam; `NEManagerStore` is the only owner of NE objects, and **every store talks to it through `SerializedVPNManager`**:
  - one FIFO async lock on the main actor for `loadAll`, `save`, `remove` and on-demand changes, so a reload can't clobber an edit in flight and two saves never race into `configurationStale`;
  - one retry, after a reload, when a save or on-demand change fails with `configurationStale`;
  - statuses are replayed after every reload (a reload mints new connection objects, and a transition in between would otherwise be lost, §11.2);
  - no save before a first successful `loadAll` (a save after a failed first load can duplicate a configuration);
  - an observable manager snapshot for the UI.
  - `loadAll` removes this user's duplicate and unaddressable configurations (duplicate `profileID`s, no `profileID`); `ProfilesStore.load` sweeps managers whose profile is gone. `create()` leaves no orphan or duplicate when the NE save fails (Import, migration). `delete()` turns on-demand off first and reports a failed remove.
- **Kill-switch consistency (draft 8, app-root review H1).** A policy change saves the **manager first** and the metadata second, and rolls the manager back if the metadata write fails, so NE (the authority, L-LC-4) and the HMAC'd metadata can't diverge on the kill switch. `syncManager` re-saves a manager that lags its profile at load and before every start. `rename`/`setNotes` don't re-save the manager of a live tunnel.
- **macOS rewrites a just-saved configuration (draft 10, E2E-1 bug 1).** On 26 and 27, about 50 ms after our first `saveToPreferences`, nehelper logs "SCPreferences signature (…) does not match saved signature ((null)), checking updated configurations", then "Updating configuration "<name>" from the corresponding SCNetworkService", and posts a new generation **without** `includeAllNetworks` (`/Library/Preferences/com.apple.networkextension.plist` then holds `IncludeAllNetworks = false`). The drift rule above heals it; the next three rules make sure nothing connects or claims protection meanwhile.
  - **Every save is read back** (`NEManagerStore.save`: `loadFromPreferences` after the save, flags compared); a discrepancy is logged at `.fault` ("saved protocol flags not kept"). A drift seen by `load` is logged at `.fault` too.
  - **Kill-switch starts fail closed (`prepareForStart`, before every start).** It saves the manager if it is behind; for a kill-switch profile it then **settles** (0.5 s after a save), **re-reads** the configurations and verifies the flags, makes **one repair** (save, settle, re-read), and otherwise refuses the start with **`.killSwitchNotApplied`** (104; app-side only, never on the wire, §5.5): "Couldn't apply the kill switch. LockPlus won't connect unprotected."
  - **The UI is honest while drifted (§11.2).** While the manager's flags differ from the metadata (`ProfilesStore.protectionMismatch`), the derived state gets `killSwitch = false` and the profile shows the strip "Restoring this profile's protection settings in macOS. The kill switch isn't active until they're verified, and LockPlus won't connect before that." (UI-CONCEPT §6.4).
- **Crash-safe payload revisions (draft 8, app-root review M4).** `replacePayload` writes `<uuid>.<revision+1>.sealed`, commits the metadata, then prunes older revisions (§3.3).
- **A failed `load()` never makes reconcile remove the extension's copies** (app-root review M2): reconcile runs only on a successful list.

### 3.5 Import caps (ported, NR §3 "Security posture")

| Input | Cap |
|---|---|
| single profile file | 1 MiB raw `.ovpn` (matches `maxOVPNSize`; comments and ignored directives are dropped before the canonical cap, which uses openvpn3's own accounting against `MAX_PROFILE_SIZE` = 262144: raw bytes + 64 per directive + 16 per argument, §8.1), 64 KiB (`.conf`) |
| zip | 500 profile entries, 10 MiB decompressed per entry (`LimitReader` semantics), 100 MiB total; read in memory only. *Draft 9.1 (as built, D91-2):* the file itself ≤ 100 MiB; ≤ 1000 central records of any kind; ratio ≤ 100:1 for entries over 64 KiB; no ZIP64, encryption, multi-disk or methods other than stored/deflate; regular files named `.ovpn`/`.conf` only (directories, `__MACOSX/` and `._*` ignored; symlinks, special files and unsafe paths get an error row); duplicate names refuse the archive. An archive-level violation refuses the whole zip with a message; an entry-level one is an error row in the batch sheet, never a silent drop. **2.0.2 (D10.4-3):** read in the validator service, not the app; an entry over **1 MiB** is an error row without bytes ("larger than 1 MB and was skipped"), the entries total ≤ **64 MiB** ("unpacks to more than 64 MB"); the file itself stays ≤ 100 MiB (checked by size before it is read, then `ReadArchiveRequest.maxArchiveBytes` = 100 MiB + 1). A service that is unavailable or died on the archive refuses it (`checkUnavailable`). |
| QR image | ~~20 MiB, 8000×8000 px~~ *2.0.2 (D-3):* not imported; image files are refused by name (§1.3 A3, §21) |
| drag-drop | the same as a file; directories are rejected |

Entry names go through `sanitizeProfileName` (a port of `sanitizeTunnelName`) and are used **only** as display names. *Draft 8 (PF 15):* the port keeps Unicode (§3.1 `ProfileName` rules); it does not narrow names to ASCII as a literal port would, because §13.1 promises that old names stay valid display names.

## 4. System extension lifecycle

### 4.1 SystemExtensionManager

```swift
@MainActor @Observable
final class SystemExtensionManager: NSObject, OSSystemExtensionRequestDelegate, OSSystemExtensionsWorkspaceObserver {
    enum State: Equatable, Sendable {
        case unknown, activating, needsUserApproval, needsReboot, ready(version: String)
        case disabledByUser                     // user switched it off in System Settings (workspace observer)
        case removedDuringUpdate                // §4.2: no enabled entry, owned managers with on-demand (Finder replace)
        case failed(ExtensionFailure)           // terminal until user acts
        case deactivating, uninstalled
    }
    private(set) var state: State = .unknown
    @ObservationIgnored private var pending: OSSystemExtensionRequest?   // retained: request.delegate is weak
    func activate() async                       // idempotent; called on every launch (L-EXT-2); quiesces first (§4.2)
    func deactivate() async throws(LPError)     // in-app uninstall path (L-EXT-4); GUI context only
    func reinstall() async throws(LPError)      // user-initiated rollback path (§4.6)
    var machServiceName: String { get }         // read from embedded ext Info.plist

    // Delegate witnesses are nonisolated. Every request (properties, activation, deactivation) is
    // submitted with queue: .main, so the witnesses hop with MainActor.assumeIsolated.
    // SAFETY: queue .main [SystemExtensions.h:95,126,142].
    nonisolated func request(_ r: OSSystemExtensionRequest,
                             actionForReplacingExtension existing: OSSystemExtensionProperties,
                             withExtension ext: OSSystemExtensionProperties) -> OSSystemExtensionRequest.ReplacementAction {
        ReplacementPolicy.decide(existing: .init(existing), embedded: .init(ext))   // pure function on Sendable copies
    }
    nonisolated func request(_ r: OSSystemExtensionRequest,
                             didFinishWithResult result: OSSystemExtensionRequest.Result) {
        MainActor.assumeIsolated { self.handleFinish(result) }
    }
    // … requestNeedsUserApproval, didFailWithError, foundProperties: same shape
    nonisolated func systemExtensionWillBecomeDisabled(_ info: OSSystemExtensionInfo) {   // OSSystemExtensionInfo is Sendable
        Task { @MainActor in self.state = .disabledByUser }
    }
}
```

- Swift 6: a `@MainActor` class conforming to `OSSystemExtensionRequestDelegate` without `nonisolated` witnesses is a compile error; the nonisolated + `assumeIsolated` shape compiles (ref/swift-concurrency SC10, ref/networkextension C12). The 5 s `propertiesRequest` timeout (§4.2 step 2) uses the one-shot gate (§5.4).
- The workspace observer is added at launch with `OSSystemExtensionsWorkspace.shared.addObserver` (15.1, below the floor; ref/networkextension C11). `systemExtensionWillBecomeDisabled` → `.disabledByUser` with a banner "LockPlus's network extension is turned off in System Settings" and the textual path; `…WillBecomeEnabled` → re-run `activate()`.
- The framework is meant for a GUI app responding to user actions; it is never called from the headless `--uninstall-system-components` or `--resume-protection` paths (ref/networkextension §2.3).

### 4.2 Activation on every launch (L-EXT-1, L-EXT-2)

`OSSystemExtensionRequestDelegate.request(_:actionForReplacingExtension:withExtension:)` is **synchronous**: it must return a `ReplacementAction` immediately and cannot await a tunnel stop. All quiescing therefore happens **before** any activation request is submitted.

1. At `applicationDidFinishLaunching`, run `activate()` once.
2. **Preflight:** submit `OSSystemExtensionRequest.propertiesRequest(forExtensionWithIdentifier:queue: .main)` and wait for `request(_:foundProperties:)` (5 s timeout through the one-shot gate; on timeout, treat it as "unknown" and go to step 4 without quiescing, logged).
   - `isAwaitingUserApproval` on any entry → show the approval **banner** rather than a new modal.
   - Find the **enabled** entry (`isEnabled && !isUninstalling`) and compare its `(bundleShortVersion, bundleVersion)` numerically with the embedded extension's Info.plist.
     - No enabled entry **and** owned managers with on-demand enabled or a `pendingResume`/`expectedUpdate` marker → the extension was removed before this launch, typically by a **Finder drag-replace**: the Finder asks the user to remove the system extension before it allows the move (forum 737969; ref/networkextension C10). No quiesce was possible and the kill switch was gone in between. `state = .removedDuringUpdate`; the UI says "The tunnel component was removed during the update. Approve it again to reconnect." Then step 4 (a fresh activation, which may need approval again). S10 records what each OS shows.
     - No enabled entry otherwise, or equal versions → step 4.
     - Enabled version **lower** than embedded (an update is pending) → step 3.
     - Enabled version **higher** than embedded (the user installed an older app) → do **not** submit. `state = .failed(.olderAppThanExtension)`. The UI offers "Reinstall tunnel component" (§4.6). The higher extension keeps running and keeps working with its own per-version Mach name, but this app can't talk to it, so the UI is read-only (status via `NEVPNStatus` only).
3. **Quiesce (only when a replacement is pending):** for every owned manager whose status is not `.disconnected`/`.invalid`, or that has `isOnDemandEnabled`:
   1. write `pendingResume = {profileID, onDemandEnabledIDs: [UUID], reason: .extensionUpdate}` to `settings.json` (unless §12.3 already wrote one). `onDemandEnabledIDs` lists **every** owned manager that had `isOnDemandEnabled` (the auto profile and `stayConnected` profiles; draft 9: the E1 keep-alive rule is dropped), not only the auto profile;
   2. set `isOnDemandEnabled = false` and save;
   3. `stopVPNTunnel()` and await `.disconnected` (15 s; on timeout continue, logged);
   4. show "Updating tunnel component…" in the menu bar and window.
   - This covers every way a new app can arrive with the old extension still running: Sparkle (variant B leaves the quiescing to this step, §12.3; install-on-quit never calls Sparkle's postpone hook, so this step is the only guaranteed path), `brew upgrade` while the app was closed and the tunnel was up (on-demand or connected), and a non-Finder copy (`ditto`, installers). In these cases the old extension has kept protecting the user until this launch, because swapping the app bundle does not touch the running extension (forum 732624). With a kill-switch profile, the Mac is unprotected from step 3.3 until the resume in step 6. That window is the price of L-KS-3 and is shown: "Updating — not protected for a moment".
4. Submit `OSSystemExtensionRequest.activationRequest(forExtensionWithIdentifier:queue: .main)` and retain the request until a terminal callback (the delegate is weak).
5. Handle the delegate callbacks (table below).
6. On `.completed` with a `pendingResume`, run `UpdateCoordinator.resumeAfterUpdate()` (§12.3 step 4).

| Callback / result | Action |
|---|---|
| `actionForReplacingExtension(existing, ext)` | **Pure compare, no side effects.** Compare `existing.bundleShortVersion/bundleVersion` with `ext.…` numerically (the parameters are `OSSystemExtensionProperties`, not bundles). The callback fires only when either string differs, or for equal versions in developer mode (`systemextensionsctl developer on`); equal versions otherwise complete with `.completed` and **the old binary keeps running** (ref/networkextension C6). Higher → `.replace`; equal (developer mode only) → `.replace`. **Lower** → `.cancel` (the request then fails with `.requestCanceled`) and `state = .failed(.downgradeRefused)`; this cannot normally happen because step 2 does not submit in that case. The only exception is `reinstall()` (§4.6), which deactivates first, so no replacement is involved. |
| `requestNeedsUserApproval` | `state = .needsUserApproval`. Show **one** sheet: an explanation, the textual path "System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Network Extensions", and "Open System Settings", which opens `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.LoginItems-Settings.extension` (undocumented URL: it opens the pane, not the item, forum 765970). **Draft 7 (P1 skeleton, 27):** the toggle reached from the "System Extension Blocked" alert did not stick on the first try; reopening the pane with the same URL and toggling again worked. While the state is `.needsUserApproval`, the banner and the onboarding step therefore keep a persistent **"Show the Switch Again"** action with that URL (UI-CONCEPT §6.14). Keep the request alive until the user acts or the app quits; never resubmit. |
| `didFinishWithResult(.completed)` | `state = .ready`, then the XPC `hello` (§5) and `ProfileStore.reconcile()`. Measured on 27 (P1 skeleton): `completed` arrives when the user approves (89 s in the run); every later launch with the same version completes in ~10 ms with no prompt; the first `hello` after approval takes ~370 ms (extension cold start), later ones 47–73 ms, well inside the 3 s `hello` timeout. |
| `didFinishWithResult(.willCompleteAfterReboot)` | `state = .needsReboot`. Show one dialog, "Restart to finish installing", with no retry. |
| `didFailWithError` `.unsupportedParentBundleLocation` | Dialog: "Move LockPlus to Applications", with a button that calls `NSWorkspace` to reveal it. |
| `.unknown (1)`, `.missingEntitlement (2)`, `.extensionMissingIdentifier (5)`, `.duplicateExtensionIdentifer (6, SDK spelling)`, `.unknownExtensionCategory (7)`, `.codeSignatureInvalid (8)`, `.validationFailed (9)` | `failed(.broken(code))`: "This copy of LockPlus is damaged. Reinstall." Include a diagnostics export button. |
| `.forbiddenBySystemPolicy (10)` | `failed(.managed)`: "Your organization blocks this extension." |
| `.requestCanceled (11)`, `.requestSuperseded (12)` | Ignore, with one refinement (draft 8, Fable verification): a request superseded by a newer request of ours leaves the state to that successor; an activation that ends canceled with **no** successor restores the state from before `activate()` (and sets `activationEndedWithoutResult`), so the UI shows its retry action again instead of a dead "Installing…". After our own `.cancel` (above) the state is `.failed(.downgradeRefused)`. |
| `.authorizationRequired (13)` | Only on deactivate: "Administrator approval required", user-initiated retry. Also what a headless (non-GUI) caller gets, which is why no headless path deactivates (§4.4). |
| `.extensionNotFound (4)` | On activation: bundle damaged (as above). On deactivation from an app whose embedded version differs from the installed one (forum 737969): the §4.6 guided manual removal. |

- **No automatic retries anywhere.** A "Try again" button exists only in the failure UI and is user-initiated.
- **As built (draft 8, Sonnet core review 3, 4, 8; Fable verification):**
  - `activate()` sets an in-flight flag before its first await, so a second caller can't submit a second request while the first is pending.
  - **Activation watchdog:** an activation request that gets no delegate callback within **120 s** ends in `.failed(.broken(code: 0))`; any callback (including `requestNeedsUserApproval`) disarms it, so a pending approval never times out.
  - **Deactivation** restores the prior state on every exit that didn't settle a new one (`.deactivating` is never a trap state), returns a distinct "cancelled" outcome for `.requestCanceled`, and runs one at a time. A `willBecomeDisabled` during our own deactivation is not `.disabledByUser`.
  - `retryAfterUserAction()` and `reinstall()` clear the XPC 4102 `.unauthorizedPeer` state (§5.4).
  - The three request dictionaries are one `[ObjectIdentifier: Pending]` map; the guided-removal poll is 2 s up to 5 min (§4.6).
- Settings › Advanced › "Reinstall tunnel component…" is in **release** builds (§4.6).
- Debug menu (DEBUG builds and `⌥`-click on About):
  - Activate;
  - Deactivate;
  - "Deactivate + Activate" (L-EXT-6; each activation of a rebuilt Apple Development extension needs approval in System Settings; deactivated-but-not-removed extensions clear at reboot);
  - "Show extension log".
- Debugging the extension: attach "by PID or Name" **as root**; the "first light" log line in `main.swift` comes before `startSystemExtensionMode()` (forum 725805).

### 4.3 Replacement policy

- The system replaces the extension when the app requests activation of a bundle whose versions differ. We answer `.replace` for higher versions (and for equal ones, which only reach us in developer mode). The tunnel has **already** been quiesced by the §4.2 preflight before the request was submitted (L-EXT-3, L-KS-3); the delegate itself does nothing but compare.
- Edge case: the system extension is enabled but `propertiesRequest` timed out, so step 3 was skipped. The replacement then happens with the tunnel possibly up. The FB17032197 XPC breakage is avoided by the per-version Mach name. The tunnel is torn down by the replacement, and on-demand restarts it on the new extension. S5 records what the user sees in this case.
- `NEMachServiceName` includes `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`, so the old extension's listener and the new app never talk across versions (FB17032197). The app connects to the name in **its own** embedded extension's plist. Before replacement completes, that lookup fails, and the app shows "Updating tunnel component…".
- **Assumption A-EXT-1:** a per-version Mach name has no side effects beyond a launchd registration per version. DTS now recommends exactly this workaround ("change the Mach service name during every update … I can't see any reason why it'd cause problems", Quinn, May 2026; FB17032197 still open; the repro needed replacement **while the VPN was running**, forum 779395). **S5 on 26 (draft 9, D9-17): no stale registration** after 6 → 7 → 9 (`launchctl print system` lists only the current job and name; replacements took 121–438 ms with no approval on 26 and 27; C20 closed). *Draft 10 (E2E-1): the product replacement 2.0.0 (200000) → (200001), triggered by the new app's launch, needed no approval on 26 or 27; `hello` 200001 ↔ 200001.* **Fallback:** a fixed name plus the mandatory stop-before-replace rule. It is weaker than the primary: it relies on the quiesce always happening, which the §4.3 timeout edge case does not guarantee (ref/networkextension C25).

### 4.4 Uninstall (L-EXT-4)

The Settings › Advanced › "Uninstall LockPlus…" sequence:
1. Authenticate with `LAContext`, then confirm.
2. For every manager: `isOnDemandEnabled = false`, save, `stopVPNTunnel()`, wait for `.disconnected` (10 s timeout).
3. XPC `wipeAllSecrets(ownerUID)`, which makes the extension delete this UID's secrets from its store (System keychain items, or the fallback's sealed files) and state entries. When the last UID is wiped, it also deletes the key material: the fallback's file key and Secure Enclave key blob, or (draft 8) the System keychain store's HMAC account key (§6.3). This step matters more with the System keychain primary: its items outlive the extension and its container, and deactivation does not reliably delete the container either (TBD-by-S5). Errors are recorded but not fatal.
   - **Residual if the wipe fails** (extension unreachable, XPC timeout, a keychain error): the extension's System keychain items (or fallback files) stay behind after the uninstall. They are root-only, so no other user can read them, but they outlive the app. The uninstall continues and its final sheet says so: "Some tunnel secrets could not be removed. Reinstall LockPlus and run Uninstall again, or remove the System keychain items labelled “LockPlus tunnel secret” in Keychain Access (administrator password required)." The failure and its code are in the diagnostics log. If deactivation later succeeds, the fallback's container files may still remain (TBD-by-S5); the same sheet covers them.
4. `removeFromPreferences()` for each owned manager (failures counted for the final sheet, never swallowed).
5. *(Draft 8: moved to step 7.)* Drafts 4–7.3 deleted the DP keychain items (master key, credentials) here, before the cancellable deactivation and regardless of step 7. That made kept profiles undecryptable and later flagged them as tampered (Fable app review H1, app-root review L3).
6. `deactivationRequest` (GUI context only). This may require admin approval or a reboot; both are shown. On `.extensionNotFound`, the §4.6 guided manual removal. **On 27 it asks for an administrator authorization** (S4/S5, draft 7.3): `sysextd` shows a `SecurityAgent` dialog, and the request stays pending until the user answers it. The confirmation in step 1 says so up front ("macOS will ask for an administrator password to remove the tunnel component"). A cancelled dialog leaves the extension active, and the final sheet says so. Unattended tests cannot deactivate. Whether the container and the System keychain items persist after deactivation is still unmeasured (TBD-by-S5).
   - **Draft 8 (app-root review H5): any deactivation failure stops the uninstall here.** Nothing local is deleted and the app is not trashed, so the user can try again; the UI shows "The tunnel component couldn't be removed… Your profiles and LockPlus itself were kept", plus the residual sheet if steps 3–4 left anything.
7. "Also delete your profiles and history" is chosen in the confirmation (default **No**). **Only with Yes**, and only now that deactivation succeeded: delete the DP keychain items (saved passwords, then the master key) **together with** the App Support data directory. With No, the master key and saved passwords stay with the profile files, so a reinstall finds the profiles intact (Fable app review H1). The Go app's data is never touched (§13.1).
8. Name every residual in the final sheet (extension secrets, VPN configurations, keychain items). `SMAppService.mainApp.unregister()` and `SMAppService.agent(plistName:).unregister(completionHandler:)` (the resume agent too, app-root review L3); `kSMErrorJobNotFound` counts as success. The Login Items row may remain until the system's overnight maintenance. **Never** run `sfltool resetbtm`: it resets every app's login items (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C16).
   - *2.0.2:* the validator service's empty sandbox container `~/Library/Containers/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.validator` stays behind: the service writes nothing, and the app can't delete another bundle's container without App Management rights. Harmless; the uninstall help names it, no code.
9. Move the app to the Trash with `NSWorkspace.recycle`, then quit. (Trashing the app in the Finder also removes the extension, WWDC19-702; `rm` does not, forum 677076.)
   - **Draft 10 (E2E-1 bug 3):** `finishUninstall` ends every attached sheet before `terminate`: AppKit refused to quit with the Settings uninstall sheet attached ("App termination blocked by modal sheet" → "Termination aborted"), and the uninstalled app kept running on both VMs.
   - **Residual: the app can't trash itself** (26: the bundle belonged to another administrator, so the move needed authentication). The uninstall is otherwise complete; the app says "The tunnel component was removed, but LockPlus couldn't move itself to the Trash. Drag LockPlus from Applications to the Trash to finish." (en, de), then quits. Neither change has run in a notarized build yet (§18).

**Homebrew (O5, Conflicts i).** The cask's `uninstall` stanza holds only `quit:`. Homebrew runs the **installed** cask's `uninstall script:` on every `brew upgrade` and `reinstall` (ref/sparkle §0 fact 9), so a destructive script there would wipe secrets on a routine upgrade, and a wrong first cask would keep doing so until users reinstall. The cleanup therefore lives under `zap script:`: `LockPlus --uninstall-system-components` runs steps 2–4 and the DP-keychain half of step 7 headless (no windows, 60 s timeout, `must_succeed: false`); zap trashes App Support too, so the master key still goes only together with the profiles. *Draft 8: the headless entry is not built yet (P5, with the cask).*
- It **never** calls `deactivationRequest`: the SystemExtensions framework is for a GUI app responding to user actions, and headless calls fail with `.authorizationRequired` (13) or give "weird results" (forums 665029, 809951; ref/networkextension C9).
- `brew uninstall` (without `--zap`) only quits the app and removes the bundle with `rm`, which leaves the extension installed and its secrets intact, so a reinstall works.
- **Zap after the bundle is gone.** The `zap script:` executable is the app itself. If the bundle no longer exists when zap runs (the user ran a plain `brew uninstall` earlier and zaps later, or Homebrew removed the app before the zap phase; the ordering is TBD-by-S5), the script fails silently (`must_succeed: false`) and only the `trash:` paths go. Left behind: the extension's **System keychain items** (or fallback files), the **NE configurations**, the app's data-protection keychain items, and the installed extension.
