The caveats and README give the cleanup: reinstall LockPlus (`brew install --cask lockplus`) and run Settings › Advanced › Uninstall LockPlus…; or by hand: remove the LockPlus configurations in System Settings › VPN, delete the "LockPlus tunnel secret" items from the System keychain in Keychain Access (administrator password), and turn the extension off in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions.
- The cask `caveats` and the README say this plainly: "To remove LockPlus completely, use LockPlus › Settings › Advanced › Uninstall LockPlus… before `brew uninstall`. `brew uninstall --zap` removes your profiles and secrets, but macOS keeps the network extension until you turn it off in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions."

### 4.5 Coexistence with the Go app

Detection (`LegacyAppDetector`, app side; the extension cannot see pf):
1. `/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper.plist` exists → helper installed.
2. Connect to `/var/run/lockplus/lockplus.sock` (0600, owned by this user, per `internal/ipc/transport_unix.go`) with a 2 s timeout and send the Go IPC status request. The probe uses an async `NWConnection` (or a dedicated queue), never a blocking `connect()` on a cooperative-pool thread.
   - The response tells us whether a tunnel is active or the kill switch is enabled. We send a read-only call only.
   - Note: the Go IPC authenticates the peer by **uid only** (`LOCAL_PEERCRED`, `internal/ipc/peercred_darwin.go`, `verifyPeerUID`), not by code signature. That is why the native app can call it at all, and it is also why §13.3's `Uninstall` RPC is callable by any same-user process.
3. `NSRunningApplication` with bundle ID `io.github.steiale.lockplus` → the Go GUI is running.
4. `/Library/Application Support/lockplus/dns-journal.json` or `pf-was-enabled` exists → state is left behind.
   - `pf-was-enabled` is written when the Go helper first loads its pf anchor and removed on every clean teardown (`internal/firewall/darwin.go`, `Apply`/`teardownLocked`). Its presence therefore means "the Go kill switch's pf rules were active and never torn down". Checking it needs no root: `stat` on a world-readable directory. It is the non-root signal for a **crashed helper with pf loaded**, since `pfctl` itself needs root.

Policy:

| Finding | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Helper reports an active tunnel or the kill switch on (pf anchor `com.apple/wireguide` loaded) | **Refuse to connect.** Dialog: "Disconnect in the old LockPlus and turn off its kill switch first", plus a button that opens the Go app. |
| Helper installed but idle | Allow connecting, with a persistent banner: "The old LockPlus helper is still installed. LockPlus can remove it; macOS asks for an administrator password." [Remove Old Helper…] (§13.3a; draft 10.2: there was no 1.x uninstaller to run). |
| Helper installed but **unreachable**, and `pf-was-enabled` exists | The helper probably crashed with its kill switch loaded, so pf may block our tunnel's traffic and the connect would fail without explanation. Allow connecting (pf may be gone), but show a warning before connecting: "The old LockPlus may have left its firewall on." The helper's LaunchDaemon has `KeepAlive=true`, and a restarted helper's `RecoverStaleState` flushes the anchors. An unreachable helper with the marker present therefore means it is crash-looping or was booted out. Offer to open the old app or to restart the Mac (a reboot clears pf rules), and link the §13.3 uninstaller. If the connect then fails with `.connectTimeout`/`.peerUnreachable`, the error banner repeats this hint. |
| Helper installed but unreachable, no `pf-was-enabled` | As "idle". |
| Leftover DNS journal or `pf-was-enabled`, no helper | Banner: "The old LockPlus left network settings behind. Restart your Mac to clear them." (a reboot clears pf rules; the DNS journal stays for the Go helper's own restore). Root state is only ever changed by the one user-approved removal of §13.3a. |

**As built (draft 8; APP-ROOT.md, `LegacyAppDetector`):**
- The probe is the Go IPC frame (4-byte big-endian length + JSON-RPC 2.0) with one read-only `Tunnel.Status` call, on its own serial queue with a 2 s deadline. It first `lstat`s the socket and talks to it only if it is a socket owned by this user (`st_uid == getuid()`; Fable app review nit).
- The finding is refreshed at launch, **before every connect while a helper is installed** (app-root review M9: the gate decided on stale data), and by Diagnostics "Run All". Every UI Connect goes through one gate (`UIEnvironment.gatedConnect`).
- Tested with fixtures only, by rule: the probe hasn't run against a live Go helper (§18). *E2E-5 ran it against live Go 1.0.68 and 1.1.0 helpers: detection and the refusal work.*

**As built (draft 10.2, E2E-5):**
- **Every Connect re-reads (F3).** `UIEnvironment.gatedConnect` clears an earlier refusal and calls `AppActions.connect`, which re-reads the helper whenever it may be installed (the cached fact or a fresh `lstat` of the plist) and then refuses, warns or starts; "Connect Anyway" re-checks too. The menu takes the same path. A refusal is never repeated from the cached notice.
- **Polling while refusing (F3).** While the finding refuses, `LegacyHelperStore` re-reads it every 5 s and stops as soon as it doesn't; a shown refusal clears when the old tunnel and its kill switch are down.
- **A strip, not a dialog (F8).** The refusal ("The old LockPlus is still protecting this Mac. …") and the crashed-helper warning are a strip above the detail with [Open the old LockPlus] [OK] or [Cancel] [Connect Anyway]. An alert sheet made AppKit refuse `terminate` (AppleScript `quit` → -128, the D10-3 pattern). "Open the old LockPlus" ends the refusal and is shown only while the old app is installed (`LegacyFacts.goAppInstalled`: a Launch Services URL for `io.github.steiale.lockplus` that exists, outside the Trash, not this app).
- **Removal (F1).** For an installed, idle helper the banner offers "Remove Old Helper…" (§13.3a).

### 4.6 Reinstall tunnel component (user-initiated rollback, M2)

Automatic replacement never downgrades (§4.3). A legitimate rollback (the user installs N-1 because N broke something) therefore needs an explicit path. It is offered in Settings › Advanced › "Reinstall tunnel component…" and in the `.failed(.olderAppThanExtension)` / `.failed(.downgradeRefused)` UI.

1. Confirmation sheet: "This removes the installed tunnel component (version X) and installs the one bundled with this app (version Y). VPN connections stop. macOS may ask for an administrator password." Buttons Cancel / Reinstall; **Cancel** is the default. LAContext is required, because a downgrade is security-relevant.
2. Quiesce as in §4.2 step 3, with `pendingResume.reason = .reinstall`.
3. `deactivationRequest`, then await the result. `.willCompleteAfterReboot` → "Restart to finish", and the app resumes at step 4 on the next launch (a marker in `settings.json`).
   - **`.extensionNotFound` (4):** deactivating from an app whose embedded extension version differs from the installed one has been observed to fail this way, and DTS won't support that state (forum 737969; ref/networkextension C8). Fallback: **guided manual removal.** The sheet opens Login Items & Extensions, shows the textual path, and asks the user to switch LockPlus's network extension off; the app observes `OSSystemExtensionsWorkspace.systemExtensionWillBecomeInactive` (or polls `propertiesRequest` every 2 s, up to 5 min), then continues at step 4.
4. `activationRequest` for the embedded extension. Since nothing is enabled, no replacement callback occurs. The normal approval rules (§4.2) apply.
5. On `.completed`: `hello`, then `reconcile()`, which re-provisions every profile; the extension's `state.plist` with a newer schema is discarded (§3.3). System keychain items written by the newer extension stay readable (same designated requirement) and are overwritten by the re-provision. Then resume.
- Never automatic, never offered by a background path, and logged at `.notice` with both versions.
- S5 records, on 26/27, whether deactivating N from app N-1 (the downgrade direction) works, which error code it returns, and whether a reboot is needed.

---

## 5. App ↔ extension IPC

### 5.1 Channel choice

- **XPC** over `NEMachServiceName` is used for everything: provisioning, auth, status detail, stats and latency. *Draft 8:* not logs (§5.2, §14.2).
  - **Assumption (confirmed by S5 on 27, and on 26 in draft 9):** it works while the tunnel is down, because launchd starts the extension when the first **message** is sent to its endpoint (a lookup alone does not launch it; the lookup fails with immediate invalidation if the extension is not activated and approved). Apple documents this for launchd services; DTS only says the sysex "operates much like a launchd daemon" (ref/networkextension C26, ref/xpc-servicemanagement C17). S5 on 27: `hello` while DOWN answers in 0–1 ms with the extension process alive and no provider instance; a not-yet-activated name gives `invalidationHandler` with **4099** at once; after a SIGKILL the next message relaunches the extension (new PID, 52–73 ms), subject to launchd's respawn throttle (§5.4); while UP the same process serves the provider and the listener.
  - The listener belongs to the **process**, not to a provider instance: `main.swift` runs `autoreleasepool { NEProvider.startSystemExtensionMode(); listener = TunnelServiceListener(peerRequirement: APP_REQ); listener.start() }` (a process-lifetime global in the extension target; the type lives in TunnelEngine and receives the requirement as a parameter, §2.2) and then `dispatchMain()`. The process can run with no provider instance, so tunnel state lives in a process-level controller. *Draft 10.3 (phase 0, 26.6.2 and 27.2):* it can also run **several**: macOS starts a second LockPlus configuration beside a running one (System Settings, `scutil --nc start`; an on-demand start of the other configuration is not measured but takes the same path), and NE creates its provider instance in this same process. The one controller still runs one session; the start guard (§7.2) refuses the second start instead of letting it displace the first.
  - Several app instances may be connected at once (one per GUI login session, or two copies of the app); the protocol is designed for that (§5.2 event filtering).
- **`sendProviderMessage`** is used for nothing in production. It needs a running provider instance and has no peer validation of its own beyond NE.
  - We keep one debug-only `ping` through it to triage "XPC unreachable but tunnel up" (§17, S5).
- **Start, stop and status** go through `NETunnelProviderSession.startVPNTunnel(options:)`, `stopVPNTunnel()`, `NEVPNStatusDidChange` and `fetchLastDisconnectError`. A slow connect is therefore never an XPC call that can time out (L-LC-3).

### 5.2 Protocol definition

Payloads are `Codable` structs encoded as binary property lists and carried as `Data`. `LPWire` owns the encode and decode, so size checks happen **before** decoding and versioning is field-additive.

```swift
// LPWire (LockPlusCore) — shared by app and extension
public let LPWireVersion: UInt16 = 1
public typealias LPReply1 = @Sendable (Data?) -> Void            // encoded LPError? (nil = success)
public typealias LPReply2 = @Sendable (Data?, Data?) -> Void     // (encoded result, encoded LPError?)

// Rules (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C8, ref/swift-concurrency SC2/SC3):
// - Data-only parameters: no collections, NSError or custom classes, so no setClasses calls exist.
// - Every reply closure is @escaping @Sendable. No `async` members (a failed connection would hang the call).
// - Exported objects on both sides are nonisolated NSObject subclasses, never @MainActor
//   (XPC delivers on a non-main queue; a main-actor @objc witness traps under SE-0423).
@objc public protocol LPTunnelServiceXPC: NSObjectProtocol {
    func hello(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)              // ClientHello → ServerHello; carries no secret
    func provisionProfile(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)   // ProvisionRequest; only after a validated hello
    func updateCredentials(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)  // only after a validated hello
    func removeProfile(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)
    func listProvisioned(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)
    func wipeAllSecrets(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)
    func validateProfile(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)    // 2.0.2: answers .extensionBusy WITHOUT decoding (kept for
                                                                    // wire stability; [7] moved to the validator service, §8.1)
    func tunnelSnapshot(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)     // TunnelSnapshot (below)
    func statistics(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)
    func pendingAuthPrompt(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)  // the awaitingAuth prompt (pending start or reasserting), or an
                                                                    // unanswered prepareStartAuth prompt (§7.2; draft 9: no stash)
    func prepareStartAuth(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)   // PrepareStartAuth → AuthPrompt(nextStart: true); no secret
    func answerAuth(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)         // only after a validated hello
    func cancelAuth(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply1)
    func sessionSummaries(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)
    func measureLatency(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)     // answers .extensionBusy (draft 9, S2 E5: a provider-originated
                                                                    // connection leaves en0 outside the tunnel; §10.1.1)
    func pushEndpoints(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)     // draft 10 (PF 50): PushEndpointsRequest → PushEndpointsReply;
                                                                    // fresh endpoint IPs into the caller's held start (§7.2, §9.3); no secret
    func armStart(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)          // 2.0.2: ArmStartRequest → ArmStartReply; the caller's next manual
                                                                    // start of its own profile carries this nonce (§7.2); no secret
    // draft 8 (Fable review M1, Conflicts ax): recentLogs and setLogLevel are REMOVED. Neither was uid-scoped: any
    // validly signed app instance of another user could read this user's engine lines or raise the log level.
}

@objc public protocol LPAppCallbackXPC: NSObjectProtocol {          // exported by the app on the same connection
    // One event in flight per connection: the extension sends the next only after `done`; newer events
    // coalesce into "snapshot dirty", so a hung app can't make the extension queue without bound.
    func tunnelEvent(_ event: Data, done: @escaping @Sendable () -> Void)
}

public struct ClientHello: Codable, Sendable { public var wire: UInt16; public var appVersion: String; public var appBuild: String }
public struct ServerHello: Codable, Sendable {
    public var wire: UInt16; public var extVersion: String; public var extBuild: String
    public var capabilities: Set<Capability>   // .openVPN, .wireGuard, .keyPassphrase, .startAuthorisation (2.0.2) (DoH/DoT: §21)
}
public enum Capability: String, Codable, Sendable { case openVPN, wireGuard, keyPassphrase, startAuthorisation }
public struct ProvisionRequest: Codable, Sendable {
    public var profileID: UUID; public var kind: VPNProtocolKind; public var revision: UInt64
    public var payload: Data                    // canonical text, ≤ 256 KiB by openvpn3 accounting (§8.1)
    public var credentials: CredentialRecord?   // ≤ 4 KiB encoded
}
public struct CredentialRecord: Codable, Sendable {
    public var v: UInt8 = 1; public var username: Data?; public var password: Data?; public var keyPassphrase: Data?
    public var proxyUsername: Data?; public var proxyPassword: Data?   // draft 8 (PF 21): inline <http-proxy-user-pass>, §8.2
}  // username ≤ 512 B, password ≤ 1024 B, passphrase ≤ 1024 B, proxy fields as username/password;
   // no CR/LF/NUL in usernames or passwords; checked by both ends (isWithinLimits)
public enum AuthKind: String, Codable, Sendable { case userPass, staticChallenge, dynamicChallenge, keyPassphrase, pendingApproval }
public enum AuthReason: String, Codable, Sendable { case initial, rejected, reconnect, sessionExpired }
public struct AuthPrompt: Codable, Sendable {
    public var promptID: UUID; public var profileID: UUID; public var kind: AuthKind
    public var challengeText: String?           // ≤ 1 KiB, server-controlled, rendered as plain text only
    public var echo: Bool; public var lockedUsername: String?; public var reason: AuthReason
    public var savedUsername: String?
    public var nextStart: Bool                  // draft 9: true only for a prepareStartAuth prompt (known-interactive, before any
                                                // start): after answerAuth the app starts the tunnel and that start takes the answer;
                                                // false = the answer goes into the pending start or the reasserting session (§8.4)
    public var expiresAt: Date                  // the prompt deadline: 10 min, CRV1 5 min (draft 7); AUTH_PENDING and after
                                                // Connected the 10 min auth deadline
}
public struct PrepareStartAuth: Codable, Sendable {  // known-interactive profiles may prompt BEFORE the start (draft 9: a UX choice)
    public var profileID: UUID; public var kind: AuthKind   // .userPass (unsaved), .staticChallenge, .keyPassphrase (unsaved)
}
public struct AuthAnswer: Codable, Sendable {
    public var promptID: UUID; public var username: Data?; public var password: Data?; public var response: Data?; public var save: Bool
}
/// Start options (`startVPNTunnel(options:)`, plist types only, nothing secret): `lp.manual` (always `1`; draft 6.1) and,
/// draft 9, `lp.endpoints` = `[hostname: [IP literal]]` the app resolved just before the start (≤ 8 hosts × 16 IPs; §9.3,
/// S2 E10). The app ALWAYS passes a non-nil options dictionary containing `lp.manual = 1`.
/// Draft 8 (PF 42, Fable nit, tunnel review T9): a start is manual ONLY when `options["lp.manual"] == 1`; nil options
/// (on-demand, `scutil --nc start`) and any other dictionary are on-demand starts (fail closed: start latch applies, no
/// prompt, no prepared answer is taken; §7.2, §15.3).
/// Draft 9 (S2 E1): NE REPLAYS the original options verbatim when it restarts a crashed provider by itself, so they
/// never carry an OTP, an answer, a promptID or any other one-shot value. `lp.promptID` is gone.
/// 2.0.2: `lp.startNonce` = the canonical `uuidString` (an NSString) of the nonce the app's `armStart` announced, fresh per
/// start. Read only from a manual start; a non-string or malformed value reads as no nonce. It is not one-shot by design:
/// NE's replay of the same options is how its own restart of an authorised session is recognised (§7.2).

/// What the extension knows that NEVPNStatus doesn't. Detail only: the UI's state still starts from
/// NEVPNStatus and is derived by one table (UI-CONCEPT §6.6, §11.2). F-4.
public struct TunnelSnapshot: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var profileID: UUID?
    public var phase: TunnelPhase               // idle, starting, connecting, awaitingAuth, establishing, connected,
                                                // reasserting, sleeping, held, stopping
    public var attempt: UInt32                  // reconnect attempt in the current reasserting episode; 0 otherwise
    public var nextRetryAt: Date?               // wall-clock estimate for the UI countdown; nil when not waiting
    public var holdReason: HoldReason?          // why the provider is holding a session without retries
    public var holdBeforeConnected: Bool        // draft 9 (S2 E14): the start completion is withheld; also while a held start retries
                                                // (NE status .connecting); false: held after Connected (NE status .reasserting) (§7.2)
    public var startLatch: StartLatch?          // expected path (draft 6): on-demand starts of this profile fail fast (§7.2)
    public var lastError: LPError?              // also the fallback for fetchLastDisconnectError (§5.5)
    public var lastErrorAt: Date?               // draft 7: when lastError was recorded; the launch-time source (§5.5, sticky)
    public var endpoint: String?, localAddresses: [String], cipher: String?
    public var epoch: UInt64                    // controller epoch; lets the app drop stale snapshots. Draft 8: 0 in a snapshot
                                                // of a profile that isn't the running session; the app compares epochs only
                                                // when both are nonzero and from the same session (app-root review H6)
}
public enum TunnelPhase: String, Codable, Sendable { case idle, starting, connecting, awaitingAuth, establishing, connected, reasserting, sleeping, held, stopping }
/// Draft 6 (Conflicts ag): a before-Connected failure fails the start and may arm this latch. `.hard` blocks every
/// on-demand start until a manual start, a higher-revision provision or updateCredentials; `.backoff` (pre-login
/// .secretStoreUnavailable, retryable kill-switch failures under on-demand) lets an on-demand start through only after
/// `notBefore` (5 s doubling to 5 min). removeProfile and wipeAllSecrets delete the latch (§7.2 Rules).
public struct StartLatch: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public enum Kind: String, Codable, Sendable { case hard, backoff }
    public var code: LPErrorCode; public var kind: Kind; public var notBefore: Date?; public var revision: UInt64
}
/// A hold after Connected has reasserting = true, status .reasserting. Draft 9 (S2 E14): with includeAllNetworks a hold also
/// happens BEFORE Connected (start completion withheld, status .connecting); `holdBeforeConnected` tells which.
public enum HoldReason: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    case blockedAfterFailure(LPErrorCode)       // §7.2 holdBlocked after a fatal engine error (kill switch on)
    case nonRetryable(LPErrorCode)              // §7.2 C16 rule: auth/profile errors under on-demand
}
```

**Event delivery (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C7).** The extension keeps a `ConnectionRegistry` actor keyed by connection, holding each peer's `{uid, pid, connectionID}` captured at accept time. Profile-scoped events (`authRequired`, `sessionEnded`, snapshot changes) go only to connections whose uid equals the profile's `ownerUID`; other connections receive `{kind: .anyTunnelStateChanged}` with no profile, endpoint or address. Auth prompts go to the owner's connections; the first `answerAuth` wins by `promptID` and the others get `promptResolved`. Draft 9: a prompt inside a pending start is pushed the same way (the start stays pending, §7.2), and `pendingAuthPrompt` returns it, or an unanswered `prepareStartAuth` prompt, until it is answered, cancelled or expires; `answerAuth`, `prepareStartAuth` and `cancelAuth` check `ownerUID` like every profile-scoped call. Entries are removed in the server-side `invalidationHandler`, the only event a listener-side connection gets when the app quits or crashes.
- **As built (draft 8; Conflicts bg; PF 22, 44; tunnel review T8):** `ConnectionRegistry` is a `Mutex`-guarded class, not an actor, because registration runs synchronously in `shouldAcceptNewConnection`, so an early invalidation can't overtake its add. Per connection, one event is in flight; **only the state-only kinds (`snapshotChanged`, `anyTunnelStateChanged`) coalesce** into one pending slot, while `authRequired`, `promptResolved` and `sessionEnded` queue in order (≤ 32 per connection; a hung app then loses the oldest, and re-pulls prompt and snapshot when it recovers). A shared slot had dropped `sessionEnded`/`authRequired`. `promptResolved` is emitted to the owner's other connections when a prompt is answered or cancelled. Event kinds: `anyTunnelStateChanged` (the only kind non-owners see), `snapshotChanged`, `authRequired`, `promptResolved`, `sessionEnded`.
- **Snapshots of other profiles (draft 8, Fable review M2; PF 38).** `tunnelSnapshot` for a profile that isn't the running session returns that profile's own latch and `lastError`, phase `.idle`, epoch 0, no endpoint or addresses; `statistics` for it are zero. A profile owner learns nothing about another profile's session.
- **Latches and wipes are per owner (draft 8, Fable review L1, L2).** Start latches, last errors, endpoint IPs and the session ring are keyed by `ProfileKey(uid, profile)`; `wipeAllSecrets` clears only the caller's. Credential records are re-written with the owner taken from the existing store entry, never from `providerConfiguration`.

Request and reply bodies (draft 8, PF 21; `LPWire/Messages.swift`, `RequestReplies.swift`): `EmptyRequest` (`listProvisioned`, `wipeAllSecrets`: the extension uses the peer's uid), `ProfileRequest` (snapshot, statistics, remove, pending prompt, summaries, latency), `UpdateCredentialsRequest`, `CancelAuthRequest`, `PendingAuthPromptReply`, `ListProvisionedReply` (≤ 500 `ProvisionedEntry {id, revision, digest}` of the caller's uid), `ValidateProfileRequest` (with `disableClientCert`, mirroring the shim rule), `ValidateProfileReply` (error, openvpn3's rejection category, and the [7a] `EvalConfig` fields `autologin`, `staticChallenge`, `staticChallengeEcho`, `privateKeyPasswordRequired`, ≤ 50 warnings), `TunnelStatistics`, `SessionSummariesRequest`/`Reply`, `MeasureLatencyReply`, `TunnelEvent`. `LPMethod` carries each method's request cap, reply cap, client timeout and `serverDeadline` (timeout − 1 s).

**`pushEndpoints` (draft 10, PF 50; fixes §20 risk 25).** Additive (a new method and new bodies), so `LPWireVersion` stays 1.
```swift
public struct PushEndpointsRequest: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var profileID: UUID
    public var endpoints: [String: [String]]     // [hostname: [IP literal]], v4 first as resolved; same shape and caps as lp.endpoints
    public static let recoverableCodes: Set<LPErrorCode> = [.dnsResolutionFailed, .connectTimeout, .peerUnreachable,
                                                            .endpointInterfaceUnusable]
    public static func appliesTo(_ snapshot: TunnelSnapshot, profileID: UUID) -> Bool   // the app side of the rule (below)
}
public struct PushEndpointsReply: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public enum Outcome: String, Codable, Sendable { case retrying, unchanged, notHeld }
    public var outcome: Outcome
}
public enum EndpointMapRules { … }   // maxHosts 8, maxIPsPerHost 16, maxHostnameBytes 253; isHostname, isIPLiteral, isValid
```
- **Wire check (`EndpointMapRules`, post-decode, `LPWireValidating`):** 1–8 hostnames of ≤ 253 bytes (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`; not an IP literal), each with 1–16 unique IP literals (`inet_pton`; no zone, port or brackets). One bad entry rejects the whole request with `.malformedRequest`; nothing is dropped silently.
- **When it applies (`appliesTo`, one list for both ends):** the snapshot is the profile's start, `holdBeforeConnected`, phase `held`, `starting` or `connecting` (a retry inside the hold), and `holdReason == .blockedAfterFailure(c)` with `c ∈ recoverableCodes`. The extension resolves the request in the **caller's** uid namespace (§5.4) and accepts it only for that (uid, profile)'s pending start in such a hold; everything else is `.notHeld` (a `.nonRetryable` hold, an after-Connected hold, a prompt, an attempt already applying settings). IPs equal, per host as sets, to the ones the start used are `.unchanged` (a repeated push can't loop the start). Otherwise `.retrying` (§7.2).
- Limits: request and reply 16 KiB (the "others" row below), client timeout 2 s (§5.4); not secret-bearing, so it needs only the ordinary hello gate.

**`armStart` (2.0.2, D10.4-5).** Additive, so `LPWireVersion` stays 1.
```swift
public struct ArmStartRequest: Codable, Sendable, Equatable, LPWireValidating { public var profileID: UUID; public var nonce: UUID }
public struct ArmStartReply: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { public var expiresAt: Date }   // the extension's wall clock + 15 s
```
- The owner is the connection's kernel-reported uid; the profile must be provisioned in **that** uid's namespace (`.profileNotProvisioned` otherwise; another uid's copy of the UUID doesn't count). The arm is keyed `(peer.uid, profileID)`; the controller's rules are in §7.2.
- Limits: request and reply 16 KiB, client timeout 2 s, ordinary hello gate, not secret-bearing. `.startAuthorisation` is in the extension's default capability set; the app uses its absence in `hello` to recognise an older extension (§7.2).

**Validator service protocol (2.0.2, D10.4-2; `LPWire/ValidatorWire.swift`).** The app ↔ `LockPlusValidator.xpc`, with the same rules as the extension's wire (Data-only parameters, binary plists through `LPWire`, caps before decode, `LPWireValidating` after it, every reply exactly once).
```swift
public let LPValidatorWireVersion: UInt16 = 1                    // independent of LPWireVersion
@objc public protocol LPValidatorXPC: NSObjectProtocol {
    func hello(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)            // ValidatorHello → ValidatorHello; always first
    func evaluateProfile(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)  // ValidateProfileRequest → ValidateProfileReply (§8.1 [1]–[7])
    func readArchive(_ req: Data, reply: @escaping LPReply2)      // ReadArchiveRequest → ReadArchiveReply (§3.5)
}
public struct ValidatorHello: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { public var wire: UInt16; public var build: String }  // build ≤ 64 B
public struct ReadArchiveRequest: Codable, Sendable { public var archive: Data }   // ≤ maxArchiveBytes = ZipCaps().maxArchiveBytes + 1
public struct ArchiveEntry: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { public var name: String; public var bytes: Data }
public struct ReadArchiveReply: Codable, Sendable {
    public var entries: [ArchiveEntry]; public var issues: [ZipEntryIssue]
    public var archiveError: ZipArchiveError?   // Phase 0 deviation: the archive-level refusal; no entries beside it
}
public enum LPValidatorMethod: String, Sendable, CaseIterable { case hello, evaluateProfile, readArchive }
```
- `ValidateProfileRequest`/`ValidateProfileReply` are reused unchanged. `ZipCaps`, `ZipArchiveError` (+ `.checkUnavailable`) and `ZipEntryIssue` moved from the app to `LPModel/ZipModel.swift` and are `Codable`.
- `ReadArchiveReply.isWireValid`: ≤ 500 entries of ≤ 1 MiB, names ≤ 255 UTF-8 bytes that pass `LPModel.ZipNames.isSafePath` (moved out of `ZipStructure`, which LPWire can't see), ≤ 64 MiB in total, ≤ 500 issues, no entries beside `archiveError`. Names are display text only and never become paths.
- Limits and client timeouts: `hello` 4 KiB / 4 KiB, 3 s; `evaluateProfile` request 300 KiB, reply 64 KiB, **8 s** (below the service's 10 s watchdog); `readArchive` request **100 MiB + 1 KiB**, reply **64 MiB + 256 KiB** (Phase 0: plist framing, names and issues on top of the caps), 30 s.
- Service side (`ValidatorServiceHandler`, nonisolated, `@unchecked Sendable` with a SAFETY note): one request runs at a time (`SerialWorker`), at most 4 accepted and unanswered (`.extensionBusy` beyond), a request still running after 10 s makes the process `exit(0)` (a strict `DispatchSourceTimer`; launchd relaunches it on the next message), no payload bytes in logs (`Logger(subsystem: "io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.validator")`).
- Client side (`ValidatorClient`, an actor in `LPXPCClient`): `NSXPCConnection(serviceName:)`, `setCodeSigningRequirement(VALIDATOR_REQ)` once before `activate()`, `hello` first on every connection object and after every interruption, a `build` other than the app's → `.versionMismatch` (only when the bundle is replaced under a running app, e.g. `brew upgrade`); one request in flight (an async gate); interruption (4097) during a call = the service died on this input: retry **once** on a fresh process, a second death → `.profileCheckCrashed` (105, app-side only, never on the extension wire); invalidation (4099) or no service → `.extensionUnavailable`; 4102 → `.unauthorizedPeer`; a timeout never invalidates the connection (the service's watchdog ends a wedged request).

Size limits are enforced in `LPWire.decode(_:max:)` (requests and replies):

| Message | Limit |
|---|---|
| `hello` request and reply | 4 KiB |
| `provision`, `validateProfile` request | 300 KiB (2.0.2: `validateProfile` is answered busy before decoding) |
| `answerAuth` request | 8 KiB |
| `sessionSummaries` reply | 100 entries, 64 KiB |
| `listProvisioned` reply (draft 8, review S16) | ≤ 500 entries, 160 KiB (~170 B per encoded entry; the headroom is test-asserted) |
| others | 16 KiB |

*Draft 8:* the `recentLogs` row is gone with the method. **After** decoding, every request type is range-checked (`LPWireValidating`: counts, field sizes, enum ranges; `CredentialRecord.isWithinLimits`) and a failure is `.malformedRequest` (review S5), and a decode fuzz test covers every request type.

Oversized messages are rejected with `.payloadTooLarge` and never decoded. These are **our** limits: XPC documents no maximum, and NSXPC has already materialised the whole `Data` before `LPWire.decode` runs, so the caps protect the plist decoder and the engine, not the XPC allocation. That is acceptable because only `APP_REQ`-signed peers get past the listener.

**Versioning:**
- `LPWireVersion` bumps only on an incompatible change; additive fields are optional.
- `hello` is always the first call on a connection. A mismatch yields `.versionMismatch`, and the app calls `activate()`, which replaces the extension.
- With per-version Mach names, a mismatch should never happen in practice. The check is a defence.

### 5.3 Peer code-signature validation (both ends)

Requirement strings are Swift constants, one line each, no comments, so the compiled requirement is the reviewed text (an xcconfig can't hold multi-line values or `//` annotations; ref/security C9, Conflicts f). The Release strings live in the `LPWire` package, which has **no** configuration-dependent code; the dev clause lives in one file compiled by the Xcode targets under an explicit condition (draft 5; see below). Annotated form:
```swift
// LPWire/SigningRequirements.swift (package: identical in every configuration)
public enum SigningRequirements {
    // anchor apple generic
    //   and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6]     Developer ID CA (G1 and G2; G2 verified, P1 skeleton)
    //   and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] Developer ID Application leaf
    //   and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY"       team
    public static let releaseSigner = #"(certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13])"#
    // 2.0.2: always this release's LP_BUILD_NUMBER (version-check.sh); decimal digits only
    public static let minimumAppBuild = "200026"
    public static func appReq(signer: String, minimumBuild: String = minimumAppBuild) -> String {
        #"anchor apple generic and identifier "io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac" and "# + signer
            + #" and info [CFBundleVersion] >= ""# + minimumBuild + #"" and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY""#
    }
    public static func extReq(signer: String) -> String { #"anchor apple generic and identifier "io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel" and "# + signer + #" and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY""# }
    public static func validatorReq(signer: String) -> String { #"anchor apple generic and identifier "io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.validator" and "# + signer + #" and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY""# }   // 2.0.2
}

// Shared/ActiveRequirements.swift: a member of the LockPlus, LockPlusTunnel, LockPlusValidator (2.0.2) and RequirementTests targets
#if LP_DEV_SIGNING
// DEV ONLY (O7, flagged for the Fable security review): also admit Apple Development
// (WWDR intermediate OID ...100.6.2.1), because Debug and FaultInjection builds are Apple Development-signed (§2.4).
// LP_DEV_SIGNING is set in Debug.xcconfig (inherited by FaultInjection.xcconfig) and never in Release.xcconfig.
let activeSigner = #"((certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13]) or (certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.1] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.12]))"#
#else
let activeSigner = SigningRequirements.releaseSigner
#endif
let APP_REQ = SigningRequirements.appReq(signer: activeSigner)        // extension and validator listeners
let EXT_REQ = SigningRequirements.extReq(signer: activeSigner)        // the app's TunnelServiceClient
let VALIDATOR_REQ = SigningRequirements.validatorReq(signer: activeSigner)   // 2.0.2: the app's ValidatorClient
```
- **Minimum app build (2.0.2, D10.4-4).** `APP_REQ` carries `info [CFBundleVersion] >= "200026"` before the team clause (so `requirementsPinTeamAndIdentifiers`' suffix check still holds). Measured (plan F1, `codesign --verify -R` against the installed 2.0.0, 200022): the comparison is **numeric** (`1000000` passes a `200022` floor; as strings it wouldn't) and the value **must be quoted** (unquoted `>= 200022` is a syntax error). **Floor = this build, always:** legitimate app↔extension pairs are the same build anyway (per-version Mach names), so the strongest floor costs no compatibility and every older signed LockPlus stops being a trusted peer the day a new extension activates. Debug builds carry `CFBundleVersion = <build>.<stamp>` and pass their own floor numerically (`floorComparesNumerically`). A peer below the floor fails on its first message, before `shouldAcceptNewConnection`, exactly like a foreign app. Rejected: a floor raised only at app-side security fixes (a judgement per release, will be forgotten); a runtime floor from the extension's own `CFBundleVersion` (the requirement would no longer be a reviewed constant); refusing by `ClientHello.appBuild` (a handler rule after acceptance); an `EXT_REQ` floor (the app reaches only the per-version, root-registered name). Open: R3 on the dev Mac proves the dynamic check enforces it as `codesign -R` does statically; if not, the claim is dropped (§20).
- **The validator service (2.0.2).** Its listener (`NSXPCListener.service()`) applies `setConnectionCodeSigningRequirement(APP_REQ)` before `resume()`, floor included, so only the same-build signed app is served; the delegate only wires the interface. The app's `ValidatorClient` sets `VALIDATOR_REQ` once before `activate()` (4102 → `.unauthorizedPeer`); `hello` carries nothing secret and its `build` must equal the app's. `common.sh` carries `VAL_ID`, `MIN_APP_BUILD`, `FLOOR`, `VALIDATOR_REQ` and `DEV_VALIDATOR_REQ`; `verify.sh static` checks the literals agree, `verify.sh pre` runs `codesign --verify -R "=$VALIDATOR_REQ"` on the service (and expects rc 3 on the extension), and with `LP_PREV_APP` set asserts that the previous notarized app fails the new `APP_REQ` with rc 3 (after checking that bundle's extension against `EXT_REQ`, so a wrong path can't pass as "rc 3").
- **Why a target-level condition, not `#if DEBUG` in the package (draft 5):** SwiftPM knows only debug and release, so package code built for the `FaultInjection` configuration (§15.2) would not see `DEBUG`; the Apple Development-signed FaultInjection app and extension would then carry the Release requirement and reject each other. `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS` of the Xcode targets is fully controlled by our xcconfigs, so `LP_DEV_SIGNING` is set exactly for Debug and FaultInjection.
- **How package code gets the strings (draft 6):** `APP_REQ`/`EXT_REQ` are module-internal globals of the app, extension and `RequirementTests` targets; the listener (TunnelEngine) and the client (`LPXPCClient`) receive them as init parameters (§2.2, §5.1, §5.4).
- **A target-level override would bypass the xcconfig (draft 6):** a `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS` set in `project.pbxproj` on a target wins over `Release.xcconfig`. `verify.sh static` and the CI `build` job therefore run `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings -configuration Release` for the `LockPlus`, `LockPlusTunnel` and `RequirementTests` targets and fail if any output line contains `LP_DEV_SIGNING`.

- **Release pins Developer ID only**, with the team ID quoted. Apple Development, Mac App Distribution and ad-hoc signatures all fail in Release by design. This is the Xcode Developer ID designated requirement minus the Mac App Store alternative, verified against the shipping Go app's DR (ref/security §6.1).
- **Dev clause (O7, Conflicts b):** Debug and FaultInjection builds add `certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.1]` (the WWDR CA that issues Apple Development certificates), so a dev app and a dev extension accept each other. The clause is compiled only under `LP_DEV_SIGNING`. Safety nets: `verify.sh` fails if the string `113635.100.6.2.1` appears in any Release Mach-O (`strings -a`, invariant 11; CI's unsigned build and the dev Mac's `release.sh` both run it), and if the Release build settings of the app, extension or `RequirementTests` contain `LP_DEV_SIGNING` (draft 6, above); the `RequirementTests` bundle holds the expected Release strings as literals and runs under the Debug **and** a Release test plan (§15.1); and `codesign --verify -R "=<req>"` (draft 10: two words, Conflicts bq) with the Release strings against the **signed** products runs on the **dev Mac** only (`verify.sh pre` in `release.sh`, §12.4; and S9/S9b), because CI builds unsigned and has nothing to check. **The Fable security review must sign off on this clause before P2a ends.** *Draft 8: signed off* (Fable security review, 2026-10-26: "sound and Release-excluded"). Its optional tightening, `and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.12]` (the Mac Development leaf) on the dev branch, is adopted (draft 8): `Shared/ActiveRequirements.swift`, `common.sh`'s `DEV_SIGNER` and the `RequirementTests` literals carry it. The `-showBuildSettings` check runs without the release `-xcconfig`, so the `strings` grep on the Release Mach-Os is the real backstop.
- A malformed string is a fatal error in Swift at `setConnectionCodeSigningRequirement`, which is why the unit test exists.
- Extension (listener side, ref/xpc-servicemanagement §5.2):
  - `main.swift` creates the listener at process scope; `TunnelServiceListener` calls `setConnectionCodeSigningRequirement(peerRequirement)` with the injected `APP_REQ` (macOS 13+) and then **`activate()`** (preferred over `resume()` for new code). This is the only check: a failing peer is "automatically rejected before consulting the delegate".
  - It does **not** also call `conn.setCodeSigningRequirement` in `shouldAcceptNewConnection`: the header says calling it more than once is an XPC error, and whether the inherited listener requirement counts as the first call is undocumented (ref/security C8, ref/xpc-servicemanagement C2).
  - **Enforcement timing:** the check is driven by the peer's **first message** (forum 760287). `shouldAcceptNewConnection` is therefore reached only by peers whose first message already satisfied `APP_REQ`. It sets both interfaces, a per-connection `TunnelServiceHandler(peer:)` holding `PeerContext {uid: effectiveUserIdentifier, pid (logs only), connectionID}`, the invalidation handler, registers the connection in `ConnectionRegistry`, calls `activate()`, and returns `true`. Rejected peers leave no trace in our logs (Console: `xpc_support_check_token … -67050`).
  - *Reviewed: "pre-check the audit token in `shouldAcceptNewConnection`" was not adopted.* `NSXPCConnection.auditToken` is SPI, and the public `processIdentifier` is PID-reuse-racy. `setConnectionCodeSigningRequirement` is the only public, race-free peer check for NSXPC on our floor (ref/security §6.3).
- App (client side):
  - `NSXPCConnection(machServiceName:, options: .privileged)` is **mandatory**: it restricts the lookup to the root bootstrap, which only root can populate, closing the "same-user process registers a lookalike name" vector.
  - `setCodeSigningRequirement(peerRequirement)` (= `EXT_REQ`, injected, §5.4) once, before `activate()`. This validates **received** messages, so the first request reaches whatever is listening before the reply is checked (forum 837286). Therefore `hello` carries no secret, and `provisionProfile`, `updateCredentials` and `answerAuth` are sent only after `hello`'s reply has arrived **on the same connection object**, and again after every interruption (§5.4; ref/xpc-servicemanagement C5).
  - The app's exported `LPAppCallbackXPC` is only reachable over this connection.
- macOS 27 adds dual classical/post-quantum code signatures (ref/security C17). **Draft 7:** `codesign` on 27.1 produced only a classical signature by default (`syspolicy_check`: "Only one signature found … skipping dual signature check"; P1 skeleton §3), so C17's assumption that our builds carry both is unconfirmed. S9 records whether a dual signature is produced at all and with which option; the Release requirements were verified on the classical signature (G2 chain). The `errSecCSStaticCodeChanged` update test (§15.5) does not depend on it.
- Test: a team-signed binary with a different identifier, an Apple Development-signed copy of the **Release** app, an unsigned binary, and a tampered copy of the real Release app each fail on the client with 4097 (`Interrupted`), 4099 (`Invalid`) or 4102 (`CodeSigningRequirementFailure`), and the extension logs no accept or handler line for them (§15.6; ref/xpc-servicemanagement C4).

### 5.4 Timeouts, ownership and rate limits

XPC has no timeouts ("just run your own timer", forum 703653). A reply-block call through `remoteObjectProxyWithErrorHandler` ends in **exactly one** of the reply block or the error handler; every timeout is a race against that guarantee. The canonical client is ref/xpc-servicemanagement §4, with `Mutex` in place of `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` (Conflicts d2):

```swift
import Synchronization

/// Resumes a continuation exactly once; later resumes are dropped. Reply block, proxy error handler,
/// timer task and task-cancellation handler all go through it (ref/swift-concurrency §6.1).
final class OneShot<T: Sendable>: Sendable {
    private enum State { case pending(CheckedContinuation<T, Never>), cancelledEarly, done }
    private let state: Mutex<State>
    init() { state = Mutex(.done) }                       // armed by `attach` inside withCheckedContinuation
    func attach(_ k: CheckedContinuation<T, Never>, ifCancelled value: @autoclosure () -> T) {
        let early = state.withLock { s -> Bool in
            if case .cancelledEarly = s { return true }; s = .pending(k); return false
        }
        if early { k.resume(returning: value()) }
    }
    func resume(_ value: T) {
        let k: CheckedContinuation<T, Never>? = state.withLock { s in
            guard case .pending(let k) = s else { return nil }; s = .done; return k
        }
        k?.resume(returning: value)                       // resumed outside the lock
    }
    func cancel(_ value: T) {                             // may run before attach (cancellation handler)
        let k: CheckedContinuation<T, Never>? = state.withLock { s in
            switch s { case .pending(let k): s = .done; return k
                       case .done: s = .cancelledEarly; return nil
                       case .cancelledEarly: return nil }
        }
        k?.resume(returning: value)
    }
}

// LPXPCClient (LockPlusCore package). Package code can't see the app target's EXT_REQ, so it is injected (§2.2).
public actor TunnelServiceClient {
    private let machServiceName: String                   // read from the embedded extension's Info.plist (§2.5)
    private let peerRequirement: String                   // EXT_REQ from the app target's ActiveRequirements.swift
    public init(machServiceName: String, peerRequirement: String) { … }   // no default for either parameter
    private var connection: NSXPCConnection?              // non-Sendable; never leaves the actor
    private var generation: UInt64 = 0
    private var helloTask: Task<Result<ServerHello, LPError>, Never>?   // per connection object

    /// Public entry: `throws(LPError)` built from a Result continuation (works on every toolchain).
    func call<Req: Encodable & Sendable, Resp: Decodable & Sendable>(
        _ method: LPMethod, _ req: Req, timeout: Duration
    ) async throws(LPError) -> Resp {
        if method != .hello { _ = try await ensureHello().get() }      // nothing secret before a validated hello
        let data = try LPWire.encode(req)
        let gate = OneShot<Result<(Data?, Data?), LPError>>()
        let raw = await withTaskCancellationHandler {
            await withCheckedContinuation { (k: CheckedContinuation<Result<(Data?, Data?), LPError>, Never>) in
                gate.attach(k, ifCancelled: .failure(LPError(.cancelled)))
                let c = currentConnection()                // body runs synchronously in the actor's isolation
                                                           // DRAFT 8 (Fable M3): as built, a non-hello call takes ONLY the
                                                           // connection whose hello reply was validated for the current
                                                           // (generation, interruption count) and never creates one; see below
                guard let proxy = c.remoteObjectProxyWithErrorHandler({ error in
                    gate.resume(.failure(LPError(xpc: error as NSError)))      // 4097/4099/4101/4102 → LPErrorCode
                }) as? any LPTunnelServiceXPC else { gate.resume(.failure(LPError(.extensionUnavailable))); return }
                method.invoke(proxy, data) { a, b in gate.resume(.success((a, b))) }
                Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: timeout)                     // the timer never invalidates the connection
                       gate.resume(.failure(LPError(.timeout, detail: method.rawValue))) }
            }
        } onCancel: { gate.cancel(.failure(LPError(.cancelled))) }
        return try LPWire.decodeReply(raw.get(), max: method.replyLimit)
    }
    // currentConnection(), ensureHello(), didInterrupt(_:), didInvalidate(_:) as in ref/xpc-servicemanagement §4
    // draft 8: the per-call timer task is cancelled when the call completes (Sonnet core review)
}
```

- **No `TaskGroup` race** around XPC or any other non-cancellable call: a task group waits for all children, so a 200 ms timeout around a continuation that ignores cancellation returned after 3.2 s in a probe (ref/swift-concurrency SC9). The extension's 1 s internal deadlines use the same gate (`ReplyGate`).
- Catch sites write `do throws(LPError) { … }`; a plain `do`/`catch` infers `any Error` (ref/swift-concurrency SC20).
- On timeout the call throws `.timeout(method)` and **ignores** the late reply. **A timeout never invalidates the connection** (that would fail every other in-flight call and look like a dead extension).
- Per-method timeouts (`LPMethod.timeout`; the extension's handler deadline `serverDeadline` is 1 s less):
  - `hello` 3 s
  - `tunnelSnapshot`, `statistics`, `pendingAuthPrompt`, `prepareStartAuth`, `cancelAuth`, `pushEndpoints` (draft 10) 2 s
  - `provisionProfile`, `updateCredentials`, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets`, `listProvisioned` 10 s
  - `validateProfile`, `answerAuth` 5 s (2.0.2: `validateProfile` answers `.extensionBusy` at once)
  - `armStart` (2.0.2) 2 s
  - `sessionSummaries` 3 s (draft 8: `recentLogs` is gone)
  - `measureLatency` 6 s
- **The hello gate as built (draft 8, Fable review M3; Sonnet core review 6, 9; PF 23, 39).**
  - **Client:** a non-hello call is sent only on the connection object whose `hello` reply passed `EXT_REQ` for the current (generation, interruption count); it never calls `currentConnection()`, so an invalidation between hello and send can't route a secret-bearing call over a fresh, unvalidated connection. A retry loop that sees no new interruption keeps the hello validated (no `.reconnecting` flicker).
  - **Server:** the listener refuses every non-hello call on a connection that hasn't completed `hello` (`.malformedRequest "hello required"`).
  - **Busy rule:** the client's own timer maps to **`.extensionBusy`** (the call timed out at our end), and a server-side `LPError(.timeout)` counts toward the 3-consecutive rule like a client timeout; it no longer resets it.
  - **In-flight cap (Fable review L6):** at most **8** handler tasks per connection; the 9th request gets `.extensionBusy "too many requests"` at once, before decoding.
- **Liveness rule (L-LC-3), refined (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C6):**
  - A timeout yields `.extensionBusy`, which the UI shows only after 3 consecutive timeouts, as a non-blocking indicator. No timeout ever triggers reinstall, reactivation or a "dead extension" dialog. This is the 7a55ba6/aa46660 lesson.
  - **Interruption** (4097: the extension crashed, was killed, or a replacement is in progress): keep the same connection object and mark it **unvalidated**. The next call re-runs `hello`; then `AuthCoordinator` re-subscribes (re-pulls `pendingAuthPrompt`) and `StatsStore` resets its `RateMeter` baseline. The next message relaunches the extension, which has lost all per-connection state. S5 (27): a reply block in flight gets 4097 ~210 ms after the kill, and `interruptionHandler` fires; the order of the two varies.
  - **Respawn throttle (draft 7, S5 on 27):** launchd does not respawn a crashed extension until **10 s after its previous spawn**. A `hello` sent within that window waits and times out at 3 s even though nothing is wrong. After an interruption the client therefore retries `hello` on the **same** connection object with `Backoff(base: 0.5 s, cap: 4 s)` for **12 s** (≥ 11 s) before mapping to `.extensionUnavailable`. A new object is required only after an invalidation (a fresh object relaunches the extension too, but is not needed after an interruption). During the retry window `ExtensionStore.link = .reconnecting(since:)`, and the derived state shows "Reconnecting to the tunnel process…", never "unreachable" (§11.2, UI-CONCEPT §6.6 row 4a). The 3-consecutive-timeouts rule above does not count these retries.
  - **Interruption while the tunnel is up (S5.5 on 27, and on 26 in draft 9):** a provider-process crash gives the app 4097 at once, but NE reports `.disconnecting` → `.disconnected` only **~5 s later** (4.99–5.19 s, S2 E1), with `fetchLastDisconnectError` = `NEVPNConnectionErrorDomain` 12 (`pluginFailed`). Without `includeAllNetworks` nothing restarts it; **with it, NE restarts the provider by itself ≈2.0–2.9 s after `.disconnected`** (the restarted session's block lands there; LK-02, E2E-1, S2 E1's open window 2.45–2.86 s; the new provider PID appears earlier, ~1 s after the kill, but that is launchd relaunching the process, not the session restart) with the original start options (S2 E1, §10.1.1), unless the manager has on-demand rules. For those ~5 s `NEVPNStatus` still says `.connected`; the derived state shows row 4a instead of "Protected".
  - **Invalidation** (4099) means "this name is not reachable now" (approval pending, replacement in progress, extension removed, or interrupted-then-unloaded), not "extension dead". Drop the connection, build a new one on the next call, map to `.extensionUnavailable`, and let the UI derive its message from `SystemExtensionManager.state`, never from the XPC error alone. A replaced extension's old name shows interruption then invalidation.
  - **Code-signing failure** (4102, `NSXPCConnectionCodeSigningRequirementFailure`: the listener's reply failed `EXT_REQ`, so whatever answered is not our extension, or our extension's signature is broken): drop the connection, map to `.unauthorizedPeer`, log at **`.fault`**, send nothing further on it, and **never** retry automatically or reinstall. The poisoned state is cleared only by a user action: "Try Again" (`retryAfterUserAction()`) or `reinstall()` (draft 8, Sonnet core review 3; before, nothing cleared it). The UI shows "The tunnel component is damaged. Reinstall LockPlus." with a diagnostics export, the same wording as the `.failed(.broken)` activation state (§4.2) (ref/xpc-servicemanagement §6 table).
- Extension side: every handler replies **exactly once, on every path**, within its internal deadline, which is 1 s below the client's (a reply block that is never called leaks memory and Mach resources). Handlers are nonisolated (`@unchecked Sendable` with a SAFETY note: only `let` references to actors and `Sendable` objects), hop into actors with `Task`, and reply through a `ReplyGate` (the one-shot gate plus a timer).
- Ownership: every profile-scoped request carries `profileID`, and the extension checks it against the connection's `effectiveUserIdentifier` (as built in draft 8: by resolving it in that uid's namespace, below).
- No rate limiting in v2.0 (cut, §21). Callers are signature-validated same-team code. Flooding by the app itself would be a bug, caught in testing. `.rateLimited` stays reserved in the error enum. The draft 8 in-flight cap (above) bounds concurrency, not rate.
- **Ownership as built (draft 8, D8-1):** the extension resolves every profile-scoped request in the **caller's** uid namespace (`effectiveUserIdentifier`), so another uid's profile is simply absent (`.profileNotProvisioned`), not `.notOwner`. `.notOwner` remains for auth prompts (`answerAuth`, `cancelAuth`, `pendingAuthPrompt`, `prepareStartAuth`), whose promptIDs are global.

### 5.5 Error model

```swift
public struct LPError: Error, Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    public var code: LPErrorCode
    public var detail: String?        // ≤ 512 chars, never contains secrets or server-controlled text
}
public enum LPErrorCode: Int, Codable, Sendable {
    // transport
    case timeout = 1, extensionUnavailable, extensionBusy, versionMismatch, unauthorizedPeer,
         payloadTooLarge, malformedRequest, rateLimited /* reserved */, notOwner, cancelled, staleAnswer
    // profile
    case profileNotProvisioned = 100, profileInvalid, profileRevisionStale, unsupportedDirective,
         killSwitchNotApplied // draft 10 (= 104, E2E-1): app-side only, never on the wire (§3.4 prepareForStart)
    // tunnel (also used as NSError codes for cancelTunnelWithError, domain "io.github.steiale.lockplus.tunnel")
    case authFailed = 200, authRequired, authTimedOut, webAuthUnsupported, keyPassphraseRequired,
         connectTimeout, peerUnreachable, dnsResolutionFailed, engineFatal, tunDeviceFailed,
         networkSettingsFailed, legacyCryptoUnavailable, serverIdentityMismatch, conflictingVPN,
         secretStoreUnavailable, blockedAfterFailure, startCancelled, engineDied, dnsPlanMissing,
         pushedOptionRejected, // draft 7: a pull-filter `reject` matched a pushed option (§8.5)
         endpointInterfaceUnusable // draft 7.3: the server is reachable only via a non-primary interface (§9.3)
}
/// The tunnel error keeps its code across fetchLastDisconnectError (CustomNSError, ref/swift-concurrency §3.1).
public struct LPTunnelError: Error, CustomNSError, Sendable {
    public static let errorDomain = "io.github.steiale.lockplus.tunnel"
    public var code: LPErrorCode; public var detail: String?
    public var errorCode: Int { code.rawValue }
    public var errorUserInfo: [String: Any] { detail.map { ["lp.detail": $0] } ?? [:] }   // plist types only
}
```

- `startCancelled` completes a pending `startTunnel` when `stopTunnel` arrives first (§7.2); it is not shown to the user when the stop reason is `.userInitiated`. **Exception (draft 6, L-OVPN-4; the normal case since draft 9):** a stop that ends a before-Connected hold (`includeAllNetworks`, S2 E14) completes the start with the held error `e`, not `.startCancelled`, so `fetchLastDisconnectError` still returns the reason the session was blocked; the app does not re-alert it after its own Disconnect (UI-CONCEPT §6.6 row 14 shows it as detail). The same holds when a profile change or removal ends a waiting start (§7.2). It is ref/networkextension C19's `.cancelled`, renamed because `.cancelled` (raw 10) already means a caller-cancelled XPC call (Conflicts ae). `engineDied` is wireguard-go closing its device (W6). `dnsPlanMissing` is a full tunnel whose engine delivered no DNS (§8.5). `endpointInterfaceUnusable` (draft 7.3, S6) replaces `.connectTimeout`/`.peerUnreachable` when the start-time endpoint interface check (§9.3) found the server's route on a non-primary interface; `detail` is the BSD interface name (`bridge100`), which is local and non-secret. `authTimedOut` (draft 9) also ends a prompt inside the pending start at its deadline. `killSwitchNotApplied` (draft 10) is the app's refusal to start a kill-switch profile whose NE configuration doesn't carry the flags after one repair (§3.4); the extension never sees or sends it.
- The extension's `cancelTunnelWithError` (kill switch off only, draft 9) carries only the code plus a non-secret `detail` in `userInfo["lp.detail"]`.
- The app localizes every message from the code; the extension has no localization (it runs as root, in an unknown locale).
- **`fetchLastDisconnectError` (ref/networkextension C5):** Apple documents that "if the error came from a tunnel provider … the error is the NSError that the provider passed". **Assumption A-ERR-1 holds in full on 27 (S12, draft 7) and on 26 (S5 VM run, draft 9):** a `cancelTunnelWithError` with domain `io.github.steiale.lockplus.spike`, code 42 and `userInfo["lp.detail"]` arrived in the app with all three intact.
  - Use the **completion-handler** form only. The Swift async variant returns `Void` and *throws* the last error, so `let e = try await fetchLastDisconnectError()` is wrong by construction.
  - **It is sticky (S12, draft 7):** the call returns the last error of **any** earlier session until a later session ends with a different one (right before S12's connect it still returned S5's code 12). The app reads it **only** on a `.disconnected` transition it observed after a `.connecting`/`.connected`/`.reasserting` status in the same app instance, never at launch as "the current error". At launch, `ConnectionStore` takes `tunnelSnapshot.lastError` with its `lastErrorAt` (§5.2) and shows it only together with a `startLatch`, a pending next-start prompt, or a `lastErrorAt` later than the app's last recorded quit (`settings.json` `lastQuitAt`) (§11.2).
  - System errors arrive in `NEVPNConnectionErrorDomain`, imported as a raw enum without `.Code`: compare `NSError.code` to `rawValue`. Mapped codes: `pluginFailed (12)` → "LockPlus's tunnel process stopped unexpectedly" (S5.5: what a provider crash while connected yields); `pluginDisabled (14)` → "The tunnel component is turned off or needs an update" (sends the user to the §4.2 approval UI); the rest → a generic message with the code in Details.
  - **Fallback and launch source:** the extension also stores `lastError` and `lastErrorAt` per profile in its state file, and the app reads them via `tunnelSnapshot`.

---

## 6. Credentials: the two-store design (L-CRED-1)

### 6.1 Ownership matrix

| Secret | App DP keychain | Extension store (§6.3: System keychain, or the fallback's container files) | Written by | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Master sealing key | ✔ | — | app | first launch |
| Extension file key (fallback only) | — | ✔ `secrets/filekey.*` | extension | first provision |
| Payload (keys inside `.conf`/`.ovpn`) | sealed file (key in DP keychain) | ✔ item `…tunnel.payload`/HMAC account (or `secrets/<uid>.<uuid>.payload`; draft 8, §6.3) | app; extension via `provisionProfile` | import, edit, reconcile |
| OVPN username/password/key passphrase | ✔ `…credentials/<uuid>` | ✔ item `…tunnel.cred`/HMAC account (or `secrets/<uid>.<uuid>.cred`) | app; extension via provision/`updateCredentials` | user saves, or "save" ticked in a prompt |
| OTP, SC/CRV1 responses, `auth-token` | never | never (memory only, zeroed) | — | per prompt |

- The app **never** reads the extension's copy, and the extension never reads the app's.
- The app's copy is the **source of truth**. The extension's copy is a cache that `reconcile()` can always rebuild.

### 6.2 App store

```swift
public protocol CredentialStore: Sendable {
    func load(_ id: UUID, gate: RevealToken?) async throws(KeychainError) -> CredentialRecord?  // nil ONLY for errSecItemNotFound
    func save(_ id: UUID, _ rec: CredentialRecord) async throws(KeychainError)
    func delete(_ id: UUID) async throws(KeychainError)                  // not-found is success
}
public enum KeychainError: Error, Sendable {
    case temporarilyUnavailable(OSStatus)   // -25308, -25315, -25320, -25291: retry after unlock/login; never "missing"
    case misconfigured(OSStatus)            // -34018 errSecMissingEntitlement: a signing/profile bug
    case other(OSStatus)
}
actor DataProtectionCredentialStore: CredentialStore { … }
```

The query (one function builds it; every call uses it; ref/security §2.2):
- `kSecClass: kSecClassGenericPassword`, `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain: true`
- `kSecAttrAccessGroup: "M53GHX9FAY.io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac"`
- service as in §3.3, account `uuid.uuidString`, `kSecAttrSynchronizable: false`
- On add: `kSecAttrAccessible: kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`. **Changed from `WhenUnlocked…`:** reconcile and provisioning run unattended (wake, `NEVPNConfigurationChange`, on-demand), possibly with the screen locked or during a dark wake; `WhenUnlocked…` is documented for foreground-only items. Device binding (§6.8) is unchanged (ref/security C5). S4 measures reads of both classes with the screen locked and in dark wake.

Behaviour:
- `load`: `kSecReturnData` + `kSecMatchLimitOne`. `save` is `SecItemUpdate` (no `kSecReturn*`/`kSecMatchLimit` in the query), falling back to `SecItemAdd` on `errSecItemNotFound`, and retrying Update once on `errSecDuplicateItem` (a race). Bulk enumeration (reconcile, uninstall) asks for attributes only, never data. Values are raw `Data`; there is no text encoding at all (the b64:/hex lesson).
- **Error classification (ref/security C6):** `load` returns `nil` **only** for `errSecItemNotFound` (-25300). `-25308`/`-25315`/`-25320`/`-25291` are `.temporarilyUnavailable` (defer and retry after unlock or login, never regenerate keys); `-34018` is `.misconfigured`.
- Calls run on the actor's executor, never on the main thread. DP keychain calls are bounded IPC to securityd with no UI, so running them on an actor is acceptable; the **legacy** reads in §6.7 are not (ref/swift-concurrency SC12).

### 6.3 Extension store (S4: System keychain selected on 26 and 27, sealed container files fallback)

**Decision (draft 4, Conflicts a):** the extension's secrets live in the **System keychain** as generic-password items it creates itself. The draft 3 design (sealed root-owned 0600 files in the sandbox container) is kept, unchanged in substance, as the **tested fallback**. Spike S4 runs both on 26/27 and selects by the go criteria in §17.

**S4 result on 27 (draft 7.3): (a) selected.** From the sandboxed root sysex (uid 0, no temporary-exception entitlement), plain `SecItem` reached `/Library/Keychains/System.keychain` as the default keychain (TN3137 confirmed). Add, read, update and delete of a 64 B item with a `kSecAttrGeneric` plist, a 256 KiB item and attribute-only enumeration all worked. There was no prompt and no `-67674`, EPERM or `-25308`. Every operation took 11–29 ms (enumeration 0.36 ms), and a marker item survived four Release → Release replacements. Every §17 go criterion is met on 27 except the reboot rows. **S4 on 26 and the 27 VM (draft 9, D9-12): (a) confirmed.** The same operations on 26.6.2 (6–27 ms per op; every item enumerated twice, as on 27), persistence across Release → Release replacement, and reads **after a reboot before the first login** (console user `root`, `scutil --nc start`: marker read in 12.4 ms on 26, 8.9 ms on the 27 VM) and after auto-login. **On-demand does not start an app-created configuration at the login window** (3 min on 26, 2 min on 27; it started 3.5–6 s after login), so "on-demand at boot" means "after the first login" (§10.4). Out of scope and still open, none blocking: Debug → Release replacement (no dev profile), the app-side DP checks (DP reads while locked; `kSecClassKey` is closed, §3.3) and persistence after deactivation (needs the SecurityAgent dialog, §4.4). If a later run fails on 26 or 27, the build switches to (b) everywhere (invariant 6).

Why the System keychain is now primary (ref/security §1.5–§1.6, §4.4):
- An NE system extension is effectively a launchd daemon, so it cannot use the data-protection keychain (TN3137; forums 721674, 824202).
- Draft 3's blocker is gone. The sandbox violations on the System keychain that DTS reported for a sandboxed NE sysex in 2021 (forum 672456; FB11916222) are "reported as fixed in macOS 14", and the fix applies to NE system extensions specifically (forums 721674, 762551). Our floor is 26.0.
- Draft 3's second reason was wrong: "In the system context the search list includes just the System keychain, which is also the default keychain" (TN3137). A plain `SecItemAdd`/`SecItemCopyMatching` **without** `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain`, `kSecUseKeychain` or `SecKeychainOpen` targets it. No deprecated API is involved.
- It is DTS's stated preference for a sysex ("That's what I'd use, possibly with a scrambling layer", forum 824202).
- It removes our own file format, AAD scheme and key wrap from the primary path, so there is less security-critical code to review.
- What it does **not** change: the boundary. Any admin can read System keychain items, exactly as with root-owned files. Root is the real boundary either way; admins are out of scope (§1.3 A2).
- Item ACLs are bound to the creating extension's designated requirement (identifier + team, not the certificate), so same-team replacements (including a renewed certificate) keep access. Debug (Apple Development) and Release extensions have different designated requirements and cannot read each other's items; a daemon cannot show the ACL prompt, so the read fails. That is harmless: the store is a **cache** that `reconcile()` rebuilds from the app (§6.4). Debug builds use the service prefix `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel.dev.` so the two never collide.

```swift
protocol ExtensionSecretStore: Sendable {                      // TunnelEngine; draft 8: every call is addressed by uid
    func put(_ kind: SecretKind, _ id: UUID, ownerUID: uid_t, revision: UInt64, _ bytes: SecretBytes) async throws(LPError)
    func get(_ kind: SecretKind, _ id: UUID, ownerUID: uid_t) async throws(LPError) -> SecretBytes?
    func entry(_ kind: SecretKind, _ id: UUID, ownerUID: uid_t) async throws(LPError) -> ProvisionIndexEntry?  // metadata only
    func delete(_ kind: SecretKind, _ id: UUID, ownerUID: uid_t) async throws(LPError)
    func deleteAll(ownerUID: uid_t) async throws(LPError)
    func index(ownerUID: uid_t) async throws(LPError) -> [ProvisionIndexEntry] // this uid's (id, kind, revision, ownerUID, digest)
}
actor SystemKeychainSecretStore: ExtensionSecretStore { … }   // primary
actor ContainerSecretStore: ExtensionSecretStore { … }        // fallback (draft 3 design)
```

**Primary: `SystemKeychainSecretStore`** (draft 8 layout; Fable review H1, L4; Conflicts ay; PF 36, 49).
- **Addressing:** every item is addressed by (ownerUID, kind, UUID). Two uids can provision the same UUID independently; a uid that learns another user's UUID (keychain attributes and NE preferences are world-readable) can't squat it. Items: `kSecClassGenericPassword`, service `…tunnel.payload` / `…tunnel.cred`, **account = hex HMAC-SHA256(account key, `"lp.acct.v1" ‖ kind ‖ ownerUID (BE) ‖ uuid`)**, so an account is neither guessable nor linkable to a profile UUID by anyone who can list attributes. `kSecAttrLabel` = "LockPlus tunnel secret" is the only attribute. No `kSecAttrAccessible` (it is ignored by the file-based keychain), no `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain`, no `kSecUseAuthenticationUI`.
- **Value:** `"LPK1" ‖ UInt32 BE metaLength ‖ SecretMeta ‖ secret`, where `SecretMeta` = `{id, kind, ownerUID, revision, digest}` as a binary plist. The provision index lives **inside `kSecValueData`**, readable by root only, never in attributes. Every read re-checks the value's metadata against the (kind, uuid, uid) it was addressed by.
- **Account key:** 32 random bytes in the item `<prefix>key` / `account-hmac`, created on the first `put`.
- Writes: `SecItemUpdate`, falling back to `SecItemAdd`. `index(ownerUID:)` lists accounts only (`kSecMatchLimitAll`, no data), reads each value's metadata and keeps the caller's entries; an item whose account isn't the HMAC of its own metadata is foreign or moved and is skipped, never reported. `provision` treats an unreadable entry as absent and overwrites it (tunnel review T7: an unreadable item used to wedge provisioning).
- **The index de-duplicates (S4, draft 7.3).** On 27 the attribute-only `kSecMatchLimitAll` query returns **every item twice** (6 entries for 3 items). The store therefore de-duplicates accounts before reading. An entry whose value can't be read or checked is reported without a digest, so `reconcile()` re-provisions that profile (§6.4) instead of trusting it.
- **Store lifecycle (draft 8, Fable verification NEW-5; PF 49).**
  - *Reset:* on the first key load of a store instance, the store checks the account key against the items. If the key is missing or not 32 bytes while items exist, or the key is valid but no item's account is the HMAC of its own metadata (no uid has any reachable entry), it deletes every `<prefix>payload|cred` item and the key, recreates the key on the next `put`, logs at `.fault` and reports the number of unmatched items through `DiagnosticsHook.secretStoreReset` (a TODO stub, §14.1). `reconcile()` then re-provisions from each app. A store in which some items still match is left alone (strays are skipped by the index).
  - *Last uid wiped:* a `deleteAll(ownerUID:)` that leaves no uid with an entry also deletes the account key; the next provision creates a fresh one.
- Error handling: `errSecItemNotFound` = absent; `errSecMDSError` (-67674), EPERM (100001) or `errSecInteractionNotAllowed` (-25308) at runtime → `.secretStoreUnavailable`, logged at `.fault`, and the S4 decision is revisited (these are the historical sandbox failure codes, ref/security §4.4).
- Items outlive the extension's container, so `wipeAllSecrets` (§4.4) must delete them explicitly.

**Fallback: `ContainerSecretStore`** (selected by S4, or at runtime by a build flag if the primary fails S4 on any supported OS):
- The directory is `<container>/Data/Library/Application Support/secrets/` (§3.3). At first use the store creates it with mode 0700 and verifies `lstat` owner `0`, mode `0700` and not a symlink. If verification fails, the store refuses to operate (`.secretStoreUnavailable`).
- Files are written with `open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600)` to a temp name, `F_FULLFSYNC`, then `rename`. Reads use `O_NOFOLLOW` and check owner and mode via `fstat`.
- Each file carries an `AES.GCM.SealedBox.combined` under the 256-bit **file key**, with the fixed-width AAD of §3.3 binding kind, owner uid (draft 8), UUID and revision. A file swapped between profiles or uids fails authentication.
- The **file key** is a CryptoKit `SymmetricKey(size: .bits256)` (zeroing storage). At rest:
  1. **Secure Enclave wrap** when the SE works (draft 9: not merely when `SecureEnclave.isAvailable`, which is true in a VM where the key can't be created, below): a `SecureEnclave.P256.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey` with the default access control (`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, no flags); its `dataRepresentation` in `se.key`; the file key HPKE-sealed to its public key in `filekey.wrapped` (format in §3.3; HPKE needs macOS 14). DTS reports this works from a daemon but has "no official answer" on support (forum 804612). **S4 verified it in the sandboxed NE sysex on 27 (draft 7.3):** `isAvailable` is true there; creating the key took 14 ms, HPKE-sealing the file key 0.9 ms, and reloading the key from `dataRepresentation` plus unwrapping 5 ms. The SE key, the wrapped file key and a sealed marker written by one build were opened by the next builds, so the SE key survives extension replacement. The sealed-file rules below (`O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, `F_FULLFSYNC`, `rename`, owner/mode checks, AAD rejection of a swapped UUID) and the raw-key path also passed. Before the first login after boot, **both creating and using** the SE key fail with `-25308` (underlying `kIOReturnNotPermitted`), so first provisioning before any login also fails. **Decision:** accepted; `kSecAttrAccessibleAlways` (DTS's documented workaround) is deprecated and deliberately not used. A pre-login on-demand start fails with `.secretStoreUnavailable` and on-demand retries after login. Until login this is a restart loop; draft 6 bounds it with a `.backoff` start latch (5 s doubling to 5 min; an on-demand start before `notBefore` fails at once without touching the store, §7.2 Rules).
  2. **Plain root file** `filekey.raw` (0600) otherwise. **Draft 9 (S4 on the 26/27 VMs, D9-12, Conflicts bm):** in a VM `SecureEnclave.isAvailable` is **true**, but creating the key fails with `-25308` (AKS `-536870174`). The choice is therefore made by trying, with one rule: **any SE error while creating the key, `-25308` included, means "no SE"** and the raw file key is created; once `filekey.raw` exists the store stays on it. On an **existing** SE key, `-25308` is the transient pre-login lock above (`.secretStoreUnavailable`, `lockedBeforeLogin`; the files stay sealed under that key), and any other **SE/HPKE** error (`se <code>`, a malformed `filekey.wrapped`) means the key is unusable: it is discarded and the raw key takes over (files sealed under the old key no longer open, the index reports them without a digest and reconcile re-provisions). A **file-I/O** error on the key files (`open` EMFILE/EINTR, owner/mode, short read, a failed write) is never "no SE": it propagates as `.secretStoreUnavailable` and leaves both keys alone (D9-20). A first provisioning that happens before any login on real hardware therefore also lands on the raw key; that is accepted (the wrap is not a boundary, below). This path runs in every VM and in tests (ref/security C3).
- **What the wrap adds:** only that copied files, disk images and backups are useless off this Mac. With FileVault on, the volume is already encrypted at rest. It does **not** stop a live root process, which can use the wrapped key as we do. It is not counted as a boundary.
- **Fallback layout (draft 8):** files are `<ownerUID>.<UUID>.<payload|cred>`, each `"LPS2" ‖ UInt32 BE metaLength ‖ SecretMeta ‖ AES.GCM.SealedBox.combined` with AAD `"lp.v2" ‖ kind ‖ ownerUID (UInt32 BE) ‖ uuid (16) ‖ revision (UInt64 BE)` (§3.3). Unreadable files of a uid are reported without a digest. The last uid's `deleteAll` also deletes `se.key`, `filekey.wrapped` and `filekey.raw`; the next provision creates a fresh file key.

Common rules:
- The store's own metadata records `ownerUID` per entry (draft 8: inside the protected value), and `deleteAll(ownerUID:)` deletes exactly that uid's entries.
- **`runStarting` requires the payload entry's owner to equal the configuration's `ownerUID`** (draft 8, Fable H1 fix 1), else `.profileNotProvisioned`. Because the lookup already happens in that uid's namespace, this is a consistency check, not a boundary (§1.3 A2, PF 47).
