| establishing | apply throws | the before-Connected failure rows | `.networkSettingsFailed`. |
| connecting/establishing | connect deadline | the before-Connected failure rows | `.connectTimeout`, or `.endpointInterfaceUnusable` when the start-time endpoint interface check flagged the server (§9.3, draft 7.3). |
| held (before Connected) | retry timer (retryable failures only; backoff 1 s … 60 s, jitter; a `.backoff` latch's `notBefore`) | starting | The whole start sequence again (reload, re-validate, new adapter). The snapshot keeps `holdReason` and `holdBeforeConnected` during the retry, with `attempt`/`nextRetryAt` (UI-CONCEPT row 3a). Success completes the start with `nil`. |
| held (before Connected) | `updateCredentials` for the profile | starting | Retry now (the new credentials may fix it). |
| held (before Connected), or its retry attempt in `starting`/`connecting`, with `holdReason == .blockedAfterFailure(c)`, `c ∈ PushEndpointsRequest.recoverableCodes` (`.dnsResolutionFailed`, `.connectTimeout`, `.peerUnreachable`, `.endpointInterfaceUnusable`) | `pushEndpoints` from the profile's owner with IPs that differ from the ones the start used (draft 10, PF 50, §5.2) | starting | **The held start takes the app-pushed IPs** (they win over the start options and the cache for this start, and are cached on success) and re-runs the start sequence now: in `held` the retry timer is cancelled and the retry fires; a retry in flight is replaced (its adapter torn down, the epoch bumped, so its late events and failures are dropped). Reply `.retrying`; the same IPs are `.unchanged` and change nothing; any other state is `.notHeld`. The snapshot keeps `holdReason`/`holdBeforeConnected`. |
| any phase before Connected (held, a retry attempt, awaitingAuth incl. `AUTH_PENDING`) | a provision with a higher revision, `removeProfile` or `wipeAllSecrets` for the profile | stopped | Complete the start with the held error (`.startCancelled` otherwise) so NE ends the session and the app can start the new revision; tear the adapter down; push `promptResolved` for a live prompt. `provision` reports the revision change before new credentials (so their retry never runs the new payload under the old configuration; D9-20). **Draft 10.7 (D10.7-1): not for a higher revision when the session has a kill switch (start-time or live flags):** that start goes on (an attempt in flight finishes, a hold stays held and its next attempt loads the committed payload); only `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets` and the user's stop end it. **Draft 10.8:** a kill-switch start in the guard is not ended either (D10.8-1), and one at a live prompt gets a fresh attempt on the new revision, the prompt resolved (D10.8-2). **Draft 10.9:** for a kill-switch start "higher" means above the revision the current attempt loaded, and an answer being saved counts as a live prompt (D10.9-4); **draft 10.10:** a start without a kill switch compares with its configuration's revision (D10.10-5), and an answer of another revision is never handed to an attempt (D10.10-1). |
| connected | path changed (physical interface or gateway set differs, still satisfied) | reasserting(.path) | `setReasserting(true)`, `adapter.reconnect(.pathChanged)` (L-RC-1). Our own utun is not a path change (§7.4, S2 E12). |
| connected | path unsatisfied | reasserting(.noNetwork) | `setReasserting(true)`. Wait for a satisfied path; no backoff consumed. |
| connected | watchdog `.stale`, or WG `wgIsClosed` (W6) | reasserting(.deadPeer) / see `.fatal(.engineDied)` | L-RC-2; a closed wireguard-go device is a fatal engine error (L-LC-1). |
| connected | adapter `.reconnecting` (openvpn3 RECONNECTING) | reasserting(.engine) | |
| reasserting | adapter data plane up (and settings reapplied if changed) | connected | `setReasserting(false)`, reset the backoff, `attempt = 0`. |
| reasserting | attempt fails | reasserting(attempt+1) | Wait `backoff.next(using: &rng)` (§7.6); publish `attempt` and `nextRetryAt` in the snapshot. |
| reasserting | budget exhausted, **kill switch off** | stopped | The cancel row below with `.peerUnreachable`. |
| reasserting | budget exhausted, **kill switch on** | reasserting | Keep retrying at the cap. Traffic is blocked while NE says `.reasserting` with the engine down or not passing traffic (S2 E4; `reasserting` with a working engine still passes traffic through the tunnel, E4r). The UI shows "Blocked — reconnecting" (UI-CONCEPT §6.6). |
| any running | `sleep()` | sleeping | `setReasserting(true)` first (Apple's order: reasserting between quiesce and reactivate, forum 95988), `adapter.sleep()`, stop the watchdog, then call the completion within 2 s (a self-imposed budget; no OS limit is documented) (L-RC-5, ref/networkextension C20). *Draft 8 (tunnel review T10):* an after-Connected `awaitingAuth` stays `awaitingAuth` across sleep with its auth deadline; `wake()` doesn't arm the reassert budget while the prompt is showing. A pending start is not put to sleep (its deadlines are on the uptime clock, which pauses). |
| sleeping | `wake()` | reasserting(.wake) | `adapter.wake()`. Interfaces are often not up yet: the transport waits for Network.framework readiness (`.waiting → .ready`) instead of treating `ENETUNREACH` as a failure, and failures in the first 10 s after `wake()` consume no backoff budget. Must reach `connected` within 30 s or follow the normal backoff path. |
| connected/reasserting/sleeping (**after Connected**) | adapter `.fatal(e)`, **kill switch off**, not the C16 case below | stopped | **Cancel after the teardown (draft 9, S2 E3).** NE never calls `stopTunnel` after `cancelTunnelWithError` (0/40), so the controller first does what `stopTunnel` would: `adapter.stop()` (its descriptors close; 5 s cap), the session summary with the final statistics sample, the pump's end and the path watcher's end; **then** `cancelTunnelWithError(e)` (L-LC-1: at once after the teardown). |
| starting/connecting/awaitingAuth/establishing (**before Connected**) | a failure `e`, **without `includeAllNetworks`**, not the C16 case below | stopped | Fail the `startTunnel` completion with `e` (status `.connecting → .disconnected`; L-LC-1). Under on-demand rules a retryable kill-switch failure (route protection) arms a `.backoff` latch. |
| connected/reasserting/sleeping (**after Connected**) | adapter `.fatal(e)`, **kill switch on** | held(.blockedAfterFailure(e.code), beforeConnected: false) | **Decision (draft 4, Conflicts k; draft 9: the only path, Conflicts bi).** The controller tears down the adapter (for OpenVPN this closes only openvpn3's `dup` of the utun fd, never NE's own descriptor, §7.3), keeps the provider alive with `reasserting = true` and **no** further retries, and records `lastError = e`. NE status is `.reasserting`, never `.connected` (L-LC-1 still holds), so the UI is truthful and on-demand does not restart anything. It stays this way until the user disconnects (Disconnect = a user stop, which E2 shows restores connectivity) or reconnects; turning the kill switch off requires disconnecting first (L-KS-2). This mirrors the Go `fwBlocked` state. **S2 (E4):** blocked for 60 s (10/10 per OS) and 600 s (1/1); the system never stopped a held provider. **`cancelTunnelWithError` is never called with the kill switch on** (E3: it is open). `blockMode = .cancel` is gone. |
| starting/connecting/awaitingAuth/establishing (**before Connected**) | a failure `e`, **with `includeAllNetworks`** (a TLS or certificate failure, `serverIdentityMismatch`, `legacyCryptoUnavailable`, `dnsPlanMissing`, `.connectTimeout`, `.dnsResolutionFailed`, a prompt's deadline, the third AUTH_FAILED of §8.4, …) | held(reason, beforeConnected: true) | **Withhold (draft 9, D9-1; S2 E14, Conflicts bh).** The controller tears the adapter down (never `apply(nil)`, §7.1), records `lastError = e` in `state.plist`, arms the C16 latch as above, and **does not complete the start**: NE stays `.connecting`, which blocks (E14a); `reasserting` is not touched. `reason` is `.nonRetryable(e.code)` under the C16 condition with a non-retryable `e`, else `.blockedAfterFailure(e.code)`. A retryable `e` (and the pre-login secret-store lock) schedules a retry inside the hold with the backoff (1 s … 60 s); a non-retryable one, and `.dnsResolutionFailed` (no provider DNS under the flag, so a retry would find nothing new; D9-20), waits; draft 10: a recoverable hold takes IPs the app pushes (`pushEndpoints`, row below). Exits: the user's stop (completes the start with `e`), a retry that connects (completes with `nil`), new credentials (retry now), pushed endpoint IPs (retry now, draft 10), a changed or removed profile (completes with `e`; in any before-Connected phase, also while a retry attempt or `AUTH_PENDING` runs). No hold deadline: the OS has none (E14b) and the product sets none. A held start is never restarted by NE, so it can't storm. |
| connected/reasserting/sleeping (**after Connected**) | adapter `.fatal(e)` with a **non-retryable** `e` (`authFailed`, `authRequired`, `profileInvalid`, `profileNotProvisioned`, `secretStoreUnavailable`, `legacyCryptoUnavailable`, `serverIdentityMismatch`, `pushedOptionRejected`; draft 8, PF 6: also `webAuthUnsupported`, `profileRevisionStale`, `keyPassphraseRequired`, `dnsPlanMissing`, `authTimedOut`) **and** the session was started by on-demand or the profile has any on-demand rule | held(.nonRetryable(e.code), beforeConnected: false) | Whatever the kill switch: with an on-demand Connect rule active, the system **restarts a tunnel the provider cancelled** (forum 747838), so `cancelTunnelWithError(.authFailed)` would immediately resend stored credentials, which §7.6 forbids. The controller holds instead and pushes `tunnelEvent(sessionEnded)`; the app, on seeing it (or on `holdReason` in the snapshot at launch), sets `isOnDemandEnabled = false`, saves, then `stopVPNTunnel()`. With the kill switch off the hold is not blocking-relevant; the user sees the error (ref/networkextension C16). |
| starting/connecting/awaitingAuth/establishing (**before Connected**) | same non-retryable condition as the row above | stopped (without the flag) / held(.nonRetryable(e.code), beforeConnected: true) (with it) | Arm a **`.hard`** start latch and push `tunnelEvent(sessionEnded)`; the app, on the event or on `snapshot.startLatch` / `fetchLastDisconnectError` at launch, disables on-demand for the profile and saves (C16). If the app is not running, the latch keeps every system restart free of credential and network I/O until it does (S2 E14c: 1 server-side `DENY` per OS with the latch, 3 without on 27). With the flag the start stays held (no restart at all). |
| any | `stopTunnel(reason)` | stopping → stopped | `adapter.stop()` with a 5 s cap and the session summary, both in a controller-owned task that is not a child of a cancelled one (SC21), then the completion. *Draft 8 (tunnel review T4, T16):* every session end (stop, failed start, cancel) first takes a final, capped `adapter.statistics()` sample for the summary, and ends and resets the session's `PacketFlowPump`. The handler is idempotent. **S2 E3 (draft 9): NE does not call `stopTunnel` after our `cancelTunnelWithError`**, hence the cancel row's teardown-first order. **The provider never calls `exit()` or `stopTunnel` itself** (NR §4 pitfall 10). |

Rules:
- `startTunnel`'s completion is called **exactly once**. `CompletionOnce` asserts this in DEBUG and logs a fault in release.
- **"Connected" (L-LC-2):** the completion is called only after the data plane is up **and** `setTunnelNetworkSettings` has completed (Apple: settings must be applied and awaited before `completion(nil)`). `NEVPNStatus.connected` is therefore truthful.
- **Credential-resend guard (C16):** the extension refuses to send **stored** credentials for a profile within 60 s of an `AUTH_FAILED` for that profile (persisted in `state.plist`), so even an unexpected restart can't hammer the server. An answer is fresh user input and is not subject to the guard. *Draft 8 (tunnel review T14):* the guard withholds only the username and password; the key passphrase and proxy credentials are still provided.
- **Row precedence for a failure:** the C16 non-retryable rows win over the kill-switch rows, which win over the kill-switch-off rows. "Before/after Connected" is decided by whether the `startTunnel` completion has been called. A prompt of a manual start wins over all failure rows, except the third rejection within 10 min, which is `.fatal(.authFailed)`. "Kill switch" after Connected means `policy.killSwitch` (`includeAllNetworks` or split-tunnel route protection); the before-Connected withhold and the no-provider-DNS rule apply to `includeAllNetworks` only (`ProviderConfiguration.includeAllNetworks`).
- **No start budget (draft 9).** Draft 6's 50 s budget is gone with the start limit it assumed (S2 E14b). Deadlines: the connect deadline per attempt, the prompt deadlines, the 10 min auth deadline after Connected, the 5 s stop cap; all on the strict clock (§7.1 rule 4).
- **Start latch:** when the controller ends a start under the C16 conditions of the rows above, it records `{profileID, code, kind, notBefore, revision}` in `state.plist` and publishes it as `snapshot.startLatch`.
  - While a `.hard` latch exists, an on-demand start of that profile ends **immediately** with the latched code, before any credential load or network I/O (held with the flag, failed without), so a system restart loop costs a process wake, never a login attempt (C16, §7.6).
  - A `.backoff` latch does the same only until `notBefore`; the next on-demand start after it runs normally, and a failure doubles the interval (5 s, 10 s, … capped at 5 min). It bounds the pre-login `.secretStoreUnavailable` loop (§6.3) and retryable kill-switch failures under on-demand rules. Success clears it.
  - **Cleared by:** a manual start (`lp.manual = 1`; `scutil --nc start` has `options == nil` and does not clear it), a provision with a higher revision, `updateCredentials` for that profile, **`removeProfile`** (the latch is deleted with the profile's provision entry) and **`wipeAllSecrets`** (every latch deleted).
  - The app, on seeing a `.hard` `startLatch` (or the error via `fetchLastDisconnectError`), disables on-demand for that profile as in C16.
- **Start authorisation (2.0.2, D10.4-5; `Controller/StartAuthorisation.swift`, pure).** `TunnelController.start` decides **first**, synchronously on the actor: before the latch, the guard loop (so a refused start never triggers kill-switch priority), any suspension and any payload or credential read. Key = `(cfg.ownerUID, cfg.profileID)`.

  | # | Start | Decision |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | manual (`lp.manual = 1`) + `lp.startNonce` matching a live arm of the key | `.armed`: the arm is consumed; the authorisation `{nonce, at}` is recorded when the start is **admitted** |
  | 2 | manual + nonce equal to the key's persisted authorisation | `.replay` (NE restarting the session after a provider crash or a network return, S2 E1: it replays the original options) |
  | 3 | not manual (nil options or no `lp.manual`) + `providerConfiguration.onDemand == true` | `.unattended` (on-demand, the PF 52 crash restart `[:]`; also `scutil`/System Settings for such a profile, D-1); recorded with a nil nonce when admitted (D10.5-1) |
  | 3b | not manual, no on-demand rules now, and the key's persisted record is an **unattended** one | `.replay` (NE restarting an unattended session whose rules went away while it ran, Fable H1b); an armed record never admits this row |
  | 4 | anything else: manual without or with a wrong nonce, an expired arm, an arm under another uid, `scutil`/System Settings of a manual profile, a manual start with on-demand rules but no nonce, a 2.0.1 app | `.refused`: `LPTunnelError(.startNotAuthorised)` = 225, recorded in `lastErrors[key]` (disk write throttled to one a minute, like 222), no payload or credential read, no latch, no guard, no effect on any running session |

  - **Arms** (`StartArms`, memory only): 15 s TTL by the extension's wall clock (an arm from the future, i.e. a clock set back, is not live); one pending arm per profile (a second arm replaces the first); at most 8 per owner uid (the oldest dropped); consumed by the first start carrying its nonce. A wrong guess burns no arm. An extension restart between arm and start makes that start fail once.
  - **Admission, not decision (deviation from the plan):** the authorisation is written right before the session begins. An armed duplicate that the 2.0.1 guard refuses or holds therefore never overwrites the record NE's replay of the **running** session of that profile needs (`aWaitingArmedDuplicateDoesNotOverwriteTheRunningSessionsAuthorisation`).
  - **Persisted** in `state.plist` (`PersistedTunnelState.authorisedStarts`, `decodeIfPresent`: a 2.0.1 state file decodes to none; at most 256, the oldest without a kill switch dropped first, never the record just admitted or the running session's, D10.8-6; a failed write is a fault log; a file of another schema keeps its records, D10.8-6). **Tied to the session, not the revision (D10.5-1):** a provision never clears it. **Cleared** by `stop(.userInitiated)` and `stop(.configurationRemoved)` of the running session, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets` (the caller's uid), `revokeUnattended` (the unattended fact of records of profiles without a plan whose session has no kill switch, never the running session's or a guarded start's, D10.6-3), the next boot (D10.6-3; not when the boot value can't be read, D10.7-4) and the end of a session **without a kill switch** (start-time or live flags; NE never restarts those). **Kept** for a kill-switch session by `providerFailed`, `noNetwork`, `sleep`, `appUpdate`, `superseded`, `other` and a crash, so NE's own restarts keep working. Pending arms are dropped only by `removeProfile` and `wipeAllSecrets` (a late stop of the old session never burns the next start's arm). A user stop of a session that is already down (no provider: a `noNetwork` gap, a crash gap) gets no `stopTunnel` and ends nothing in the extension (draft 10.9, D10.9-1: the round 3 notice is removed; residual §20 risk 29 (1)). *(Draft 10.6 said such a record "matters only to a replay with the same nonce": wrong for an unattended record, which admits any non-manual start of the profile; Fable round 3 L1.)* A replay waiting in the guard whose record a live user act ended meanwhile (the user's stop of the running session, a removed configuration, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets`) is refused (225); a record is put back at admission only after a non-user removal (D10.7-3, round 3 N1).
  - A start whose `providerConfiguration` doesn't parse has no profile to authorise: it skips the table, reads nothing and ends `profileInvalid` (2.0.1 re-check N3 behaviour kept).
  - **App side:** every GUI start arms immediately before `managers.start` with a fresh nonce and puts it in the options; a failed arm fails the start. An **older extension** (2.0.1, still running until its replacement is approved) is recognised only when a non-definite, non-timeout arm failure is followed by a successful `hello` without `.startAuthorisation`; the app then starts without a nonce (that extension enforces nothing). The headless resume agent arms over a live `XPCTunnelService` (Mach name from the embedded extension, `EXT_REQ`) before it changes any setting (cap min(2 s, remaining); the arm's 15 s TTL outlives the agent's 5 s watchdog); on failure an on-demand profile (inferred from `pausedState.onDemandEnabledIDs`, because a manager snapshot doesn't expose `providerConfiguration.onDemand`) starts with `crashRestart` options, a definite refusal is a failed start, anything else is `.armUnavailable` (nothing changed, the agent stays registered, the next run retries). The PF 52 crash restart stays `[:]`.
  - Residuals: NE's replay must hand back the options dictionary with `lp.startNonce` intact (S2 E1 says it replays verbatim; if a macOS ever strips unknown keys, the replay of a kill-switch session without on-demand would be refused and the Mac left open: E2E-8 S6/S8 and the plan's stop condition). *(Draft 10.4 also listed "an edit of a connected kill-switch profile followed by an NE crash" with a "small window": wrong for Save Only, where the window lasted until the user disconnected; fixed by D10.5-1, no longer a residual.)* A lost record (disk full, a state file of another schema) still refuses NE's replay (fault-logged, §20 risk 29). While the old extension runs and its replacement awaits approval, kill-switch profiles aren't started without a nonce (D10.5-8).
- **Prompts and answers (draft 9, §8.4; replaces the draft 6 auth stash):** one live prompt per session (`AuthBroker.live`), in controller memory only; its answer is bound to the **next engine attempt of the same pending start** and consumed exactly once **at `provide_creds`** (`SecretBytes`, zeroed right after). `prepareStartAuth` answers (at most one per (owner, profile), 10 min) wait for the owner's next manual start, which takes them once; dropped by expiry, `cancelAuth`, a newer prepared prompt, a higher-revision provision, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets` and process exit. No start option names a prompt or carries an answer (S2 E1: NE replays options on its own restart).
- **The app has no other state source (L-LC-1, L-LC-4):** UI state comes from `NEVPNStatus`, plus `fetchLastDisconnectError` on `.disconnected`, plus `tunnelSnapshot` for detail, mapped by one derived-state table (§11.2, UI-CONCEPT §6.6). "Blocked" is derived from the snapshot's `holdReason` (adapter stopped) or the kill switch with `.connecting`/`.reasserting`, never from `.reasserting` alone (S2 E4r, RS2 8).

### 7.3 Data plane and fds

- **The utun fd is not API (ref/networkextension C18).** Quinn: the utun backing of `NEPacketTunnelFlow` "is an implementation detail … Apple platforms are moving towards a user-space networking architecture" (forum 733565). Both engines nevertheless use it, as WireGuardKit always has. Risk R13 (§20) tracks it; the fallback below is designed and selectable at runtime.
- **One selection rule for both engines (ref/wireguard D10, §3):** upstream WireGuardKit scans fds `0…1024` and returns the **first** socket whose control ID is `com.apple.net.utun_control`, which matches every utun control socket in the process, including a lingering openvpn3 dup. `ProviderHost.tunnelFileDescriptor(matching:)` therefore collects **all** matching fds; if more than one qualifies, it picks the one whose `UTUN_OPT_IFNAME` interface carries the IPv4 address just applied (`getifaddrs`) and asserts uniqueness. The chosen fd is passed explicitly (draft 8: to `wgTurnOn` by the extension's `WireGuardGoBackend`, which replaces patch W3's `adapter.start(uapi:tunFD:)`; §9.2); nothing scans again. Draft 8 (tunnel review T17): the rule also matches an IPv6-only plan (by the applied IPv6 address). **S7 confirmed the rule is necessary (draft 7.3).** NE gives every session a new utun (utun11, utun12 and utun13 were seen). A dup lingering from an earlier session kept its dead interface alive and was a real candidate (`7:utun11, 8:utun12, 10:utun12`). The `getifaddrs` match picked `utun12` for WG and for the following OVPN session, while upstream's "first match" would have taken fd 7.
- **WireGuard:** settings are applied first, then the fd is handed to `wgTurnOn`, which `dup()`s it, sets the dup non-blocking and wraps it; `wgTurnOff` closes only the dup and its route socket (ref/wireguard §3).
- **OpenVPN:** **Decision:** openvpn3's `tun_builder_establish()` returns **`dup()` of the NE utun fd**, after the controller has applied the settings. openvpn3's `TunBuilderClient` (`openvpn/tun/builder/client.hpp`; the `tun/mac` client is not compiled, §8.1) then reads and writes utun frames on that descriptor.
  - **Why `dup` (N2):** `TunBuilderClient` stores the returned fd in a `TunPersist` = `TunPersistTemplate<ScopedFD>`. On macOS `retain_sd` is false, so the wrapper is `NO_RETAIN` and its `close()` **closes the fd** whenever the tun client stops; the `Tun` stream itself `release()`s, so there is exactly one close per dup (ref/openvpn3 §4.1). Returning NE's own fd would let openvpn3 close the provider's utun descriptor on the first reconnect, AUTH_FAILED or stop.
  - **Threading (ref/openvpn3 §9.1, ref/swift-concurrency §8.2–§8.3, SC7):** `connect()` blocks until disconnect and runs every callback (`event`, `log`, `socket_protect`, every `tun_builder_*`) on its own thread. Each session gets a **dedicated `Thread`** (`lockplus.openvpn3.connect`, QoS `.userInitiated`, large stack), bridged with one `withCheckedContinuation`; `Task.detached` and the cooperative pool are forbidden for it. `tun_builder_establish()` must return synchronously, so it posts `AdapterEvent.networkSettings(plan, ticket)` and waits on an `EstablishTicket` (a `Mutex` + `DispatchSemaphore`, SAFETY) **only on that thread**, with a 10 s deadline inside the connect deadline. The controller applies the settings and calls `ticket.answer(fd)`; every stop or teardown path answers `-1` **before** `client.stop()`, otherwise `stop()` posts to an io_context whose thread is blocked in `establish`. The semaphore wait is the one legitimate blocking wait in the extension.
  - **One client per attempt:** `OpenVPNClient` is single-use (`ClientState::attach()` throws on a second `connect()`), so every attempt (initial, after `DYNAMIC_CHALLENGE`, `NEED_CREDS` or `AUTH_FAILED`) uses a new instance with a new `eval_config` and `provide_creds` (ref/openvpn3 §1 item 1). The thread is joined before the instance is destroyed.
  - **Reconnects:** with `tunPersist = false`, every engine-internal reconnect closes the descriptor and calls `tun_builder_new()` … `tun_builder_establish()` again. Each call returns a fresh `dup()` (S11: the previous dup is already closed when the next `establish` runs, so the process never holds more than NE's fd plus one dup). **The controller re-applies settings only when the plan changed (MUST):** S11 measured 27 ms median per reconnect with the diff against 70 ms when every reconnect re-applied.
  - **Decision (S11, draft 7.3): `tunPersist = false`, final.** With `tunPersist = true`, openvpn3 keeps the descriptor (`tun_builder_establish_lite()`) only when the pushed tun properties are identical. A server with `duplicate-cn`, common in the wild, assigns a new address on every reconnect, so it never triggers there. Where it does trigger, it gains ~5 ms over the plan diff (22 vs 27 ms median), which is noise for `reasserting`.
  - **AF header:** `cliopt.hpp` sets `tun_prefix = true` on macOS in the tun-builder path, so the builder client handles the 4-byte utun AF header. S11 confirmed it on the wire (IPv4 ping and TCP bulk in both directions, no shim-side framing).
  - **`holdBlocked` (§7.2):** tearing down the adapter closes only openvpn3's dup. NE's utun fd and the provider's `reasserting` state (or, before Connected, the pending start) stay intact, so the blocked session persists.
  - **Assumption A-OVPN-FD: confirmed on 27 (S11, draft 7.3).** openvpn3 closes exactly the dup it got (one close per dup) and never NE's fd. NE's fd stayed open on the same interface across 20 reconnects, an AUTH_FAILED inside a held session, a held teardown and the recovery, with `tunPersist` on and off and on servers with changing and stable addresses. The fd count stayed flat (13 while up, 8 after a held teardown, 7 = the process baseline after `down`), and NE closes its own fd when the session ends.
- **Fallback for both engines: a `packetFlow` pump (`dataPlane = .packetFlow`).** `readPacketObjects`/`writePacketObjects` feed the far end of a `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_DGRAM)` whose near end the engine gets as its tun device, adding or stripping the utun AF header. For OpenVPN the near end is what `establish` returns. For WireGuard it is what `wgTurnOnPF` wraps (fork patch W10, §9.2). **Draft 8 (PF 33):** `TunnelController`'s `dataPlane` is fixed at `.utunFD` in the product; `.packetFlow` is the R13 fallback, built and tested in code, selected only by a code change. There is no user or configuration switch. A utun selection failure fails the start with `.tunDeviceFailed`; it does not fall back at runtime. The leak harness's `.packetFlow` pass therefore needs a FaultInjection-only switch, which isn't built yet (§15.3, §18). S11 ran both engines in this mode (OVPN 20/20 reconnects in every server × `tunPersist` combination plus recovery; WG 3/3 sessions). Pump rules (MUST, S11, draft 7.3):
  - **One `PacketFlowPump` per NE session.** It is created on first use in a session and shared by every adapter start in that session (reconnect, held → restart, a new client per attempt). Engines **attach** and **detach** their socketpair; the pump keeps reading the flow and drops packets while nothing is attached. Reason: NE serves only one outstanding `readPackets`. A second pump's read starved the first, and the stopped pump's callback never re-armed, so `packetFlow` stopped delivering after an in-session adapter restart (S11 v3, recovery ping 0/3). The pump ends with the NE session. *Draft 8 (tunnel review T16):* it is ended and reset on **every** session end, including a failed start; before, only `stop()` ended it, and the next start reused a pump still reading the old flow.
  - **Engine fds are read with `DispatchSource` read sources (draft 8, Conflicts at; PF 43; replaces draft 7.3's "readers poll").** S11 found that a reader thread blocked in `recv` on an AF_UNIX datagram socket is **not** woken by `shutdown()` on macOS (v3 leaked one fd and one thread per reconnect, 1 → 23 AF_UNIX fds over 20 reconnects); the spike therefore polled every 200 ms. As built, each attached fd gets one `DispatchSource.makeReadSource` (kqueue) on the pump's serial queue; an event drains up to a batch of datagrams without blocking and hands them to the flow. Retiring an fd cancels its source at once: nothing ever blocks in `recv`, and there is no thread per attach. EOF or a hard error cancels the source. An `attach` after `endSession` closes the fd and creates no source (Fable verification NEW-3).
  - **Fds are closed only under the send lock.** Detach retires the fd in the same `Mutex` that guards the sends, so a send can never hit a closed (or reused) descriptor number. *Draft 8:* the close happens in the read source's cancel handler, under that lock.
  - **Empty packets are dropped** (draft 8, Fable review L3): an empty datagram would index past the 4-byte AF header and trap the root extension.
  - **Socket buffers ≥ 1 MB** (`SO_SNDBUF`/`SO_RCVBUF` on both ends): the AF_UNIX datagram default of 2 KiB is smaller than one packet.
  - **Cost (draft 9: measured relay-free on the 26/27 VMs, D9-14).** WireGuard in `packetFlow` loses **22 % (26) / 27 % (27) of its upload** (386–399 vs 492–523 Mbit/s on 26; 468–486 vs 612–652 on 27), download ±0–10 %, at 10–20 % more extension CPU. OpenVPN's throughput is unchanged (it isn't CPU-bound at ~80 %), but its extension CPU rises **85–95 %** (153–168 % vs 80–87 % of a core). The 10–15 % assumed in earlier drafts holds for neither (through the relay in draft 7.3 only the CPU difference showed: ~60 %). `packetFlow` stays the R13 fallback only (§20 risk 13).

### 7.4 Path monitoring and sleep/wake (L-RC-1, L-RC-5)

- `PathWatcher` is **one** `NWPathMonitor()` (no interface restriction; `Sendable`, `@Sendable` handler) feeding an `AsyncStream(bufferingPolicy: .bufferingNewest(1))` whose `onTermination` cancels the monitor. `NEProvider.defaultPath` is deprecated in macOS 15 and not visible in Swift 6 (only `__defaultPath`), so draft 3's KVO half is dropped (ref/networkextension C3, SC19).
  - It debounces for 500 ms on the injected clock and emits `.changed(PathSnapshot)` only when `(status, interface names+types, gateways, isExpensive)` actually changed.
  - **It ignores the provider's own utun (S2 E12, draft 9, D9-11).** Inside the provider, while connected, the unrestricted monitor reported `satisfied`, wired, the physical gateway, `supportsIPv6 = false` and **`availableInterfaces = [en0, en0, utunN]`**: our own tunnel interface is listed, and en0 twice. `PathSnapshot.interfaces` is therefore built from the physical interfaces only: names starting with `utun`, `ipsec`, `tun`, `tap`, `gif` or `stf` are dropped (ours and any other VPN's; `ppp` stays, PPPoE is a real path) and duplicates are collapsed, so our own utun appearing, disappearing or being listed twice is never a path change. Status, gateways and `usesInterfaceType` already describe the physical path.
  - It is the **only** network-change source for both engines: the upstream Swift `WireGuardAdapter` and its monitor aren't linked (draft 8: W13; drafts 4–7.3 removed the monitor with W2), and openvpn3 has no lifecycle monitor in TunBuilder mode (`MacLifeCycle` exists only in the excluded tun/mac path; ref/openvpn3 item 25).
- WireGuard: on `.changed`, the controller calls `adapter.bumpSockets()` (`wgBumpSockets`: recreates the UDP sockets on the same port and sends a keepalive only if the current keypair is younger than 180 s), then forces a handshake (§9.3) and waits up to 15 s. Endpoint IPs are rotated from the list cached at connect, not re-resolved; upstream re-resolves only on iOS (ref/wireguard D4).
- OpenVPN: `client.reconnect(0)`, which gives a new transport socket on the new interface.
- Sleep (`disconnectOnSleep = false`):
  - `sleep(completionHandler:)`: `reasserting = true` first; **no `setTunnelNetworkSettings(nil)`** on kill-switch profiles (C20; the §7.1 `apply(nil)` rule); WG stops the watchdog only; OVPN calls `client.pause("sleep")`, which sends exit-notify and tears down the session and tun (closing our dup).
  - **WireGuard timers survive sleep only because of the Go runtime patch** (`goruntime-boottime-over-monotonic.diff` makes `nanotime` count sleep, so an expired keypair is known to be expired after wake). `libwg-go.a` is built from the patched GOROOT, which CI checks (§9.2; ref/wireguard D13).
  - The completion is called within 2 s (self-imposed).
- Wake:
  - The transport waits for readiness (`.waiting → .ready`) instead of failing on `ENETUNREACH`; no backoff budget is consumed in the first 10 s.
  - WG: `wgBumpSockets` + **forced handshake (mandatory)**: after more than 180 s asleep a bump sends nothing (`SendKeepalivesToPeersWithCurrentKeypair` skips keypairs older than `RejectAfterTime`).
  - OVPN: `client.resume()` (a new session), then `client.reconnect(0)` if not CONNECTED within 5 s.
  - Failure after the backoff budget → `cancelTunnelWithError` (kill switch off) or keep blocking (kill switch on).

### 7.5 Handshake watchdog (L-RC-2)

The watchdog ticks every 10 s while `connected` (on the injected `SuspendingClock`).
- **WireGuard:**
  - `age = now − lastHandshake` from `wgGetStats` (`last_handshake_time_sec/nsec`, wall clock; negative values clamped to 0).
  - When `age > 180 s` (RejectAfterTime) **and** tx bytes grew since the last tick, the adapter is `.stale`. `tx_bytes` includes handshake initiations and keepalives, so "tx grew" does not prove user traffic; the age condition carries the weight. It forces a handshake and gives it 3 × 5.5 s.
  - Still stale → reasserting(.deadPeer). It rotates to the next **cached** endpoint IP and never re-resolves (S2 E10, draft 9: a provider `getaddrinfo` under `includeAllNetworks` blocked 30 s and failed, also while held; A-WG-DNS confirmed; ref/wireguard D6).
  - The controller also polls `wgIsClosed` at 1 Hz (W6): a self-closed wireguard-go device (it calls `device.Close()` itself after a TUN read error, with no notification) is `.fatal(.engineDied)` (L-LC-1).
- **OpenVPN:**
  - openvpn3 keepalive/`ping-restart` handles dead peers internally and reports `RECONNECTING`. Without any liveness directive, openvpn3 defaults to keepalive 8 s / 40 s (`proto.hpp:505-510`), so our floor is optional (ref/openvpn3 item 20).
  - Floor (kept for parity with the Go `args()` floors): only if the profile has none of `ping`/`ping-restart`/`keepalive`, normalization appends `ping 10` + `ping-restart 60`. `ping`/`ping-restart` are honoured only **without** `keepalive`; with `keepalive` present they are untouched push-only options and therefore fatal, so the normalizer drops them in that case (§8.2).
  - The watchdog additionally checks that `transport_stats().lastPacketReceived` is younger than 120 s.

### 7.6 Backoff and timeouts (L-RC-3)

```swift
struct Backoff: Sendable { // full jitter, capped
    var base: Duration = .seconds(1), cap: Duration = .seconds(60), factor = 2.0, attempt = 0
    mutating func next(using rng: inout some RandomNumberGenerator) -> Duration // random(0.8…1.2) * min(cap, base * factor^attempt)
    mutating func reset()
}
```

- Every retry loop in the codebase uses `Backoff`; a lint rule flags `while` + `sleep` without it. Tests pass a seeded generator.
- **Draft 8 (tunnel review T1):** `next` computes in Double seconds and caps the exponent (≤ 32) **before** multiplying. The first build multiplied a `Duration` by `2^attempt`, which overflowed `_Int128` after ~69 attempts and crashed the extension after about 80 minutes of a kill-switch outage. A 200-attempt test guards it.
- The kill-switch-off budget is 5 min of reasserting; with the kill switch on it is unbounded at the cap.
- AUTH_FAILED is **never** retried automatically with the same stored credentials. It always produces a prompt (account-lockout protection), plus the 60 s resend guard (§7.2).
- openvpn3 `connTimeout = 0`; we enforce our own deadline: before Connected the connect deadline per attempt (WG 45 s, OVPN 50 s; draft 9: no start budget; it stops while a prompt waits), after Connected the reconnect budget, which pauses during auth.
- **Strict timers (draft 9, S2, D9-5):** every deadline here runs on the controller's clock, `StrictSuspendingClock` in production (`.strict`, zero leeway; §7.1 rule 4). Before Connected with `includeAllNetworks`, a retryable failure retries inside the held start with this `Backoff` (§7.2).
- The `.backoff` start latch (§7.2) uses a separate fixed schedule (5 s doubling to 5 min, no jitter needed: one restart source) persisted in `state.plist`, because the process may exit between restarts.
- **Server-requested delays are applied inside openvpn3** (`AUTH_FAILED,TEMP[backoff N]`, `RESTART` 5 s, transport/tun errors 5 s). The `RECONNECTING` event carries **no** delay (draft 3 was wrong; ref/openvpn3 item 21). Our own backoff applies only to engine-level failures that end `connect()`. The c15d1ba lesson is honoured because openvpn3 never skips its own pause.

### 7.7 Statistics and sessions

- `statistics()` costs:
  - WG: one `wgGetStats` call (patch W5: per peer `endpoint`, `last_handshake_time_sec/nsec`, `rx_bytes`, `tx_bytes`; **no keys**), on the adapter's `workQueue`, summed over peers. `getRuntimeConfiguration`/`wgGetConfig` (whose text contains `private_key` and `preshared_key` in hex) **no longer exists** (draft 8: W11 removed the export; invariant 10; ref/wireguard D8).
  - OVPN: `transport_stats()` (`bytesIn`/`bytesOut`); `connection_info()` and `session_token()` are read **inside the `CONNECTED` event callback** on the connect thread and cached by the shim (their cross-thread use is gated in openvpn3). **Draft 8 (PF 30):** openvpn3's `ConnectionInfo` has no cipher field, so `AdapterStats.cipher` comes from the negotiated-cipher log line, or is nil, and the detail panel hides the row (UI-CONCEPT §6.4).
- The app polls at 1 Hz while a consumer is visible (the menu is open, the menu-bar rate label is on, the hero or Activity is on screen) and at 0.2 Hz otherwise; with no consumer and no active tunnel it stops (§11.2). The extension caches stats for 250 ms.
- Sessions: the controller mints a session UUID at `connected`. At `stopped` it appends `SessionSummary(id, profileID, start, end, rx, tx, endReason)` to a 100-entry ring in `state.plist` (draft 8: per owner uid; rx/tx from a final capped statistics sample on every end path, tunnel review T4).
- The app pulls `sessionSummaries(after:)` on launch and on every `.disconnected`, and merges into `history.json` keyed by session UUID (idempotent: a summary already present is skipped; §15.1 tests the merge). History is correct even for on-demand sessions that run while the app is closed.

---

## 8. OpenVPN specifics

### 8.1 Import pipeline (L-OVPN-1)

```
untrusted bytes
  → [1] size cap (1 MiB), NUL check, UTF-8 not required (bytes)
  → [2] OVPNTokenizer  (Swift line-for-line port of internal/ovpn/parse.go: parseLine, fgets/buf_parse,
                       readInline prefix-close semantics, <connection> re-parse, BOM, OPTION_LINE_SIZE=256,
                       OPTION_PARM_SIZE=256, MAX_PARMS=16, bypass_doubledash)
  → [3] Allowlist      (port of internal/ovpn/allowlist.go + inspectProfile: rules, inline modes,
                       setenv/setenv opt recursion, ports, providers, dev/dev-type, http/socks proxy)
  → [4] EngineSupport  classify each accepted directive: .mapped | .ignored(reason) | .unsupported(reason)
                       (table GENERATED from openvpn3's lists, see §8.2)
  → [5] Normalizer     emit CANONICAL text: one directive per line, every argument double-quoted with
                       only \\ and \" escapes, inline blocks as "<name>\n…\n</name>" with body lines
                       validated (no line starting with "</"), comments dropped, ignored directives dropped,
                       floors appended (ping/ping-restart only without keepalive, mssfix 1300 only if
                       no MTU directive), `remote-cert-eku "TLS Web Server Authentication"` appended when
                       `remote-cert-tls server` is present without `remote-cert-eku` (§1.3 A4),
                       `dev`/`dev-type` rewritten to `tun`, `<connection>` blocks may hold only
                       remote/port/proto (anything else ⇒ reject "not supported inside <connection>"),
                       inline <auth-user-pass> EXTRACTED to CredentialRecord and removed.
                       Draft 7 (S13/S8): a repeated singleton directive (cipher, auth, tls-version-min,
                       remote-cert-tls, reneg-sec, tun-mtu, …) is deduped keeping the LAST, like
                       openvpn 2.x and openvpn3, with an import note (otherwise [7b] rejects
                       "specified multiple times"). Draft 8 (PF 12): the REPEATABLE directives are an
                       explicit list (remote, route, route-ipv6, dns, dhcp-option, setenv, pull-filter,
                       …); every other mapped directive keeps its last occurrence; `http-proxy` without a TCP remote ⇒
                       reject (openvpn3 fails it); `cipher none` and every 64-bit-block cipher ⇒
                       reject (§8.6); `auth-nocache` appended for OTP-class profiles (§8.4).
                       Caps on the OUTPUT, using openvpn3's own accounting: raw bytes (comments
                       included) + 64 per directive + 16 per argument < 262144 (MAX_PROFILE_SIZE;
                       draft 8, PF 11: the directive name also counts as a 16-byte term, which is
                       conservative and kept); canonical DIRECTIVE lines ≤ 254 bytes (draft 8, PF 10,
                       Conflicts bb: canonical text must survive the extension's re-run of [1]-[6] with
                       the 256-byte OPTION_LINE_SIZE) and inline-block body lines ≤ 512 bytes
                       (MAX_LINE_SIZE); directive names ≤ 64 chars; each <connection> block ≤ 4096
                       bytes; over ⇒ reject with the limit named
  → [6] Differential   OpenVPN3Options.parse(canonical) → [[String]] must equal our directive stream
                       exactly (names, args, inline bodies); mismatch ⇒ reject "parser disagreement"
                       (2.0.2: ShimOptionsParser in LPEngineCheck; validator service at import,
                       extension at start)
  → [7] openvpn3 check (2.0.2: validator service, evaluateProfile XPC; was: extension, validateProfile):
                       (a) ClientAPI eval_config(canonical) → EvalConfig: error/message,
                           staticChallenge(+echo), autologin, privateKeyPasswordRequired,
                           remoteHost/Port/Proto, serverList;
                       (b) construct ClientOptions(options, cc) with a no-op TunBuilder stub, no
                           transport start, Config.disableClientCert mirrored from the profile
                           (cert+key absent ⇒ true), and a capturing Log::Context; its constructor runs
                           handle_unused_options and throws UNUSED_OPTIONS for unknown, removed,
                           server-only, push-only, standalone, not-implemented-fatal and management*
                           directives. ANY exception ⇒ reject (several option_errors from
                           check_for_incompatible_options carry no ExceptionCode; S13), with openvpn3's
                           category text mapped to our "Not supported" group (§8.3). ALSO reject when the
                           captured log contains the non-fatal categories "Unused ignored meta options"
                           (unknown inline blocks such as <pkcs12>) or "Unused options, probably
                           specified multiple times". OPENSSL_init_crypto(OPENSSL_INIT_NO_LOAD_CONFIG)
                           runs before any openvpn3 call (no-autoload-config, §2.2, is the second layer)
  → ImportReport + Profile + canonical payload
```

- ~~Steps [1]–[6] run in the app at import. Step [7] runs at import too, through the `validateProfile` XPC~~ **2.0.2 (D10.4-1), where each step runs:**

  | Step | 2.0.1 | 2.0.2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | [1]–[5] (memory-safe Swift, with caps) | app at import and in the editor; extension at provision, `validateProfile` and start | app at import and in the editor (unchanged; per keystroke); validator service inside its evaluation; extension at provision and start |
  | [6] differential (openvpn3 C++ `OptionList`) | extension (`validateProfile`, provision, start); the app linked `OpenVPN3Options` but never called it | validator service; extension **only at start**, on the session's own payload bytes |
  | [7] `eval_config` + `ClientOptions` (openvpn3 + OpenSSL PEM/ASN.1) | extension (`validateProfile`, provision, start) | validator service only; in the extension only inside the session's own connect (`LPOpenVPN3Session`), as before |
  | canonical fixed point (Swift) | — | extension at provision and start (replaces [6]/[7] at provision) |
  | zip read (`ZipStructure` + ZIPFoundation) | app (unsandboxed, holds the sealing key) | validator service (`readArchive`): archive ≤ 100 MiB, entries ≤ 1 MiB each, reply ≤ 64 MiB of entries (§3.5) |

  The app sends the canonical text to the service (`evaluateProfile`), so `UNUSED_OPTIONS` still surfaces **before** the profile is saved, not at `connect()`, from import, the editor, the Go migrator and the launch re-verify (`ServiceProfileValidator`, one injected validator). **"Not yet verified"** now means the service gave no answer (unavailable, invalidated, a version mismatch): the profile is saved, Connect is disabled until [7] passes, and the re-verify (`ProfilesStore.verifyPending`, at launch after load and after each `hello`) retries through the service, independent of the tunnel component (profiles imported during onboarding, before approval, are checked at once; a 2.0.1 "Not yet verified" profile is checked on the first launch). The explanation reads "LockPlus hasn't checked this profile with its OpenVPN engine yet. It tries again automatically; until then the profile can't connect." **`checkCrashed`:** a file the service died on twice (`.profileCheckCrashed`, `ValidatorClient` retries once on a fresh process) or that ran past the 8 s `evaluateProfile` timeout (below the service's 10 s watchdog, so a hanging file surfaces as `.timeout`) is **refused**, not "Not yet verified": report reason `.checkCrashed` in the Not-supported group, "LockPlus couldn't check this file safely.", and the re-verify never feeds it to the service again. Residual: a slow first launch of the service could turn a legitimate profile into `checkCrashed` (E2E-8 V1/V2 measure the first-use latency).
- **The extension (2.0.2):** `PayloadValidator` has two methods. `validateForProvision`: OpenVPN `OVPNImporter.importProfile(payload)` with no [6] parser, any Not-supported item rejects (`OpenVPNEngineCheck.firstBlocking`), no inline credentials, and `OVPNImporter.isCanonicalFixedPoint(payload)` (the tokenizer streams of the payload and of `importProfile(payload).canonicalText` are equal and the normaliser appended nothing; stream equality, not byte equality, so harmless whitespace or quoting differences in 2.0.1-stored payloads pass; directive order isn't normalised, as in the normaliser); WireGuard `WGImporter`. `validateForStart`: the same + the [6] differential of the payload bytes. There is no `evaluate` and no `evaluateBytes` in `Tunnel/`. The fixed point is what lets [6]/[7] stay out of provisioning: the app compared that exact stream with openvpn3 at import, and the session's own connect runs [7] anyway. A compromised **signed** app could provision a payload [7] would refuse; it then fails at connect inside the session, which parses only Swift-validated canonical text that two parsers agreed on at start. `CanonicalFixedPointTests` cover every corpus canonical text and the migration fixture; E2E-8 V5 covers a real 2.0.1 store (stop condition: never ship a check that refuses stored 2.0.1 payloads). *Draft 8:* the app chooses WireGuard or OpenVPN by sniffing the content, not by the file extension (app-root review M11).
- **Deliberate behaviour changes from the Go app (draft 8, PF 14),** stated in the import and migration reports: inline lines over 512 bytes are rejected; unknown ciphers (for example CAMELLIA) are rejected; `auth none` is accepted. `<connection>` child arguments get the same control-character check as top-level arguments (Sonnet core review 13).
- *Why [7b] is needed:* `eval_config` (`OpenVPNClientHelper::parse_config`) does **not** call `handle_unused_options`. Only the `ClientOptions` constructor does, and that constructor normally runs inside `connect()`. **S13 confirmed it is side-effect free** (draft 7): all 484 generator and corpus cases ran under a deny-default `sandbox-exec` profile (network, DNS, file writes and file reads outside the loader's set → SIGKILL) with byte-identical results, 0 TunBuilder calls, 0 `socket_protect`, 0 events. The one I/O found was OpenSSL's config auto-load (`openssl.cnf`), removed by `OPENSSL_INIT_NO_LOAD_CONFIG`/`no-autoload-config`; it also affected every connect. No vendored `handle_unused_options` is needed. S14 showed the [7b] construction (`ParseClientConfig::parse` → `ClientOptions::Config` with an event-queue stub → `new ClientOptions`) works without `connect()` and is thread-safe under 4 × 50 concurrent evaluations.
- *[7b] is a backstop, not a filter (S13):* raw into [7b], openvpn3 rejected only 51 of the 108 Go reject fixtures. It accepts scripts (`up`, `tls-verify`, `plugin`: "no script/plugin support" warnings), file-path forms (it never opens files; `ca /etc/x` is taken as PEM text), `setenv PATH/DYLD…`, `lport`/`local` and parser-level tricks, and it silently ignores unknown options inside `<connection>`. The allowlist stays the gate.
- *Why the log capture:* inline blocks are **meta** options in openvpn3, and an untouched meta option is only a warning, so `<pkcs12>` would pass a throw-only check and then fail at connect via the external-PKI path (ref/openvpn3 §1 item 10, item 13). The external-PKI check itself runs in `connect_setup`, **before** `ClientOptions`, which is why [7b] mirrors `disableClientCert`.
- ~~The extension repeats [1]–[7] in `provisionProfile` **and** [1]–[6] again before every `startTunnel`.~~ *2.0.2:* the extension runs [1]–[5] + the fixed point in `provisionProfile` and + [6] before every `startTunnel` (above); [7] only inside the session's connect.
- The engine only ever sees canonical text that two independent parsers agree on, and that the engine's own option consumer accepted, so a tokenizer divergence cannot become a bypass.
- **Build rules for openvpn3 (MUST; recipe in ref/openvpn3 §9.2):**
  - **pin `release/3.11.8`** or a later release tag, **never master** (O2): master as of 2026-10-17 lacks the `remote-cert-tls` fix (`32f53472`), which exists only on the release branch. The dependency watch diffs the release branch.
  - **OpenSSL 3.5 LTS**, static, `no-shared no-module no-autoload-config` (the legacy provider is built in but never enabled: `enableLegacyAlgorithms` is never set, §8.6). 3.11.8 does not compile against OpenSSL 4.0 (support is master-only, `28469efe`); move to 4.x only when a release tag supports it (§8.6 rationale).
  - dependencies for the 3.11.8 pin: asio **1.24.0** with the **7 patches** in `deps/asio/patches/`, lz4 (static, `-DHAVE_LZ4`), OpenSSL. Not needed: fmt (master only), xxHash, jsoncpp, LZO. A move to master later would need asio 1.38.2 + 6 patches and fmt.
  - compile units: `client/ovpncli.cpp` (one TU includes the whole core, after the shim's `OPENVPN_LOG` setup) + `openvpn/crypto/data_epoch.cpp` + an lz4 unity file + the ObjC++ wrapper (§2.2); C++20, exceptions and RTTI on. The core TU proves its own flags at compile time: `static_assert(__cplusplus >= 202002L)`, `#error` unless `USE_TUN_BUILDER`, `USE_OPENSSL`, `ASIO_STANDALONE`, `__cpp_exceptions` and `__cpp_rtti` are set, and `#error` if any banned define (below) is set, because `swift build -v` no longer prints the clang lines to grep (S14);
  - defines: `-DUSE_ASIO -DASIO_STANDALONE -DHAVE_LZ4 -DUSE_OPENSSL -DUSE_TUN_BUILDER -DOPENVPN_CORE_API_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN`. `USE_TUN_BUILDER` is **not** automatic on macOS (`ovpncli.cpp` defines it only for Android/iOS); without it `cliopt.hpp` selects `openvpn/tun/mac/client/tuncli.hpp`, whose `tunsetup.hpp` shells out to `/sbin/route` and `ifconfig`;
  - exclude `openvpn/tun/mac/**` from the target sources; CI greps the extension's symbols for `MacTun`/`TunMac`/`MacLifeCycle` and for `_system/_popen/_exec*/_posix_spawn*/_fork/_vfork`, and its strings for `/sbin/route`/`ifconfig`, and fails if any is found (verified by S14: 0 `TunMac|MacTun|MacLifeCycle` symbols, 89 `TunBuilderClient` symbols, no undefined `system/popen/execv*/posix_spawn*/fork`, no `/sbin/route|ifconfig` strings). **Draft 8 (Conflicts be; PF 29): `_execve` is the one exception**, and only when `check-symbols.sh` (`nm -A -u` over every arm64 object) attributes it solely to `libwg-go.a` members: it comes from Go's `runtime`/`syscall` inside `libwg-go` and was there before our patches. In the linked extension, which can't be attributed per object, any forbidden import other than `_execve` fails, and `_execve` fails unless a `libwg-go.a` object accounts for it. The sysex sandbox denies process-exec; a FaultInjection test that proves an exec attempt fails is still to be added (§15.2);
  - **banned defines** (CI greps the compile flags): `OPENVPN_COMMAND_AGENT`, `OPENVPN_EXTERNAL_TUN_FACTORY`, `OPENVPN_FORCE_TUN_NULL`, `OPENVPN_DEBUG_VERBOSE_ERRORS`, `OPENVPN_SHOW_SESSION_TOKEN`, `OPENVPN_PACKET_LOG`, `OPENVPN_DEBUG_CLIPROTO`; no script support, no file access (`merge_config(path)` is never called, only `merge_config_string`). The sandbox would deny exec and file access anyway; the build rules make it impossible rather than merely denied.
  - Xcode 27 changes some libc++ behaviour (`multimap::find` order, `std::map` bounds with non-strict-weak comparators, `bitset::operator[]`); openvpn3's unit tests and S13 run on the pinned Xcode.

### 8.2 Directive mapping

The Go allowlist was written for openvpn **2.7**; openvpn3 supports a subset. Draft 1 asserted openvpn3's handling per directive. Draft 2 **derives** it, because openvpn3 rejects at `connect()` (via `handle_unused_options`, `cliopt.hpp` ≈ 945) every directive that its option consumers did not `touch()`, unless the directive is on a non-fatal list.

**How `EngineSupport` is generated (run on every openvpn3 bump; draft 8: as built below the steps):**
1. Extract openvpn3's lists from the pinned `openvpn/client/cliopt.hpp`. Each list maps to a class:
   - `settings_ignoreWithWarning`, `settings_feature_not_implemented_warn` and `settings_script_plugin_feature` are non-fatal ("Unsupported option (ignored)" etc.) → **ignored(warn)**, dropped from canonical text;
   - `settings_ignoreSilently` → **ignored(silent)**, dropped;
   - `settings_removedOptions`, `settings_serverOnlyOptions`, `settings_standalone_options`, `settings_feature_not_implemented_fatal`, `settings_pushonlyoptions` and any `management*` directive are fatal if untouched → **unsupported** unless step 2 proves the profile parser touches them;
   - a directive on no list is fatal if untouched (`UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED OPTIONS`) → **unsupported** unless step 2 proves otherwise.
2. **Empirical touch test:** for every directive on the Go allowlist, the generator builds a minimal valid client profile plus that directive (with representative arguments from the shared fixtures) and runs [7b] (`ClientOptions` construction) in a host-side test binary.
   - Accepted with no warning → **mapped**.
   - Accepted with a warning → **ignored(warn)**.
   - `UNUSED_OPTIONS` → **unsupported**, or, if the directive is harmless and droppable, **ignored(warn)** by a reviewed override list in `EngineSupportOverrides.swift`, which records the reason.
3. Emit `LPParsing/OVPNEngineSupport.generated.swift`. It is committed, and the openvpn3 tag is recorded in its header.

**As built (draft 8):** the generator is `Tests/LPParsingTests/EngineSupportGenerator.swift` in LockPlusCore, run with `LP_REGEN_ENGINE_SUPPORT=1 swift test --filter EngineSupportTests`. Its input is the S13 spike's classification CSV (`native/spike/s13-s8/results/engine-support.csv`, from the empirical [7b] run against `release/3.11.8`) plus reviewed additions; the table header records openvpn3 `release/3.11.8` (4f3bdef7) and OpenSSL 3.5.9. The CI `engine-support` job regenerates and requires a clean diff (§12.4). Re-running step 2 against a **new** openvpn3 tag needs the host-side [7b] harness, which P2 didn't port from the spike: it is a prerequisite of the first openvpn3 bump (§18).

Tests:
- A unit test regenerates the table in CI and **diffs** it against the committed file. Any difference fails the build, so a submodule bump cannot silently change the classification.
- A second test asserts that the table covers exactly the allowlist's key set.

**First generator run (S13, draft 7; `native/spike/s13-s8/host/gen_engine_support.py`, results in `s13-s8/results/`):** over the 133 allowlist directives (154 variant cases) plus the 145 other names openvpn3 knows: **67 mapped, 38 ignored(warn), 9 ignored(silent), 14 dropped (reviewed overrides), 5 unsupported** (`rport`, `proto-force`, `socks-proxy`, `fragment`, `<pkcs12>`). Every row matched the table below except four, now folded in: `http-proxy` needs a TCP remote; `setenv opt X` is only a warning in openvpn3 for most X; inline `<verify-hash>` is a meta warning (already dropped); and openvpn3 never consults `settings_feature_not_implemented_fatal` (those names fail as `UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED OPTIONS`; still fatal, so the import report maps that category to "Not supported"). All 17 fatal directives of ref/openvpn3 §1 item 9 were confirmed fatal and are handled: 12 dropped with a note, 4 rejected (`rport`, `proto-force`, `socks-proxy`, `fragment`), `dev utunN` rewritten. *Draft 8:* the production generator reads that run's CSV instead of porting the script (below).

Expected classification (corrected against `release/3.11.8` source for draft 4, ref/openvpn3 §6.3 and items 15–19; confirmed by the S13 run with the draft-7 corrections; the generated table is authoritative where they differ):

| Group | Directives | Expected class |
|---|---|---|
| Role/transport | `client`, `proto`, `remote`, `remote-random`, `remote-random-hostname`, `port`, `float`, `server-poll-timeout` | mapped |
| | `tls-client` + `pull` | mapped **only as a pair** (openvpn3 converts them to `client`); either alone → reject |
| | `<connection>` | mapped; only `remote`/`port`/`proto` inside are honoured, anything else inside → reject at import ("not supported inside <connection>") |
| | `rport`, `proto-force` | **unsupported** (unknown to openvpn3 ⇒ fatal) |
| | `nobind` | ignored(silent) |
| | `resolv-retry`, `connect-retry(-max)`, `connect-timeout`, `explicit-exit-notify`, `socket-flags` | ignored(warn) (openvpn3 sends exit-notify on graceful stop anyway) |

| Proxy | `http-proxy host port`, `<http-proxy-user-pass>`, `http-proxy-option` | mapped together (credentials → `proxyUsername/Password`); without `http-proxy` → reject; **`http-proxy` with no TCP remote → reject** (openvpn3: "cannot connect via TCP-based proxy because no TCP server entries exist"; S13) |
| | `socks-proxy` | **unsupported** (not-implemented-fatal) |
| TLS/crypto | `ca`/`cert`/`key`/`extra-certs`/`tls-auth`/`tls-crypt`/`tls-crypt-v2` (inline), `verify-x509-name`, `peer-fingerprint`, `remote-cert-ku`, `remote-cert-eku`, `ns-cert-type` (OpenSSL), `crl-verify` (OpenSSL), `auth`, `cipher`, `tls-version-min`, `tls-cipher`, `tls-ciphersuites`, `tls-groups`, `tls-cert-profile`, `key-direction`, `hand-window`, `tran-window`, `tls-timeout`, `reneg-sec` | mapped (tls-crypt-v2 per spike gate) |
