| | `cipher` naming a 64-bit-block cipher (BF-*, DES-*, DES-EDE*/3DES, DESX, RC2-*, CAST5-*, IDEA-*), `cipher none`, `auth` with a digest under 160 bits | **unsupported** (draft 7, §8.6: each would need `enableLegacyAlgorithms`, which is never set) |
| | `pkcs12` (inline) | **unsupported**: openvpn3 never reads it (a meta-option warning only), so the table rejects it explicitly; [7b]'s log capture is the backstop |
| | `data-ciphers(-fallback)`, `ncp-ciphers`, `tls-version-max`, `reneg-bytes`, `reneg-pkts`, `replay-window`, `compat-mode` | ignored(warn) (openvpn3 advertises every allowed cipher in IV_CIPHERS) |
| | `ecdh-curve` | ignored(silent) |
| | `dh` | dropped from canonical text with a warning (server-only: fatal if passed through) |
| | `verify-hash` | dropped with a warning (not-implemented-fatal) |
| Compression | `comp-lzo`, `compress` | mapped. **Decision:** `compressionMode = "asym"` (decompress only, VORACLE) |
| | `allow-compression` | ignored(warn) |
| DNS/routes | `dhcp-option`, `dns`, `route`, `route-ipv6`, `route-nopull`, `redirect-gateway`, `redirect-private`, `block-ipv6`, `pull-filter`, `route-metric` | mapped (`pull-filter`: accept/ignore/reject, prefix match on the last token, first match wins; `reject` → `CLIENT_RESTART` every 5 s, never fatal in openvpn3, so the shim makes it fatal, §8.5). `route-nopull` does **not** filter pushed `dns` (S13: confirmed) |
| | `block-outside-dns` | touched by openvpn3 (Windows semantics); dropped |
| | `topology`, `route-gateway` | **push-only** (fatal in a profile) → dropped with an info note ("set by the server") |
| | `route-ipv6-gateway`, `register-dns`, `dhcp-renew`, `dhcp-release`, `dhcp-pre-release`, `tap-sleep`, `dns-updown` | **unknown to openvpn3 (fatal in a profile)** → dropped with a note |
| | `route-delay`, `allow-recursive-routing`, `route-method`, `ip-win32` | ignored(warn) |
| MTU | `tun-mtu`, `tun-mtu-max`, `mssfix` | mapped |
| | `link-mtu`, `tun-mtu-extra` | ignored(warn) |
| | `mtu-disc` | ignored(warn) (not-implemented-warn) |
| | `fragment` | **unsupported** (openvpn3 throws "fragment … not supported"; the server requires it) |
| Liveness | `keepalive` | **mapped** (read by `ProtoConfig::load` although it is on ignoreWithWarning; default 8 s/40 s when absent) |
| | `ping`, `ping-restart` | mapped **only without `keepalive`**; with `keepalive` they are untouched push-only options ⇒ fatal, so the normalizer drops them |
| | `inactive` | mapped |
| | `ping-exit` | push-only, never read on the client ⇒ dropped with a warning |
| | `ping-timer-rem` | fatal in openvpn3 (`UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED OPTIONS`) → dropped with a warning (it only matters for p2p); `setenv opt ping-timer-rem` is only a warning in openvpn3 (S13), and the normalizer drops it too |
| Auth | `auth-user-pass` (bare or inline), `auth-nocache`, `static-challenge`, `push-peer-info` | mapped (inline user+pass locks the creds: `provide_creds` is then ignored) |
| | `auth-retry` | ignored(warn) (superseded by our prompt flow) |
| Logging | `verb`, `mute-replay-warnings` | ignored(silent) |
| | `mute` | ignored(warn) |
| Harmless/Windows/Linux | `persist-key`, `persist-tun`, `disable-occ`, `disable-dco`, `user`, `group`, `providers` (`legacy` is never honoured: no `enableLegacyAlgorithms`, §8.6), `setenv-safe` | ignored(warn), dropped |
| | `fast-io`, `sndbuf`, `rcvbuf`, `tun-ipv6`, `script-security` | ignored(silent), dropped |
| | `ignore-unknown-option` | mapped (openvpn3 honours it; the names it lists are still checked by our allowlist) |
| | `setenv` (UV_/IV_ and listed names) | mapped (touched; UV_* sent only with push-peer-info; `setenv IV_SSO` stripped, §8.4) |
| `setenv opt X …` | inner X is checked by the allowlist, then classified as X **by our table** (draft 7, S13: openvpn3 downgrades any untouched X to the warning "Ignored options prefixed with 'setenv opt'" unless X is removed, server-only, standalone or push-only, so `setenv opt socks-proxy`/`management`/`register-dns` pass openvpn3 and [7b] does **not** back-stop them). **Normative (draft 8, PF 17; a fuzz finding):** a nested `setenv opt setenv opt X …` is classified by the **innermost** directive X | as X |
| `dev`/`dev-type` | `tun`/`tunN` only (allowlist) | rewritten to `dev tun`: **mandatory**, because openvpn3 requires the value to start with `tun` (`utunN` ⇒ "bad dev-type") |
| `management*`, `log*`, `status`, `daemon`, `writepid`, … | not on the Go allowlist | **forbidden** (and fatal in openvpn3) |
| Everything not on the allowlist | | **forbidden** (import rejected; line and name shown, never the arguments) |

- openvpn3 honours some directives the Go allowlist rejects (`client-cert-not-required`, `sni`, `allow-password-save`, `tcp-queue-limit`, `remote-cache-lifetime`, …). **Decision:** add `client-cert-not-required` and `sni` to the allowlist (both inert locally); the rest stay rejected.
- Routes with an explicit gateway IP (`route 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0 10.8.0.5`) or a non-canonical form (`10.1.2.3/16`) are dropped by openvpn3 with a log line, not fatal. The import report says so; the normalizer rewrites a profile route's explicit gateway to `vpn_gateway` with a note.

Directives classed "dropped" never reach openvpn3, so they cannot trigger `UNUSED_OPTIONS`. The [7b] check is the backstop for anything the table gets wrong.

### 8.3 Unsupported-directive UX

- The import sheet shows the profile name, endpoint and protocol, then three collapsible groups:
  - **Will be ignored** (grey), e.g. "line 12 `verb` — logging is managed by LockPlus";
  - **Not supported** (red);
  - **Security warnings** (orange): "server identity not pinned" (S13: the real Acme profile has neither `remote-cert-tls` nor `verify-x509-name`, so it gets this warning: any certificate from its CA would be accepted), "legacy CBC encryption" (non-AEAD, §8.6), "compression enabled by server".
  - A 64-bit-block cipher (BF-CBC, DES, 3DES) is **Not supported** (draft 7), with the message "This profile uses <cipher>, an outdated cipher LockPlus doesn't support. Ask the server's operator to enable AES-GCM." (§8.6).
- Any *Not supported* or *forbidden* item disables Import. The user can copy the report.
- The report is persisted in `Profile.importReport` and shown again in Detail › Profile info.
- Multi-file and zip imports show one row per file with ✔/⚠/✖ and the same per-file reports. This is the `ZipImportResult` UX.

### 8.4 Auth flows (L-OVPN-3, L-RC-4)

`EvalConfig` determines the up-front needs:
- `autologin == false` → user/password needed;
- `staticChallenge != ""` → an SC prompt with `staticChallengeEcho`;
- `privateKeyPasswordRequired` → passphrase (detected from PEM markers).

The shim's `Config` (ref/openvpn3 §11 checklist):
- `content` = canonical text; `ssoMethods = ""`, so **IV_SSO is never advertised** (a unit test asserts the value, and the §15.2 test server logs the peer info to prove no `IV_SSO` reaches it);
- `retryOnAuthFailed = false`, `autologinSessions = true`, `info = true`, `echo = false`, `connTimeout = 0`, `tunPersist = false` (S11), `googleDnsFallback = false`, `dhcpSearchDomainsAsSplitDomains = false` (§8.5), `compressionMode = "asym"`;
- **`disableClientCert = !(profile has cert && key)`**: otherwise `externalPki` is true for every username/password-only profile and `connect_setup()` fails with "Missing External PKI alias" (ref/openvpn3 §1 item 5, item 10);
- `enableNonPreferredDCAlgorithms`/`enableLegacyAlgorithms` per §8.6; `privateKeyPassword` when needed; `guiVersion = "LockPlus <ver>"`; `platformVersion` = macOS version (sent only with `push-peer-info`); `proxy*` from inline creds.
- Overrides on our `OpenVPNClient` subclass: `get_async_stop()` returns a shim-owned `openvpn::Stop` (below; **the `Stop` must outlive the client object**), `socket_protect()` → `true` (NE already exempts provider sockets from the tunnel; it does not bind them, and NE scopes them to the primary interface, §9.3), `pause_on_connection_timeout()` → `false`, EPKI callbacks → error, `remote_override_enabled()` → `false`.

**Lifecycle facts (ref/openvpn3 §1, §3.4):**
- **One `OpenVPNClient` per attempt** (§7.3): every "fresh `connect()`" below means a new instance, a new `eval_config` and a new `provide_creds`, on a new connect thread.
- **Early `stop()` is lost** unless handled: `stop()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `reconnect()`, `session_token()` and the stats calls are silent no-ops until `connect()` has finished its setup. The shim overrides `get_async_stop()`; `Stop` is sticky, so `Stop::stop()` is safe before, during and after `connect()`. The adapter's cancellation handler calls it (after answering any pending `EstablishTicket` with `-1`).
- **`Stop` lifetime (MUST, S11, draft 7.3; Conflicts as).** `~OpenVPNClient` (the base destructor) destroys `ClientState`, whose `AsioStopScope` unregisters from the `Stop` under the `Stop`'s mutex. A `Stop` held as a member of our `OpenVPNClient` subclass is destroyed **before** the base destructor runs, so every teardown locks a destroyed mutex and aborts (`std::terminate` in `AsioStopScope::~Scope`; every OVPN stop on the S11 v2 build). The `Stop` therefore lives in the owning wrapper and is **declared before the client** (members are destroyed in reverse order, so it is destroyed after the client), or the adapter heap-owns it and releases it after the client is destroyed. The subclass holds only a pointer. §15.1 tests create → stop → destroy, connect → stop → destroy, and destroy without connect under ASan.
- `connect()` returns a `Status` with `error = true` **only** for setup failures (bad profile, `UNUSED_OPTIONS`, missing EPKI alias). After the event loop starts it returns `error = false` even after `AUTH_FAILED`: the outcome is derived from events.
- **`parse_dynamic_challenge` needs openvpn3's process init alive (MUST, draft 8, PF 35).** Called without the `InitProcess` scope, it crashed the extension (the CRV1 crash found in P2b). The shim holds the process init for the duration of the call.
- **An attempt that never started its thread is still finished** (draft 8, tunnel review T11): the adapter marks the attempt done on the bail path, so `stop()` can't wait forever for a connect thread that never ran.

`ProvideCreds` has exactly `username`, `password`, `http_proxy_user`, `http_proxy_pass`, `response` and `dynamicChallengeCookie`; there are no per-call caching fields. `provide_creds` is ignored when the profile has an embedded `<auth-user-pass>` with a password, or is autologin with `autologinSessions` (creds locked); our normalizer extracts inline creds (§8.1), so that case doesn't arise. Credential caching is internal: `ClientCreds` keeps username/password for the session and prefers a pushed `auth-token` (session ID) on reconnect. The levers are what we pass to `provide_creds`, and **`auth-nocache`** (decision, draft 7, Conflicts ai): the normalizer appends `auth-nocache` to the canonical text of every **OTP-class** profile (static challenge, `appendOTP`, CRV1-capable, i.e. any profile whose answer contains a one-time code). S8 showed it gives a server log identical to the draft-2 `purge_user_pass()` patch (`Clearing credentials` right after the first auth write; the next reconnect, ping-restart or renegotiation hits `NEED_CREDS` before anything is sent), so the patch (`0001-expose-purge-user-pass.patch`) and its MPL publication duty are **dropped**. With an `auth-gen-token` server it costs nothing (the token is used on reconnect); a later token rejection yields `SESSION_EXPIRED` (the `.sessionExpired` prompt). Non-OTP profiles keep cached credentials, so a rejected token auto-retries via `SESSION_AUTH_FAILED`. (A patch-free purge through `Private::ClientState` from the shim's core TU is possible but couples us to internals; not used.)

Facts the auth design relies on (`release/3.11.8`, ref/openvpn3 §7):
- `purge_user_pass()` clears `username` and `password` only: **not** `response`, the CRV1 dynamic challenge or `session_id_username`.
- `password_needed_` becomes true once a non-empty password was set. `client_auth` throws `NEED_CREDS` iff there is no session ID, a password is needed and none is defined, **before** writing anything, so after a purge nothing (in particular no spent OTP) reaches the server (M6). For SC profiles the stale `response` survives the purge, but `NEED_CREDS` fires first.
- `NEED_CREDS` and `DYNAMIC_CHALLENGE` are flagged `fatal` but are prompts, not errors: openvpn3 emits the event, stops, and `connect()` returns.
- Consequence for `awaitingAuth(.reconnect)`: on `NEED_CREDS` the shim reports `authRequired(.reconnect)`, the session ends, and the answer goes to a **new client** with `provide_creds` carrying the **username again** plus the fresh password/OTP. The controller stays in `reasserting` (status never `.connected`) across that gap, and the utun descriptor is re-established through the normal `tun_builder_establish()` path (§7.3).
- openvpn3 honours `auth-nocache` natively (profile and pushed): `purge_user_pass()` after every auth write. S8: equivalent to the patch, adopted (above).
- **S8 verified on the test servers (draft 7):** password, server reason text, `AUTH_FAILED,TEMP[backoff N]` (no event, `RECONNECTING` after N+1 s), SCRV1 (both echo flags) and the shim's concat string, CRV1 across two processes and two clients (the cookie's username wins over the supplied one), auth-gen-token reconnects (also after a real 70 s ping-restart), `SESSION_EXPIRED` after a rejected token with OTP-class credentials cleared, `AUTH_PENDING` then CONNECTED. Without `auth-nocache` and without a token, M6 reproduced: the stale OTP was re-sent on reconnect and on every `reneg-sec`. IV_SSO never appeared in 34 connects' peer info.

| Flow | Sequence |
|---|---|
| Password (saved) | Extension loads the creds (unless within 60 s of an AUTH_FAILED for this profile, §7.2), then `provide_creds(username, password)` before `connect()`. No prompt. The core re-sends them on every key negotiation (initial, `reneg-sec`, reconnect) unless `auth-nocache` purges. |
| Password (not saved / `appendOTP`) | **Known-interactive: the app may prompt before the start (draft 9: a UX optimisation, the user types while the Mac is still online).** `prepareStartAuth(profileID, .userPass)` → `AuthPrompt(nextStart: true)` → the sheet (username prefilled, password empty) → `answerAuth` → `startVPNTunnel(options: ["lp.manual": 1])`; that start takes the answer (once), and `provide_creds` (when openvpn3 requests the credentials) consumes it. With `appendOTP`, the sheet shows a saved-password field plus a "One-time code" field, and the app concatenates `base + otp` into `password`. "Save" persists the **base** password only. If the profile needs input the app didn't predict (or the answer was lost with a failed start), `NEED_CREDS` asks **inside the pending start** (§7.2). |
| Static challenge (SC) | **Known-interactive:** prompted before the start, exactly as the row above (`prepareStartAuth(profileID, .staticChallenge)`; the challenge text comes from the profile's `static-challenge`, so the app knows it up front), or inside the start if that answer is missing. Prompt has the password field plus the challenge text as a label and a response field (echo per flag; `staticChallengeEcho` is `"1"` only). `ProvideCreds.response = response`; openvpn3 sends `SCRV1:b64(pw):b64(resp)`. **openvpn3 never reads the format argument**, so the concat format is the shim's job: when the canonical `static-challenge` has a third argument `concat`, the shim sends `password = pw + resp`, `response = ""` (Go `combineStaticChallenge` semantics). Not a spike question any more. |
| Dynamic challenge (CRV1) | The first connect with user/pass gets `AUTH_FAILED,CRV1:…` → event `DYNAMIC_CHALLENGE` (`fatal = true`, `info` = the whole cookie) → stop. `parse_dynamic_challenge(cookie, dc)` gives `challenge/echo/responseRequired/stateID` but **not** the username; the read-only display username (`lockedUsername`) comes from `openvpn::ChallengeResponse(cookie).get_username()`. The answer goes to a **new client** with `ProvideCreds{username: stored username, password: base password (non-empty), response, dynamicChallengeCookie: cookie}`; openvpn3 itself sends the cookie's username and builds `CRV1::<state>::<response>`. The base password must be non-empty so that `password_needed_` is set and a later purge yields `NEED_CREDS` instead of re-sending the spent CRV1 response. **Inside the pending start (draft 9, D9-3).** The attempt's client receives the challenge and is discarded (`OpenVPNClient` is single-use, ref/openvpn3 §1 item 1); the start stays pending in `awaitingAuth(beforeConnected: true)` with the cookie (`SecretBytes`; it carries the server's state ID and the username) and, if the base password came from an answer rather than the store, that base password too. The app shows the CRV1 sheet and sends `answerAuth(promptID, response)` into the running start; the controller starts a **new attempt in the same start**: a **new** client: `eval_config` → `provide_creds{username: stored or carried, password: stored or carried base password, response, dynamicChallengeCookie: cookie}` → `connect()`. openvpn3 then sends the cookie's username and the password `CRV1::<state>::<response>` (`ClientCreds::get_password()` returns the CRV1 string whenever a dynamic challenge is set; the base password is held only for `password_needed_`, ref/openvpn3 §7 item 3). The cookie and the response are consumed by that one `provide_creds` and zeroed. Nothing is carried across starts: if the user stops the start, or the provider restarts, the next start is a fresh first connect and the server issues a new challenge. **State lifetime (S8, draft 7):** server-defined; the client carries the cookie indefinitely. The test server accepted answers after 61 s and 291 s and refused them after 301 s (its configured 300 s); Acme's window is TBD-by-S8 (real-credential run, manual). The CRV1 prompt deadline is therefore 5 min, not 10. **An expired or already-used state comes back as a plain `AUTH_FAILED`, with no new challenge**, indistinguishable from a wrong response. So `AUTH_FAILED` in a start that sent a CRV1 response is never shown as "wrong password": within the same start the controller runs one fresh first connect (new client, base credentials, no cookie; the base password is kept for this, §6.5) to get a new challenge and prompts again in the same start with `reason: .rejected` ("The code was not accepted or has expired. Enter the new code."). It counts toward the 3-rejections-in-10-min limit. If that fresh connect is itself rejected, the normal `AUTH_FAILED` row applies. |
| AUTH_FAILED | Event `AUTH_FAILED` (with `retryOnAuthFailed = false` → stop; `info` = the server's reason). If creds were stored: clear the extension's password copy, arm the 60 s resend guard, then prompt `reason: .rejected` with the server's reason text (sanitized, ≤ 200 chars) shown as secondary text. If they were not stored: prompt `.rejected`. **Never** auto-retry. During the first connect (a manual start) the `.rejected` prompt is answered **inside the pending start** (draft 9, §7.2): the answer is a new attempt in the same start. After 3 consecutive rejections within 10 min: `.authFailed` ends the attempt by the §7.2 `.fatal` rows with no prompt. Before Connected that means the failure rows (a held start with `includeAllNetworks`, a failed start otherwise), with a `.hard` start latch under on-demand rules; during a reconnect it is after Connected: `held(.nonRetryable)`/`held(.blockedAfterFailure)`, or a cancel after the teardown with the kill switch off. |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED` | A rejected auth-token when user interaction is needed (SC/CRV1 response or web auth seen) → stop → the same prompt with `reason: .sessionExpired`. |
| `AUTH_FAILED,TEMP[backoff N,…]` | **Not** fatal: openvpn3 restarts after its backoff. No prompt. |
| `SESSION_AUTH_FAILED` | A rejected auth-token with a usable stored password: openvpn3 purges the session ID and retries automatically with the stored password (log only). For OTP profiles the password was cleared by `auth-nocache` (below), so there is **no usable password** and openvpn3 emits **`SESSION_EXPIRED`** (fatal) instead, not `SESSION_AUTH_FAILED` and not `NEED_CREDS` (ref/openvpn3 §7 item 5, `cliproto.hpp:729-800`; **S8 confirmed**, for SC users even without the purge, since the stored OTP is never resent): the row above applies (stop → prompt with `reason: .sessionExpired` → new client). |
| CRV1 or `AUTH_FAILED` **after Connected** (draft 8, tunnel review T2, T3) | A dynamic challenge during a reconnect goes to `awaitingAuth(.reconnect)` like any after-Connected prompt, and the answer's new client gets **the cookie and the base credentials** in `provideAuth` (the first build lost both, so the server rejected the answer and looped into the 3-rejection fatal). An `AUTH_FAILED` after Connected sets `rejectedStoredCredentials` when stored credentials were used, so the stored password is cleared and the 60 s resend guard is armed, exactly as before Connected. |
| Reconnect requiring auth | openvpn3's **internal** reconnect (ping-restart, transport error, our `reconnect(0)`, server `RESTART`) and TLS renegotiation re-send the cached credentials, or the `auth-token` if the server pushed one. For OTP profiles (`appendOTP`, static challenge, CRV1) a re-sent password contains a **spent OTP**, which servers count as a failed login (M6). Rule (draft 7): every OTP-class profile carries `auth-nocache` (above). **With an auth-token** the engine-internal reconnects use the token and never prompt; **without one** the next internal reconnect or renegotiation hits `NEED_CREDS` → `awaitingAuth(reason: .reconnect)` with the backoff/budget paused → the user enters a fresh code → new client. Renegotiation (`reneg-sec`) without an auth-token therefore also prompts. S8 showed on the test servers that no stale OTP reaches the auth log (SC, `appendOTP`, CRV1; reconnect, ping-restart and renegotiation). Whether Acme and Globex push `auth-token`, and their `reneg-sec`, stay TBD-by-S8 (real-credential run, manual). Non-OTP profiles keep cached credentials. The draft-2 fallback (disable engine-internal reconnect) is not needed. |
| Deferred auth (`AUTH_PENDING`) | Can arrive without SSO (generic out-of-band approval such as a push-MFA prompt on the user's phone). **Decision:** wait. The controller enters `awaitingAuth(.pendingApproval)` and the UI shows "Waiting for sign-in approval…" with Cancel; openvpn3 extends its own connection timer. **Before Connected** (the usual case; draft 9) the wait happens inside the pending start, up to the server's `timeout`, capped at the 10 min auth deadline (no start budget any more, S2 E14b); the connect deadline stops while it waits. A deadline ends it through the failure rows (`.authTimedOut`: held with the flag, a failed start otherwise). After Connected (a reconnect) the same 10 min cap applies. |
| Web/SSO | Event `INFO`/`INFO_PRE` with `WEB_AUTH:`/`OPEN_URL:`/`CR_TEXT:` (`INFO` needs `Config.info = true`) → `.webAuthUnsupported` immediately (no hang): the before-Connected failure rows (held with the flag, a failed start otherwise), the after-Connected rows after. **A server may send them although we never advertise `IV_SSO`** (draft 7, S8: the test server sent `AUTH_PENDING info=timeout 60` and then `INFO WEB_AUTH::…`), so the shim cancels on the `INFO` even during an `awaitingAuth(.pendingApproval)` wait instead of waiting out the pending timeout. The import pre-check warns when the profile contains `setenv IV_SSO` (stripped). |
| Encrypted key | Supported: `Config.privateKeyPassword` from `CredentialRecord.keyPassphrase` or a `.keyPassphrase` prompt. An unsaved passphrase is known-interactive (PEM markers): prompted before the start via `prepareStartAuth`, like an unsaved password, or inside the start. |
| Proxy auth without inline creds | `.unsupported` at import (the Go `msgProxyAuth` equivalent). `PROXY_NEED_CREDS` at runtime is fatal. |

**Auth inside the pending start (draft 9, D9-3, §7.2, Conflicts bh; replaces draft 6's two-start flow).** S2 E14b measured no start time limit on macOS 26/27, so a first connect waits for the human **inside** the pending start:
1. **Known-interactive profiles** (`EvalConfig` says: unsaved user/password, static challenge, unsaved key passphrase) may prompt in the app **before** the start (`prepareStartAuth` → sheet → `answerAuth` → `startVPNTunnel(options: ["lp.manual": 1])`); the owner's next manual start of that profile takes the answer, once. A UX choice: the user types while the Mac is still online. It changes nothing below.
2. **Every prompt during the connect** (CRV1, a rejected password, an unexpected `NEED_CREDS`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `AUTH_PENDING`) keeps the start pending in `awaitingAuth(beforeConnected: true)` and pushes `tunnelEvent(authRequired)` (`nextStart = false`) to the owner's connections; the app also pulls it with `pendingAuthPrompt` on `.connecting`.
3. The app shows the sheet and sends `answerAuth` on the hello-validated connection (§5.3). For a prompt that ended the engine attempt, the controller starts a new attempt in the same start with the answer, the CRV1 cookie and the carried base credentials; for `AUTH_PENDING` the answer goes to the running attempt. There is **no "connect again" step**: the start that asked is the start that connects.
4. The answer is consumed exactly once **at `provide_creds`** (`SecretBytes`, zeroed right after).
5. Deadlines: 10 min (CRV1 5 min, the server's state lifetime; `AUTH_PENDING` the 10 min auth deadline). On a deadline: with `includeAllNetworks` the start is held, blocked (`.authTimedOut`); otherwise it fails. Cancel: `cancelAuth` takes the same rows with `.authRequired`, and the app's Cancel also stops the start (a user stop), so nothing stays blocked.
6. While the prompt shows under the kill switch, traffic is blocked (`.connecting`, S2 E14a); the UI says so (UI-CONCEPT §6.6 row 3).
7. **Start options never carry the answer, an OTP or a promptID** (S2 E1: NE replays the original options when it restarts a crashed provider by itself). A replayed manual start is an ordinary start: it prompts again if it needs input.
8. After Connected (reasserting) nothing changes: reconnect prompts keep the 10 min deadline.
9. An **on-demand** start never prompts (nobody answers): the failure rows with a `.hard` latch (C16).

Prompt delivery (F-9):
- If an app connection exists, `tunnelEvent(authRequired)` is pushed to the owner's connections (§5.2).
- On every app launch and every `NEVPNStatus` change to `.connecting` or `.reasserting`, the app calls `pendingAuthPrompt` (draft 9: a `.disconnected` start leaves no prompt behind).
- The menu bar shows "Authentication required…" (and the item "Enter Code for Acme…").
- **Where the prompt appears:** a **sheet on the main window** when it is visible. Otherwise the app posts a user notification and, only after a **user gesture** (clicking the notification, the menu item or the Dock icon), opens the main window with the sheet, or a **non-activating `NSPanel`** reached from that gesture. The app never steals focus with an activating panel on its own: a focus-stealing credential window is spoofable and trains users to type secrets into whatever pops up. Activation from a background event is not guaranteed anyway (`NSApp.activate()` "does not guarantee that the app will be activated").
- **Notification content:** the body names the **profile only** ("Acme needs sign-in"); never the challenge text, the server's message or a username. **No `UNTextInputNotificationAction`** for codes: an OTP typed into a notification bypasses the sheet's secure field and lives in Notification Center state.
- If no app answers a prompt by its deadline: `.authTimedOut` through the §7.2 rows (inside a pending start: held with the flag, a failed start otherwise). An unanswered `prepareStartAuth` prompt expires silently after 10 min (nothing was started).
- **Assumption:** on-demand profiles that need interactive auth are rejected as on-demand targets in the UI ("Requires a one-time code; can't auto-connect"). *Draft 8 (app-root review L8):* `OnDemandPlan` also refuses `stayConnected` on interactive or unsaved-password profiles.
- **Server text in the sheet (draft 8, Fable app review L8):** the challenge and the server's reason are displayed only after stripping C0/C1 and bidi control characters, collapsing newlines and capping at ~256 characters (the wire cap stays 1 KiB).
- **A failed `answerAuth` is visible (draft 8, app-root review M5):** the prompt is shown again with an inline error line saying why; it is never silently dropped. The username field is prefilled from `savedUsername` (tunnel review T15).

Stale answers:
- Every prompt has a fresh `promptID`. `answerAuth` with a non-current ID returns `.staleAnswer`, and the app discards its form. This replaces the Go `authCh` drain. With several connected app instances, the first answer wins and the others get `promptResolved`.

### 8.5 Pushed options and DNS mapping (L-DNS-2)

openvpn3 merges profile and pushed options, applies `pull-filter` (accept/ignore/reject, first match wins, matching the Go `filterPushed`) and `route-nopull` (which filters pushed `dhcp-option` but **not** pushed `dns`), and then calls the TunBuilder callbacks once per session in a fixed order (ref/openvpn3 §4.2): `tun_builder_new` → addresses → routes → `reroute_gw` → DNS → proxies → allow-family → remote address → layer → MTU → `establish`. Our shim's `TunBuilder` collects a `NetworkPlan`:

```swift
public struct RedirectGateway: Sendable, Equatable { public var v4: Bool; public var v6: Bool }  // draft 8: no RG_* flags (unused)
public struct NetworkPlan: Sendable, Equatable {
    public var ipv4: [IPv4Assignment], ipv6: [IPv6Assignment]
    public var includedRoutes4: [Route4], excludedRoutes4: [Route4]       // excluded = net_gateway routes only
    public var includedRoutes6: [Route6], excludedRoutes6: [Route6]
    public var redirectGateway: RedirectGateway                        // a struct, not a tuple: tuples block Equatable synthesis (SC14)
    public var allowIPv4: Bool, allowIPv6: Bool                        // tun_builder_set_allow_family (block-ipv4 / block-ipv6)
    public var dns: DNSPlan?                                           // nil = the engine delivered no DNS
    public var mtu: Int?, remoteAddress: String                        // remoteAddress from tun_builder_set_remote_address
}
public struct DNSPlan: Sendable, Equatable {
    public var servers: [String]            // ordered by priority; draft 8 (PF 4): a `:port` suffix is stripped and the server
                                            // kept (NE has no per-server port), matching the mapping table below
    public var searchDomains: [String]
    public var splitDomains: [String]       // resolve-domains / DOMAIN when split
    // DoH/DoT transports are cut from v2.0 (§21); `transport DoH|DoT` servers are used as plain DNS inside the tunnel
}
```

| Source | Maps to |
|---|---|
| `dns server N address A …` (2.7 profile or push; a pushed priority replaces the profile's) | `servers`, ordered by ascending N (int8 priorities; a pushed negative priority is rejected by the pull filter); a `:port` suffix is stripped (Go `stripDNSPort`) |
| `dns server N resolve-domains d …` | `splitDomains` |
| `dns search-domains d …` | `searchDomains` |
| `dns server N transport DoH\|DoT`, `sni` | ignored with an import/connect note ("encrypted DNS transport not used; queries go in plain text inside the tunnel"). The server addresses are still used (§10.3) |
| `dhcp-option DNS`/`DNS6` | `servers`, **only if no `dns server` exists** (2.7 semantics; openvpn3 ignores every `dhcp-option` value once a `--dns server` exists) |
| `dhcp-option DOMAIN`, `DOMAIN-SEARCH` | `searchDomains` (and `splitDomains` when `dnsMode == .split`). openvpn3 on macOS would turn them into **split** domains by default (`dhcpSearchDomainsAsSplitDomains = true`), which for a full tunnel would send every other query to the local resolver; the shim sets the flag to **false** (Conflicts q; ref/openvpn3 §1 item 8) |
| `dhcp-option ADAPTER_DOMAIN_SUFFIX` | first entry of `searchDomains` |
| `dhcp-option PROXY_HTTP/HTTPS/PROXY_AUTO_CONFIG_URL/PROXY_BYPASS` (`tun_builder_set_proxy_*`) | **Decision:** ignored in v2.0 with a connect note ("the server's proxy settings are not applied"); `NEProxySettings` is §21 |
| `dhcp-option WINS` | ignored (callback returns true) |
| PUSH_UPDATE changing DNS/routes | **supported (S13):** openvpn3 stops the tun impl and re-runs the full TunBuilder sequence (new `tun_builder_new` … `establish`, so a new dup) and re-emits CONNECTED (≥ 3.11.7) → the controller re-applies settings with a short `reasserting`. An update **replaces** that option type (a pushed `dns` update dropped the earlier search and resolve domains). **Residual (upstream race):** a second update arriving ~15 ms after the first is logged but never applied (no TunBuilder sequence, no CONNECTED). The client cannot see the loss: the controller only re-applies what openvpn3 delivers, and `DNSVerifier` checks the applied plan, not the server's intent. Documented, on the dependency watch, reported upstream (non-security) |

- **`pull-filter reject` loops (S13, draft 7):** a matching `reject` makes openvpn3 emit `CLIENT_RESTART` ("rejected pushed option: …") and reconnect every 5 s, forever, without a fatal event. The shim treats the **first** such `CLIENT_RESTART` as `.fatal(.pushedOptionRejected)` (non-retryable; detail = the option **name** from our own filter, never the server's arguments).
- **DNS callback:** `tun_builder_set_dns_options(const DnsOptions&)` is the **only** DNS callback since 3.11 (S13: one call with server priority, resolve-domains and search domains; pushed `dhcp-option DNS/DOMAIN` ignored when a `dns server` exists; `reroute_gw` called exactly once); the legacy `tun_builder_add_dns_server`/`add_search_domain` were removed and are not implemented (ref/openvpn3 item 22). It is **not called at all** when no server address exists, and a DNS parse error drops all DNS with only a log line. Therefore: a **full tunnel whose plan has no DNS** gets `dns = nil`, and the controller fails the connect with `.dnsPlanMissing` when the profile is kill-switch (a system resolver outside the tunnel would leak or simply not work), and otherwise connects with the import-report warning of §10.2. `googleDnsFallback` stays false.
- **Default routes:** openvpn3 never emits `0.0.0.0/1` + `128.0.0.0/1`. It calls `tun_builder_reroute_gw(ipv4, ipv6, flags)` **exactly once**, always (even with `false, false`); `ipv4` → `NEIPv4Route.default()`, `ipv6` → `NEIPv6Route.default()`. IPv6 is rerouted only when `ifconfig-ipv6` was pushed, so a v4-only full tunnel arrives as `v4 = true, v6 = false`, and §10.5 applies the `::/0` blackhole (`allowIPv6 == false` from `block-ipv6`, or no IPv6 assignment). `RG_LOCAL` means the server is on-link.
- **The tunnel's own subnet (draft 10, E2E-1 bug 2; 146f0cd).** `NEIPv4Settings`' subnet mask does not route the tunnel's connected subnet on macOS: an OpenVPN `topology subnet` split tunnel without pushed routes connected as 10.81.0.2/24 with only the host route, and couldn't reach the server's tunnel address (or a DNS server on the tunnel network). For a family **without** redirect-gateway, `NetworkSettingsBuilder` adds the connected v4/v6 subnets of the tunnel addresses as included routes (also a WireGuard `Address = 10.0.0.2/24`). Full tunnels need nothing. Test `splitTunnelRoutesItsOwnSubnet`; E2E-1's subnet case passed on 26 and 27 (route `10.85/24 → utun`, split DNS answered by 10.85.0.1).
- **`RG_BLOCK_LOCAL` (draft 8, PF 3; corrects drafts 4–7.3).** It means "no LAN access", but `excludeLocalNetworks` is a **protocol** flag of the saved NE configuration, which the provider can't change. It is therefore honoured only when the **profile** has it at import: the app then saves the profile with `excludeLocalNetworks = false` whatever `allowLAN` says. A **pushed** `block-local` is ignored, with a connect note. Draft 4's "forces `excludeLocalNetworks = false`" from the provider was not implementable.
- **`net_gateway` routes** arrive as `tun_builder_exclude_route` → `excludedRoutes` (only meaningful without `includeAllNetworks`, where excluded routes have no effect).
- **Pushed excluded routes are bounded (draft 8, Fable review M4; PF 40, 48).** Without a bound, a server could push `route 0.0.0.0 128.0.0.0 net_gateway` plus `128.0.0.0/1` and send everything around the tunnel while the UI says "Protected" (with the kill switch off, where excluded routes take effect). `ExcludedRouteGuard` rules, applied by the controller to every plan:
  - **full tunnels only;** split tunnels are unaffected;
  - an excluded route the **profile itself declares** (`route … net_gateway` in the canonical text) is exempt from both rules and doesn't count;
  - an **undeclared** pushed excluded route shorter than **/16** (IPv4, `minPushedPrefix4`) or **/48** (IPv6, `minPushedPrefix6`; Fable verification decision (a), superseding the first fix's /32) fails the session with `.pushedOptionRejected`;
  - at most **16** undeclared pushed excluded routes are accepted, IPv4 and IPv6 together (`maxUndeclaredPushed`); the 17th fails the session with `.pushedOptionRejected`, detail `route count`.
  - Whether NE honours `excludedRoutes` under `includeAllNetworks` and openvpn3's `net_gateway` pull path were not verified by the review; the guard applies either way.
- **Endpoint protection (draft 4, F-3, Conflicts d).** `NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings(tunnelRemoteAddress:)` is set to the address openvpn3 reports via `tun_builder_set_remote_address` (the **currently used** server IP), because under `includeAllNetworks` the always-excluded set includes control traffic "that communicates directly with the VPN server" (Apple routing doc; S2 E5 showed the exemption covers every provider socket, not just the transport, draft 9). **No excluded host route to the server is added** (draft 3 did): the transport is carried by NE's exemption of the provider's own sockets (`socket_protect()` returns true for that reason), under `includeAllNetworks` excluded routes "have no effect" anyway (WWDC25-234), and without the kill switch an excluded `/32` lets *any* process reach the server IP outside the tunnel, which is the TunnelCrack **ServerIP** leak. Every included route is kept as pushed, subject to the cap and `pull-filter`. S2 E7 (draft 9): the transport works without the route on 26 and 27 (WG UDP, OVPN UDP and TCP), so none is added.
  - On macOS in TunBuilder mode openvpn3 adds no remote-bypass routes itself (`remote_bypass` is set only for tun/mac, tun/win and iOS with `tunPersist`).
  - On every switch to a different server IP (remote-list failover, WG endpoint rotation, §9.3), the settings are re-applied with the new `tunnelRemoteAddress` **before** the first packet to it (ref/networkextension C14).
- Pushed-route caps: at most 1024 routes; prefix lengths are re-checked by our `NetworkPlan` validator (3.11.8 wraps an overflowing `/4294967320` to `/24`; fixed on master only); routes with prefix length < 1 are only honoured via `redirect-gateway`.

### 8.6 Legacy CBC and crypto (L-OVPN-2)

- `cipher X` without `data-ciphers`, where X is a CBC cipher, is the 2.7 trap that the Go `legacyDataCiphers` shim fixed.
- openvpn3 negotiates via IV_CIPHERS, which always lists **every** allowed data-channel cipher: `data-ciphers` in the profile is ignored. `cipher` remains the fallback for non-NCP servers, and with **no** `cipher` the fallback is **BF-CBC/SHA1**. The default (preferred) set is AEAD only (AES-128/192/256-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305); the non-AEAD data channel requires `enableNonPreferredDCAlgorithms = true`; 64-bit block ciphers (BF-CBC, DES) and digests under 160 bits need `enableLegacyAlgorithms = true`.
- **Decision (ref/openvpn3 item 27, narrowed by draft 7):** the normalizer sets a per-profile `legacyCrypto` flag from `cipher`/`auth` only (never from `data-ciphers`):
  - `cipher` names a non-AEAD cipher with a 128-bit block (AES-*-CBC, the real Acme case); **or**
  - `auth` names SHA1 together with a CBC cipher.
- That flag sets `enableNonPreferredDCAlgorithms = true` (S13: a CBC-only server connects with it and fails "no shared cipher" without it; spike gate passed).
- **Decision (owner, final for v2.0; draft 7, Conflicts aj): `enableLegacyAlgorithms` is never set**, and every profile that would need it is rejected at import as **unsupported** with a clear message (§8.3): `cipher` BF-CBC, DES, 3DES (DES-EDE3-CBC) or any other 64-bit-block cipher (DESX, RC2, CAST5, IDEA), and `auth` with a digest under 160 bits (MD5). Reasons:
  - They are outdated, and they would need OpenSSL's legacy provider, which the static build contains but never enables.
  - Neither real profile needs it (Acme: AES-CBC, not 64-bit; Globex: AEAD).
  - Re-enabling 64-bit ciphers needs a new owner decision (§21).
- **Non-NCP servers (S13, 2.4.7 server):** a profile with **no** `cipher` against a server that doesn't negotiate falls back to BF-CBC, which openvpn3 then can't use: `openssl_cipher_error: BF-CBC: not usable` and a `RECONNECTING` loop every 2 s with no fatal event. The shim treats the first such error as `.fatal(.legacyCryptoUnavailable)` (non-retryable). The import can't know whether the server negotiates, so a profile without `cipher` imports normally (2.4+ servers negotiate) and the error message says "This server needs an outdated cipher LockPlus doesn't support". A profile `cipher AES-256-CBC` against a non-NCP **BF** server connects but passes no traffic (a mismatch openvpn3 can't detect); the §7.5 `lastPacketReceived` check turns it into a reconnect loop, and the documented symptom is "connects, no traffic".
- A pushed `cipher none` cannot downgrade the session (openvpn3 ignores it; S13: the client stays on AES-256-GCM). A profile `cipher none` is rejected at import (S13: openvpn3 itself accepts it).
- **Why OpenSSL 3.5 LTS (nice-to-have rationale):** it is the current LTS line (supported to 2030) and the newest series that `release/3.11.8` compiles against (4.0 support is master-only). OpenSSL updates are tracked by the watch job and the 14-day SLA (§9.2, §22).
- **Epoch data keys (S13):** 2.7 servers negotiate `aead-epoch` with 3.11.8 for AES-256-GCM and CHACHA20-POLY1305 (UDP, TCP, tls-crypt-v2); not with CBC. Nothing to do.
- The UI shows a "Legacy encryption" badge on CBC profiles.
- Spike gate: a CBC-only server connects (S13: passed).

### 8.7 Logging (L-OVPN-2)

- openvpn3 has no `verb`. The shim's `log(const LogInfo&)` forwards each line through `OVPNLogRedactor` before it reaches `Logger`:
  - lines containing `auth-token`, `PUSH_REPLY`/`PUSH_UPDATE` keep only the option **names**;
  - `CRV1`/`SCRV1`/`password`/`private key` lines are dropped;
  - IPv4/IPv6 addresses and hostnames are logged `.private`.
- `sslDebugLevel = 0`. openvpn3 already prints `Session token: [redacted]` (unless `OPENVPN_SHOW_SESSION_TOKEN`, which is banned) and hides the auth-token in its PUSH dump.
- The banned defines of §8.1 (`OPENVPN_DEBUG_VERBOSE_ERRORS`, `OPENVPN_PACKET_LOG`, `OPENVPN_DEBUG_CLIPROTO`, …) are enforced by CI on the compile flags.
- `log()` runs on the connect thread: it appends to the `Mutex` `LogRing` synchronously and never awaits.
- Log levels: default `.info` (state transitions, cipher, error codes); `.debug` adds the redacted engine lines. There is no level at which keys or packets are logged. *Draft 8:* the extension's level (`EngineLogLevel`) is a startup setting of the Tunnel target; no XPC call can change it (`setLogLevel` was removed, §5.2).

---

## 9. WireGuard specifics

### 9.1 Parser and validator (port of `internal/config`)

`LPParsing/WGConfig.swift` is the **only** WireGuard parser: upstream's wg-quick parser lives in the WireGuard app, not in the `WireGuardKit` product, and (draft 8) the Swift `WireGuardKit` product with `TunnelConfiguration` isn't shipped at all (W13, §9.2). Reference semantics are `wg(8)` (`config.c`) and `wg-quick(8)` (`darwin.bash`), ref/wireguard §5:
- **wg-quick compatible:**
  - strip a UTF-8 BOM;
  - **strip everything from the first `#`** (`${line%%\#*}`), **except** in `PreUp`/`PostUp`/`PreDown`/`PostDown`, whose values are stored **unstripped** (wg-quick's `unstripped_value`), so a `#` inside a hook survives export;
  - `;` lines are a **LockPlus leniency**, not wg syntax (the Go app accepted them); they are skipped and recorded in the import report;
  - section names and keys are case-insensitive (a superset of wg-quick);
  - `key = value` splits on the first `=`; whitespace is trimmed around key and value;
  - repeated `Address`, `DNS`, `AllowedIPs` and the four hook keys accumulate in order; **any other duplicate known scalar key is an error** (as upstream; never silently take the last). *Draft 8 (PF 13):* duplicates of **unknown** keys are kept in `extraKeys`, matching the Go parser.
- **Bare IPs** in `Address`/`AllowedIPs` get `/32` or `/128` (`splitPrefixes`). This is required, not cosmetic: wireguard-go's UAPI `allowed_ip` uses `netip.ParsePrefix`, which rejects bare IPs.
- **Prefix lengths above 32/128 are rejected**, never clamped (upstream Apple clamps silently).
- Host bits set (`10.0.0.1/24` in `AllowedIPs`) → accepted, the route normalized to the network address, with a warning.
- `DNS` entries: an IP is a server; a hostname matching the RFC 1035 regex is a search domain.
- Unknown keys are preserved in `extraKeys` for export round-trips, never applied.
- `PreUp`/`PostUp`/`PreDown`/`PostDown`, `SaveConfig`, `Table` and `FwMark` are preserved but **never executed or applied**. The import report lists them as "ignored".
- Multiple `[Interface]` sections, or the same peer public key twice, are errors.
- Errors never echo line contents (a key could leak).
- *Draft 8 (PF 34, residual):* `PrivateKey`/`PresharedKey` are base64 `String`s during the parse and can't be zeroed; they move to `SecretBytes` right after parsing (§6.5).

Validator rules (port of `validator.go`):
- keys are base64 of 32 bytes; `PresharedKey` likewise, emitted to UAPI only when set;
- addresses and AllowedIPs are CIDRs;
- the endpoint is `host:port` (IPv6 in `[]`), with the host an IP or RFC 1035 name and the port 1–65535;
- MTU 576–65535 if set (**Decision:** a warning above 9000);
- ListenPort 1–65535 (absent → wireguard-go picks a random port, kept across `BindUpdate`);
- PersistentKeepalive 1–65535, or **`0`/`off`** to disable (upstream Apple rejected `off`);
- at least one peer;
- **no CR/LF in any value**, extra keys included;
- the `Table` and `FwMark` syntax is checked; both accept `off`, and `FwMark` accepts `0x…` hex.

The validator returns `[ValidationIssue(field: "Peer[0].Endpoint", message: LocalizedStringResource)]`, so the editor can attach issues to lines. `LPParsing` + TunnelEngine generate the UAPI text (draft 8: into exactly-sized `SecretBytes`, §6.5); WireGuardKit's model types are not used.

### 9.2 WireGuardKit fork strategy (ref/wireguard §9)

- **Base:** wireguard-apple `2fec12a` (upstream tip; no commits since 2023-02-15). *Draft 8 (Conflicts az; PF 18):* the committed series `Vendor/patches/wireguard-apple/NNNN-*.patch` is the source of truth; `Tools/bootstrap/vendor.sh` fetches the pinned upstream commit, applies the series and runs the bridge's Go tests on every bootstrap. The planned fork repository `github.com/steiale/wireguard-apple` (branch `lockplus`, submodule) doesn't exist yet and isn't needed. The Mullvad fork (`mullvad-master`) is watched for platform fixes and cherry-picked from only.
- **What the extension links (draft 8, Conflicts av; PF 31, 45):** only the `WireGuardKitGo` C interface (`libwg-go.a` and its header). The extension's own `Tunnel/WireGuardGoBackend.swift` drives it through the `TunnelAdapter` protocol; the upstream Swift `WireGuardAdapter`, `WireGuardKit` and `WireGuardKitC` are not shipped (W13). The patch rows below that changed the Swift adapter (W2, W3, W9) are therefore dropped, and W8's log mapping lives in the backend's Go logger callback.
- **wireguard-go (O3):** `go.mod` pins wireguard-go **master by pseudo-version** (`v0.0.0-20261024220952-b3bc704ef0ee` at writing), not the newest tag: tag `0.0.20250522` lacks `2631ce9` (2026-10-06, duplicate response consumed after an intermediate initiation, a session-reuse race) and `b3bc704` (2026-10-25, uint16 overflow in the IPv6 receive bounds check). - **Do not carry:** `exit(0)` in `stopTunnel` (the radar 32073323 workaround: it would kill unrelated state in a two-engine extension); a `handleAppMessage` that returns the runtime configuration (private key included) to the app; the iOS paths (`temporaryShutdown`, `withReresolvedIP`, `wgDisableSomeRoamingForBrokenMobileSemantics`); the IPv6 address prefix clamp to `/120`.
- **Go entry rules (ref/swift-concurrency §9.2, SC17):** Go is entered only from the adapter's serial `workQueue` (draft 8: the extension's `WireGuardGoBackend` queue) (the bridge's handle map is shared state), bridged with `withCheckedContinuation`, never from the controller actor or a cooperative-pool thread. The log callback is `@convention(c)`-compatible, captures nothing, touches only `Logger` and the `Mutex` `LogRing`, and never awaits or calls back into Go. Strings returned by Go (`wgGetStats`, `wgVersion`) are C-heap allocations the caller `free()`s.
- **Build** (ref/wireguard §4.2, ref/toolchain T10): the External Build System target `WireGuardGoBridgemacOS` (§2.2) runs the patched Makefile with `CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64`, `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags='-w -buildid='`, writing `libwg-go.a` into `CONFIGURATION_BUILD_DIR`. The Makefile copies `go env GOROOT` and applies `goruntime-boottime-over-monotonic.diff`; a failing patch fails the build, and a Go bump is therefore a fork change.
  - **The runtime patch is load-bearing** (sleep-aware timers, §7.4). CI checks `grep -q libc_mach_continuous_time <patched GOROOT>/src/runtime/sys_darwin.go`, `nm -gU libwg-go.a | grep -c ' T _wg'` against the expected export count (`WG_EXPORT_COUNT` = 11 in `pins.sh`, draft 8), and `wgVersion()` against the pinned short SHA.
- **Symbol hygiene (S7; build half done in P1, runtime half in draft 7.3):** `libwg-go.a` exports generic C symbols `_fatalf`, `_threadentry`, `_crosscall1`, `_crosscall2` and `_x_crosscall2_ptr` besides `_wg*`/`_x_cgo_*`/`__cgo*`. `Tools/build/check-symbols.sh` (a CI step) compares the strong global definitions (`nm -gUm`, including hidden "private external" ones, which still clash in a static link) pairwise across `libwg-go.a`, OpenSSL, openvpn3+asio, lz4 and the ObjC++ wrapper (draft 8: WireGuardKitC is gone, W13; every arm64 object is checked, not one sample, and no `find | head` under `pipefail`, Sonnet core review 10), and openvpn3's weak symbols against every strong list. S14 result: **0 duplicates**, and a Swift 6 binary with both stacks links with no `ld:` lines and runs (including the Go → C logger callback and 4 × 50 concurrent openvpn3 [7b] evaluations next to Go calls). Go crypto is pure Go, so no OpenSSL symbols clash. The single-extension design stands on build grounds. **The S7 runtime half passed on 27 (draft 7.3)**, so the design stands at runtime too and the two-extension fallback is dropped. All runs were in one PID: 50 alternating WG/OVPN sessions, 50 WG stop/start runs **without `exit()`** (radar 32073323 does not bite in a system extension: 79 `wgTurnOff` → `wgTurnOn` runs in one Go runtime), and a 65 min soak of 739 sessions. There was no crash, the process had 8 fds after every `down`, the footprint went 19.7 → 20.7 MB (flat after 30 min), RSS stayed at 34.4–35.5 MB and Go threads stayed bounded (28 → 31). An ASan build showed no memory error (§2.2).
- **Dependency watch (monthly CI job; F-6; draft 8: not built yet, §18):** diffs and opens an issue for: wireguard-go master (`git log <pin>..origin/master -- device/ conn/ tun/tun_darwin.go ipc/ rwcancel/`), wireguard-apple and the Mullvad fork, openvpn3 **release branch** tags (including whether a tag fixes the PUSH_UPDATE race, §8.5), OpenSSL 3.5.x, asio patches, **Sparkle** releases and advisories, **ZIPFoundation** (pinned 0.9.20, ≥ 0.9.18 for CVE-2023-39138; releases and GHSA; an upgrade re-runs the 2026-10-27 review on the diff, the crafted corpus and `fuzz_zip_import`), and the **Go toolchain** security releases (e.g. CVE-2026-27144). Every wireguard-go bump runs `go test ./device/... ./conn/... ./tun/...` on macOS arm64, also under `-race`, and re-runs the S7 soak. A High/Critical advisory in any of these triggers the §22 14-day release SLA.
- **Exit if wireguard-go on darwin stalls:** Mullvad's GotaTun (Rust, a BoringTun fork) is the candidate; it has no NE integration today (§20 risk 7).

### 9.3 Endpoint resolution, data-plane-up, MTU (L-MTU-1)

- **Resolution happens in the app, before the start (draft 9, D9-9; S2 E10, Conflicts bk).** S2 measured a provider `getaddrinfo` of an uncached hostname under `includeAllNetworks` (with `allowLAN` off): it **blocked 30 s and failed** (`EAI_NONAME`), in `startTunnel` and while held; a cached name answered in 0.3 ms, and with `allowLAN` on a LAN resolver answered (305 ms), because DNS to the LAN is exempt. The provider's DNS goes through mDNSResponder, which the flag blocks whenever the tunnel isn't carrying it. Therefore:
  - **The app resolves** the profile's endpoint hostnames (`ProfileSummary.endpoints`; draft 10: `resolvableEndpoints`, the remotes plus the `http-proxy` host, PF 51) right before `startVPNTunnel`, while no tunnel of ours is up (a switch waits for `.disconnected` first, §6.2): `StartEndpointResolver` (LPRouteProbe) runs `getaddrinfo(AF_UNSPEC, SOCK_DGRAM, AI_ADDRCONFIG)` per hostname, concurrently, ≤ 3 s each; all results, v4 first, de-duplicated (Go `orderIPsV4First`). A host that doesn't resolve in time is left out. The result goes into the start options as **`lp.endpoints = [hostname: [IP literal]]`** (≤ 8 hosts × 16 IPs; IP-literal endpoints need no entry).
  - **The extension's cache** (`state.plist` schema 3: hostname → IPs per (owner, profile)) fills the gaps: a start's map is merged over it and written back on success; WireGuard's own resolutions (kill switch off only) are merged too. On-demand starts (nil options) and the headless resume start use the cache alone.
  - **The adapters get the merged map and `providerDNS = !includeAllNetworks`.** WireGuard uses the map's IPs for each peer hostname; it may resolve a missing hostname only without the flag, through `GetAddrInfoResolver` with a **2 s deadline**. OpenVPN's canonical profile is **rewritten before openvpn3 sees it** (`OVPNRemoteRewriter`, on the bytes; key material never becomes a `String`): every `remote "<hostname>" …` line, at top level and inside `<connection>` blocks, becomes one remote (or one block) per IP, in order; IP-literal remotes stay; openvpn3 resolves nothing for literals, and `remote-random-hostname` skips them. Under the flag a hostname without IPs is **dropped**; without it the hostname stays for openvpn3.
  - No endpoint IPs left (peer 0 for WireGuard, every remote for OpenVPN) → **`.dnsResolutionFailed`** (`detail` "no endpoint IPs") at once, never a 30 s hang; with the flag that is a held start: nothing inside the hold can add IPs (D9-20), so it waits for the user's next Connect (which resolves afresh) or for the app's push.
  - **The app pushes fresh IPs into a held start (draft 10, PF 50; Conflicts bp).** On a network change (after a 2 s settle) or on wake, if a profile is `.connecting` and its snapshot shows a recoverable before-Connected hold (`PushEndpointsRequest.appliesTo`, §5.2), `ConnectionStore.pushFreshEndpointsIntoHeldStart` resolves `resolvableEndpoints` again and sends them with `pushEndpoints`; the start retries at once (§7.2). An on-demand start (cache only) whose cached IPs went stale can now recover without the user. **Limit:** the hold itself blocks under `includeAllNetworks` (E14a), so the app's lookup succeeds only where DNS is answered without the network: mDNSResponder's cache, or a LAN resolver with `allowLAN` on (E10: 305 ms). The stale-cache residual (§20 risk 25) is mitigated within that limit, not closed.
  - While `reasserting` nothing re-resolves: WireGuard rotates through the IPs of its start (§7.4, §7.5, ref/wireguard D4/D6). A profile whose hostname has never resolved while the app ran can't start under the flag from on-demand alone; the app's next manual start resolves it (draft 10: or the app's push into the held start, within its limit).
  - ~~Residual: an `http-proxy` given by hostname is still resolved by openvpn3; under the flag such a profile needs an IP for the proxy (import note).~~ **Draft 10 (PF 51): the app resolves the proxy too.** `OVPNNormalizer` records the accepted `http-proxy` in `ProfileSummary.proxyEndpoint`; the app resolves it with the remotes into `lp.endpoints`; `OVPNRemoteRewriter` rewrites `http-proxy "<host>"` to the map's first IP. Under the flag an unresolved proxy host fails the attempt with `.dnsResolutionFailed` "proxy host not resolved" (a hold the push above can recover). The import warns (`.proxyHostUnresolved`, a security warning) when the name doesn't resolve at import. Profiles imported before this have no `proxyEndpoint` until re-imported or edited. *Draft 10.1 (review PF-R5):* the proxy's IP comes from the app's unauthenticated DNS answer (or the cache), and openvpn3 sends the profile's proxy credentials (`Proxy-Authorization`) to whatever answers there before any server authentication; a spoofed answer can collect them. The tunnel itself stays safe (the server is still authenticated through the proxy), so this is documented, not changed (§20 risk 26).
  - A lint rule allows name resolution in the extension only in `GetAddrInfoResolver` (§12.4).
- **Data plane up:** after the controller has applied the settings and `adapter.start(uapi:tunFD:)` returned, it calls `wgSendHandshake` and polls `last_handshake_time_sec` (`wgGetStats`) every 250 ms.
  - The first nonzero value newer than start means connected. With `PersistentKeepalive` set, `Up()` already initiates; without it nothing is sent until the forced handshake (or the first tun packet).
  - It retries the handshake **every 5.5 s** (outside `RekeyTimeout`, so retries are not silently rate-limited) and moves to the next endpoint IP after 2 failures, up to the 45 s connect deadline.
  - **Every endpoint switch** (`wgSetEndpoint` with `update_only=true`) re-applies the settings with the new `tunnelRemoteAddress` first (§8.5). Server roaming may later override the endpoint with the source of an authenticated packet; that is expected.
  - Handshake RTT for Diagnostics = `last_handshake_time_ns − sentNs` (both wall clock, from W4).
- MTU:
  - `NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings.mtu` is **always** set explicitly: `policy.mtuOverride ?? config.MTU ?? 1420`. `tunnelOverheadBytes` is not used, so the value shown in Detail is deterministic; wireguard-go never sets the MTU itself (mtu 0 in `CreateTUNFromFile`).
  - **Decision (ref/wireguard D12, Conflicts l):** default **1420 for every endpoint family** (wg-quick parity: link MTU − 80, and 80 = IPv6 40 + UDP 8 + WireGuard 32, so 1420 is already IPv6-safe on a 1500 link).
  - A parse failure is an import error, never a silent fallback (the c7e3a74 lesson).
- MSS: NE does not clamp MSS. For WireGuard the MTU is the lever. For OpenVPN, `mssfix 1300` is the floor (§8.1). The fragment and RDP/SMB cases stay in the harness (L-KS-4).
- Keepalive floor: WG profiles without `PersistentKeepalive` stay as they are (the user's choice), but the import report suggests 25 s when the kill switch is on.
- IPv6 for v4-only full tunnels: §10.5.
- **Provider sockets use the primary interface (S6, draft 7.3; applies to both engines; Conflicts ar).** NE scopes the extension's own sockets to the **primary interface** (the one carrying the default route, en0 on the dev Mac), not to the interface the routing table picks for the destination. A server reachable only via a non-primary interface is therefore unreachable from the extension. Examples: a VM host-only or shared bridge (`bridge100`), Docker Desktop or colima, a second NIC, a Thunderbolt bridge, or USB Ethernet while Wi-Fi is primary. Evidence: with the endpoint on `bridge100`, wireguard-go sent handshake initiations without a send error, `nettop` showed the flow on en0, and the server's counter didn't move, while a user-space `sendto` from Terminal reached it. Pointing `tunnelRemoteAddress` elsewhere changed nothing. A LAN host on en0's own subnet, or the Mac's own en0 address, works. The Go app (a root daemon using normal routing) reaches such servers today, so this is a **regression**, recorded in §20 risk 22 and in the migration report (§13.1). Engineering response:
  - **Endpoint interface check (`RouteProbe`, LockPlusCore, Darwin `PF_ROUTE` `RTM_GET`, no new dependency).** For each endpoint IP it compares the route's interface with the default route's interface. It runs in the app at import (WG literal or currently resolvable endpoints, OVPN `remote`s), where a mismatch is an import-report **warning**, never a rejection, because the topology may differ later. It also runs in the extension in `starting`, before settings are applied, where the result is logged and kept for the start. **As built (draft 8, PF 7, 32):** the start-time check uses the IPs known at that moment (`lp.endpointIPs` from the start options, or the cached last good resolution); it is **not** repeated after WireGuard or openvpn3 resolve a hostname themselves, because the adapters were frozen by then. That gap is a residual, revisited in P3 if the limitation shows up in the field.
  - **Error mapping.** If the start-time check flagged the endpoint and the start then ends in `.connectTimeout` or `.peerUnreachable`, the start fails with **`.endpointInterfaceUnusable`** and `detail` = the interface's BSD name (§5.5). The app shows "This server is only reachable via bridge100, a network LockPlus's tunnel can't use" (UI-CONCEPT §6.15). The connect is still attempted, because the scoping is measured on 27 only. If S6 on 26 shows the same behaviour, a flagged start fails fast (no handshake or TLS reply within 5 s), instead of spending the connect deadline.
  - **S6b: dropped** (draft 7.3 owner decision, D73-owner; draft 8 removes the leftovers). The idea was to bind the transport socket (`IP_BOUND_IF`/`IPV6_BOUND_IF`) to the routed interface. It could never help kill-switch profiles, because under `includeAllNetworks` NE's NECP rules deny a provider connection that requires an interface other than the system's choice (§10.1, forum 756704). The limitation is accepted; `RouteProbe` and `.endpointInterfaceUnusable` explain it to the user.

---

## 10. Network policy

### 10.1 Kill switch (L-KS-2, L-LC-4)

`NetworkPolicy` → `NETunnelProviderProtocol` (all flags written explicitly on every save):

| Profile | `killSwitch` | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| full tunnel (WG `0.0.0.0/0`/`::/0`, OVPN `redirect-gateway`) | on | `includeAllNetworks = true`, `excludeLocalNetworks = allowLAN`, `excludeAPNs`, `excludeCellularServices`, `excludeDeviceCommunication` from the policy, `enforceRoutes = false` (it would be ignored anyway: the two are mutually exclusive) |
| split tunnel | on | `includeAllNetworks = false`, `enforceRoutes = true` (included routes are scoped to the VPN and supersede the routing table and apps' interface scoping), **`excludeLocalNetworks = allowLAN`** (with `enforceRoutes`, local subnets are carved out of included routes; ref/networkextension C21). The UI calls this **"Route protection"**, not "kill switch", and explains that non-tunnel traffic is not blocked. |
| any | off | `includeAllNetworks = false`, `enforceRoutes = false`, `excludeLocalNetworks = false` (it has no effect without one of the two) |

Rules:
- `ProfileStore.updatePolicy` throws `.mustBeDisconnected` unless the manager's status is `.disconnected` or `.invalid`. The UI disables the toggles while connected, with an explanation. (DTS has since said such flags may be saved while up and "should come into effect promptly", forum 749321; an older answer said the opposite. L-KS-2 stands either way.)
- The policy is set when the manager is saved. **Every** connect path (window, menu bar, on-demand, System Settings) uses the same saved configuration, so policy cannot depend on the UI path (L-LC-4).
- **The protocol-level flags are authoritative (F-2, Conflicts c).** The macOS 27.0 SDK declares settings-level `includeAllNetworks`/`excludeLocalNetworks` (typed `NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings.IPFamily`), `enforceRoutes` and the `exclude*` flags on `NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings`, documents that "the includeAllNetworks property in NEVPNProtocol class takes precedence if set", and marks them all `API_UNAVAILABLE(macos)`. Rule for v2.0: `NetworkSettingsBuilder` **never sets** a settings-level flag; if a future SDK makes them available on macOS, the only allowed alternative is setting each one **equal** to the protocol flag, after S2 E11 has measured precedence and mid-session toggling on that OS. A lint rule flags any use of those properties.
- With a kill-switch profile reasserting with the engine down, held, or with a start pending (`.connecting`), traffic is blocked (S2 E4, E14a, draft 9); `reasserting` with a working engine still passes traffic through the tunnel (E4r). A user stop, a failed start and `cancelTunnelWithError` are **open** (E2, E14c, E3), so the extension never ends a kill-switch session by itself (§7.2). The UI state comes from the derived-state table (§11.2).
- **Updates while blocked (L-KS-3):** see §12.3 and §4.2. The tunnel is stopped and on-demand disabled before the extension is replaced, then both are restored.
- **Built-in exclusions (SDK header, `NEVPNProtocol.h`):** with `includeAllNetworks`, the system **always** excludes "traffic necessary for connecting and maintaining the device's network connection, such as DHCP", traffic "that communicates directly with the VPN server" (routing doc), "traffic necessary for connecting to captive networks", carrier-routed cellular services, and companion-device traffic. The leak harness pass criterion (§15.3) already allows DHCP/ARP/ND/RA. The captive-network exemption is undefined in scope (it presumably covers the system's captive probe and the Captive Network Assistant, not arbitrary browser traffic). S1 records what passes while a kill-switch tunnel is up or reasserting on a portal network, and LK-15 treats any such traffic as expected only if it matches that recorded set.
- Under the flag NE installs NECP rules on the provider to prevent VPN loops; a provider connection that **requires** an interface other than the system's choice is denied, with no workaround (forum 756704). Neither engine binds to an interface (wireguard-go sets no `IP_BOUND_IF`). Independently of the flag, NE scopes provider sockets to the primary interface (S6, draft 7.3, §9.3). A server behind a non-primary interface is unreachable with or without the kill switch; the binding experiment (S6b) was dropped (§9.3).
- **The provider's own sockets are exempt and bypass the tunnel (S2 E5, draft 9, D9-10).** A new TCP connection or ICMP echo from the provider works under the flag and while held (TCP 49–50/50, ICMP 43–46/50), and its packets leave **en0 in clear, outside the tunnel**; the provider cannot reach an address inside its own tunnel (0/20). So the extension opens **no connection besides the engines' transport**: `measureLatency` answers `.extensionBusy`, liveness uses the transport (WG handshake RTT, openvpn3 transport stats), and the extension's `RouteProbe` is a numeric `PF_ROUTE` lookup with no packet sent. The transport itself needs no excluded server route (E7) and OpenVPN over TCP works under the flag (E6: 1 h of load and two server resets per OS, 5 s openvpn3 back-off, 0 probe packets on en0).
- **Assumption A-KS-1:** on macOS 27, `includeAllNetworks` with the exclude flags still permits AirDrop and Xcode device debugging (`excludeDeviceCommunication`), and blocks all other non-tunnel traffic, including the app's own (Sparkle) and iCloud Private Relay. Spike S2 validates this (LK-13 matrix). **Fallback:** document the exceptions and add a per-profile "compatibility" toggle that disables `includeAllNetworks` and uses `enforceRoutes`. *Draft 9:* in the VMs (no AirDrop, Xcode devices, Wi-Fi or Apple ID) only APNs (`excludeAPNs`) and the tail of Apple QUIC flows opened before `.connected` (≤ 3.3 s) left en0 while connected; no new connection did. The AirDrop/Xcode/iCloud Private Relay rows stay a manual LK-13 matrix on real hardware.

#### 10.1.1 What `includeAllNetworks` does when the tunnel ends (H1)

The Go kill switch (`internal/helper/firewall.go`) keeps a tunnel that **died unexpectedly** in `fwBlocked`: "blocked (fail closed, nothing passed but loopback/DHCP/ND) until the user disconnects or reconnects it, or turns the kill switch off". Only a user-initiated disconnect removes the rules. The native app must not drop that silently.

Prior evidence since draft 3 (ref/networkextension §5.2, C17): Apple's response on FB13812251 (iOS, 2024): with `includeAllNetworks` "default drop is enabled … If you leave the config enabled, and from your extension, you try to cancel the tunnel … traffic will get dropped until tunnel comes back up"; the workaround is to disconnect from the app or the VPN UI. A 2025 iOS report says a provider **crash** also left the device offline while NE restarted it. The routing doc states that traffic is dropped whenever the VPN "transitions away from the connected state". None of this was macOS evidence, so S2 measured it on 26 and 27 with kill-switch WG and OVPN-over-TCP profiles (draft 9: done, relay-free, on LP-macOS-26 26.6.2 and LP-macOS-27 27.0.1; raw data in `native/spike/RESULTS-S2-VM.md`). On macOS, **a cancel and a failed start are open, not blocked** (unlike the iOS report), a pending start and a held session block, and a crash opens for ~2.5 s:

| # | Event | Expected before S2 | What we measure | **S2 result (26.6.2 = 27.0.1 unless noted; draft 9)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `kill -9` of the provider process | **blocked** (iOS 2025 report) while `nesessionmanager` restarts the provider (on-demand) or until the session is torn down | time to `.disconnected`/`.reasserting`; packets on `en0` (BPF) during and after. Prior data (S5.5 on 27, stub provider without the flag): NE reported `.disconnecting` ~5 s after the kill, then `.disconnected` with `pluginFailed` (12); no restart without on-demand rules | **Blocked 5.0 s, then OPEN 2.45–2.86 s, then NE restarts the provider itself and blocks again** (44/44). Status leaves `.connected` at 4.99–5.19 s. The restart reuses the original start options and happens only with the flag. With an on-demand Connect rule the restart is **gone** (27: open 4.1–4.5 s until an on-demand trigger; 26: ≥ 30 s in 7/8 runs). → residual, no keep-alive rule (D9-8) |
| E2 | `stopVPNTunnel()` from the app or `scutil --nc stop` | **open** immediately: a user stop (Apple's recommended way out) | same | **Open** from `.disconnecting` (+0.03–0.11 s), as expected |
| E3 | `cancelTunnelWithError` from the provider (fatal error) | **blocked** (FB13812251, iOS) until the tunnel is back or the user disconnects | same, and what `NEVPNStatus` says meanwhile (expected `.disconnected` while blocked) | **Open** from `.disconnecting` (20/20 per OS), status `.disconnected` ("Plugin initiated"), no restart; **NE never calls `stopTunnel` afterwards (0/40)** → never cancel under the kill switch (D9-7) |

Recorded per OS (26, 27).
