**LK-02 outcome (draft 9, from S2 E1; D9-8):** after `kill -9` of the provider with the kill switch on, **no packet leaves a physical interface except to the VPN endpoint, except within ≤ 4 s after NE reports the failure** (measured open window 2.45–2.86 s + 1 s), and the tunnel comes back without user action (NE's own restart). The status leaves `.connected` within **8 s** (measured 4.99–5.19 s; the app already shows row 4a from the XPC interruption, §5.4). Draft 7's "until the user acts or the tunnel reconnects" can't be met: the system reconnects by itself, but only after the open window. For a profile with on-demand rules NE doesn't restart at all (E1+od); LK-02 for those profiles states the measured open time and is a documented regression (§20 risk 24). *Draft 10:* with the app running, such a profile is restarted by the app ~1.5 s after `.disconnected` (`CrashRestartPolicy`, §10.4); without the app, unchanged. **E2E-1 (product build 200001, WG, kill switch, no on-demand rules):** probe packets on en0 only from +5.52 to +7.23 s (26, **1.70 s**) and from +5.62 to +7.31 s (27, **1.68 s**) after the kill; a new provider PID 1 s after the kill; `.connected` again ~7.8 s after it. GO against the ≤ 4 s bound.

**Design per S2 result (draft 9: the measured row is selected; the alternatives are kept for the record).** After Connected: `.holdBlocked` only (Conflicts k, bi). Before Connected: **withhold** (Conflicts bh reverses ag).

| S2 result | Design | Selected? |
|---|---|---|
| E4 blocked (expected) | On a fatal error **after Connected** with the kill switch on, the provider does **not** cancel. It stays alive with `reasserting = true`, the adapter stopped and `holdReason = .blockedAfterFailure`. NE status is `.reasserting`, so the UI can say "Blocked" truthfully, and no on-demand rule restarts anything. The user ends it with **Disconnect** (a user stop, E2). This replicates `fwBlocked` for engine failures. | **Yes** (E4: 600 s, never stopped) |
| E4 blocked but the system stops held providers | `blockMode = .cancel`, relying on E3. | No: never stopped; and E3 is open. `.cancel` is removed (Conflicts bi) |
| E3 open (measured) | `cancelTunnelWithError` only with the kill switch off, and only after the adapter stopped and the summary was written (NE never calls `stopTunnel` after it). | **Yes** (D9-7) |
| E1 open, then NE restarts by itself (measured) | Nothing can block from a dead process; NE's own restart closes the window after 2.45–2.86 s. The window is a documented residual (§20 risk 24, help page). | **Yes** (D9-8) |
| E1 open → on-demand keep-alive rule (draft 7.3 mitigation) | A connect rule while connected. | **Dropped**: it disables NE's restart (open 4.1–4.5 s on 27, ≥ 30 s on 26; Conflicts bj) |
| E5 works, and bypasses the tunnel (measured) | No provider-originated connection besides the engines' transport (privacy: it would leave en0 in clear). `measureLatency` stays unavailable; liveness uses the transport. | **Yes** (D9-10) |
| E6 hangs | A forced compatibility toggle for OVPN-TCP kill-switch profiles. | No: E6 works |
| E7 fails | Re-add the excluded `/32`/`/128` for non-kill-switch profiles. | No: E7 works |
| E10 fails (measured) | The app resolves before the start (`lp.endpoints`), the cache fills gaps, the provider never resolves under the flag (§9.3). | **Yes** (D9-9) |
| E2 blocked | Disconnect saves on-demand off first and waits for `.disconnected`. | No: E2 open |
| E14b ≈ 60 s (draft 6's expectation) | Fail the start + latch within a 50 s budget; two-start auth. | No (E14b: no limit) |
| E14b ≥ 15 min on 26 and 27, E14a blocked (measured) | **Withhold:** before-Connected failures of `includeAllNetworks` profiles hold the pending start (blocked) instead of failing it (open); retryable ones retry inside the hold; auth happens inside the pending start for every profile (§7.2, §8.4). The derived state shows UI-CONCEPT §6.6 rows 3, 3a and 3b. No hold deadline (none needed by the OS). | **Yes** (D9-1, D9-3) |
| E14a open | The withhold alternative would be ruled out. | No: E14a blocked |
| E14c blocked after a failed start | Row 13 ("Blocked" while `.disconnected`, Restore Internet). | No: removed with row 13 |
| E14c open after a failed start (measured) | The withhold makes a failed start unreachable for `includeAllNetworks` profiles; without the flag a failed start is "Not protected" with the error (row 14). | **Yes** |
| E14c: an on-demand restart sends credentials despite the latch | A bug. | Not seen: 1 `DENY` per OS with the latch |

**Regressions against the Go kill switch (user-facing, in the release notes and help):**
- The Go app also blocked when the **helper itself** was killed (pf rules persist in the kernel). **Draft 9 (S2 E1):** a crash of LockPlus's tunnel process leaves the Mac online for **under 2 s** (1.3–1.7 s measured on product builds in E2E; 2.45–2.86 s in the S2 spike) before macOS restarts it; with an auto-connect (on-demand) profile, macOS does not restart it by itself, and the Mac stays online until the app or a network change starts it again (draft 10: the running app restarts it ~1.5 s after macOS reports the disconnect, §10.4; without the app, unchanged). The help page states both.
- The Go app's DNS protection (pf rules for port 53/853 outside the tunnel) has no separate switch: with `includeAllNetworks`, DNS follows the kill switch (§10.2).
- Split-tunnel "route protection" (`enforceRoutes`) does not block non-tunnel traffic, unlike the Go kill switch, which blocked everything except tunnels on any profile. This is shown in the UI (table above).
- **Switching profiles** is an unprotected moment: LockPlus runs one tunnel at a time (a design decision, not a macOS limit; macOS 26 can run several packet tunnels, but the kill switch routes everything through one), so switching from one kill-switch profile to another stops the first (open, E2) before the second starts, and the second may start only after `.disconnected` (NE drops a start issued while it is still stopping, ≤ 20 s). The window is short and shown (UI-CONCEPT §6.2), and LK-17 measures it.

#### 10.1.2 Residual attacks, documented (F-3)

- **TunnelVision (CVE-2024-3661):** a rogue DHCP server pushes option-121 routes more specific than the tunnel's. With the kill switch on, `includeAllNetworks` defeats it. With the kill switch **off**, it applies, as for every VPN client without a kill switch; split-tunnel route protection (`enforceRoutes`) keeps the tunnel's own routes but does not stop the rogue routes for other destinations. The help page says so next to the kill-switch toggle.
- **TunnelCrack LocalNet:** `allowLAN` is off by default (F-1); turning it on exempts local subnets by design, and a hostile network can claim a public range as "local".
- **TunnelCrack ServerIP:** no host route to the server exists (§8.5). Under the kill switch the system's own "communicates directly with the VPN server" exemption remains; whether it is keyed to the server IP for *other* processes is what LK-16 measures (user-space `curl` to the connected server IP must go **only** inside the tunnel).

### 10.2 DNS (L-DNS-1, L-DNS-2, L-DNS-3)

`NetworkSettingsBuilder.dns(plan, policy, isFullTunnel)`:

| Case | `NEDNSSettings` |
|---|---|
| no servers (`plan.dns == nil` or empty) | `nil` (system DNS) for **non-kill-switch** profiles; the import report warns for full tunnels ("DNS will go to your local resolver through the tunnel"). A **kill-switch** full tunnel without DNS fails with `.dnsPlanMissing` (§8.5). |
| full tunnel, any `dnsMode` | `servers`, `searchDomains = plan.searchDomains`, **`matchDomains = [""]`**. Apple: when the VPN becomes the default route, its servers become the default resolver and `matchDomains` is ignored, so `[""]` matters for split mode; it is set anyway for uniformity (NR §4 pitfall 12; ref/networkextension C22). |
| split, `.tunnelOnly` | the same, `matchDomains = [""]` (here it is what makes the tunnel resolver the default) |
| split, `.split` | `matchDomains = plan.splitDomains ∪ plan.searchDomains`. Domains only in `splitDomains` are resolved but not appended as search suffixes: `matchDomainsNoSearch = true` for that set. NE applies `matchDomainsNoSearch` per settings object, so when both kinds exist we keep `false` and also list the search domains in `searchDomains`. If the union is empty, `.split` falls back to `[""]` and the UI says so. |

- **`allowFailover = false`** is set explicitly and unconditionally (baseline on the 26.0 floor; drafts 4–7 gated it with `#available(macOS 26, *)`): the 26 SDK added it ("failover to the default system resolver is permitted on resolution failure") with an undocumented default, and failover to the local resolver would leak (ref/networkextension C22).
- **L-DNS-1:** DNS is owned by the NE session. When the extension dies, the system removes the settings, so there is no journal. Test: `kill -9` the extension, then `scutil --dns` is back to baseline (§15.3, LK-11).
- **L-DNS-3:** `DNSVerifier` runs in the app, 3 s after every `.connected` and on demand in Diagnostics:
  1. Parse `scutil --dns` (spawned as the user, read-only) and `SCDynamicStoreCopyValue("State:/Network/Global/DNS")`.
  2. Expect resolver #1 to carry the plan's servers, and the tunnel interface to own the catch-all domain when the plan has `[""]`.
  3. Resolve a random label under `lockplus-check.invalid` through the system resolver and confirm the query completes.
  - The result is `.ok`, `.mismatch(details)` (an MDM profile or another VPN overrode it) or `.unknown(reason)`.
  - **`.unknown` is never shown as safe.** The banner says "Couldn't verify DNS" (the c9e9ffd lesson).
  - *As built (draft 8, app-root review M6):* `scutil --dns` runs through `ProcessRunner` (§14.2); the lookup in step 3 runs under `withDeadline` (a `TaskGroup` race couldn't time out). Whether mDNSResponder answers `.invalid` locally, which would make step 3 prove nothing, is still to be checked; until then a completed query is treated as "the resolver responded", never as "the query went through the tunnel".
- The Diagnostics "DNS leak test" is the same verifier plus a list of the effective resolvers, each tagged tunnel or non-tunnel.
  - It never infers "leak" from a resolver answering, because with `includeAllNetworks` every resolver answers through the tunnel. The real leak test is the harness's capture on the physical interface.
  - BSD tools that read `/etc/resolv.conf` don't see split DNS; the help page notes it.
- **Connection self-test, DNS row (2.0.2, D10.4-8, §11.5).** The same `DNSVerifier` result, plus, for profiles whose tunnel owns the catch-all (`isFullTunnel` or `dnsMode == .tunnelOnly`), a route check: each name server of the default resolver (the one without a domain) → `RouteProbe.interface(forIP:)` (`RTM_GET`, IP literals only) must be the tunnel's utun. A server routed elsewhere is **Mismatch** ("another resolver or route handles DNS"), except under `includeAllNetworks` (the self-test approximates it as full tunnel + kill switch): there NECP scopes every socket to the tunnel, so a route-table answer of en0 is **Couldn't verify**, never a leak (the rule above). No tunnel interface known, an empty default resolver or a server without a route is Couldn't verify; Couldn't verify is never drawn as safe. A profile that sets no DNS server (the WireGuard split case of D10.3-6 F4) shows "The profile sets no DNS server: DNS stays as it is" and the row doesn't count toward the overall verdict.

### 10.3 DNS over HTTPS/TLS (cut from v2.0)

- v2.0 always uses plain `NEDNSSettings` to the profile's or the server's DNS servers. They are inside the tunnel, so confidentiality holds as far as the VPN server. The import report notes it when a profile asks for `transport DoH|DoT`.
- `NEDNSOverHTTPSSettings`/`NEDNSOverTLSSettings` as tunnel settings, and the former spike S3, move to §21.

### 10.4 Wi-Fi auto-connect (on-demand)

- macOS honours on-demand rules only on the **enabled** configuration, and only one packet-tunnel configuration is active. *Draft 10.3:* phase 0 measured that a second LockPlus configuration **can** be started beside a running one (System Settings, `scutil`; on-demand likely); the extension refuses it (§7.2 start guard).
- **Decision:** auto-connect designates **one** profile (`AutoConnectRules.profileID`). Its manager gets:
  ```swift
  let probes = [URL(string: "https://<pages-host>/probe.txt")!,                     // ours, static, 200 "ok" (§2.5: steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates)
                URL(string: "https://www.apple.com/library/test/success.html")!]  // second host, different operator (N7)
  func connect(_ type: NEOnDemandRuleInterfaceType) -> [NEOnDemandRule] {        // one connect rule per probe host
      probes.map { let r = NEOnDemandRuleConnect(); r.interfaceTypeMatch = type; r.probeURL = $0; return r }
  }
  let trusted = NEOnDemandRuleDisconnect(); trusted.interfaceTypeMatch = .wiFi; trusted.ssidMatch = rules.trustedSSIDs
  let wifi = connect(.wiFi)
  let eth: [NEOnDemandRule] = rules.connectOnEthernet ? connect(.ethernet)
                              : [{ let r = NEOnDemandRuleIgnore(); r.interfaceTypeMatch = .ethernet; return r }()]
  let portal = NEOnDemandRuleIgnore();     portal.interfaceTypeMatch = .any   // both probes failed: likely captive portal
  manager.onDemandRules = [trusted] + wifi + eth + [portal]; manager.isOnDemandEnabled = rules.enabled && !paused
  ```
- `stayConnected` profiles get `connect(.any) + [portalIgnore]`.
- **As built (draft 10):** `OnDemandPlan` builds exactly this order: our `probe.txt` rule, then Apple's, then Ignore (`ManagerConfiguration.probeURLs`; test `connectRulesProbeOurHostThenApplesThenIgnore`). E2E-1 found the 2.0.0 builds (200000, 200001) configuring **only Apple's** page (rules `Connect/WiFi`, `Connect/Ethernet` with `URLStringProbe https://www.apple.com/library/test/success.html`, then `Ignore`); a06412a fixed it after the run.
- A Connect rule starts the VPN lazily, when an application opens a network connection, not at the moment the rule matches (`NEOnDemandRule.h`).
- Both probe hosts must serve TLS ≥ 1.2 (the default minimum for apps linked on 26+).
- **Probe host dependency (N7).** A connect rule matches only when its probe returns HTTP 200 (`NEOnDemandRule.h`). If the probe host is down, blocked, or its TLS fails, the rule doesn't match, evaluation falls through to Ignore, and **auto-connect silently stops protecting** (fail open). Rules are evaluated in order, so a second connect rule with a probe on an independent host (Apple's HTTPS success page) matches when the first host is unavailable. Both probes are **HTTPS**: a portal that answers a hijacked plain-HTTP request with its own `200` login page would otherwise make the rule match; with HTTPS that request fails certificate validation. If both hosts are unreachable on a working network, the tunnel stays down: the app (if running) shows "Auto-connect couldn't verify this network" with a "Connect now" button, and its 15 s re-probe (below) tries both URLs (*draft 10: neither is built; §18 backlog*). The help page documents both hosts and the fail-open case. The probe file on the Pages host must exist before the first beta (CI checks that it returns 200; *draft 10: no such check exists in `.github/workflows`; §18 backlog*). **During P1** the Pages host is still undecided (§2.5), so S1 uses Apple's page as the first probe and a **temporary** host as the second (a static `probe.txt` on the §15.7 test VPS behind a valid TLS certificate); nothing shipped ever references the temporary host.

**Captive portals (M4).** On-demand plus `includeAllNetworks` would otherwise make hotel and airport login pages unreachable: on-demand connects on joining the network, the tunnel can't reach its server until the user has logged in, and the kill switch blocks the login page.
- `probeURL` on the connect rules: the rule only matches when the probe returns HTTP 200. On a captive network the probe is intercepted or redirected, so the connect rule does not match and evaluation falls through to the final **Ignore** rule. The tunnel stays down, the system's Captive Network Assistant appears, and the user logs in. The probes are static files on our GitHub Pages host and on apple.com; they carry no identifier and are fetched by the system, not by us. Their privacy note is in the help page.
- The `includeAllNetworks` header states that "traffic necessary for connecting to captive networks" is always excluded from the tunnel (§10.1). That does **not** make the rules above unnecessary: it is undocumented whether the exemption covers a browser login page or only the system's captive probe and CNA, and it does nothing for on-demand trying to connect before the login. S1 records what reaches the portal while a kill-switch tunnel is reasserting; if the CNA login works through the exemption on 26/27, "Pause protection" becomes a fallback rather than the main path for the already-connected case.
- After the login no network change happens, so on-demand may not re-evaluate (TBD-by-S1). The app (if running) watches `NWPathMonitor` and re-probes the same URL every 15 s for up to 10 min after joining a network where the connect rule didn't fire. When the probe succeeds, it calls `startVPNTunnel` on the auto profile. Without the app running, protection starts on the next network change. The UI states this. *Draft 10: the 15 s re-probe is not built (§18 backlog); today protection starts on the next network change, app running or not.*
- **"Pause protection for N minutes"** covers the case where the tunnel is **already up** (or reasserting/blocked) when the portal appears, e.g. after joining a new network while connected with the kill switch:
  - In the menu bar: "Pause protection ▸ 5 min / 15 min / 1 hour" (shown by the §11.3 rule). The same entries appear in the Blocked hero, with the hint "Use this to log in to a Wi-Fi network".
  - Action: confirmation, "LockPlus will disconnect and allow unprotected internet for 15 minutes." Then `pausedUntil = now + N` and `pausedState = {profileID?, onDemandEnabledIDs, agentBuild: CFBundleVersion}` in settings (written atomically), register the resume agent (below), `isOnDemandEnabled = false` and save, then `stopVPNTunnel()`. The agent is registered **before** the tunnel stops, so a crash at any later point still resumes.
  - While paused, the menu-bar icon shows the warning badge with "Paused — 12 min left", and the menu offers "Resume protection now".
  - On expiry (an app timer, also checked on wake and launch): restore on-demand, and `startVPNTunnel` if the paused profile was connected. Then clear `pausedUntil` and `unregister(completionHandler:)` the agent (`kSMErrorJobNotFound` = done).
  - If the app is quit while paused, the quit dialog defaults to "Resume protection and quit".
  - **A pause must not outlive a crashed app (N3).** The app bundles `Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.resume.plist` and registers it with `SMAppService.agent(plistName:)` for the duration of each pause:
    ```xml
    <key>Label</key><string>io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.resume</string>
    <key>BundleProgram</key><string>Contents/MacOS/LockPlus</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key><array><string>LockPlus</string><string>--resume-protection</string></array>
    <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><dict/>   <!-- every minute; fires missed during sleep are coalesced into one at wake -->
    <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>
    <!-- no ProcessType: Background throttling competes with the 5 s budget (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C14) -->
    ```
    - **Schedule (corrects draft 3, Conflicts p; ref/xpc-servicemanagement C10):** `StartInterval` fires that fall during sleep are **missed**, not coalesced ("If the system is asleep … that interval will be missed due to shortcomings in kqueue(3)", `launchd.plist(5)`); coalescing at wake is `StartCalendarInterval`'s behaviour. A static every-minute calendar entry (`{}`, all fields wildcards) is valid in a bundle plist; only an absolute date is impossible. Bound: expiry is honoured **≤ 60 s after expiry or wake**. TBD-by-S5 (that `{}` loads via SMAppService and fires at wake); fallback `StartInterval 60`, with the bound "≤ 60 s of awake time after wake" (the app's own wake check covers the running-app case).
    - `LockPlus --resume-protection` is handled in `main.swift` before `NSApplicationMain`. It runs headless with no UI and exits within 5 s:
      1. it takes the GUI **instance lock** non-blocking (`flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on `instance.lock`, held by every GUI instance for its lifetime); if that fails, a GUI instance owns expiry, so it exits 0. (`NSRunningApplication` can't tell: the agent *is* that bundle, and a launchd-spawned process is not a LaunchServices app.)
      2. If `pausedUntil` is in the future, it exits 0.
      3. Otherwise it performs the expiry steps above with `NETunnelProviderManager` (same binary, same signature and entitlements), writes `settings.json` atomically (`fsync` + `rename`) with `pausedUntil` cleared, **then** calls `SMAppService.agent(plistName:).unregister()`. That call **kills this process** ("If the service … is currently running it will be killed"), so nothing may follow it (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C11).
      4. *Draft 8 (built as `Headless/HeadlessResume`; app-root review L12):* if the NE managers can't be loaded, it changes nothing (the pause and the agent stay) and exits, so the next fire a minute later retries; a failed load never clears the pause.
    - `RunAtLoad` covers reboot and logout: the agent runs at the next login and resumes at once if the pause expired meanwhile. It **also fires immediately at `register()`**, while the GUI is running; the instance lock makes that run exit at once (one process spawn per pause; C13).
    - **Re-registration after updates (C12):** `SMAppService` requires re-registering an agent whose executable changed, and our `BundleProgram` is the main binary that every update replaces. On every launch with `pausedUntil` set and `pausedState.agentBuild != CFBundleVersion`: `unregister(completionHandler:)` → await → `register()`. With `pausedUntil == nil` but `status != .notRegistered`: unregister the stale registration.
    - **Why not an absolute date:** `SMAppService.agent` accepts the standard launchd keys only for a plist **inside the signed app bundle**, so it cannot carry a per-pause time. Writing a plist to `~/Library/LaunchAgents` with `launchctl bootstrap` would work, but it is the unmanaged path that NR §1 ("Login item" row) replaces with `SMAppService` (and macOS 27 refuses quarantined plists).
    - Registering may show the system's "Background Items Added" notification, and the user can disallow it in Login Items; on macOS 27 a "Background App Activity" off-switch also stops it. If `status` is `.requiresApproval` (or `register()` throws `SMAppServiceErrorDomain` code 1, "Operation not permitted", which is how approval-pending shows up), the pause sheet says "If LockPlus quits unexpectedly, protection resumes the next time it opens", the previous launch-time behaviour.
  - Pause is never automatic.
- **Manual connect of another profile** makes it the enabled config, which suspends the auto profile.
  - When the user later disconnects it, the app (if running) re-enables the auto profile and restores its on-demand state.
  - The UI explains: "Auto-connect resumes when you disconnect Work".
  - **E2E-3 (measured on 26.6.2 and 27.0.1): NE does NOT suspend the other configuration's on-demand, and that blocks the started one.** While another of our configurations has on-demand enabled, an interface change (en0 down/up, a Wi-Fi change) makes nesessionmanager drop the primary interface ("en0 => (null)") and it never sees it return ("(null) => en0" only after the session ends). The pending or connected kill-switch session's en0-scoped pass policies are never re-added, Drop-All stays, and the kernel marks every new tunnel-process socket defunct (`necp_socket_find_policy_match: Marking socket … as defunct`): a held start sends nothing, a connected one never comes back. The auto profile's own session is unaffected, and without another on-demand configuration both recover (held start 9.6–15.7 s, connected 11.1 s). **As built:** every start from the app first sets `isOnDemandEnabled = false` on every other configuration (a pause, not a §10.4 suspension) and waits 1 s for nesessionmanager to process that change (200003 showed a configuration change landing inside the pending kill-switch start has the same effect); while another profile is starting or active, no path re-enables it (`ProfilesStore.onDemandPlan` holds it back: the end of a suspension, a settings re-save); the auto profile is restored when that profile ends, when its start fails at once, or at the next launch if nothing else is active. A suspension ends on a change of the network's physical interfaces (de-duplicated, "none" while there are none), not on a status flip: our own kill-switch start turns the app's path `unsatisfied` and lists en0 twice, which 200003 still counted as a network change. The headless resume restarts a manual profile without re-enabling other configurations' on-demand. **Residual:** a start from System Settings (not through the app) still meets the NE behaviour.

  **Review 2026-10-30 (`reviews/2026-10-30-fable-ondemand-pause.md`), as built:**
  - **Durable pause record.** `AppSettings.onDemandPausedByStart` lists the configurations a start paused. The ID is written (through, `writeSynchronously`) BEFORE its pause; `restoreIfIdle` restores exactly those (only ones that still exist and whose plan still wants on-demand; the rest are dropped) and clears them. A failed restore is noted in Diagnostics, stays recorded, and is retried on every status event and at launch; the Auto-Connect pane says "Auto-connect is off; LockPlus couldn't turn it back on." while the manager disagrees with the plan and nothing holds it back. Pause protection takes the record over into `pausedState`; the headless resume records what it leaves off. One restore function and one predicate (`othersBusy`: another profile starting, active, switching in, or awaiting NE's restart after a crash) serve `holdsBackOnDemand`, the restore and the deferral of `load()`.
  - **Only this user's configurations are paused** (`stored.ownerUID == ownerUID`). **Residual:** another user's on-demand configuration can still trigger the NE bug (fail-closed, not a leak). *E2E-4 U3: `loadAllFromPreferences` does return other users' configurations; U13: any real change of one during our pending start breaks it the same way.*
  - **A failed pause is a start failure** ("Auto-connect of X couldn't be paused; not connecting."); whatever was paused already comes back.
  - **Crash of the manual profile:** superseded by review 2 below (R1); the first build's 1.5 s grace was shorter than NE's measured restart.
  - **Settle** is relative to the last manager mutation of any origin (`SerializedVPNManager.waitUntilSettled`, 1 s); `load()` makes no manager changes (drift re-saves, orphan sweep) while anything starts or runs and runs them when idle. Saves that change nothing are skipped.
  - **Races:** after pause and settle the statuses are checked again; an on-demand start of another profile that landed meanwhile turns the start into a switch. A start with no status for 30 s stops holding the auto profile back. A second Connect while one is in flight is ignored (*review 4: of any profile, not only the same one*). A switch away from the auto profile pauses first and records no Disconnect suspension; the auto profile returns with the record when the other ends. The pane promises "resumes when you disconnect X" only while a recorded (or imminent, in the start window) pause holds.
  - **Headless resume** verifies the profile through the same `prepareForStart` (kill-switch flags read back); if it can't, nothing starts and everything paused for the pause comes back.
  **Second review 2026-10-30 (`reviews/2026-10-30-fable-ondemand-pause-2.md`), as built (R1–R12):**
  - **R1, crash of the manual profile.** `CrashRestartPolicy.decide` returns `.expectSystemRestart` for a kill-switch profile without on-demand rules (NE restarts it itself, ≈2.0–2.9 s after `.disconnected`, never earlier). On a fresh crash the disconnect then stays in `awaitingRestart` (nothing restored, the auto profile held back) until the session is back (`handle()` clears it when the status turns active); a 30 s fallback restores if it is still `.disconnected` (NE never restarted it). *E2E-4 (U8: `.connecting` 0.98–1.04 s after `.disconnected` on 26 and 27): the fallback is 10 s (`systemRestartTimeout`).* The 1.5 s grace remains only for the app's own `.restart` decision (a profile WITH on-demand rules). Other skips (no kill switch, user action, restart limit) restore after the grace. **Residual:** a session restarted outside the app, or a crash while the app isn't running, meets the NE behaviour with the auto profile on (U8 measures the exact timing).
  - **R2/R3, one restore set.** The restore set is the pause record plus every profile whose plan wants on-demand while its manager is off (`wantsRestore`; Auto-Connect turned on or re-pointed during a session, a failed restore). It is evaluated from every status event while nothing is busy (no `restoring` flip when there is nothing to do). A rule edit or "Add Current Network" in a start window saves nothing (`resaveOnDemand` honours the same deferral as `load()`); `hasDeferredSync` is the single "run at idle" flag (`runDeferredSync`: `load()` then `resaveOnDemand()`, inside the restore task so a start's pause waits for it). `load()` re-checks the deferral before every mutation.
  - **R4.** `othersBusy` also reads the live manager statuses, so a session of a previous instance, System Settings or the headless agent counts from launch, whatever the order of `profiles.load()` and `connection.start()`.
  - **R5.** The end of a user pause and of an extension update hand paused on-demand back through the record only (`returnOnDemand`: record, then `connect(target)` or `restoreIfIdle()`); nothing is enabled beside an active or starting session.
  - **R6/R8.** The headless resume waits the settle after its own saves before it starts (cap 2 s: the 5 s watchdog); the app's wait is capped at 5 s. A configuration that never settles (a steady stream of `NEVPNConfigurationChange`) is no start: fail closed, noted ("kept changing; not connecting. Try again in a moment."), what was paused comes back.
  - **R7/R9/R10.** The 30 s no-status timeout also abandons its start's pre-start Task (a per-start token), so it can't start beside the restored profile. `fetchLastDisconnectError` is bounded (10 s, then treated as no crash). ~~A running profile's own manager is exempt from the `load()` deferral while nothing else starts or switches, so the PF 55 drift heal of the live profile still happens.~~ Superseded by review 3 (N3): a live session's flags are never saved.
  - **R11.** A queued settings write saves the value as of the write (latest wins); the record changes are one durable write.
  - **R12.** The extension restarts its path watcher at every start (fresh baseline) and compares interface names only (a type-label change is no arrival).
  - **Extension:** the path watcher runs from `startTunnel` (a new monitor at Connected resets the baseline); arriving at a network retries a pending WireGuard attempt or a retryable hold at once, never while there is none, at most 10 per session.

  **Third review 2026-10-30 (`reviews/2026-10-30-fable-ondemand-pause-3.md`), as built: one state machine (N1–N10).**
  - **Invariant.** No save of another own manager and no on-demand enabled on another own manager between the pause and the started session ending or failing. The running profile's own manager never gets a flag save while its session is live (L-KS-2); on-demand, rule and name saves only while it is `.connected` and nothing else is busy (S2 E9). *E2E-4: plus the protective flag heal while `.connected` (U7).*
  - **States** (`ConnectionStore.pending`, one entry per profile, one timer each, `startingTimeout` 30 s; the header comment of `ConnectionStore` draws the same machine):
    - *idle* → `.starting(issued: false)` on a Connect; → `.waitingForStop(of: old)` on a Connect while another profile is active (a switch: pause first, then stop it) or while the profile itself is still `.disconnecting` (N1b) *(E2E-4 fix: or while another profile is still `.disconnecting`)*; `.waitingForStop` → `.starting(issued: false)` at the old session's `.disconnected`, or after NE's Stopping budget (22 s); the app's own crash restart (`.restart`) enters `.starting(issued: true)` from `.awaitingRestart`;
    - `.starting(issued: false)`: prepare (flags verified), pause the others (record first), the profile's own on-demand back, settle (≤ 5 s), then `startVPNTunnel` → `.starting(issued: true)`; another profile active after the settle (F6) → `.waitingForStop` of it;
    - `.starting(issued: true)` → *idle* on any status (active: the session runs; otherwise the start ended);
    - `.starting(issued: false)` ignores a non-active status: it is a stale report of the previous session (a reload's replay, the old session's `.disconnected`) (N1a);
    - *E2E-4 fix:* a watched session's `.disconnecting` that is not the user's (and no entry of the profile) → `.awaitingRestart` at once (the fetch phase; `holdTeardown`, timer 22 s); the `.disconnected` below replaces it;
    - an observed disconnect that is not the user's → `.awaitingRestart` while the cause is read (≤ 10 s, timer 15 s), unless a start of the same profile is already pending or waits for exactly this stop (it holds everything itself and is not replaced); no fresh crash → *idle*; a fresh crash of a kill-switch profile without rules stays until NE's restart reports an active status, the timer (30 s from the decision), or its manager is removed (N7); the app's own restart (with rules) after the 1.5 s grace; the user's Connect of the same profile takes it over;
    - every entry ends on its timer, a failure, or a newer entry (a per-entry token: a Task that outlives its entry does nothing); the user's Disconnect ends a `.waitingForStop` (review 5: also a `.starting(issued: false)`, and so do Cancel and Pause);
    - *E2E-4 200011:* `.waitingForNetwork` (a start without a network: nothing issued or paused, not busy, no timer) and `.awaitingNetworkRestart` (NE's restart after "No network available": busy, no timer without a network, persisted); see the E2E-4 block below.
  - **Busy** = any entry (a start, a start waiting for a stop, a restart awaited) or any active status (ours or the live manager's; *E2E-4: any configuration's, another user's and a stray's included*; *E2E-4 fix: any LIVE status, `.disconnecting` included*). A Connect of a profile that is still `.disconnecting` waits like a switch and starts at its `.disconnected` (N1b, S2).
  - **Restore** (`restoreIfIdle`): only when nothing at all is busy (a profile that is itself starting or active is never restored, N3; nothing flips `restoring` while busy, N5) and no extension hand-over is under way (N2). The set is the record plus every plan that wants on-demand while its manager is off, computed once per pass; one `restore(id)`; a failure is noted and retried at the next status event.
  - **Deferral** (`ProfilesStore.mutationBlocked`, one closure): `load()` and `resaveOnDemand()` change no manager while busy, except the `.connected` profile's own on-demand/rules while nothing else is (never a `.connecting` one: NE's on-demand start, NE's restart, a System Settings start). A live manager that is behind (flags or revision) is never saved: a flags drift of a running session is noted in Diagnostics ("…while it was connected. LockPlus restores them before it connects again.") and healed at idle (`runDeferredSync`) or at the next start (`prepareForStart` verifies the flags) (N3, U7 reopened). *Superseded by E2E-4 for a drift that weakens a `.connected` session: healed at once (U7).*
  - **Extension update / reinstall (N2).** While `pendingResume` or `expectedUpdate` is set every on-demand plan is held (`AppSettings.extensionHandOver`), nothing is restored or dropped from the record; `resumeAfterUpdate` clears the markers in the same durable write that hands their ids to the record, then connects the profile that was connected.
  - **Settings durability (N4).** Every settings write goes through one ordered queue into `SettingsFileStore` and saves the value as of the write; a durable change (the record, the pause, the hand-over markers) awaits its write. Only the quit paths (`AppEnvironment.stop`, Sparkle's `prepareForInstall`) write on the calling thread; each write carries a sequence number and the file store drops one older than what is on disk.
  - **Crash decision (N6)** reads `includeAllNetworks` as the session was started with (verified at our start; read from the manager when a session we didn't start appears), not the manager's current, possibly drifted flags.
  - **Headless resume (N8)** records what stays off before the start and caps its settle by what is left of the 5 s budget (1 s reserved for the start, the write and the unregister): a slow run ends fail-closed through its own write, not in the watchdog's exit.
  - **Pause protection (N9)** turns off and lists only this user's configurations.
  - **The app owns "Connect on demand" (N10).** For every own configuration the app re-applies its plan: a manager whose plan wants on-demand while it is off (the checkbox cleared in System Settings, a failed restore) is turned back on at the next status event while idle, and every manager save the app makes carries the plan (held → off). The Auto-Connect pane is the only place to change it; the System Settings checkbox is overridden.

  **Fourth review 2026-10-30 (`reviews/2026-10-30-fable-ondemand-pause-4.md`), as built:**
  - **One start at a time (#1).** A Connect while any entry exists is ignored, except over its own profile's `.awaitingRestart`; before, the guard was per profile, so a Connect of Z inside X's pending kill-switch start paused (saved) X's own on-demand there and started Z beside X. A hand-back (`returnOnDemand`) whose connect is ignored leaves its ids recorded; they return when the pending start's session ends. The switch wait is a map entry (`.waitingForStop(of:)`, simplification 1).
  - **A Connect of a profile whose live status is active is no start (#5)** (no `prepareForStart` on a live manager, no `startVPNTunnel` into a live session). The sidebar's context menu offers Connect for every profile, the active one included; the menu bar does not (clicking the active profile disconnects).
  - **Hand-over (#2, #3).** Every clear of an extension hand-over marker restores what the marker held off (`ConnectionStore.endExtensionHandOver`: an install that didn't happen, an activation completed with nothing quiesced). A failed activation (refused, cancelled with no successor, the watchdog) or a reinstall's failed or cancelled deactivation hands back through `resumeAfterUpdate`: the installed extension keeps running the tunnels. Not once our reinstall removed it (or it was gone at the preflight): the hand-over stays, and the Auto-Connect pane says "Auto-connect is paused while the tunnel component is updated." whenever a marker holds the plans.
  - **Headless retry (#6).** A run that finds the target already live (the previous run's watchdog exit after the start) neither verifies nor starts it again; it records what stays off and clears the pause.
  - **No save of another manager while busy (#8).** An import, an editor save, a policy change or rename, the onboarding's first save and a delete's removal wait while another profile is starting or running (`saveManagerUnlessBlocked`; the delete's removal goes to the orphan sweep). The metadata is saved; the manager is "behind" until `runDeferredSync` or `prepareForStart`. *Review 5 #4:* a delete whose on-demand disable failed removes at once (noted in Diagnostics): an enabled on-demand configuration beside the session is the E2E-3 trigger itself.
  - `withDeadline` cancels its sleeper when the body wins (#4).

  **Fifth review 2026-10-30 (`reviews/2026-10-30-fable-ondemand-pause-5.md`), as built (nothing above LOW remained):**
  - **The user's Disconnect, Cancel and Pause end a start that hasn't been issued (#1)** (`cancelPendingStarts`: `.starting(issued: false)` and `.waitingForStop`); the start's Task sees its entry gone after each await and starts nothing; what it paused comes back at idle, or, under a pause, is handed to the pause's restore list. A start issued meanwhile is stopped by the pause like a running session; on-demand a cancelled start turned on meanwhile is turned off by the pause too.
  - **A Connect while NE is already Stopping waits (#2):** the live status and the handled event are both checked for `.disconnecting` (the active check already reads the live one).
  - **Watchdog hand-back (#3).** After the activation watchdog (sysextd never answered; a late `.completed` is ignored), the properties are read again: the tunnels go back only if the version that was installed at the quiesce is still the enabled entry and nothing awaits approval (`WatchdogHandBack`); otherwise the hand-over stays (the Auto-Connect pane says so) until "Try again". Other activation failures hand back as in review 4.
  - **Onboarding (#5):** a first save deferred while a VPN runs says when it happens instead of "done". The Sparkle abort logs after the hand-over ended (#6).
  - **The ignored Connect is visible (§3).** `ConnectionStore.startHold` derives why a Connect would be ignored from `pending`: *preparing* (`.starting`), *waiting for a stop* (`.waitingForStop(of:)`), *awaiting a restart* (`.awaitingRestart` after the crash decision), *reading a disconnect* (its fetch phase: only another profile's Connect is held). UI-CONCEPT row 12a shows the first three while the status is `.disconnected`/`.invalid` (never "Connecting…": no `NEVPNStatus` exists yet), with Cancel except while a restart is awaited. Every Connect (hero, toolbar, sidebar context menu, menu bar, ⌘K) is disabled while held, with the reason as help; the UI is stricter than the store in one case (a Connect over the profile's own awaited restart is not offered: its prepare and pause would save managers inside NE's pending restart). `connect` returns whether it took the Connect; a hand-back whose connect was ignored because another start was in flight is noted in Diagnostics ("Work wasn't reconnected: …"). There is no Dock menu yet (UI-CONCEPT §8.2); it follows the same rule when built.
  **E2E-4 (2026-10-30, product build 200006 and the 200005 predecessor; LP-macOS-26 26.6.2 and LP-macOS-27 27.0.1; `native/e2e/RESULTS-E2E-4.md`, PENDING-FOLD 58), measured and decided:**

  | # | Question | Measured on 26 and 27 | Decision (as built) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | U13 | A REMOVAL of another configuration inside a pending kill-switch start | Breaks it exactly like a save: the start never connects, NECP defuncts the tunnel process's sockets, en0 isn't re-detected after a network change. **Any real configuration change** of another manager does it (an `excludeLocalNetworks` change on a manager with on-demand off too), not only on-demand. An unchanged save and a no-op on-demand off are harmless | A removal stays deferred to idle (review 4 #8); the residual below |
  | U2 | A save of another manager after the started session reports `.connecting` / `.connected` | `.connecting`: unsafe on both. `.connected`: on 26 the tunnel never came back after the next network change (3/3); on 27 it came back in 8–10 s | No post-start pause of a session we didn't start; every non-essential mutation waits while ANY configuration is live (below) |
  | U3 | Does `loadAllFromPreferences` return other users' configurations? | Yes; another administrator can save and remove them without a prompt | Ours are never touched by another user's app except through NE (admins are trusted, out of the threat model, §1.3 A2); our own sweep removes only this user's (below) |
  | U5 | Does an on-demand-only save make nehelper rewrite other fields (PF 55)? | No: an `isOnDemandEnabled`-only save changes no other field | Nothing to change |
  | U7 | A protocol-flag save on a CONNECTED session | Applied at once, no teardown: `includeAllNetworks` off → the LAN reachable within 2 s; on again → blocked within 1 s. So a drift weakens the live session, and a protective re-save takes effect at once | **Reversed (review 3 N3):** the running profile's own manager whose flags are WEAKER than its plan is healed immediately when `.connected` (below) |
  | U8 | NE's own restart of a crashed kill-switch profile without on-demand rules | `.disconnected` → `.connecting` after 0.98–1.04 s on both OSes | The R1 fallback shrinks from 30 s to **10 s** (`systemRestartTimeout`, ≈10× margin) |
  | U9 | `NEVPNConfigurationChange` per save | Exactly one per real save (other users' changes included) while the listener reloads; an unchanged save raises none | The R8 settle cap (5 s) stands; a steady stream needs steady real changes |
  | U12 | After a failed replacement activation (code 8), does the old extension keep working? | Yes through NE: it stays enabled and starts profiles; but the new app can't reach it over XPC (the Mach service name is per build, `…tunnel.v200006` vs `…v200005` → 4099) | Hand-back via NE kept; the honest "couldn't update" state (below) |
  | U14 | Does the old entry stay enabled after a failed replacement? | Yes, on 26 and 27 | Review 4 #3's assumption holds; the watchdog's fresh read (review 5 #3) stays |

    *E2E-4 200011 (no-network restart), fixed after the run, as built:* NE refuses a start without a network ("No network available", `NEVPNConnectionErrorDomain` 2; the app sees only `.disconnecting` → `.disconnected`, the 4 ms `.connecting` is never delivered) and, for a kill-switch session without on-demand rules, restarts it by itself with no start command when any interface returns (`.connecting` 1.1–1.3 s after the link is up, after 10, 30 or 120 s); a stop of the disconnected session cancels that restart, code 2 stays sticky after it, and a profile without the kill switch is not restarted. The app restored the paused auto profile at the refusal's `.disconnected`, so the restart ran beside on-demand ON (the E2E-3 failure mode). Two layers:
    - **No `startVPNTunnel` without a network.** `startNow`, and `runStart` again right before the start, check the app's NWPathMonitor (`ConnectionStore.networkAvailable`: an interface other than a tunnel, the `isArrival` identity; unknown before the first reading = available). Without one the start waits in `.waitingForNetwork`: nothing is issued and **nothing is paused** (the pause happens at the actual start, as for every start): the wait has no time limit, and a quit or crash meanwhile must not leave the auto profile off for it; NE's on-demand can't start anything without a network, and an on-demand start landing as the network returns meets the start's existing F6 switch. The entry is therefore **not busy** (restores and deferred mutations run; NE has nothing pending), but it is a start: every other Connect is held (one start at a time). When an interface returns the start runs normally (prepare, pause, settle) after `endpointPushSettle`. If the network goes during the prepare or settle, the start goes back to waiting and what it paused comes back. Row 12a: "Waiting for a network to connect X…" / "Not protected until a network is available.", Cancel.
    - **Safety net, `.awaitingNetworkRestart`.** A disconnect not caused by a stop of ours, of a session whose session-time kill switch is on and whose manager has no on-demand rules, with error code 2 (`holdForNetworkRestart`): our issued start whose first status was `.disconnecting` (`issuedEnding`) or `.disconnected` (the error is read after the `.startEndedEarly` hold is entered; code 2 converts it), and any watched session (NE's, System Settings', ours seen active). While the path has no interface nothing is restored, with no timer; once it has one, NE's restart is awaited (its active status ends the hold) with `systemRestartTimeout` (10 s) as the fallback, disarmed again if the network goes. Busy, so no restore, mutation or other start's pause runs inside it. Row 12a: "X connects when a network is available." / "Not protected until a network is available.", Cancel = a user stop (`stopVPNTunnel`, issued synchronously before the restore), which cancels NE's restart. A Connect of another profile stops X the same way, then proceeds; X's own Connect is held (NE connects it). Pause stops X too and records X as the profile to reconnect. No "stopped unexpectedly" notice for it.
    - **Durability.** `AppSettings.networkRestartHold` is written durably (awaited, like the pause record) when the hold begins and cleared with it. At launch the hold is re-entered before the launch's restore if the configuration still exists, is `.disconnected`, has the kill switch and no on-demand (otherwise the record is dropped); its fallback arms only after the first path reading with an interface. The headless resume leaves everything alone while the held session is live (`.networkRestartPending`, retried next minute), and otherwise stops it (cancelling NE's restart) before it restores anything, unless it is the profile it restarts itself.
    - **Residuals.** A refusal while LockPlus isn't running (NE's or System Settings' start) meets NE's restart with whatever on-demand is on. If NWPathMonitor reports an interface that NE considers unusable, the start is issued and refused; the safety net holds then, and the 10 s fallback counts from the hold (re-disarmed when the monitor catches up). A sticky code 2 read at a later unrelated end of a kill-switch session (a stop elsewhere) holds for the fallback after the network is present (≤ 10 s), or until it is, which costs nothing while there is no network.

- **Turning Auto-Connect on** (the toggle, or picking another profile while it is on) ends that profile's Disconnect suspension (E2E-3); while one is active the Auto-Connect pane says so, why, and how to end it.
- Disconnecting the auto profile from our UI while on-demand is active sets `isOnDemandEnabled = false` until the next network change: "Paused until you join another network". Otherwise on-demand would immediately reconnect.
  - **As built (draft 8, app-root review H2):** the first build turned on-demand off on every Disconnect and never back on. Now a user Disconnect records the suspended profile IDs and the current network signature in `settings.json` (`onDemandSuspended`, `onDemandSuspendedNetwork`). `NetworkWatcher` (one `NWPathMonitor` on its own queue; the signature is the path status plus the physical interfaces in use, tunnels excluded, so our own connect isn't a change) restores on-demand when the signature differs. Because the record is persisted, the suspension also ends at the next launch if the Mac is on another network by then. Disconnecting a **manual** profile re-enables the auto profile (above). A failed on-demand disable in `stop()` is reported, not ignored.
  - **Pause and quit (draft 8, app-root review H4, M7):** "Resume Protection and Quit" and "Disconnect and Quit" finish (bounded) before the menu action calls `terminate` (§11.3); `pausedState` is cleared only after the restore has run; pausing while paused keeps the original restore list.
- **SSID → specific profile map** (Go `SSIDTunnelMap`) is **cut from v2.0** (§21). Migration reports the Go map as "not migrated" (§13.1).
- **No on-demand keep-alive rule (draft 9, D9-8; Conflicts bj).** Draft 7.3 planned an `.any` connect rule on a connected kill-switch profile to restart a crashed provider. S2 E1 showed NE restarts it by itself under `includeAllNetworks` (open 2.45–2.86 s), and that **any** on-demand Connect rule disables that restart (open 4.1–4.5 s on 27 until an on-demand trigger, ≥ 30 s on 26). It is not built. Consequence: **a kill-switch auto-connect profile (any profile with on-demand rules) has no automatic restart after a provider crash**; it stays open until a Network.framework client's connect triggers on-demand or the user acts. Documented residual (§20 risk 24). ~~An app-side `startVPNTunnel` on `pluginFailed` (RS2 2) is not built in v2.0.~~
- **App-side restart after a provider crash (draft 10, PF 52; Conflicts bo): built, bounded** (`CrashRestartPolicy` in `ConnectionStore`). On an observed `.disconnected` with `NEVPNConnectionErrorDomain` 12 (`pluginFailed`), after a **1.5 s** grace, the app starts the profile only if it is **still `.disconnected`**, has `includeAllNetworks` **and** on-demand enabled (exactly the case NE doesn't restart, E1+od), the user didn't stop it, no switch or pause is pending, and **fewer than 3** such restarts happened in **10 min** (a crash loop then waits for the user). The start has on-demand semantics (no `lp.manual`: the start latch applies, no prompt, cached endpoints), as NE's own restart would. NE's own restart (no on-demand rules, ≈2.0–2.9 s after `.disconnected`) is never raced: for that case the app waits for the session instead of a grace (§10.4, review 2). It works only while the app runs; without it the residual is unchanged.
- **Saving a connected manager is safe (S2 E9, draft 9).** Saving `onDemandRules`, `isOnDemandEnabled` or `localizedDescription` on the connected manager keeps the session on 26 and 27 (same PID, no traffic gap), so the §10.4 rule changes and rename-while-connected need no deferral (N5). Flag changes by the user stay disconnected-only (L-KS-2). ~~No path saves a live manager's protocol flags, including the drift heal (review 3, N3).~~ *E2E-4 (U7): NE applies a flag save to a connected session at once, so a drift that weakens the running profile is healed on the connected session (above); every other flag change waits for the session to end.* E9 and U7 measured `.connected` only: a manager inside its own pending start (`.connecting`) is never saved.
- **On-demand at boot means after the first login (S4, draft 9).** NE did not start an app-created configuration at the login window (2–3 min, even with root traffic); it started 3.5–6 s after login.
- **Assumption A-OD-1 (NR Q1):** `ssidMatch` in on-demand rules is evaluated by the system without our app holding Location authorization. Evidence so far (ref/networkextension C28): the on-demand engine evaluates SSID rules in a system process, and a developer reports `.wiFi` + `ssidMatch` starting the VPN, while the **app's** own CoreWLAN SSID read needs Location under a linked-on-or-after policy; no Apple statement either way. Spike S1 validates it, first with a `.mobileconfig` and then with our app.
  - **Fallback:** the app-assisted mode (CoreWLAN + Location) drives `startVPNTunnel`/`stopVPNTunnel` and on-demand toggling for all rules. It is documented as requiring the app to be running.
- Adding SSIDs: the user types them; "Add current network" needs Location and is optional.
- Profiles that need interactive auth cannot be the auto profile (§8.4).

### 10.5 IPv6 for v4-only full tunnels (M5)

A full-tunnel profile that assigns only IPv4 (WG `AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0` without `::/0`; OVPN `redirect-gateway def1` without IPv6 settings) leaves the LAN's IPv6 default route in place. With the kill switch **on**, `includeAllNetworks` captures it (LK-09). With the kill switch **off**, every IPv6 destination goes around the tunnel.

**Decision (draft 3, N4; replaces draft 2's "whatever the kill-switch setting"):** the blackhole **follows the kill switch**. It applies to a v4-only full-tunnel profile when `killSwitch` is on (the default for full tunnels, §3.1), or when the per-profile toggle **"Block IPv6 without the kill switch"** (`blockIPv6WithoutKillSwitch`, off by default) is on. With the kill switch off and the toggle off, IPv6 goes to the LAN, exactly as in the Go app, which blocked v6 only with its kill switch on.
- Why not always: the blackhole drops silently (no ICMPv6 unreachable comes back), so clients **without** Happy Eyeballs (many CLI tools, some games, older SDKs) wait for a full connect timeout per AAAA address before falling back. And `::/0` into the tunnel also captures **LAN IPv6** (on-link ULA/GUA hosts, printers, NAS), which a user who turned the kill switch off usually wants reachable. Both costs are accepted where the user asked for strict protection, not otherwise.
- The toggle is policy (`NetworkPolicy`, mirrored as `providerConfiguration.blockIPv6`), so it obeys L-KS-2: it changes only while disconnected. The import report and Detail say which case applies: "IPv6 is blocked while connected (this profile tunnels IPv4 only)" or "IPv6 traffic bypasses the VPN (this profile tunnels IPv4 only; turn on the kill switch or 'Block IPv6' to prevent this)".

When it applies, `NetworkSettingsBuilder` routes `::/0` into the tunnel as a **blackhole**:
- `ipv6Settings` gets a unique local address (`fdxx:…/128`, derived from the profile UUID) and `includedRoutes = [::/0]`.
- WireGuard: wireguard-go drops packets that match no peer's AllowedIPs, so the IPv6 traffic dies inside the tunnel.
- OpenVPN: openvpn3 reroutes IPv6 only when `ifconfig-ipv6` was pushed, so a v4-only full tunnel arrives as `tun_builder_reroute_gw(v4: true, v6: false)`; the shim makes the same plan, and also when `tun_builder_set_allow_family(AF_INET6, false)` reports `block-ipv6` (openvpn3 adds `block-ipv6` itself when `allowUnusedAddrFamilies == "no"`).
- A cleaner v4-only IPv6 block (`NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings.includeAllNetworks = .ipv6`-style per-family settings) is declared in the 27.0 SDK but unavailable on macOS; it is listed in §21 and would need the §10.1 precedence rule.
- Effect: dual-stack apps fall back to IPv4 through Happy Eyeballs after the IPv6 attempt fails; other clients see the timeouts described above.
- With the kill switch on and `allowLAN`, `excludeLocalNetworks` keeps exempting local IPv6 despite the `::/0` route (S2 E8, draft 9: on-link link-local and ULA hosts reachable, global IPv6 blocked with 0 packets on en0).
- Split-tunnel profiles are untouched: IPv6 not covered by the tunnel goes to the LAN by design.
- Tests: LK-09 in three variants (kill switch on; off; off with the toggle); §15.1 `NetworkSettingsBuilder` table test: the blackhole appears exactly when `isFullTunnel && !hasIPv6 && (killSwitch || blockIPv6WithoutKillSwitch)`.
