## 11. UI architecture

### 11.1 App structure

The visual design is UI-CONCEPT (Direction B, O6). This section is the architecture behind it.

```swift
@main struct LockPlusApp: App {
    @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor(AppDelegate.self) var delegate
    var body: some Scene {
        // 1. Hidden helper FIRST: it gives AppKit code a SwiftUI context for openSettings/openWindow.
        Window("LockPlusBridge", id: "bridge") { SceneBridge().frame(width: 0, height: 0) }
            .windowResizability(.contentSize)
            .defaultLaunchBehavior(.presented)
            .restorationBehavior(.disabled)
        Window("LockPlus", id: "main") { MainView().environment(delegate.env) }
            .defaultSize(width: 920, height: 620)
            .windowResizability(.contentMinSize)            // MainView sets minWidth 720, minHeight 480
            .defaultLaunchBehavior(.suppressed)              // menu-bar app: no window at login unless asked
        WindowGroup("Edit Profile", for: Profile.ID.self) { $id in EditorWindow(id: id) }
            .restorationBehavior(.disabled)                  // §11.4: secrets are never restored
        Settings { SettingsView().environment(delegate.env) }   // AFTER the bridge (order matters since 15.5, so on every supported OS)
    }
}
```

- Scene order and the bridge follow ref/swiftui-appkit §4 (items 4–5): a SwiftUI `Window` used as the primary scene quits the app when it closes, so `AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed` returns `false` and the hidden bridge is the first scene. "Settings…" from the status menu posts `.lpOpenSettings`; the bridge view calls `AppActivation.becomeRegular()` and then `openSettings()`. `showSettingsWindow:` has been dead since macOS 14 and is not used (S15: it returns `true` and opens nothing).
  - **S15 on 27 (26 pending on the VM):** closing "main" keeps the app alive and drops it back to `.accessory`; Settings opens from the status menu with no window open, from inside an open menu, via `@Environment(\.openSettings)` in the header's `NSHostingView` and via `SettingsLink`. The bridge does **not** have to stay ordered in for `openSettings` on 27, so the 1×1 off-screen fallback is unnecessary there. **Keep it ordered in anyway, together with the `false` delegate answer:** while the alpha-0 bridge is ordered in, AppKit never asks `applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed`; with the bridge ordered **out** and a delegate answering `true`, the app quits at launch (0.1 s). Both halves stay, so neither alone can cause that.
- `AppDelegate` owns `AppEnvironment` (all stores), `MenuBarController`, `UpdateController` and `LoginItemController`.
- **Activation policy (exact rule, item 6):** the app starts `.accessory` from `applicationWillFinishLaunching` (no `LSUIElement`). `AppActivation.becomeRegular()` switches to `.regular` and calls `NSApp.activate()` **before** opening any main, editor or Settings window (otherwise the window opens behind the frontmost app). On `NSWindow.willClose`, when no main, editor or Settings window remains (the bridge, sheets and panels don't count), it switches back to `.accessory`. `activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` is not used. Activation from a background event is not guaranteed, which is why auth prompts never rely on it (§8.4). **S15 (27):** with no user gesture, `NSApp.activate()` after `.regular` left the app inactive and the new Settings window behind the frontmost app. Safety net (draft 7): 0.4 s after opening a window, if `!NSApp.isActive`, call `orderFrontRegardless()` on it, so it is at least visible (it stays inactive). A real click in our own menu is a user gesture and is expected to activate; that is a manual check still open on 27 and 26.
- On quit, `applicationWillTerminate` calls `NSStatusBar.system.removeStatusItem` (L-MB-1, 92a45b5). Quit confirmation happens **only** for a quit from our own menu (§11.3); Sparkle's install, Homebrew's `quit:` and logout get `.terminateNow` (ref/sparkle C13, §5.4). *As built (draft 8):* the menu's Quit runs its dialog (and the bounded resume or disconnect) before it calls `terminate`, and `applicationShouldTerminate` only asks about unsaved profile editors.
- Navigation is a two-column `NavigationSplitView` (UI-CONCEPT §6.3): profiles are listed **in the sidebar**, then the sections, each with a shortcut:
  - **Profiles** (list in the sidebar, Detail on the right, Editor in its own window) ⌘1;
  - **Activity** (live chart + session history; draft 3's Statistics and History merged) ⌘2;
  - **Auto-Connect** ⌘3;
  - **Diagnostics** (health report: tunnel, DNS, IPv6, other VPNs, old helper; routes; problems; 2.0.2: the Connection Test, §11.5) ⌘4;
  - **Logs** ⌘5.
- Settings window tabs (UI-CONCEPT §6.13): **General** (launch at login, open window at login, language, appearance, notifications), **Menu Bar** (rate label, icon style, "Show in menu bar"), **Profiles** (new-profile defaults, export all), **Advanced** (the app's log level, release candidates, reinstall tunnel component, export diagnostics, uninstall, debug submenu in dev builds), **About**. **Appearance** (System / Light / Dark, default System) sets `NSApp.appearance` for every window and applies live; the 1.x theme carries over to it at migration. The menu bar status item always follows the menu bar, not this setting.
- `LoginItemController` (ref/xpc-servicemanagement C15): the "Launch at login" toggle reflects `SMAppService.mainApp.status == .enabled`, re-read every time Settings appears (there is no change notification). `.requiresApproval` shows the toggle on with "Allowed in System Settings › Login Items" and a button calling `SMAppService.openSystemSettingsLoginItems()`; `.notFound` (observed after a user disables the item) and `.notRegistered` show off. Register on toggle-on (`kSMErrorAlreadyRegistered` = success; error code 1 = approval pending), `unregister(completionHandler:)` on toggle-off (`kSMErrorJobNotFound` = success). Never auto-register (NR pitfall 14).
- **Preview mode (draft 8; APP-ROOT.md; Fable app review M1).** A "no extension" preview runs the real app root (stores, actions, derived state, menu bar, windows) over simulated backends: simulated activation, NE managers and XPC, an in-memory keychain, a reset preview data directory, a Go-migration fixture, and nothing installed, saved or registered. It exists in **Debug builds only** (`#if DEBUG`): a Release build ignores `LP_PREVIEW_MODE`, `-LPPreviewMode` and the XCTest environment and always uses the live backends, `PreviewBackends`/`PreviewUpdater` aren't compiled into Release, `verify.sh static` fails if preview code is in the Release app, and a UnitRelease test asserts it. Before the fix the shipped app could have shown a fake "Protected". Under XCTest (Debug) the host always uses the preview backends and submits no system-extension request. Launcher: `Tools/dev/preview.sh`.
- **Opening files (2.0.2, D10.4-7).** `.ovpn`, `.conf` and `.zip` open from Finder (double-click, Open With) and by a drop on the Dock icon (document types: §2.5). `AppDelegate.application(_:open:)` hands the URLs to `OpenDocumentRouter` (`@MainActor`): a cold launch's open event arrives before the environment exists, so the router queues until `environmentReady(env)` (called after `env.start()`); non-file URLs are dropped and logged, duplicates removed, at most 1000 URLs kept in memory; the pure `plan(_:)` answers `.importFiles`, `.tooMany(n)` (more than **20** files over all queued events: the main window opens with "Open at most 20 files at a time.") or `.nothing`. A flush calls `openMainWindow()` (switches to `.regular`, activates) and then the ordinary `importFiles`, i.e. the drag-into-window path: the same caps, the zip read in the validator service, the preview or batch sheet, and **nothing is saved or provisioned before the user's Confirm**. A folder gets the importer's folder message. The "Edit Profile" `WindowGroup` has `.handlesExternalEvents(matching: [])`, so an open never spawns an empty editor window (E2E-8 O7 checks there is exactly one main window; fallback if SwiftUI still routes the event to a scene: a `kAEOpenDocuments` handler in `applicationWillFinishLaunching` feeding the same router). Rejected: `DocumentGroup`/`NSDocument` (LockPlus has no documents), `onOpenURL` (delivered to a scene, races the bridge window), exported UTIs.
- **No QR import (2.0.2, D-3).** It never existed; the two "Import QR Code Image…" menu items, the onboarding button and the drop overlay's QR text are removed ("Drop .conf, .ovpn or .zip"); `ImportPanel.run` has no image mode.
- **One GUI instance (draft 8, Fable app review L5).** The `instance.lock` is advisory; after its retries a second instance shows "LockPlus is already running" and quits.
- Onboarding is a sheet on first launch (UI-CONCEPT §6.14):
  1. welcome;
  2. install the tunnel component (activation and approval);
  3. allow the VPN configuration (the first `saveToPreferences` triggers the system prompt);
  4. import, offering the Go migration (§13) if detected, file/zip (2.0.2: the dead "QR Image…" button is removed, D-3), or the `/etc/wireguard` scan (port of `scanner.go`);
  5. done, with the notification permission request (§11.7) and the menu-bar callout.

### 11.2 State management

All stores are `@MainActor @Observable`. They are driven **only** by `NEVPNStatus` notifications, XPC results and the app's own pause state (L-LC-4).

| Store | Source of truth | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ProfilesStore` | `ProfileStore` actor + `ManagerStore` | `NEVPNConfigurationChange` → reload |
| `ConnectionStore` | `NEVPNStatusDidChange` per manager (filtered to that manager's current `connection`, below); `fetchLastDisconnectError` (completion form) only on an **observed** `.disconnected` transition (§5.5, sticky); `tunnelSnapshot` (`lastError`/`lastErrorAt` at launch) | Exposes `activeProfileID`, `status`, `snapshot`, `lastError`, and the **derived state** (below); persists `lastQuitAt` in `settings.json` |
| `PauseStore` (or folded into `ConnectionStore`) | `settings.json` `pausedUntil`/`pausedState` | so the hero, the menu and the Dock menu read one source (UI-CONCEPT §9 item 7) |
| `StatsStore` | XPC `statistics` polling (§7.7) | Owns the `RateMeter`; `current: Rate?` and `samples: [RateSample]` are **separate** properties so the rate text and the chart invalidate independently |
| `ExtensionStore` | `SystemExtensionManager.state` + `hello` | Draft 7: `link: .validated / .reconnecting(since:) / .unavailable`, from the §5.4 interruption and respawn-throttle handling |
| `AuthCoordinator` | `tunnelEvent(authRequired)` + `pendingAuthPrompt` + `prepareStartAuth` | Single sheet; queues by promptID. Draft 9 (§8.4): every prompt during a connect is answered **into the pending start** (no second start, no `lp.promptID`); known-interactive profiles may prompt before `startVPNTunnel` (`prepareStartAuth`, then one start that takes the answer); Cancel on an in-start prompt is also a Disconnect |
| `HistoryStore`, `SettingsStore`, `LogsStore`, `DiagnosticsStore` | files / XPC | |

- **As built (draft 8; APP-ROOT.md):** the composition root is `AppEnvironment` (live or, in Debug, preview backends; one `UIEnvironment`); `UIBinder` maps stores to the UI models (pure `UIMapping`, Observation re-arm). Every store reaches NE through `SerializedVPNManager` (§3.4). `ConnectionStore` drops a snapshot only when both epochs are nonzero and from the same session, and resets the epoch floor per session (app-root review H6, L4); user stops expire, and a sticky `fetchLastDisconnectError` is cross-checked against `lastErrorAt` (M8). `LogsStore` pages log reads instead of rescanning 24 h every 5 s (M10). `ExtensionStore` exposes the client's own link status instead of mirroring it. `AuthCoordinator.lastError` re-shows a prompt whose answer failed (§8.4).
- **Draft 10 (E2E-1, PF 50–53).** `ProfilesStore.protectionMismatch(id)` (the manager's flags differ from the metadata, §3.4) makes the derived-state input `killSwitch = false` and sets `ProfileItem.protectionRepairing`, which shows the "Restoring this profile's protection settings…" strip on a kill-switch profile; nothing claims the kill switch while it holds, and `prepareForStart` refuses a kill-switch connect that stays drifted (`.killSwitchNotApplied`). `ConnectionStore` also owns the held-start push (`pushFreshEndpointsIntoHeldStart`, on a `NetworkWatcher` change and `didWake`, §9.3), the bounded crash restart (`CrashRestartPolicy`, §10.4) and `restartedAfterCrash`: a `.connected` within 120 s of an observed crash, without a user Connect or Disconnect in between, sets it, and the hero shows the info strip "Reconnected after a tunnel process restart." (UI-CONCEPT §6.4); the user's Connect or Disconnect, or the next disconnect, clears it.
- **2.0.2 (D10.4-6, D10.4-10).** `ConnectionStore.runStart` arms the extension (`StartArming.arm`, §7.2) after the settle, the network check and the active-session checks, immediately before `managers.start`; `gone()` and the network are re-checked after the await; a failed arm is `fail(id, error)` and nothing starts; `lastArmedAt[id]` records the arm. A 225 is read like a 222 (`readRefusal`, `checkNoNetworkRefusal`, the disconnect handler; its own freshness rule, never for a connected session; never "stopped unexpectedly"). The automatic-retry fix: `prepareForStart(_:admissible:)`, `pauseOtherOnDemand(except:token:)` and `restoreOwnOnDemand` re-check `startMutationAllowed(id, token)` inside the serialization (the attempt token is current and, for an automatic retry, `!othersBusy(except:)`); a refused automatic retry ends with `abandonAutomaticRetry` (Diagnostics "didn't retry …"), also from `failPause`. `ProfilesStore.pendingRollbacks[id]` holds `{metaRevision, managerRevision}` (memory only) and the rollback compares against the manager's revision. `DiagnosticsStore` owns the connection self-test (`runSelfTest`, §11.5).
- A connect click calls `session.startVPNTunnel(options:)`. The button shows "Connecting…" **only** because `NEVPNStatus` says `.connecting`. There is no optimistic UI state that can drift (7a6e365, cfc7fe9).
- **Derived state (F-4).** `ConnectionStore.derivedState` is a pure function of `(NEVPNStatus, killSwitch, lastError, snapshot.phase/attempt/nextRetryAt/holdReason/holdBeforeConnected/startLatch, awaitingApproval, pausedUntil, ExtensionStore.state, ExtensionStore.link)`; the full table with glyphs and copy is UI-CONCEPT §6.6. It is the **only** mapping from engine state to UI state, it is unit-tested row by row (§15.1), and the menu bar, the menu header, the hero and the sidebar all read it. Key rows: `.connecting` + `phase == .awaitingAuth` → "Sign in to connect <profile>" with the sheet (draft 9: the prompt answers into the pending start), "No traffic leaves this Mac until you sign in or disconnect" with the kill switch (S2 E14a); **`.connecting` + `holdReason != nil`** (draft 9, the withheld start, S2 E14) → "Blocked — <profile> couldn't connect: <error>", with retry text while a retryable failure retries, or "<error>. Auto-connect is paused", never "Connecting…"; `.reasserting` + kill switch + `holdReason == nil` → "Blocked — reconnecting" with attempt and countdown; `.reasserting` + `holdReason != nil` → "Blocked — <error>" with **no** retry text (draft 3's UI showed retries for a state that never retries); `.disconnected` + a `.hard` `snapshot.startLatch` → the error with "Auto-connect is paused". **`.disconnected` is never "Blocked" (draft 9):** S2 measured a cancel and a failed start as open, and the extension no longer does either under the kill switch, so draft 6–8's rows 13/13b (Restore Internet, "Sign in to connect" after a failed start), the `blockMode`/E3/E14 inputs and `pendingPrompt` are gone. "Blocked" never comes from `.reasserting` alone (S2 E4r). `ExtensionStore.link` (draft 7): `.connected` + `link == .reconnecting` → "Reconnecting to the tunnel process…" (UI-CONCEPT §6.6 row 4a), because after a provider crash `NEVPNStatus` keeps saying `.connected` for ~5 s (§5.4, S2 E1).
- **Store rules (ref/swift-concurrency SC16):**
  - Notification observers use `queue: .main` and extract `Sendable` values (status, `ObjectIdentifier`) before `MainActor.assumeIsolated` (SAFETY: queue `.main`), or iterate `NotificationCenter.notifications(named:)` in a `@MainActor` task.
  - **`NEVPNStatusDidChange` arrives once per live `NEVPNConnection` object (S5, draft 7):** every `loadAllFromPreferences()` mints new connection objects, and with `object: nil` each transition was delivered 3–4 times after three loads. The observer keeps a transition only if `ObjectIdentifier(note.object) == ObjectIdentifier(manager.connection)` for the manager `ManagerStore` currently holds (or registers with `object: manager.connection` and re-registers after every reload).
  - Every closure handed to XPC, NE or Dispatch from a store is `@Sendable` or built in a `nonisolated` function (§0 MUST; S5 and S15 crashes).
  - Each polling task (stats 1 Hz / 0.2 Hz, the 15 s captive re-probe once built, §10.4) has exactly one owner that cancels it on hide and in `deinit`, holds `[weak self]`, and sleeps with tolerance. Polling stops while no tunnel is active.
  - Stores never decode XPC payloads; actors do. CPU-heavy helpers called from UI code (the editor highlighter, the tokenizer; 2.0.2: the zip read is in the validator service) are `@concurrent` with `Sendable` inputs and outputs.
  - `MenuBarController` re-renders through `withObservationTracking`, re-armed in `Task { @MainActor in … }`. *Draft 7.1:* `Observations` and `Task.immediate` (26.0) are baseline now and may be used anywhere. The header keeps the re-arm pattern because S15 validated it while the menu tracks, and `Observations` delivers asynchronously and transactionally, which S15 did not test. Switching the header to `Observations` needs an S15 re-run.
  - The XPC callback sink (`AppCallbackSink`) is a nonisolated `Sendable` class that yields into an `AsyncStream<TunnelEvent>` (`.bufferingNewest(64)`) consumed by a `@MainActor` task owned by `AppEnvironment`; it is **never** `@MainActor` (a guaranteed trap on the first event). Dropping old events is safe: the app re-pulls `pendingAuthPrompt` and `tunnelSnapshot` on every status change.
  - Since Swift 6.2, `@Observable` skips notifications when an `Equatable` property is set to an equal value, so re-assigning an unchanged 1 Hz rate costs nothing.

### 11.3 MenuBarController (L-MB-1)

```swift
@MainActor final class MenuBarController: NSObject, NSMenuDelegate {
    private let item = NSStatusBar.system.statusItem(withLength: NSStatusItem.variableLength)
    private let menu = NSMenu()
    private let headerItem = NSMenuItem()
    private let headerHost: NSHostingView<MenuHeaderView>        // created ONCE, reused across opens
    private let header = MenuHeaderModel()                       // @Observable; the only thing the header reads
    private var observing = false                               // one withObservationTracking registration at a time
    private var menuIsOpen = false
    init(env: AppEnvironment) {
        headerHost = NSHostingView(rootView: MenuHeaderView(model: header))
        // default sizingOptions: `[]` makes fittingSize return {0, 0} (S15; Conflicts ah)
        headerHost.setAccessibilityElement(false)                // VoiceOver uses the duplicated standard items (Conflicts j)
        super.init()
        item.behavior = .removalAllowed                          // respects user removal; we must offer a way back
        item.autosaveName = "LockPlusStatusItem"                 // stable forever, or the user's choice is lost
        menu.delegate = self; menu.autoenablesItems = false
        headerItem.view = headerHost
        item.menu = menu                                         // native; no synthetic clicks, no event monitor (3f14acd)
    }
    func menuNeedsUpdate(_ menu: NSMenu) { header.refresh(from: env); resizeHeader(); rebuildStandardItems(keeping: headerItem) }
    func menuWillOpen(_ menu: NSMenu) {
        menuIsOpen = true; env.stats.addConsumer(.menu); menuOpenedThisLaunch = true // StatsStore polls at 1 Hz (§7.7)
        observeHeader()
    }
    func menuDidClose(_ menu: NSMenu) { menuIsOpen = false; env.stats.removeConsumer(.menu) }  // re-arm stops while closed
    /// No state timer (ref/swift-concurrency §10.2, Conflicts aa): re-render when ConnectionStore/StatsStore change.
    private func observeHeader() {
        guard !observing else { return }; observing = true
        withObservationTracking { header.refresh(from: env) } onChange: { [weak self] in
            Task { @MainActor in
                guard let self else { return }; self.observing = false
                self.resizeHeader()
                if self.menuIsOpen { self.observeHeader() }      // re-arm only while open
            }
        }
    }
    func render(state: DerivedState, rate: Rate?)                // glyph + label + accessibility label
}
```

- **Header (ref/swiftui-appkit §1.3, item 10–11):** the header item and its `NSHostingView` are created once; `menuNeedsUpdate` refreshes the header model and rebuilds only the standard items. Width is fixed at 300 pt; height = `fittingSize.height`, re-applied after each update (frame changes during tracking are honoured). **No state timer (draft 5, Conflicts aa):** the header re-renders through the `withObservationTracking` re-arm pattern (ref/swift-concurrency §10.2), driven by `ConnectionStore` and by `StatsStore`, which polls at 1 Hz while the menu is a registered consumer; the session clock ("02:14:07") is recomputed on each of those updates. **S15 (27):** main-actor work (a `@MainActor` task, `DispatchQueue.main.async`, an actor hop from an XPC-style queue) **is** serviced while the menu tracks; the header updated 7–8 times in ~8 s open (real pixels, screenshots 3 s apart), its frame never changed, and body evaluations stop while the menu is closed. The state timer is therefore dropped from the plan. **Fallback, kept only until S15 runs on 26:** a 1 Hz `Timer` added in `RunLoop.Mode.common` in `menuWillOpen` and invalidated in `menuDidClose` (a `.default`-mode timer froze during tracking, as expected). The hosting view keeps its **default** `sizingOptions` (Conflicts ah). The state line gets `lineLimit(2)` with the height following `fittingSize`: "Not protected" already truncated next to the gear and the switch in English at 300 pt. The header is opaque `lp.card` with a 12 % state tint, **never `glassEffect`** (the menu is already glass on 26+; "Glass can't directly sample other glass"). `NSHostingMenu` is not used for it. The header is **not an accessibility element**; its switch and its facts are duplicated by standard items (below) and by the status item's label (Conflicts j, corrected in draft 5).
- **Icon (item 8):** a template symbol from the custom `lockplus.lock` family, sized with `NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: ~15–16, weight: .medium)` and tuned by eye on 26 and 27 (30 pt measured). `NSStatusBar.thickness` (22 on 27) is never used for layout. Seven states, each a distinct silhouette or badge (UI-CONCEPT §7.2): unprotected, connecting/reasserting, protected, blocked, needs attention, paused, error-stopped. The **Color** icon style uses a non-template tile with a navy glyph. Color is never the only signal. While connecting, a 3-frame template sequence runs on a ~120 ms `.common` timer (`NSStatusBarButton` has no symbol-effect API); static with Reduce Motion (S15: works, and the Reduce Motion gating works). **The custom `lockplus.lock` family is a hard requirement (S15):** with stock SF Symbols the clock and xmark badges blur into similar dots at 16 px, Magic Replace between stock `lock.open` and `lock.fill`/`lock` falls back to down-up (no shackle morph), and Draw On on stock `lock.fill` renders as a fade. The custom family needs bolder, distinct badge shapes, a shared layer structure for the morph, and Draw annotations. An `NSImageView` overlay in the status button (option b) is rejected: it needs a transparent placeholder image or the item collapses, and it sits a few pixels low. This is the one `Timer` in `MenuBarController`: a frame clock for an animation, not a state re-render (Conflicts aa).
- **Rate label (item 9):** `button.attributedTitle` uses `NSFont.monospacedDigitSystemFont(ofSize: NSFont.smallSystemFontSize, weight: .regular)`; format per `menuBarRateLabel` (`↓1.2M ↑30K`, `↓1.2M`, or none), shown only while connected and hidden while blocked. `monospacedDigitSystemFont` fixes digit widths only (`K`, `M`, `,` stay proportional), so `item.length` is set to the widest possible label for the current locale, measured once with `NSAttributedString.size()`; the label never jitters (2d08dc8).
- `RateMeter` implements the baseline rule:
  ```swift
  struct RateMeter: Sendable {
      private var baseline: (rx: UInt64, tx: UInt64, t: ContinuousClock.Instant)?
      mutating func ingest(rx: UInt64, tx: UInt64, at t: ContinuousClock.Instant) -> Rate? {
          guard let b = baseline else { baseline = (rx, tx, t); return nil }
          let dt = (t - b.t).timeInterval; guard dt >= 0.5 else { return nil }   // bytes AND time skip together
          defer { baseline = (rx, tx, t) }                                       // commit together, one assignment
          return Rate(down: Double(rx &- b.rx) / dt, up: Double(tx &- b.tx) / dt) // counter reset → treat as 0
      }
      mutating func reset() { baseline = nil }                                   // after an XPC interruption (§5.4)
  }
  extension Duration {                                                          // LPModel; Duration has no `.seconds` instance member (SC15)
      var timeInterval: Double { Double(components.seconds) + Double(components.attoseconds) * 1e-18 }
  }
  ```
- **Visibility (item 7; corrects draft 3):** there is no reliable signal that the icon is hidden. `isVisible` stays `true` when the item is hidden for lack of space (the notch); `occlusionState` no longer reflects status-item visibility on macOS 27 (FB23349447); there is no API to read System Settings › Menu Bar › "Allow in the menu bar". Policy:
  1. open the main window once on first launch and after every update;
  2. record whether the menu was opened (`menuWillOpen`) in each launch (`menuOpenedLaunches`); if it wasn't in the last 5 launches, open the window at launch and show the Settings › Menu Bar helper ("The menu bar icon may be hidden…");
  3. observe `isVisible` by KVO (`.removalAllowed`: Cmd-drag removal sets it false) and offer **"Show in menu bar"** in Settings › Menu Bar, which sets `isVisible = true`, plus "Open LockPlus" in the Dock menu;
  4. keep the Dock/main-window path complete for every action (HIG: "Avoid relying on the presence of menu bar extras").
  - *Draft 8 (UI review H2, M5, M6):* turning "Show in menu bar" **off** really hides the item, after a warning ("Hide the menu bar icon?") because it may be the only UI; the standard items are rebuilt when the header's observation fires while the menu is open, and the header's countdowns read a 1 Hz tick.
- **Menu contents** (standard items below the header; UI-CONCEPT §6.2):
  - **directly below the header, always:** "Disconnect Work" while a tunnel is connecting/connected/reasserting/held, otherwise "Connect <last-used profile>". It performs the header switch's action, so VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access users have the switch as a standard item;
  - **while VoiceOver runs** (`NSWorkspace.shared.isVoiceOverEnabled`, read in `menuNeedsUpdate`, which runs before every open): a non-interactive status text item, `NSMenuItem.sectionHeader(title:)` (14.0+), carrying the header's facts in one sentence: state, profile, rates and the sparkline's last-minute summary ("Protected, Work, download 1.2 megabytes per second, upload 30 kilobytes per second; last minute average 800 kilobytes per second, peak 10 megabytes per second"). Sighted users don't see it, because the header already shows the same facts;
  - a "Profiles" section header (`NSMenuItem.sectionHeader`); each profile as an item with its state glyph (`preferredImageVisibility = .visible` under `#available(macOS 27, *)`, because macOS 27 hides all menu item images by default for apps linked on its SDK; item 3; S15 confirmed: unset, `.automatic` and `.hidden` all hide the image), `subtitle` (14.4+) for "Protected · 02:14", the active one checked; "More Profiles ▸" after 8; utility items stay `.automatic`;
  - "Enter Code for Acme…" (bold, ↩) when auth is pending;
  - **Pause rule (one rule for both docs, F-15, Conflicts v):** "Pause Protection ▸ 5 min / 15 min / 1 hour" is shown while any owned tunnel is connecting, connected or reasserting/held, **or** any owned manager has on-demand enabled; "Resume Protection Now (12 min left)" replaces it while paused (expiry is enforced by the resume agent even if the app is gone, §10.4); otherwise it is hidden (there is nothing to pause);
  - "Update Available…" when Sparkle's gentle reminder has an update (§12.1);
  - "Open LockPlus", "Settings…", "Quit LockPlus".
- **Quit** (only from our own menu, §11.1): if a tunnel is connected, "The tunnel stays connected after quitting. Disconnect?" — Keep / Disconnect / Cancel. While paused: "Resume protection and quit" (default) / "Quit and stay paused" / Cancel; "stay paused" leaves the resume agent registered, so the pause still ends on time. *Draft 8:* the dialogs run before the menu action calls `terminate`, and "Resume protection and quit"/"Disconnect" finish (bounded) first (app-root review H4); drafts 4–7.3 ran them inside `applicationShouldTerminate` with `.terminateLater`.

### 11.4 Editor

- An `NSTextView(usingTextLayoutManager: true)` (TextKit 2) in `NSViewRepresentable`. `TextEditor(text: Binding<AttributedString>)` is rejected: it is 26-only and has no substitution control.
- Disabled: smart quotes and dashes, text replacement, spelling correction, continuous spell checking, grammar checking, automatic link detection, automatic text completion, **Writing Tools** (`writingToolsBehavior = .none`: the buffer holds a private key), inline prediction (`inlinePredictionType = .no`). Font: monospaced. `usesFindBar = true`.
- **Never read `.layoutManager`**: it silently switches the view to TextKit 1. DEBUG builds observe `NSTextViewWillSwitchToNSLayoutManagerNotification` and `assertionFailure`. The gutter enumerates `textLayoutManager` fragments (not `NSRulerView`/`NSLayoutManager` samples) and uses its own gesture recognizer (macOS 27 moved `NSTextView` selection to gesture recognizers; no `mouseDown` overrides).
- Syntax highlighting is a `ConfigHighlighter` driven by **our own parsers**, run `@concurrent` with a 150 ms debounce, applied on the main actor as **rendering attributes** (`textLayoutManager.setRenderingAttributes`), not `textStorage` edits, so the undo stack and layout stay clean:
  - WG: section headers, known keys, values, comments, ignored keys (dimmed with a tooltip).
  - OVPN: directive names colored by `EngineSupport` class (mapped / ignored / forbidden underlined in red), inline tags, comments.
- Diagnostics: `ValidationIssue`s appear as line annotations in the gutter and a list in the inspector. Save stays disabled while there are errors.
- No web view. CodeMirror is not carried over.
- Opening the editor of an existing profile requires `RevealGate` (A6). The new-profile editor does not.
- **Private-key masking:** a live `NSTextView` still holds the real bytes even when bullets are drawn. **Decision:** the key line is masked with a custom `NSTextLayoutFragment` that draws bullets until "Show" is clicked (`RevealGate`, already satisfied for this window); the underlying text stays the real key so the parser and Save work. Prototype 7 confirms; fallback: keep the key out of the text and show a placeholder line that Save re-inserts. **As built (draft 8, UI review H3, H4, M15; Fable app review L2):** masking fails **closed**: a line is drawn masked while the analysis is stale (an insert above a key line can't draw it unmasked; a pixel test covers it). While masked, VoiceOver and the accessibility API get a masked value (`accessibilityValue`, `accessibilityString(for:)`), copy and ⌘A ⌘C over a key are refused with an explanation, and Services, Share, Look Up and the find bar can't reach the key text. Revert asks first; closing or quitting with unsaved edits asks to save.
- **Secret capture hygiene (F-7):**
  - the editor window, the "Show password" sheet and any window that renders a secret set `NSWindow.sharingType = .none`. This works at the **CGWindow level only** (screenshots and screen recording through window-server capture); capture paths that don't honour it (some ScreenCaptureKit configurations, AirPlay/Sidecar mirroring, cameras, an admin) are out of scope and the help page says so;
  - copying a secret (key, password) writes `NSPasteboard` items with the extra types `org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType` and `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` (clipboard managers skip them) and clears the pasteboard after **60 s** if its `changeCount` is still ours;
  - the editor window is **not restorable** (`isRestorable = false`, `.restorationBehavior(.disabled)`), has **no autosave** (it is not an `NSDocument`), and its undo stack is cleared (`undoManager.removeAllActions()`) on close and after Save;
  - Duplicate (⌘D) goes through `RevealGate` because it copies the payload.

| `KofiBanner.svelte` | About + a one-time note after the 10th successful session | no banner in the main view |
| — (new in 2.0.2, D10.4-8) | Diagnostics › **Connection Test** (`ConnectionSelfTest`, `DiagnosticsStore.runSelfTest`) | Rows IPv4, IPv6, DNS and an exit-address text; one SF Symbol + text per row with VoiceOver labels; "Copy Results". **Triggers (user button presses only; nothing runs it on its own):** "Test Connection" in Diagnostics; "Run All"/⌘R (`AppEnvironment.runDiagnostics` runs the DNS checks and the self-test together); the hero's "Run Diagnostics" action (shows Diagnostics and runs it); and, while connected, a "Test Connection" link in the protection hero for the current profile (opens Diagnostics and runs the test). Runs only while that profile is `.connected`, one at a time, dropped on any status change. **Contacts only `OnDemandPlan.ownProbeURL`** (`steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates/probe.txt`, F8), at most two fetches: `NWConnection`, TLS, IP family forced, `preferNoProxies`, 6 s, generic `User-Agent`; `LiveSelfTestNetworking` refuses any other URL, and every path ends in one `finish` (cancel, handlers nil, a single resume). Each fetch's `localEndpoint` is mapped to an interface with `getifaddrs`; the tunnel interface is found from the snapshot's tunnel addresses (the snapshot carries no utun name). **IPv4/IPv6 verdicts** (pure `classify`, table-tested): only HTTP 200 with the exact body `ok` counts (a captive portal's 200 can't produce "through the tunnel"); source = a tunnel address or interface = the tunnel → "Through the tunnel (utunN, from <address>)"; a split profile → "Outside the tunnel, as expected for this profile"; a full tunnel with no tunnel identity known → "Couldn't reach the test host" (never a false leak); otherwise "Bypasses the VPN"/"Outside the tunnel" (IPv4 outside = problem; IPv6 outside = problem with the kill switch or Block IPv6, else warning). IPv6 failures: no physical v6 default and no tunnel v6 → "No IPv6 on this network"; a prompt refusal (not a timeout) under a full v4-only tunnel with the kill switch or Block IPv6 → "Blocked, nothing leaves outside the tunnel"; a split profile that doesn't tunnel v6 sends nothing and shows "Not part of this tunnel" (the attempt would go out on the LAN). **DNS:** §10.2. **Exit address (D-5):** not checked; the text says websites usually see the VPN server's address (named) and that LockPlus asks no third-party service to confirm it. **Overall:** problem > warning > inconclusive > ok; inconclusive (any "Couldn't …") is never drawn as safe. Copy Results omits the VPN server address and the profile name; the bundle copy is `selftest.txt` (§14.2). |
| Latency | `measureLatency` XPC | WG: the handshake RTT (forced handshake, W4). OVPN while connected: the engine's keepalive round trip if openvpn3 exposes one, otherwise "—". OVPN while disconnected: a TCP connect for `proto tcp` endpoints, made before any `includeAllNetworks` session exists (§10.1.1 E5). **Only to the profile's own endpoints** (no probe oracle). ICMP from the root extension is cut (§21). *Draft 8 (PF 8):* the XPC method exists, but its measurement isn't built: it waits for the S2 E5 result (§10.1.1). |
| Import from clipboard | `ImportCoordinator` | **Pasteboard privacy (F-8):** the app checks (15.4 APIs, baseline on the 26.0 floor, no `#available`) `NSPasteboard.general.accessBehavior` (`.alwaysDeny` → "Clipboard access is off for LockPlus in System Settings") and calls `detectPatterns(for:)`/`detectMetadata` (no alert) to enable "Import from Clipboard" only when the content can be a profile or an image. It **reads** the pasteboard (which may show the system paste-permission alert) only on the user's ⇧⌘V or menu choice, never in the background, and never logs or retains what it read beyond the import. |

### 11.6 Localization and accessibility

- `Localizable.xcstrings` and `InfoPlist.xcstrings` (app and extension), **en (source) and de** (draft 8, Conflicts bc; UI review M17). Korean and Japanese are dropped for v2.0 and removed from `knownRegions`; a settings file that says `ko`/`ja` decodes as "System". Every key has a German translation, and the catalog is re-synced from the real build (`Tools/ui/sync-strings.sh`).
  - **German register: du (owner, final, draft 9.1).** The catalog uses du throughout; new strings follow it.
  - German-length rules from the UI review: no fixed-size onboarding sheet or 300 pt header that clips German, no `lineLimit(1)` on rows that carry sentences, no hard-coded units (`Measurement`/`Duration` formatters instead of "s" and "KB/s"), and no sentence fragment reused after both ":" and "because" (`reason()` and `causeReason()` are separate keys). A German-length smoke render runs with the screenshots (`Tools/ui/render-screenshots.sh`, `-de` variants).
  - Inflected counts (`^[…](inflect: true)`) go through `String(AttributedString(localized:).characters)`; `String(localized:)` shows the raw markup.
  - A one-off script seeds the catalogs from `frontend/src/i18n/*.json` (201 keys) through a mapping table. It is committed, not run at build time.
  - Error codes map to `LocalizedStringResource` in the app only.
  - No `Text` + `Text` concatenation (deprecated in the 26 SDK) and no non-localized interpolation into `LocalizedStringResource` (warns); counts use "Vary by Plural" (item 19). Pseudo-localization (`-NSDoubleLocalizedStrings YES`) runs in the preview matrix.
- Appearance override: Settings › General › Appearance (System / Light / Dark) sets `NSApp.appearance` (nil, Aqua, Dark Aqua) at launch as soon as settings load and again on every change, so every window switches at once; the menu bar item keeps following the menu bar.
- Language override: Settings writes `UserDefaults.standard.set([code], forKey: "AppleLanguages")` and applies it after a restart. "System" removes the key. The picker offers System, English and Deutsch.
- Accessibility (item 16; UI-CONCEPT §8.2):
  - every control has a label. The status item's accessibility label uses **one** wording everywhere: "LockPlus, protected, Work, download 1.2 megabytes per second, upload 30 kilobytes per second"; blocked: "LockPlus, blocked, waiting to reconnect Work"; refreshed at most once a second and only on change;
  - state is never conveyed by color alone (seven glyph silhouettes; a unit snapshot test, §15.1);
  - full keyboard navigation and the UI-CONCEPT §8.1 shortcuts: ⌘1–⌘5 sections, ⌘N New WireGuard Profile, ⌥⌘N New OpenVPN Profile, ⌘O Import, ⇧⌘V Import from Clipboard, ⇧⌘E Export, ⌘E Edit Config, ⌘D Duplicate, ⌘⌫ Delete (draft 8, UI review H1: only while the sidebar has focus, so it never collides with text editing, and always confirmed first), ⌘K Connect/Disconnect (one binding; the UI review removed duplicates), ⇧⌘K Resume Protection, ⌘R Run All diagnostics (2.0.2: also the connection self-test while connected), ⌘F Find (draft 3's "⌘N import" is superseded);
  - Reduce Motion is honoured explicitly (`accessibilityReduceMotion`) in charts and glyph animation;
  - section titles carry `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)` so VoiceOver's built-in Headings rotor works; a custom `accessibilityRotor` only for the editor's Issues list;
  - state changes post `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement`, with `accessibilitySpeechAnnouncementPriority = .high` for Blocked and auth (UI tests assert them, §15.1);
  - asset-catalog colors have High Contrast variants, and a unit test checks every documented contrast pair (§15.1).

### 11.7 Error surfacing (L-OVPN-4)

- Every terminal tunnel error reaches the UI through `fetchLastDisconnectError` (completion form) or the `tunnelSnapshot.lastError` fallback, and is mapped by the derived-state table.
- It is shown as an inline banner in Detail and in the menu header and status line, with a localized message and a "Details…" disclosure (code, time, the extension's non-secret detail).
- A "Blocked — <error>" state always offers **Disconnect** ("Disconnect and Restore Internet"), the only documented way out (ref/networkextension C17). Draft 9: there is no blocked state while macOS says `.disconnected` (S2 E3, E14c are open), so Restore Internet is gone.
- A prompt inside a pending start is **not** an error: it is the sign-in state of the connect (UI-CONCEPT §6.6 row 3, draft 9). `.authRequired`/`.authFailed` after a failed start (kill switch off) or a held start (with it) is an error with a Sign In… action.
- **225 `.startNotAuthorised` (2.0.2, D10.4-6, D-1).** Copy: "This profile was started outside LockPlus (for example from System Settings) and was refused. Connect it from LockPlus." (de: "Dieses Profil wurde außerhalb von LockPlus gestartet (zum Beispiel in den Systemeinstellungen) und abgelehnt. Verbinde es in LockPlus."); reason fragment "it was started outside LockPlus". **Diagnostics line rule:** when one of this user's profiles ends with 225 and the app did **not** arm that profile within the last 15 s, Diagnostics gets "<name> was started outside LockPlus and refused. Connect it from LockPlus." (at most once per profile per 5 min, the throttle shared with 222); within 15 s of the app's own arm it is the app's own failure and shows only in the hero. A 2.0.1 app instance still running in another user's session after the update gets 225 with its generic copy; relaunching fixes it (release note).
- Import, provision and XPC errors appear as sheet alerts. Background failures (reconcile, history sync) appear in a "Problems" list in Diagnostics with a sidebar badge, never as modal spam.
- **Draft 10 (PF 53):** a reconnect after a tunnel-process crash (§11.2 `restartedAfterCrash`) posts "Reconnected to <name> after a tunnel process restart." instead of "Connected to <name>." (de: "Nach einem Neustart des Tunnelprozesses wieder mit <name> verbunden."); like "Connected", it is not a problem notification, so only the "Connect and disconnect" setting shows it.
- **User notifications** (`notifications` setting: Only problems (default) / Connect and disconnect / Off) are posted only while no LockPlus window is key, and name the profile only (§8.4). Authorization: requested **once**, at the end of onboarding, after a sentence explaining why ("LockPlus tells you when protection stops unexpectedly"). If denied, Settings › General shows "Notifications are off for LockPlus in System Settings" with an "Open System Settings" button; the app never asks again on its own, and choosing a non-Off setting while authorization is `.notDetermined` asks then.

### 11.8 Design tokens and app icon (new, item 20)

- Colors are asset-catalog Color Sets with Any/Dark and **High Contrast** variants, exposed as `Color.lp.*`/`NSColor.lp.*` (UI-CONCEPT §2.2); views never use raw hex. They are generated by `Tools/ui/gen_colors.py`, and a unit test checks every documented contrast pair. **Draft 8 token changes** (contrast test): dark-mode `lp.stroke` is mint **50 %** (45 % measured 2.93:1 on `lp.card`, below the 3:1 non-text threshold; High Contrast dark 65 %), and dark editor comments (`lp.syntaxComment`) use mint **65 %** instead of 55 % (55 % was 4.16:1 on `lp.sunken`; High Contrast 75 %) (UI-CONCEPT §2.2, §6.9).
- **Dark-mode sidebar selection (draft 8, UI review M18):** the selected row stays legible in dark mode; views don't force a `foregroundStyle` against the system selection. Checked live, not only in offscreen renders.
- `ConnectButtonStyle` (sage fill, navy label in dark mode), the `LockGlyph(state:size:)` view over the custom `lockplus.lock` symbol family (annotated for Draw in the SF Symbols 7 app at Regular, Ultralight and Black), and the surface helper `.lpSurface(_:)`: hero card and menu header are **opaque** `lp.card` with a 12 % tint on every OS (content layer: no Liquid Glass, HIG); `glassEffect` only for floating functional controls (baseline on the 26.0 floor; draft 7's `.regularMaterial` fallback for 15 is gone), with `lp.card` under Reduce Transparency (ref/swiftui-appkit §2.3).
- App icon: one Icon Composer `.icon` file (default, dark and mono appearances); With the 26.0 deployment target Xcode generates no pre-26 fallback images (draft 7 needed them for 15.1). No `AppIcon` asset catalog (it would be replaced). Status glyphs stay a custom symbol family in `Assets.xcassets`. Building the `.icon` needs Xcode 26+; the pinned 27.1 qualifies.

## 12. Updates and distribution

### 12.1 Sparkle 2 configuration (L-UPD-1)

- **Sparkle 2.10.1, SPM rule Exact** (ref/sparkle C1), in the app only. Not "≥ 2.9": SPM's default rule would auto-update within major 2. The floor is **2.9.6** (local privilege escalation and package-install fixes; GHSA-3x7w-j75x-ppq5, GHSA-4v99-qgq9-6pxp; CVE-2026-47121/47122; F-6) and 2.10.0 for the macOS 27 delta fix. The release tools (`generate_keys`, `sign_update`, `generate_appcast`) come from the same checksum-pinned SPM artifact, copied to `~/Code/lockplus-release/tools/sparkle-2.10.1/bin`. Sparkle advisories are on the §9.2 watch list; a fixing release ships within the §22 SLA.
- Integration (ref/sparkle §2.5): `SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: false, …)`, started only **after** `SystemExtensionManager.activate()` has finished its preflight, so the first update alert never lands on top of "Updating tunnel component…". Updater and user-driver delegates are held **strongly** by `UpdateController` (Sparkle holds them weakly since 2.8.1). All Sparkle API is main-thread only. "Check for Updates…" items are enabled from KVO on `canCheckForUpdates`; we never call `checkForUpdatesInBackground()`.
- **Feed and flags pinned (draft 8, Fable app review M3, M4; app-root review L9).** Sparkle reads `SUFeedURL` and the automatic-update booleans from user defaults before Info.plist (`SUHost.m`, `SPUUpdater.m`), so any process that can write our defaults could redirect the feed. As built, `UpdateController`: never starts the updater while the feed URL or the public key is a placeholder (§2.5); calls `clearFeedURLFromUserDefaults()` before starting; returns the Info.plist value from the delegate's `feedURLString(for:)`; and sets `automaticallyChecksForUpdates = true` and `automaticallyDownloadsUpdates = false` explicitly after `startUpdater()`. `installHandler()` follows Sparkle's documented contract, and the "no update" path doesn't fire the error branch. The dead `terminationIntent`/`installHandlerBound` state is gone from `UpdateCoordinator`.
- **Gentle reminders** (the app is `.accessory` most of the time, and Sparkle otherwise shows scheduled alerts behind other windows): `supportsGentleScheduledUpdateReminders = true`; Sparkle shows the alert itself only in immediate focus (at launch); otherwise the menu gets "Update Available…", which calls `checkForUpdates()` (ref/sparkle §5.6, C20).
- An EdDSA key pair is generated once with `generate_keys --account lockplus-native` on the dev Mac (a named account keeps it apart from other Sparkle projects; `-s <key>` on the command line is never used).
  - **The private key never enters CI (M1), and neither does anything else that makes a release (N1).** The EdDSA key lives in the dev Mac's login keychain, with an offline backup in 1Password (exported with `-x`, then `rm -P`). The Developer ID identity (backed up as a `.p12`), both Developer ID provisioning profiles and the `notarytool` keychain profile live there too. Alex runs `Tools/release/release.sh <tag>` on the dev Mac, which builds, signs, notarizes and EdDSA-signs in one place (§12.4), then publishes the appcast to gh-pages: first to the `rc` channel only, then, after the release gates (§12.4) are green, to everyone.
  - Why: once the old EdDSA key validates an archive, Sparkle accepts any valid code signature (§1.3 A5). The EdDSA key is therefore the **only** thing standing between a compromise and every user. Nothing CI produces is ever signed.
  - **Releases fail hard without it**: `release.sh` exits non-zero if the key is missing, and there is no "grace mode".
  - **Key rotation (corrects N1, Conflicts o):** held key → a normal zip signed with the old key carrying the new `SUPublicEDKey`; lost key → a Developer ID-signed, notarized DMG whose `edSignature` uses the new key, reaching old clients after the 20-day signed-feed expiry (§1.3 A5). `release.sh --rotate-key {held|lost}` produces the item; the lost-key folder holds only the DMG (archives are keyed by version, so a zip and a DMG of one version overwrite each other).
  - Blast-radius limits if it leaks anyway: §1.3 A5.
- Appcast: `https://steiale.github.io/lockplus-updates/appcast.xml` (§2.5; final, draft 9.1: the public repo `steiale/lockplus-updates` on GitHub Pages, a dedicated repo because Pages does not redirect after a rename).
  - Archives and deltas on the GitHub Releases of `steiale/lockplus-updates`. Redirects to the asset CDN are fine: Sparkle validates by signature, not by host. No custom download host logic, so the redirect-host problem (8f578a8) disappears.
  - `SURequireSignedFeed = YES` with `SUVerifyUpdateBeforeExtraction = YES`; the signature sits in a trailing `<!-- sparkle-signatures: … -->` comment and the feed must be served byte-exact (`.nojekyll` on gh-pages; the served bytes are verified after every publish, §12.4).
  - Release notes are embedded markdown (`<description sparkle:format="markdown">`, `--embed-release-notes`), so no separately signed notes files exist.
  - **The channel is live (draft 10, E2E-1).** The owner published a signed, empty appcast; "Check for Updates" on 2.0.0 answered "You're up to date!" on 26 and 27. Because of `SURequireSignedFeed`, **every published appcast must be signed**: the owner signs it on the dev Mac with `sign_update --account lockplus-native` (release step, §12.4) before pushing gh-pages; agents never run it (the key is the owner's).
- Downgrades: Sparkle refuses them twice (the appcast driver offers only newer `CFBundleVersion`s; the installer aborts with `SUDowngradeError` if the host is newer). There is **no** `bestValidUpdate(in:for:)` override: Sparkle's API docs discourage it, and it risks breaking channel, phasing and minimum-version logic (ref/sparkle C4). The extension refuses downgrade replacement (§4.2). A user who deliberately installs an older version uses "Reinstall tunnel component" (§4.6). There is no silent rollback path.
- Deltas: `generate_appcast --maximum-deltas 3` (default 5; 3 versions per branch kept). Deltas need every shipped full zip in the persistent `~/Code/lockplus-release/updates/`, outside the per-tag fresh clone. Deltas are prevalidated with the old key only (no Developer ID fallback); a failed delta falls back to the full archive.
- **Channels:** the appcast has the default channel plus `rc`, via `sparkle:channel` and `SPUUpdaterDelegate.allowedChannels(for:)` (`["rc"]` when "Receive release candidates" is on; the default channel is always included). Toggling it calls `updater.resetUpdateCycleAfterShortDelay()`. Turning it off after installing an RC leaves the user on that RC until the default channel passes it (no downgrade); since promotion reuses the same item, that state is short. The leak harness and update tests use this shipped mechanism (§15.3, §15.5); no test-only feed override exists in the binary.
- A pulled item is not a recall: a downloaded or staged update still installs. A bad release is fixed by shipping N+1.

### 12.2 Distribution artifacts

- `LockPlus-<ver>.zip` (for Sparkle and the cask) contains exactly `LockPlus.app`, built with `ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent` from the **stapled** app (zips can be notarized but not stapled). The beta channel uses `LockPlus Native.app` (§13.4). CI asserts the top-level name (L-DIST-1). *Draft 10:* `release.sh` asserts it too and ignores the `__MACOSX/` directory that `--sequesterRsrc` adds (f6980aa).
- `LockPlus-<ver>.dmg`: `create-dmg` (or `hdiutil create`) from the **already stapled** app, **without** `--codesign`/`--notarize` (create-dmg signs without `--timestamp` and `-i`); format UDZO; then `hdiutil verify`, `codesign -s "Developer ID Application: …" --timestamp -i io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.dmg`, `notarytool submit --wait`, `stapler staple`, and `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` (ref/toolchain T13). It is the manual-download artifact and, for a lost-key rotation only, the Sparkle enclosure (§12.1). `sign_update` runs after stapling, because stapling modifies the file.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` and the CycloneDX SBOM (§12.4) are attached to the release.
- Homebrew cask `lockplus-native` during beta, `lockplus` after cutover (O5, Conflicts i):
  ```ruby
  cask "lockplus" do
    version "2.0.0"; sha256 "…"
    url "https://github.com/steiale/lockplus-updates/releases/download/v#{version}/LockPlus-#{version}.zip"
    name "LockPlus"; homepage "https://github.com/steiale/lockplus"
    auto_updates true
    depends_on macos: ">= :tahoe"; depends_on arch: :arm64     # = LSMinimumSystemVersion 26.0 (draft 7: :sequoia + 15.1)
    app "LockPlus.app"
    uninstall quit: "io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac"           # runs on every upgrade: nothing destructive here
    zap script: { executable: "#{appdir}/LockPlus.app/Contents/MacOS/LockPlus",
                  args: ["--uninstall-system-components"], sudo: false, must_succeed: false },
        trash: [
          "~/Library/Application Support/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac",
          "~/Library/Preferences/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.plist",
          "~/Library/Caches/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac",
          "~/Library/HTTPStorages/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac",
          "~/Library/Saved Application State/io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.savedState",
        ]
    caveats "… (§4.4 wording: in-app Uninstall removes the network extension; brew uninstall --zap does not;
             a zap after the app is already gone can't remove secrets or VPN configurations, see §4.4 cleanup)"
  end
  ```
  - Homebrew runs the **installed** cask's `uninstall` stanza on every `brew upgrade`/`reinstall` (only `signal:` is skipped), so **the first published cask must already have this shape**; a wrong first cask keeps wiping users until they reinstall (ref/sparkle C14). `quit:` sends Cmd-Q, waits ≤ 10 s and reopens the app after the upgrade; our quit path answers `.terminateNow` for it (§11.1).
  - Since Homebrew 5.2, `brew upgrade` also upgrades `auto_updates` casks whose installed bundle is older than the tap's version. After Sparkle has updated the bundle, a plain `brew upgrade` leaves it alone.
- **Zap audit (L-DIST-1):**
  - the native zap never lists `~/Library/Application Support/lockplus` or `wireguide-plus`;
  - the `lockplus` (Go) and `wireguide-plus` cask zaps are re-audited at cutover so they never list `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac` paths;
  - CI greps every cask file in the tap for cross-references, and asserts that no `uninstall script:` exists in the native cask.
- Brew detection, if any (e.g. "updates are managed by Homebrew"): check the absolute paths `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/lockplus*` and never shell out without a full PATH (15b0d2a).
  - **Decision:** with `auto_updates true`, Sparkle stays enabled for cask users too.

### 12.3 Update flow with extension re-activation (L-UPD-1, L-KS-3, L-EXT-3)

Sparkle facts that shape the flow (ref/sparkle §0, §5.1):
- "Install and Relaunch" calls `updater(_:shouldPostponeRelaunchForUpdate:untilInvokingBlock:)` **once per install session**. **Install-on-quit** (the alert's "Install on Quit" button, automatic downloads, or a dismissed staged update) **never** calls it: the bundle is swapped after any quit and nothing relaunches.
- Swapping the app bundle does **not** touch the running system extension (the system keeps its own copy, forum 732624), and it is not a Finder delete, so it does not trigger the "remove the extension" prompt. The extension changes only on the new app's `activationRequest`.
- Sparkle 2 has no "did relaunch after update" callback; the maintainer's guidance is to detect a changed bundle version at launch, whatever installed it. That is §4.2.

**Decision (draft 4, Conflicts h): variant B.** The postpone hook only records intent; the §4.2 launch preflight, which already has to handle install-on-quit, brew and drag-replace, does all quiescing:
1. Sparkle downloads and verifies the update (through the tunnel if connected; that is fine).
2. `shouldPostponeRelaunchForUpdate` → `UpdateCoordinator.prepareForInstall`: write `expectedUpdate = {from: CFBundleVersion, to: item.versionString}` to `settings.json` and **always** invoke the block within a bound (≤ 20 s). *Draft 8:* no `terminationIntent` is needed: §11.3's quit dialog runs only for a quit from our own menu, before it calls `terminate`, so Sparkle's quit event never meets it. The tunnel keeps protecting the user during the install.
3. Sparkle sends an Apple quit event; `applicationShouldTerminate` returns `.terminateNow`. The bundle is swapped (quarantine stripped, `gktool` scan) and the app relaunched (only if it was running when the install began).
4. The new app launches and calls `activate()`. Its preflight (§4.2 steps 2–3) finds the old extension enabled with a lower version and quiesces: `pendingResume` written, on-demand off on **every** owned manager that has it (N5), `stopVPNTunnel()` and wait for `.disconnected` (15 s). From here until step 6 **the Mac is online without the tunnel**, as in draft 3 but for a shorter time (no install or relaunch inside the window). Then the request is submitted and `actionForReplacingExtension` returns `.replace` by pure comparison. On `.completed`, the app connects to the new versioned Mach name and runs `hello` and `reconcile`.
5. `UpdateCoordinator.resumeAfterUpdate()` restores on-demand on every manager in `pendingResume.onDemandEnabledIDs`, calls `startVPNTunnel` for `pendingResume.profileID`, re-registers the resume agent if a pause is active (§10.4), then clears `pendingResume` and `expectedUpdate`.
6. If activation needs approval or a reboot: on-demand stays restored but the tunnel can't start. The UI shows the approval/reboot dialog. With a kill-switch profile, nothing is blocking in the meantime (the tunnel is off), and the UI says so explicitly: "Not protected until the update finishes".
7. **Failure branch:** `updater(_:didAbortWithError:)` or `didFinishUpdateCycleFor:error:` with an error, after `prepareForInstall` → `installDidNotHappen`: clear `expectedUpdate`. (Under variant A it would also resume the stopped tunnel; under B nothing was stopped.)
8. The `updater(_:mayPerform:)` delegate refuses a new update session while a replacement or resume is in progress ("LockPlus is finishing a tunnel component update").

- **Variant A** (draft 3: quiesce inside the postpone hook) stays specified in ref/sparkle §5.3 as the S10 alternative. S10 measures the unprotected window of both and the failure states F5/F6 (install fails after the tunnel was stopped; relaunch never happens); B is kept unless S10 shows the preflight path misses a case.
- The **first launch after any update** always runs `activate()` (L-EXT-2), so even an update installed by brew, by a non-Finder copy or on quit replaces the extension. A Finder drag-replace may already have removed the extension (§4.2, `.removedDuringUpdate`).

### 12.4 Release pipeline and CI

**Release path (corrects draft 3, Conflicts g; ref/toolchain §5–§8, T2):** the release archive is built **unsigned** and signed manually, inside-out, with the golden entitlements. This is Apple's documented flow for products Xcode can't export, it behaves the same on every Xcode version (Xcode ≤ 26 exports Developer ID NE apps with the wrong entitlement values; the Xcode 27 fix is only forum-reported for 27.0b1 and absent from the 27.0/27.1 release notes), the pre-signing Mach-Os are exactly what CI builds (for the `repro` comparison), and the signed entitlements are the golden files by construction. `xcodebuild -exportArchive` with `ExportOptions-DeveloperID.plist` is an **optional alternative**, adopted only if S9 shows its entitlements are byte-identical (after normalization) to the golden files.

Workflows (`.github/workflows/native-ci.yml`), path-filtered on `native/**`, `permissions: contents: read`, actions pinned by commit SHA, `DEVELOPER_DIR` set to the pinned Xcode and every job asserting `toolchain.lock`:

| Upgrade test | manual, on a VM snapshot or a spare Mac (§15.5) | N-1 → RC via the `rc` channel; the checklist result is attached to the draft release. Required for promotion. |

Refuses to run unless both gates and (from M4) `repro` are recorded as passed. |

- **`verify.sh pre`** (signed, before upload): `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app; for app and extension: `Authority=Developer ID Application: … (M53GHX9FAY)`, a secure `Timestamp=` (not "Signed Time"), `flags=0x10000(runtime)`, `CodeDirectory v=20[4-9]`; entitlements dumped with `codesign -d --entitlements - --xml` and diffed (normalized JSON) against the golden files (the deprecated `:-` form is not used); no `com.apple.security.cs.*` and no `get-task-allow`; `codesign --verify -R "=<APP_REQ>"`/`-R "=<EXT_REQ>"` with the Release strings (draft 10: two words, Conflicts bq), and the negative check `APP_REQ` on the extension must exit **3** ("does not satisfy"; any other code fails, so a syntax error can't pass it); both embedded profiles have `ProvisionsAllDevices`; the linkage and string checks of the `build` job; `syspolicy_check notary-submission` (**required**: with `check-profile.sh` it is the only check that catches a bundle without its profiles, which notarization accepts and `distribution` passes; P1 skeleton, §2.7; E2E-1 found a profile bound to the wrong certificate with it). **Draft 10 (d55f291):** on macOS 27.0.1 it reports every unnotarized Developer ID executable as a Fatal "Gatekeeper rejected this file" (-67018); `verify.sh pre` tolerates exactly that finding, requires "Passed amfi_preflight" and fails on anything else.
- **`verify.sh post`** (after stapling): `stapler validate`; `syspolicy_check distribution` (primary for Gatekeeper, but **not** a profile check; `spctl -a -t exec -vvv` is secondary, "much less accurate"); `codesign -vvvv -R "=notarized" --check-notarization` on the extension; `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` on the DMG.
- **`release.sh` as built (draft 10; 150df23, 91cbd25).** A minimal chain of the "Release build" row: `check-profile.sh` on both profiles, `build-unsigned.sh` → stage → `sign-inside-out.sh --embed-profiles` → `verify.sh pre` → notarize the app zip (`--wait`, the log always fetched, any issue fails) → staple → zip the stapled app → DMG (signed, notarized, stapled) → `verify.sh post` → `SHA256SUMS.txt`, into `$LP_BUILD_ROOT/release/out/`. Not yet: the fresh-clone, signed-tag and `version-check.sh --tag` gates, the upload, the appcast steps (`--stage-rc`, `--promote`, `appcast-fixup.py`) and the SBOM (§18). The notary keychain item is readable only while the owner's Mac is unlocked, so `release.sh` retries "No Keychain password item" every 60 s for `LP_NOTARY_WAIT_MIN` minutes (default 30); it never touches keychains. It built 2.0.0 (200000) and (200001) for E2E-1. **Owner step until `--stage-rc` exists:** sign the appcast with `sign_update --account lockplus-native` and verify it before publishing (§12.1).
- **Clean-VM gate** (M2, S9, §15.5): download the release with Safari so it is quarantined, optionally offline to prove the staple works, install, approve, activate, `systemextensionsctl list`; a fresh snapshot each time (Gatekeeper caches results).
- **SBOM (F-13, ref/toolchain §11):** `Tools/release/sbom.sh` merges `Package.resolved` pins, `go list -m -json all` for `libwg-go.a`, and `git submodule status --recursive` (openvpn3, OpenSSL, asio, wireguard-apple) into one CycloneDX 1.6 JSON document with `purl`, `version` and `licenses` (static map: OpenSSL Apache-2.0, openvpn3 MPL-2.0, wireguard-go MIT, Sparkle MIT, ZIPFoundation MIT), attached as `LockPlus-<ver>.cdx.json`. It uses `jq` only; `syft` would be a new tool and is not adopted without Alex's approval.
- Notarization: two submissions per release (app zip, DMG); most finish within 5 min, 98 % within 15; the limit is 75 per day. The keychain profile is the existing team credential `wireguide-notarize` or a new `lockplus-notarize`. If the dev Mac's own LockPlus kill switch is on, the notary and CloudKit (stapler) hosts are reached through the tunnel.
- **CI holds no signing material (N1):** no Developer ID certificate, provisioning profile, App Store Connect API key or EdDSA key in repository or environment secrets; no `secrets.*` anywhere. §15.6 checks this on every release.
- The dev-Mac release is the cost of N1: releases depend on that machine (§20 risk 9). The checkout is a fresh clone per release, never the working copy, so local uncommitted changes or a stale build folder can't end up in a release.
- **Local test runs (draft 8).** Hosted tests (`LockPlusTests`, host LockPlus.app) need `-derivedDataPath` on the **internal disk** (e.g. `~/Code/lockplus-build/<name>-dd`): with derived data on an external volume the ad-hoc test host waits forever on a removable-volume TCC approval ("The test runner hung before establishing connection"). Two hosted runs of the same bundle ID at once also collide. Package tests run with `swift test` (scratch path under `$LP_BUILD_ROOT/spm/`), never from a test plan. `macho-hashes.sh` no longer exits 1 when the last file isn't a Mach-O (review 2), and `Tools/dev/build.sh` creates `build/` first.
- `xcode-27` is a preview image that "may be unstable" and may queue; `lint` and the package `swift test` steps stay runnable on `macos-26` with Xcode 26.6 as a fallback, which holds only while the packages keep `swift-tools-version` ≤ 6.2.
