## 13. Migration from the Go app (L-MIG-1)

### 13.1 Copy-only importer (native app)

`GoAppMigrator` runs during onboarding, or later from Settings › Advanced › "Import from Old LockPlus…" (built in draft 10.2, E2E-5 F4: a sheet that looks for the Go data every time, so skipping the offer in onboarding isn't final; onboarding says so under the offer).
1. **Detect (migration matrix, 2026-11-09: every 1.x version group, `~/Code/lockplus-build/migration-matrix.md`):** the **union** of `~/Library/Application Support/lockplus/` (LockPlus 1.0.57+) and `…/wireguide-plus/` (WireGuide+ 1.0.1–1.0.56), `GoAppMergedSource`. Go copied only the tunnels across (1.0.62+, and only when that version ran), so users who stopped at 1.0.57 or 1.0.61 have tunnels in both.
   - Tunnels by base name; `lockplus` wins a name clash. If `lockplus/tunnels/.legacy-migrated` exists, Go already copied `wireguide-plus`'s tunnels, so it adds none (deletions the user made in `lockplus` since stay deleted).
   - The same payload in both directories (under any names) is one tunnel, `lockplus`'s; two names in one directory stay two.
   - `config.json`, `wifi_rules.json` and `history.json` come from `lockplus`, else from `wireguide-plus` (Go never copied them).
   - Upstream WireGuide's `…/wireguide/` (also WireGuide+ 1.0.0's) is **never** read automatically. When it has tunnels, the report says: "WireGuide's profiles (the separate app) are on this Mac too. LockPlus doesn't import them on its own: choose Import Profile… and pick them in ~/Library/Application Support/wireguide/tunnels."
2. **Enumerate:**
   - `*.conf` → WG;
   - `*.ovpn` → OVPN (`.ovpn` presence is authoritative, as in Go `LoadMeta`);
   - `<name>.meta.json` → `{auto_reconnect, notes, protocol}`.
   - Skip dotfiles, `*.tmp`, `*.corrupt.*` and symlinks (`lstat`).
3. **Per tunnel:** run the native import pipeline (§8.1/§9.1) on the file bytes. The result is ✔ imported (new UUID), ⚠ imported with an import report, or ✖ rejected with the reason. The display name is the old file name.
   - Old names like `work.vpn` that the Go rules rejected are still valid display names now, and non-ASCII names keep their Unicode (draft 8, PF 15).
   - **The report states the deliberate behaviour changes** (draft 8, PF 14): inline lines over 512 bytes are rejected, unknown ciphers (e.g. CAMELLIA) are rejected, and `auth none` is accepted (§8.1).
   - *As built:* `GoMigrationReader` (LPParsing) reads the Go files with `O_NOFOLLOW`, regular files only; tested with a fixture tree only, by rule.
   - **Endpoint interface check (draft 7.3, S6):** the §9.3 `RouteProbe` runs on every migrated endpoint. A server routed via a non-primary interface (a local VM or Docker server, a second NIC) is imported with a ⚠ note: "This server is reached through bridge100. The old LockPlus could use that network, but the new tunnel can't (§20 risk 22). Keep using the old app for it, or make the server reachable on your main network."
4. **Policy:** from `config.json`:
   - `kill_switch` → `killSwitch` for full-tunnel profiles (route protection for split);
   - `dns_protection` → `dnsMode = .tunnelOnly` either way: **`dns_protection=false` also maps to DNS through the tunnel**, with a migration-report note (draft 8, PF 16; the native app has no "DNS outside the tunnel" mode, §10.2);
   - `auto_reconnect` → `stayConnected = false` (the extension always reconnects), with a note.
5. **Credentials:** §6.7, opt-in. Both service names (`io.github.steiale.wireguide-plus.ovpn`, `io.github.steiale.lockplus.ovpn`) are looked up in both keychains. WireGuide+ 1.0.50–1.0.56 and LockPlus 1.0.57–1.0.65 wrote the **System** keychain through their root helper (not readable without administrator rights: skipped by design); 1.0.66+ the login keychain (imported). Every System keychain item of an imported OpenVPN profile is named in the report, with or without the opt-in: "<profile>: the old LockPlus kept this password in the System keychain, which LockPlus can't read. Enter it again on first connect."; the rest are counted.
6. **Settings:**
   - `language` (`auto` → `.system`), `log_level`;
   - `theme` ("system" | "light" | "dark", anything else is system) becomes the Appearance setting, taken over only while LockPlus's still at its default (like `language`); the report needs no note for it;
   - `tray_icon_style` → `menuBarIconStyle` (`color` → `.color`, anything else → `.monochrome`);
   - `onboarding_complete = true`;
   - `auto_start` → offer "Launch at login?" (we never auto-register; NR §4 pitfall 14). *Draft 10.2 (E2E-5 F5):* the migration report has an "Open LockPlus at login" checkbox when `auto_start` was on or 1.0.x's LaunchAgent existed. That agent (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.github.steiale.lockplus.gui.plist`, label `io.github.steiale.lockplus.gui`, program `…/LockPlus.app/Contents/MacOS/lockplus`) starts the **native** binary after a Finder Replace (case-insensitive volume): the app removes exactly that file at every launch, in the migration and in a second instance (user domain, no administrator; a regular file of this user with the Go label and a `…/Contents/MacOS/lockplus` program, never a symlink, never `launchctl bootout`, which could hit this very process) and offers its own launch at login (a banner if outside the migration). A second instance started by that agent (`XPC_SERVICE_NAME` is its label) or as a login item (`keyAELaunchedAsLogInItem`) quits silently instead of showing "LockPlus is already running". Go 1.1 used `SMAppService.mainApp`: its Background Task Management item belongs to the Go bundle ID and no API lets another app remove it, so the report says: "System Settings › General › Login Items may still list the old LockPlus. Turn it off there; LockPlus has its own setting.";
   - *Migration matrix:* WireGuide+ 1.0.1–1.0.56 had the same agent as `io.github.steiale.wireguide-plus.gui.plist` (program `…/WireGuide+.app/Contents/MacOS/wireguide-plus`), which keeps launching the old app (and with it its helper) after the update put LockPlus next to it. It is removed with the same rules (`ProgramArguments[0]` or `Program`); upstream WireGuide's `com.wireguide.gui` is never touched.
   - `kofi_dismissed` → `supportNoteShown = true`.
7. **Wi-Fi rules** (`wifi_rules.json`):
   - `enabled`, `trusted_ssids`;
   - `default_tunnel` + `auto_connect_untrusted` → auto profile (by name → UUID). *Draft 10.2 (E2E-5 F2):* a changed rule set runs the same on-demand re-save as the Auto-Connect pane (`UIBinder.requestOnDemandResave`, one pass at a time, through `ProfilesStore.resaveOnDemand` and its mutation rules: deferred while a profile is busy), so the auto profile's configuration ends with `OnDemandEnabled = true`;
   - `ssid_tunnel_map` is **not migrated** (`ssidProfileMap` is cut, §21). The migration report lists it: "Per-network profile choices aren't supported yet".
8. **History** (`history.json`): each session becomes a `HistoryEntry` with a new UUID, `profileID` by name match (nil if none), and `endReason` mapped from `disconnect_reason` (draft 8, PF 16: the Go `reconnect` and `health_check` reasons map to `.replaced`).
9. **Marker:** `migration.json = {completedAt, source: path, items: [{oldName, newID, digest, result}], complete, steps}` (draft 8: `source` is stored relative to the home directory, Fable app review nit). Automatic migration runs only when no **complete** marker exists. A manual re-run dedupes by payload digest. **Nothing in the Go directories is ever written, moved or deleted.**
10. **Resumable (draft 10.2, E2E-5 F4).** E2E-5 killed the app during the saved-password prompt: the profiles existed, nothing else did, and the offer said "all already imported". Now:
    - `migration.json` is written after every created profile and after each step (`credentials`, `settings`, `history`) with `complete: false`, and marked complete at the end. A marker without `complete` (written before 10.2) counts as complete.
    - *Review F4-1:* the incomplete marker is written at the top of `run()`, before the first profile is created; only an incomplete marker means "interrupted" (matching profiles without a marker were imported by hand and get the normal offer). A re-run after a complete migration keeps the marker complete.
    - An incomplete marker is offered as "Finish importing from LockPlus 1.x": the profiles still missing, then only the steps that never ran. Existing profiles are mapped by marker item or payload digest (never imported twice), so the auto-connect profile, trusted networks, history and saved logins reach them. Onboarding's step 4 offers it; after onboarding, a banner ("Importing from LockPlus 1.x didn't finish." [Not Now] [Finish Import…]). Finishing adds what's missing and overwrites nothing (review F4-1): trusted networks are merged, the auto profile is set only when none is chosen, and language, log level and icon style are taken from the old app only while they still have LockPlus's default (pre-release review: a kill before the settings step used to drop them).
    - *Pre-release review (2026-11-09):* one run at a time (Import is disabled while it runs; the Settings re-scan waits). A run in which any profile failed (locked profiles, a failed save) applies no settings, Wi-Fi rules or history and leaves the marker incomplete ("Finish Import" retries the profiles, then applies them once). An earlier run's profile is recognised by its marker item even after the user edited it; a retried tunnel replaces its marker item; migrated history entries have stable IDs (no duplicates after a kill); a resumed run reads the saved logins of the profiles it creates. At launch the Go data is read only when the marker says an import didn't finish, and the plan (with the old profiles' private keys) is dropped as soon as no offer needs it.
    - A manual re-run after a **complete** migration imports profiles (and their saved logins) only: settings and Wi-Fi rules the user changed since aren't overwritten.
11. **Report (draft 10.2, E2E-5 F6, F7).** Imported; Needs attention, each with the profile name and the first reason (a security warning, an ignored line that changes behaviour such as `up`, not yet verified); Not migrated; "Good to know": ignored lines that change nothing (`nobind`, `verb`, `persist-*`, Windows and server options, DNS/compression/reconnect that LockPlus manages), per-profile notes (auto-reconnect built in, a username imported without a password), and the whole-app notes (DNS always through the tunnel, per-network choices with the old map itself, "CafeNet → ovpn-tcp"); the launch-at-login offer; a last line that depends on the helper (installed: "If the old LockPlus offers its update to 1.2, that update removes the helper; otherwise choose “Remove Old Helper…”"; gone: the old app can be deleted). The saved-password offer counts **saved logins** (a Go item may hold only a username, Go's "Save username") and says macOS asks for the **login keychain password** once per item.

### 13.2 Coexistence period

*Migration matrix:* the 1.x update for WireGuide+ users installs `LockPlus.app` next to `WireGuide+.app` (bundle ID `io.github.steiale.wireguide-plus`; Finder never replaces it). While it is installed, the main window offers it for the Trash: "WireGuide+, the old version of LockPlus, is still installed. LockPlus replaces it." [Not Now] [Move to Trash…], confirmed ("Move WireGuide+ to the Trash?", "You can put it back from the Trash."), through `NSWorkspace.recycle` after checking the bundle's ID again. Never while it runs ("Quit it, then you can move it to the Trash."); a failure says to drag it to the Trash. Not Now hides it for this launch. A running WireGuide+ counts as "the old app is running" for the helper removal too.

Both apps are named `LockPlus.app`; they differ in bundle ID (`io.github.steiale.lockplus` vs `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac`), data directory and keychain services (§4.5 rules apply). *Draft 10.2 (E2E-5, measured with Finder):* the user path is the DMG drag to Applications. Finder asks "An older item named “LockPlus” already exists": **Replace** fails with "in use" while the Go app runs and, once it is quit, deletes the Go app (not to the Trash) and leaves its helper running; **Keep Both** gives `LockPlus 2.app` (native) next to the Go app. The Go updater can't deliver 2.0 (it takes only its own zip naming and Ed25519 signature). So after the usual Replace the old app is gone and its helper stays: §13.3a removes it.

### 13.3 The Go app's final release (v1.2.0 "Farewell")

Added to the Go codebase (Go release line, Fable security review mandatory):
- On launch, a dialog: "LockPlus has a new version. Your tunnels will be copied by the new app. Remove the old helper now?"
- **"Remove"** calls a new helper RPC, `Uninstall`, which runs as root:
  1. Disconnect all tunnels (stop openvpn, close utun).
  2. Flush pf anchors `com.apple/wireguide` and `com.apple/wireguide/dns`.
  3. Restore the pf enable state from `pf-was-enabled`.
  4. Restore DNS from `dns-journal.json` (the existing journal-restore code path).
  5. Remove `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper` and `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/openvpn`, `/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper.plist`, `/var/run/lockplus`, and `/Library/Application Support/lockplus`.
  6. `launchctl bootout system/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper` as the last step, from a detached child.
- **Caller authentication, stated:** the Go IPC server authenticates peers by **uid only** (`LOCAL_PEERCRED` → `verifyPeerUID`, `internal/ipc/peercred_*.go`), with no code-signature check. Any process running as the GUI user can therefore call `Uninstall`. The impact is **denial of service only**: it disconnects the Go tunnels, removes the Go kill switch, restores DNS and removes the helper. No secret is read and nothing is executed with attacker input. Same-user malware can already disrupt the Go app (`kill`, socket floods), so this is accepted and not hardened in a release whose purpose is removal. The Fable review checks that the RPC takes **no arguments** (no paths, no names) so this stays true.
- The GUI then removes its LaunchAgent and login item and shows "Install LockPlus 2" with the download link and the cask command.
- It does **not** delete `~/Library/Application Support/lockplus` or the legacy keychain items, so a later re-migration stays possible. The user can delete them from the native app (Settings › Advanced › "Remove old LockPlus data…", with confirmation, LAContext, and only after a completed migration marker).
- The custom Go updater serves v1.2.0 as its last update.

- *Status (draft 10.2):* the owner decided on 2026-11-09 to ship v1.2.0; it is built separately on the Go release line. Until a user has it, the native copy says so conditionally ("If the old LockPlus offers its update to 1.2, …").

### 13.3a Native removal of a leftover Go helper (draft 10.2, E2E-5 F1)

For users who never update 1.x (after a Finder Replace there is no 1.x left to update), native 2.0 removes the Go helper itself.

**Every helper generation (migration matrix, 2026-11-09).** One run handles all of them; the busy, identity, DNS-journal and old-app refusals apply to each:
- LockPlus 1.0.57–1.1.0: `io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper` (below; Developer ID, identifier `lockplus-helper`).
- WireGuide+ 1.0.1–1.0.56: `io.github.steiale.wireguide-plus.helper` (RunAtLoad + KeepAlive, never removed by any 1.x): its plist, binary, `/var/run/wireguide-plus`, `/var/log/wireguide-plus-helper.log` and `/Library/Application Support/wireguide-plus` (root). Early builds weren't Developer ID signed, so it is identified by its exact `Label`, `ProgramArguments[0]` and root ownership, never by the `lockplus-helper` requirement.
- `com.wireguide.helper` is upstream WireGuide's **live** label (WireGuide+ 1.0.0 used it): ours only if its binary satisfies `anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY"`, checked app-side (`SecStaticCodeCheckValidity`, to show the banner) and again as root (every action on it is gated on that check). Otherwise it, its socket, log and data directory are left alone.
- The detector probes each helper's socket (`/var/run/lockplus/lockplus.sock`, `/var/run/wireguide-plus/wireguide-plus.sock`) and reads each data directory's DNS journal and `pf-was-enabled`. The pf anchor `com.apple/wireguide` is shared with upstream WireGuide: its kill switch also blocks the removal, and the "busy" copy says so ("If you also use WireGuide, its kill switch counts too: turn it off for the removal."). WireGuide+ ≤ 1.0.62 used `com.apple.wireguide` (dot), which pf never evaluates: inert.

**Mechanism (decision).** One privileged run after one administrator authentication, through `do shell script theScript with prompt thePrompt with administrator privileges` in a constant AppleScript handler. *Review (F1-4):* the handler is compiled and called **in-process** (`InProcessAppleScriptRunner`: `NSAppleScript` on the main actor, `executeAppleEvent` with one subroutine event `ascr`/`psbr` whose two text parameters are the script and the prompt), so the authorization dialog names LockPlus; through `/usr/bin/osascript` it would very likely name "osascript", and users shouldn't learn to approve that. `OsascriptPrivilegedRunner` (`osascript -e 'on run argv' … (item 1 of argv) …`) is the fallback **only** when the handler can't be built in-process (no `NSAppleScript`, a compile error); every execution error is the run's answer (-128 → cancelled, anything else → failed with the system's message), so a failure never leads to a second, osascript-branded dialog, and every error and fallback is logged with its number (Fable pre-release A-2). *Measured (E2E-6, 200013):* on 26 (26.6.2) the dialog is titled "LockPlus" and shows our prompt line ("LockPlus wants to remove the helper of the old LockPlus (1.x)."); on 27.2 macOS replaces it with its own consent, "Allow administrator access for “LockPlus”?" / "This will allow “LockPlus” to access and modify your data, files, and settings on this Mac.": it names LockPlus, but **our prompt line isn't shown on macOS 27**, so the app's banner and button text must carry the explanation (what is removed and why) on their own. No osascript process ran on either OS: the fallback wasn't taken.
- `AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges` is deprecated since 10.7 and unavailable in Swift.
- An `SMAppService` daemon would install a permanent root helper (and need approval in Login Items) to remove another one: the opposite of the goal, and new root attack surface for one action.
- `do shell script … with administrator privileges` is the supported one-shot elevation for an app: the system's authorization dialog (on 27 preceded by "Allow administrator access for a script started by “LockPlus”?"), nothing left installed. It runs `/bin/sh -c` as root, which is acceptable only because the script is fixed (below).
- The script and the prompt are passed as **parameters** (event parameters in-process, argv for osascript) to a constant AppleScript handler, so neither is ever parsed as AppleScript source and nothing needs quoting; the script is a compile-time constant in the signed binary (`LegacyHelperRemoval.script`), not a file in the user-writable bundle.
- *Accepted, inherent:* that constant lives in a binary inside the user-writable `/Applications` bundle; a same-user attacker who patches it gets root at the next approval. Same trust model as the Go installer and every `with administrator privileges` app; mitigated only by Gatekeeper and the signature check at launch.

**Script contract (`LegacyHelperRemoval.script`).** No interpolation of any value from the user, the Go app or the file system: the body interpolates only its own compile-time constants (`oldAppPattern`, `wireGuide100Pattern`, the `journalstale`, `dnsonly` and `tunnelstale` functions), none of which carries runtime data (Fable follow-up check). Idempotent; it refuses rather than guesses, and ends with one `LP_RESULT=` line:
1. `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, `umask 077`, `cd /` and `set -f` (no relative path, no globbing; the functions rely on it; E2E-7 F3 review). *Fable pre-release A-1:* the body runs as `exec /usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin /bin/sh -c '<body>'` (one single-quoted argument, each `'` written as `'\''`; Fable follow-up LOW-2: no here-document, so no temp file anywhere, and `TMPDIR` is unset too), so the root shell gets none of the app's environment (`/bin/sh` is bash 3.2 and honours `SHELLOPTS`, `BASH_XTRACEFD`); the in-process runner also unsets `SHELLOPTS`, `BASH_XTRACEFD`, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `CDPATH`, `GLOBIGNORE` and `POSIXLY_CORRECT` before `executeAppleEvent`, which covers the outer `sh -c` that starts the wrapper.
2. **Busy → refuse (§4.5):** any `*.json` in `/Library/Application Support/lockplus/tunnel-states` (a Go tunnel is up) or any rule in the pf anchor `com.apple/wireguide` or its legacy `com.apple/wireguide/dns` sub-anchor (review F1-3) → `busy`. *E2E-7 F3:* a hard-killed helper leaves its state files (`{"tunnel_name","interface_name":"utunN"}`, no pid; only its next start clears them), so they are **stale**, not busy, only while launchd doesn't know the label (`launchctl print` exit 113; a loaded job is busy even with no process, exit 0 without a PID), `pgrep` finds neither the helper binary nor the old app, and every `*.json` is a root-owned regular file (not a symlink) directly in a root-owned directory naming exactly a `utun` absent from `ifconfig -l` (which must list `lo0`); any other answer or error stays `busy`. The pf, DNS-journal and old-app checks then run as usual, and `tunnel-states` goes with the data directory (step 5). *Accepted (Fable F3 review L3):* the old helper's crash recovery never runs then, so its endpoint bypass host routes (`internal/network/darwin.go` `Cleanup`) stay until a restart and can break a connect to the same server after a network change; the script prints `LP_STALE=tunnel-states` and the "removed" copy suggests a restart ("…left network routes behind: if LockPlus can't connect to a server, restart your Mac."). *L4/L5:* LockPlus's own utun can reuse the recorded number. Each `busy` prints a constant reason line first (`LP_BUSY=tunnel` from the state files, `LP_BUSY=pf` from the anchor rules); only `LP_BUSY=tunnel` while LockPlus is connected says to disconnect LockPlus first, then the old LockPlus or a restart. A pf busy (a Go or WireGuide kill switch) or a busy without a reason line keeps the plain copy that names the kill switch.
3. **Identity → refuse if not the Go helper:** `/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper.plist`, if present, must be a root-owned regular file (not a symlink) whose `Label` is `io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper` and `ProgramArguments[0]` is `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper` → else `not-go-plist`. That binary, if present, must be a root-owned regular file that satisfies `anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "M53GHX9FAY" and identifier "lockplus-helper"` (the Go installer's own pin, `internal/elevate/spawn_darwin.go`) → else `not-go-binary`.
3a. **Un-replayed DNS → refuse (review F1-2):** if `dns-journal.json` exists and launchd doesn't know the label, nothing would ever replay the journal (only the helper's startup does; `networksetup` DNS survives a restart) → `dns-unrestored`. *E2E-6 N1, review 650b251:* unless the journal is **stale**. `journalstale` reads the journal's `dns` map with `plutil` and judges each recorded service:
   - recorded nothing (Go 1.1.0 writes `null` for an Automatic baseline, which `plutil -type` reports as `(any)`; or `[]`): stale only while the service shows Automatic; a resolver there now is the VPN's → `dns-unrestored` ("set DNS to Automatic and try again" works);
   - recorded the user's own servers (e.g. a Pi-hole): stale only while exactly those are set again; otherwise → `dns-unrestored-manual`: "Restart your Mac — the old helper then restores your DNS settings — then remove it." (the old helper replays the journal at its next start; LockPlus never replays it as root);
   - `networksetup`'s text is localized, so only IPv4/IPv6 literal lines count; exit 0 with none is Automatic, in any language. Its stderr (CFPreferences warnings) is discarded;
   - fails closed: not a dictionary, a value that is neither null nor an array of at most 64 strings, a service name plutil can't address (`.`, `@`, empty), a non-zero exit or an error line from `networksetup`.
   A stale journal is removed with the data directory. *Caveat:* the journal's `search` domains aren't compared, so removing a stale journal doesn't restore search domains the VPN may have set; the user fixes them in System Settings › Network if needed. The app no longer refuses on the journal file alone (only root can read it); the copy offers three ways out: open the old LockPlus once (only when it is installed), set DNS back to Automatic and try again, or restart the Mac (the helper replays the journal at boot). While the journal is there and the helper isn't running, the store re-reads every 5 s, so the banner clears once a restarted helper has replayed it.
3c. **DNS protection left on → its own refusal (E2E-6 N2):** Go 1.0.68's "disconnect + quit" with DNS protection on leaves port-53-only rules in `com.apple/wireguide` (block port 53 except to a gone utun). With no tunnel up, an anchor whose rules are **all** port-53 rules (`dnsonly`) → `dns-protection-left`: "The old LockPlus left its DNS protection on. Restart your Mac to clear it, then remove the helper." Any other rule stays `busy`. The rules are not flushed by LockPlus.
3d. **Not responding → refuse without a prompt (Fable follow-up LOW-3):** app-side, a helper socket that is there but doesn't answer a connect, write or reply within the shared 2 s deadline is "not responding" (no socket or a refused connect is "not running", as in Go 1.2.0): "The old helper isn't responding. Restart your Mac, then remove it." The two known sockets are probed in parallel under one 2 s deadline.
3b. **Old app running → refuse (Fable pre-release A-3):** as root, right before the bootout, `pgrep -f '/Contents/MacOS/(lockplus|wireguide-plus)( |$)'` (the Go executable is lowercase `lockplus`, WireGuide+'s `wireguide-plus`; native 2.0's is `LockPlus` and never matches) → `old-app-running`, mapped to "Quit the old LockPlus first". The app's own check can be stale by then (the user opens the old app while the dialog is up).
4. `launchctl bootout system/io.github.steiale.lockplus.helper`: the helper's SIGTERM handler runs its cleanup (flushes its pf anchors, restores pf and DNS from its journal). Wait ≤ 10 s until launchd no longer knows the label → else `still-running`.
5. Remove only these exact paths: the plist; the binary; `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/openvpn` only if root-owned and signed as the Go app's `openvpn`; the socket `/var/run/lockplus/lockplus.sock` and its directory if empty; `/var/log/lockplus-helper.log` (root-only, may hold openvpn output); in `/Library/Application Support/lockplus` (root-owned, not a symlink) always `tunnel-states` and `ovpn-run` (generated profiles with inline keys; review F1-5), then the directory if empty. If `dns-journal.json` or `pf-was-enabled` is still there (the cleanup didn't run), that directory is kept and the result is `removed-left-state`: "…it left network settings behind. If websites don't load, set DNS back to Automatic in System Settings › Network, then restart your Mac." (a restart clears pf, not DNS).
6. Verify: plist and binary gone and the label unknown → `removed`, else `incomplete`.

*Leftovers come from root (E2E-6 N3):* 1.0.x's `/Library/Application Support/lockplus` is root 0700, so the app's `lstat` of `dns-journal.json` and `pf-was-enabled` fails; before the removal the app can know only what needs no root (the helper plist, the socket and its answer), so the crashed-with-firewall and leftover rows can't trigger for 1.0.x until the root step. The script reports what it kept, and why, as `LP_KEPT=<dns-journal|pf-was-enabled> <path>` lines next to its result, and the app takes the removal's "left network settings" from them instead of its own facts.

*Cosmetic, accepted (Fable follow-up):* starting native 2.0 from Terminal by a lowercase path (`…/MacOS/lockplus` on a case-insensitive volume) matches `old-app-running`. WireGuide+ ≤ 1.0.62's rules in the dot anchor `com.apple.wireguide` aren't listed by the script; pf never evaluates that anchor, so it is no protection gap. WireGuide+ 1.0.0's GUI (`com.korjwl1.wireguide`, executable `wireguide`) counts as the old app (app-side and as root) only when its `com.wireguide.helper` is ours, so a running upstream WireGuide never blocks a removal. The `com.wireguide.helper` signature check runs on the detector's queue, cached by path, mtime and size.

*Orphan binary (Fable pre-release A-4):* a helper binary without its plist (nothing launches it) is its own finding, `orphanBinary` ("A file of the old LockPlus helper is still installed. LockPlus can remove it; …"), and is removable: the script skips the plist checks and removes the binary only if it passes the same signature pin. Next to leftover network state it is removable too, except while a DNS journal waits for its replay (`dns-unrestored`, never "busy").

*Accepted (Fable pre-release A-5):* the main thread blocks for the whole dialog and script (inherent to `NSAppleScript`, whose contract is the main thread; the dialog is modal anyway). The localized prompt line lives in bundle resources, which the hardened runtime doesn't re-validate at run time: a same-user writer can change the dialog's text line, but not the script (a constant in the signed binary). Cosmetic, within the trust model above.

**App side (`LegacyHelperStore.removeHelper`).** Re-reads the helper first and enforces the button's rule (`canRemoveHelper`, review F1-6): only an idle helper; not while the Go app runs (review F1-1: its health monitor pings every 5 s and reinstalls a missing helper behind its own administrator prompt, so the banner says "Quit the old LockPlus first" and the store re-reads every 5 s until it quits); not while an unreachable helper's DNS journal exists (F1-2). No prompt in those cases; otherwise runs the script, reads the facts again and trusts only them (a `removed` with the plist still there is `incomplete`). UI states: removing ("Removing the old LockPlus helper…"), removed (or removed with network state left: restart), cancelled, failed (busy, not the old helper, incomplete, the system's message), with Try Again while the helper is still installed. Unit tests use a fake runner; the real command never runs in tests (the script is checked statically and with `sh -n`). **Not yet run against a live Go helper** (next E2E).

### 13.4 Cask transition

1. Beta: the native cask `lockplus-native` installs `LockPlus Native.app`, and the Go cask `lockplus` stays. Both zaps are scoped (§12.2).
2. Cutover:
   - publish Go v1.2.0 (cask `lockplus` 1.2.0);
   - wait 2 weeks;
   - switch the `lockplus` cask to the native 2.x artifact (`LockPlus.app`) with the §12.2 shape: `uninstall quit:` only, the native `--uninstall-system-components` under `zap` (O5). The upgrade from Go 1.2.0 runs the **installed Go** cask's `uninstall` stanza once, which only concerns the Go app.
   - `caveats` say: "If you used LockPlus 1.x, open it once to remove its helper (or run `…/LockPlus.app/Contents/MacOS/lockplus --uninstall-helper` before upgrading)."
3. `lockplus-native` is deprecated with `deprecate! because: "renamed to lockplus"`. Beta users keep the `LockPlus Native.app` path, and Sparkle updates it in place.
4. The wireguide-plus cask's zap is re-audited.

## 14. Observability

### 14.1 OSLog

| Subsystem | Categories |
|---|---|
| `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac` | `lifecycle`, `extension`, `xpc`, `profiles`, `import`, `keychain`, `connection`, `menubar`, `update`, `migration`, `diagnostics`, `ui` |
| `io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel` | `lifecycle` (incl. "first light" in `main.swift`, L-EXT-6), `xpc`, `controller`, `engine.wg`, `engine.ovpn`, `auth`, `dns`, `path`, `watchdog`, `secrets` |

Privacy rules:
- Interpolate only enums, state names, error codes, durations, counts and UUIDs as `.public`.
- Hostnames, IPs, SSIDs, usernames, profile names and challenge text are `.private(mask: .hash)`.
- Secrets are **never** passed to `Logger`; the `SecretBytes` type makes it impossible by accident.
- Server-controlled strings are `.private` and length-capped at 256.
- In addition, the extension writes records into an in-memory `LogRing` (2000 entries, `Mutex`, synchronous append from any thread). **The ring applies the same masking** as the unified log: every value that would be `.private` in `Logger` is stored already replaced by its hash (`<host#3fa2>`) (F-11).
- **Draft 8 (Fable review M1, Conflicts ax):** the ring is no longer read over XPC: `recentLogs` and `setLogLevel` were not uid-scoped and are removed. The ring keeps OpenVPN event names and, at `.debug`, the redacted engine lines, but **is delivered nowhere yet**. **TODO (`DiagnosticsHook`):** an owner-tagged ring (each line tagged with the session owner's uid) plus an owner-scoped way to put it into **that owner's** diagnostics bundle only. The same hook stub reports `secretStoreReset` (§6.3). The extension's log level (`EngineLogLevel`, default `.info`) is a startup setting of the Tunnel target.
- Profile names in the app's logs (draft 8, Fable app review L1): the id prefix is `.public`, the name `.private(mask: .hash)`.

### 14.2 Diagnostics bundle (F-11)

Settings › Advanced › "Export diagnostics…" (LAContext not required, because the bundle has no secrets) first shows a **"What's inside" preview**: the list of files below with their sizes and a scrollable, redacted view of each, plus a note on what is hashed and what is kept. *Draft 8 (Fable app review L6):* the "kept readable" set (DNS server IPs, tunnel routes, the default gateway, the probe hosts) applies **only to `routes.txt` and `dns.txt`**; everywhere else, including `profiles.json`, those values are hashed like any other address. Then it writes a zip (0600, `O_NOFOLLOW`; draft 9.1: built in memory with ZIPFoundation under a top-level `LockPlus Diagnostics/` folder, no scratch files and no `ditto`; written with `AtomicFile.writeUserFile`, which never changes the chosen folder's permissions, uses an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` 0600 temp file and reports failures instead of claiming success) containing:
- `system.json`: macOS version, model, app and extension versions, extension state (`propertiesRequest`), SIP status;
- `profiles.json`: profile metadata with names **hashed**, endpoints replaced by `host#hash:port`, policies, import reports;
- `ne-configs.json`: manager summaries (flags, on-demand rules with SSIDs hashed, probe hosts), never `providerConfiguration` raw values beyond the policy keys;
- `logs-app.txt` (last 24 h, `OSLogStore(scope: .currentProcessIdentifier)`, exported **through the Redactor**: unified-log `.private` values are visible to the process that wrote them) and `logs-tunnel.txt`. *Draft 8:* `logs-tunnel.txt` is the extension's unified-log output read with **`/usr/bin/log show --style ndjson` run as the user** (no XPC surface; macOS already shows `.private` values as `<private>`, the command shows only what this account may read, and the Redactor runs over it). A non-admin account gets "not permitted", which is recorded in the bundle and shown as a Logs footer as a documented gap;
- `dns.txt` (`scutil --dns` with server IPs kept, search and match domains hashed), `routes.txt` (draft 8: from `netstat -rn`; destinations inside the tunnel's routes and the default gateway kept; LAN host routes and other interfaces' non-default routes hashed), `history-summary.json` (counts only);
- every system tool runs through **`ProcessRunner`** (draft 8, app-root review M10, Fable app review L4): read-only, as the user, by absolute path, no shell and no PATH lookup; the pipe is drained to EOF continuously (the first N bytes kept), so a chatty tool never stalls on a full pipe; completion comes from `terminationHandler`; the timeout keeps its sub-second part; nothing blocks the cooperative pool;
- `crash/*.ips`: our own crash reports from `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` (app) and, if readable, the extension's, each passed through the Redactor (paths with the user name, thread names and any string literals); no third-party crash SDK is used. *Draft 8 (Fable app review L7):* each report is opened `O_NOFOLLOW` and checked with `fstat` (no symlink race);
- `legacy.json` (§4.5 findings).
- `selftest.txt` (2.0.2, D10.4-8): the last connection self-test report, in English, passed through the Redactor like every non-kept file, so its addresses are hashed (only if a test ran this session).

**One `Redactor` policy for every file:** a pure, unit-tested function with corpora of keys, passwords, CRV1/SCRV1 strings, auth-tokens, PEM blocks, user names, SSIDs and hostnames. Every file in the bundle (including `ne-configs.json`, `routes.txt`, `dns.txt` and the `.ips` files, which draft 3 passed through unredacted) goes through it, with the same hash salt per bundle so the same host hashes identically across files. A test builds the full bundle of a fixture system with planted secrets and asserts none appear in any file.

## 15. Testing strategy

### 15.1 Unit (LockPlusCore, TunnelEngine, app stores)

Framework and rules (ref/swift-concurrency §12, SC18): Swift Testing; `confirmation(expectedCount:)` checks when its closure returns and does **not** wait for late events, so tests await the work that produces them; `.timeLimit` has a one-minute minimum, so short deadlines come from the injected clock. **`ManualClock`** (~70 lines in `TunnelEngineTestSupport`; synchronous sleeper registration under a `Mutex`, `waitForSleepers(n)`, `advance(by:)`) replaces swift-clocks (a new dependency, and `megaYield`-based). The unit scheme sets `LIBDISPATCH_COOPERATIVE_POOL_STRICT=1`; a nightly TSan job covers `TunnelEngine` and the shim (§12.4). `Backoff` gets a seeded generator.

- **OVPN tokenizer:** port every case of `internal/ovpn/validate_test.go`, `ovpn27_test.go` and `realprofiles_test.go`:
  - quotes, single quotes, backslashes;
  - inline close tags with trailing text;
  - `<connection>` re-parse and nesting rejection, and a non-remote/port/proto directive inside `<connection>` rejected;
  - BOM, NUL, 256-character lines, 16-parameter truncation;
  - `--` prefixes;
  - `setenv opt` recursion.
  - The Go test vectors are exported as JSON fixtures by a one-off Go test helper committed to the Go tree, so both implementations run the **same** vectors.
- **Allowlist:** every rule, every rejection message (directive name only, no args).
- **Differential (L-OVPN-1):**
  1. Swift tokenizer vs `OpenVPN3Options` on the corpus (unit) and under fuzzing (§15.4). A mismatch on canonical output fails.
  2. Canonical → openvpn3 → re-serialize is the identity.
  3. The Go 2.7 tokenizer vs the Swift port on the shared fixtures. Equality is required.
- **EngineSupport:** covers exactly the allowlist; the regenerated table equals the committed one (§8.2); the canonical caps (openvpn3's size accounting with the 16-byte name term, 254-byte directive lines and 512-byte inline body lines (draft 8), 64-char names, 4096-byte `<connection>`) reject at the boundary +1; the repeatable list keeps every occurrence and every other directive keeps its last; a nested `setenv opt setenv opt X` is classified as X; `ping`/`ping-restart` are dropped when `keepalive` is present; `remote-cert-eku` is appended exactly when `remote-cert-tls server` is present without it.
- **Normalizer, draft 7 (S13/S8):** a repeated singleton keeps the last occurrence and adds a note; `http-proxy` with only UDP remotes is rejected; `cipher none`, every 64-bit-block cipher and `auth MD5` are rejected with the §8.3 message; `auth-nocache` is appended exactly for OTP-class profiles; `setenv opt X` is classified as X by our table for every X on the S13 fixture list (`socks-proxy`, `management`, `register-dns`, `ping-timer-rem`, …); the shim config never sets `enableLegacyAlgorithms`.
- **Shim config:** `ssoMethods == ""` (**IV_SSO never advertised**), `disableClientCert == !(cert && key)`, `dhcpSearchDomainsAsSplitDomains == false`, `retryOnAuthFailed == false`, for every fixture profile.
- **Metadata HMAC:** a flipped bit in any field → quarantine; a missing master-key item (`errSecItemNotFound`) with files present → "locked" UX and no key is generated, while `-25308`/`-34018` give "Keychain unavailable" instead (§6.8); an older validly MAC'd file (lower `metaRevision` or `payloadRevision` than the manager's `providerConfiguration`) → quarantine, and the manager is not re-saved (§3.4, N6); `payloadKey` ≠ `macKey` (HKDF separation).
- **Keychain error classification:** each OSStatus of §6.2 maps to its `KeychainError` case; only -25300 yields `nil`.
- **RevealGate (F-10):** every code path to `ProfileStore.payload(for:)` **and to `CredentialStore.load` from UI code** (Edit Config, Export, Export All, **"Show password"**, **Duplicate**, the editor's key "Show") goes through `RevealGate` (a test enumerating the call sites via a protocol witness and the `RevealToken` parameter, §1.3 A6); the gate's context is invalidated at expiry, lock, sleep and deactivation.
- **Signing requirements (draft 5):** one configuration compiles only one variant, so "both Release and both Debug strings compile" in one run is impossible. The host-less `RequirementTests` bundle (it compiles `ActiveRequirements.swift` with the same conditions as the app and extension) holds the **expected Release strings as literals** and runs under two test plans: **Unit** (Debug: asserts `SigningRequirements.appReq/extReq(signer: releaseSigner)` equal the literals, the live `APP_REQ`/`EXT_REQ` equal the literals with the dev clause, and all four compile with `SecRequirementCreateWithStringAndErrors`) and **UnitRelease** (Release configuration: asserts the live `APP_REQ`/`EXT_REQ` equal the Release literals byte for byte, compile, and contain no `100.6.2.1`). CI runs both plans (§12.4 `build` job); `verify.sh` adds the `strings` check on the Release Mach-Os and the `-showBuildSettings -configuration Release` check for `LP_DEV_SIGNING` on the three targets (§5.3, draft 6).
- **Activation preflight:** a table test of `propertiesRequest` results × manager states → quiesce/submit/refuse/`.removedDuringUpdate` decisions (§4.2); the replacement delegate is a pure function (equal versions → `.replace`, lower → `.cancel`).
- **`LegacyAppDetector` table (F-14):** helper plist present/absent × socket reachable (active / idle / kill switch on) / unreachable × `pf-was-enabled` × DNS journal × Go GUI running → exactly the §4.5 policy row.
- **WG parser and validator:** port `parser_test.go` and `validator_dns_test.go`; add wg-quick inline-comment (and unstripped hooks), bare-IP, CRLF, `PersistentKeepalive = off`, prefix > 32/128 rejected, duplicate scalar rejected, host-bits normalization, `FwMark` `0x`/`off` cases.
- **Legacy keychain decode:** b64, hex and plain fixtures (`keychain_darwin_test.go` vectors).
- **NetworkSettingsBuilder:** the `::/0` blackhole appears exactly when `isFullTunnel && !hasIPv6 && (killSwitch || blockIPv6WithoutKillSwitch)` (§10.5, N4); **no excluded route to `remoteAddress` is ever produced** (§8.5); `tunnelRemoteAddress` equals the plan's current server IP; no settings-level `includeAllNetworks`/`excludeLocalNetworks`/`enforceRoutes`/`exclude*` property is set (§10.1); `allowFailover == false` always; MTU 1420 default for both families; `excludeLocalNetworks` per the §10.1 table, false when the **profile** has `block-local` (draft 8: a pushed one is ignored with a note, §8.5); **`ExcludedRouteGuard`** (draft 8): on a full tunnel an undeclared excluded route of /15 (v4) or /47 (v6) fails with `.pushedOptionRejected`, /16 and /48 pass, the 17th undeclared route fails with detail `route count`, profile-declared `net_gateway` routes are exempt and uncounted, and split tunnels are untouched.
- **Shim fd ownership:** `tun_builder_establish` never returns the provider's fd number, and closing what it returned leaves the provider's fd valid (`fcntl(F_GETFD)`), §7.3 (N2); with two utun control sockets open, the selection rule picks the one carrying the applied address and asserts uniqueness (D10); with a lingering dup on an older utun plus two candidates on the current one (the S7 `s7fdrule` layout), it picks the current interface.
- **Shim `Stop` lifetime (draft 7.3, run under the `asan` job, §12.4):** create → stop → destroy, connect → reconnect ×3 → stop → destroy, stop before connect, and destroy without connect all finish without an abort or an ASan report (§8.4; the host-side `ovpn-lifecycle` pattern of S11).
- **`PacketFlowPump` (draft 7.3, §7.3; with a fake flow):** exactly one outstanding `readPackets` per session across 20 attach/detach cycles and a held restart; packets read while nothing is attached are dropped and the read is re-armed; a retired fd's read source is cancelled at once and its fd closed under the send lock (draft 8; AF_UNIX fd count back to baseline after 20 cycles); no send after a retire; an `attach` after `endSession` closes the fd and creates no source; an empty packet is dropped; the pump is ended on a failed start too; both ends get buffers ≥ 1 MB; AF header added and stripped for v4 and v6.
- **`RouteProbe` (draft 7.3, §9.3):** with an injected routing table, an endpoint routed via the default route's interface → ok; via another interface → flagged with that interface's name; a flagged start that times out fails with `.endpointInterfaceUnusable` (and `detail` = the name), an unflagged one with `.connectTimeout`.
- **`EstablishTicket`:** first answer wins; a timeout answers `-1`; a stop answers `-1` before `client.stop()`.
- **Resume agent:** `--resume-protection` with `pausedUntil` in the future, in the past, absent, with the instance lock held by a GUI instance, and with a stale `agentBuild` → no-op / resume + durable write + unregister / unregister / exit / re-register (§10.4, N3).
- **Auto-profile suspend/resume (F-14):** manually connecting another profile disables the auto profile's on-demand; disconnecting it restores exactly the saved on-demand state; disconnecting the auto profile sets "paused until another network"; the §12.3 update path restores every manager in `onDemandEnabledIDs` (N5).
- **Session merge (F-14):** `sessionSummaries` merged into `history.json` by session UUID is idempotent (a re-pull adds nothing), keeps on-demand sessions recorded while the app was closed, and respects the 500-entry cap.
- **DNS mapping:** a table test of `DNSPlan` → `NEDNSSettings` for each §10.2 row; `DOMAIN` lands in search domains (flag false); a full kill-switch tunnel with `dns == nil` fails with `.dnsPlanMissing`; the pull-filter vectors from `config.go` `filterPushed`.
- **State machine:** `TunnelController` with `FakeAdapter`, `FakeHost`, `ManualClock`, `FakePathWatcher`. One test per transition row in §7.2, plus:
  - completion called exactly once (`CompletionOnce` returns `false` on a second call; the test fails on `false`);
  - `stopTunnel` during each pending start phase → start completion `.startCancelled` first (the held error `e` when it ends a before-Connected hold), then teardown, then the stop completion;
  - `fatal` → `cancel` with the kill switch off, **after** the adapter's stop completed, the session summary was written and the path watcher ended (draft 9, S2 E3: the test holds the adapter's stop and sees no cancel until it returns); `fatal` → `held(.blockedAfterFailure)` with it on, for every after-Connected code, and **never** a cancel (route protection included);
  - non-retryable error under on-demand → after Connected `held(.nonRetryable)` and `sessionEnded` (status `.reasserting`, `setReasserting(true)`); before Connected a `.hard` latch is armed and `sessionEnded` pushed, the start fails with `e` without `includeAllNetworks` and is held with it (`setReasserting` never called);
  - **withhold (draft 9, S2 E14):** with `includeAllNetworks` every failure before Connected (validation, store, settings, `dnsPlanMissing`, a connect deadline, an engine error, a prompt deadline, a cancelled prompt) holds the start with the adapter down and no completion; a retryable one retries inside the hold on the clock (not before its backoff deadline) and a retry that connects completes the start once with success; a non-retryable one never retries (1000 s pass, nothing restarts); `stopTunnel` completes the start with `e`; a higher-revision provision, `removeProfile` or `wipeAllSecrets` ends a pending start in any phase (held, a retry attempt in flight, `AUTH_PENDING`, with `promptResolved`); `.dnsResolutionFailed` holds without retry; `updateCredentials` retries at once; route protection (split tunnel) and kill switch off fail the start as before; latches as in draft 6 (`.hard` for a non-retryable `e`, `.backoff` for a retryable one under on-demand rules, none for a manual session without on-demand rules);
  - start latch: an on-demand start (`options == nil`) with a `.hard` latch, or a `.backoff` latch before `notBefore`, ends before any credential load or network I/O (`FakeAdapter.start` never called): failed without the flag, **held** with it (a `.backoff` latch then retries at `notBefore`); the backoff doubles 5 s → 5 min and success clears it; a manual start, a higher-revision provision, `updateCredentials`, **`removeProfile` and `wipeAllSecrets`** clear it; the pre-login `.secretStoreUnavailable` arms `.backoff`, never `.hard`;
  - **no start budget (draft 9):** `ControllerConfig` has none; each attempt is bounded by its connect deadline (WG 45 s, OVPN 50 s, also during a slow `host.apply`), a prompt in the start by its own deadline (nothing ends it at 50 s);
  - **auth inside the pending start (draft 9):** a manual start whose attempt ends with CRV1 / `AUTH_FAILED` (< 3) / `NEED_CREDS` stays pending in `awaitingAuth(beforeConnected: true)` with exactly one prompt (`nextStart == false`, deadline 10 min, CRV1 5 min), no latch and no error recorded; the matching answer starts a new attempt in the same start whose adapter consumes `{answer, cookie, carried base credentials}` once, and the start then completes once with success; a second answer is stale; the third rejection is the failure rows; the prompt deadline and `cancelAuth` take the failure rows (held with the flag); an on-demand start never prompts (`.hard` latch); `AUTH_PENDING` keeps the running attempt, stops the connect deadline and is answered through `provideAuth`; `prepareStartAuth`'s answer is taken by the owner's next manual start only, once (not by an on-demand start; dropped by a failed start, expiry, `cancelAuth`, a newer prompt, `removeProfile`, `wipeAllSecrets` and a higher-revision provision); start options carry nothing but `lp.manual` and `lp.endpoints` (a promptID in them has no effect);
  - CRV1 inside the start: the new attempt's `AdapterStart.stash` holds the response, the cookie and the carried (or stored) base credentials; **draft 7:** `AUTH_FAILED` after a CRV1 response triggers exactly one fresh first connect in the same attempt (no cookie), prompts again with `reason: .rejected`, counts toward the 3-in-10-min limit;
  - **engine loops made fatal (draft 7):** a first `CLIENT_RESTART` "rejected pushed option" → `.fatal(.pushedOptionRejected)`; a first `BF-CBC: not usable` → `.fatal(.legacyCryptoUnavailable)`; an `INFO WEB_AUTH:` during `awaitingAuth(.pendingApproval)` → `.webAuthUnsupported` at once;
  - **endpoints and DNS (draft 9, S2 E10):** the start's `lp.endpoints` win over the cache and are cached on success; the start-time interface check gets their union; `providerDNS` is false with `includeAllNetworks`; WireGuard under the flag never calls its resolver and fails at once without IPs; without the flag it resolves a missing host within 2 s and reports it for the cache; the OpenVPN rewriter turns hostname remotes (top level and `<connection>` blocks) into one remote per IP, leaves inline blocks alone and drops unresolved hosts under the flag;
  - **strict timers and paths (draft 9):** `ProductionTunnelController` is `TunnelController<StrictSuspendingClock>`; the strict clock fires on time, honours cancellation (also before it sleeps) and returns at once for a past deadline; `PathSnapshot` drops our utun and duplicates (`[en0, en0, utun4]` → `[en0]`), so a utun-only difference never reasserts a connected session;
  - *(draft 8: `apply` takes a non-optional spec, so "never passes `nil`" holds by type, C20, Conflicts au);*

### 15.2 Integration (on a signed dev build, self-hosted Mac)

Dev builds are Apple Development-signed (O7), so XPC integration runs with the Debug requirement; the Release requirement is exercised only by the shipped RC (§15.3, §15.6).
- Activation outcomes: approval needed (fresh VM), replace, downgrade refused, `.unsupportedParentBundleLocation` (app run from `~/Downloads`), user disables the extension in System Settings → `.disabledByUser`.
- XPC peer validation: an unsigned client, a team-signed client with the wrong identifier, and the right one; the client error codes are 4097/4099/4102 and the extension logs nothing for rejected peers.
- Extension secret store (S4 selected (a) on 27, draft 7.3: the System keychain store on every run, the container fallback once per release): provision, read at connect, update, delete, `wipeAll` (System keychain items gone; container files gone). Fallback files are root 0600 in a 0700 dir; a planted symlink in `secrets/` is refused. Secrets stay readable after an extension update and after a reboot (before and after login) (S4). A 256 KiB payload round-trips. `index()` returns each provisioned profile exactly once (the raw query returns duplicates, §6.3).
- **Exec is denied (draft 8, PF 29; to add):** a FaultInjection hook in the extension attempts an `execve` and the test asserts it fails under the sysex sandbox, which backs the `_execve`-from-`libwg-go` allowance (§8.1).
- **ASan integration run (draft 7.3, §2.2; self-hosted Mac, once per release, non-gating like the rest of §15.2):** an ASan build of the extension (runtime embedded in its own `Frameworks`) runs the S7 sequence (50 alternating WG/OVPN sessions, 50 WG stop/start, the fd-rule fault case), the S11 reconnect run in both data-plane modes and the store checks, plus a deliberate 1-byte overflow (`asanSelfTest`) to prove the instrumentation is live. Pass: no ASan report and no crash report.
- Activation preflight (§4.2): `brew upgrade` and a non-Finder copy with the app closed and the tunnel up → on launch the tunnel is stopped before the request, replaced, and resumed; a Finder drag-replace → the system's removal prompt, then `.removedDuringUpdate` and fresh activation. "Reinstall tunnel component" from N to N-1, including the `.extensionNotFound` guided-removal path (§4.6).
- Captive portal (§10.4): a test AP with a portal (a small Linux VM serving a 302) → no on-demand connect, CNA appears, the app connects after the probe succeeds; "Pause protection" round trip; the same with the first probe host blackholed (the second rule connects); pause, then `kill -9` the app, sleep across the expiry, and reboot before expiry → the resume agent resumes at wake/login within the §10.4 bound (N3, N7).
- WG against a test server (docker on a VPS): connect, data-plane-up timing, endpoint failover (first A record blackholed; settings re-applied with the new `tunnelRemoteAddress`), MTU applied (`ifconfig utunN`), 50× stop/start in one extension process without `exit` (K15).
- OVPN against test servers:
  - UDP, TCP, tls-crypt-v2;
  - CBC-only (`cipher AES-256-CBC`, no NCP) connects; a BF-CBC profile is **rejected at import** (draft 7, §8.6); a profile without `cipher` against the non-NCP 2.4.7 server fails with `.legacyCryptoUnavailable` within 5 s, with no reconnect loop;
  - a profile `pull-filter reject "redirect-gateway"` against the push server fails with `.pushedOptionRejected` on the first push, with no 5 s restart loop;
  - password-only profile without cert/key (`disableClientCert`);
  - password, SC (SCRV1 and concat), CRV1 (a server that issues a CRV1 with a username; the display name comes from the cookie), AUTH_FAILED → re-prompt, `AUTH_FAILED,TEMP` → no prompt, `SESSION_EXPIRED` → prompt, `AUTH_PENDING` → "Waiting for sign-in approval" then connect (approved within 30 s; and approved after 55 s → the start fails with `.authRequired` before 50 s and the next start succeeds);
  - **auth inside the pending start (draft 9):** unsaved password and SC prompt before the start (the server log shows exactly one login and one start); CRV1: the start stays `.connecting`, the answer in the same start sends `CRV1::<state>::<response>` with the cookie's username (server log), an answer given after 4 min still connects (the server's 300 s window), the sheet expires at the 5 min prompt deadline, and an answer to an expired state yields a fresh challenge rather than "wrong password" (draft 7); a rejected password re-prompts in the same start and the next attempt sends the new password; with the kill switch the Mac stays blocked while the sheet shows (capture on en0) and a cancel restores it; a start that waits 5 min for an answer is not stopped by the system (`log stream` on `nesessionmanager`, S2 E14b);
  - an OTP profile on a server **without** `auth-gen-token`: force a reconnect (`ping-restart`) → a prompt appears and the server log shows no login attempt with the stale OTP (M6); the same with `auth-gen-token` → silent reconnect;
  - a profile with each openvpn3-fatal directive class (server-only, push-only, removed, `management*`, unknown) and an unknown inline block (`<pkcs12>`) → rejected at **import** by [7b], never at connect;
  - **LK-OVPN-CERT:** a server presenting a CA-signed certificate **without EKU** → `CERT_VERIFY_FAIL` with `remote-cert-tls server`, and with only the appended `remote-cert-eku`; CONNECTED with neither (proves the server discriminates; the S13 `noeku` server). The clientAuth-only server (`ovpn-badeku`) stays as a second case but is not the regression test (§1.3 A4);
  - WEB_AUTH → `.webAuthUnsupported` within 2 s; the test server's logged peer info contains **no `IV_SSO`**;
  - a server pushing `dns server`, `dhcp-option`, PUSH_UPDATE (CONNECTED re-emitted, settings re-applied), plus profile `pull-filter ignore "dhcp-option"`;
  - `stopTunnel` during `connect()` setup is honoured (`get_async_stop`).
- **Real profiles (spike gate and regression):** Acme and Globex, run manually on each release candidate. Credentials are never in CI.
- L-LC-1: close the wireguard-go device via `wgDebugCloseDevice` (W6) → `wgIsClosed` → status leaves `.connected` ≤ 5 s.
  - **Fault injection lives only in a separate `FaultInjection` build configuration** (its own scheme and its own compile flag `LP_FAULT_INJECTION`; never archived for release). `FaultInjection.xcconfig` includes `Debug.xcconfig`, so FaultInjection builds are Apple Development-signed with the unsuffixed NE value and inherit `LP_DEV_SIGNING`: the FaultInjection app and extension accept each other through the dev clause (§5.3). Both flags are target-level conditions, never package conditions (§2.2), and the fault hooks themselves live in the extension target or behind the Go build tag of W6. **Package `DEBUG` paths are off in FaultInjection builds** (draft 6): Xcode builds SPM package targets with the release settings for a configuration not named Debug (forum 45506), so package-level `#if DEBUG` code, `assert`/`assertionFailure` (for example in `CompletionOnce`) and `-Onone` don't apply there; FaultInjection tests must not rely on them. S14 confirmed this with a compiled probe package (`-showBuildSettings` returns nothing for package targets in Xcode 27.1, §2.2). CI's `build` job and the dev-Mac `release.sh` both assert that the Release binary contains no `debugInjectFault`/`wgDebugCloseDevice` symbol.
  - These tests are **non-gating** for releases: they verify engine logic, not the shipped binary. The release gates (§15.3) use only the shipped RC.

### 15.3 Leak harness (L-KS-1, L-KS-4, L-DNS-1)

`Tools/leak-harness/lp-leakcheck` (*draft 8: not built yet*; P3/M4 item, §18):
- runs as root on the self-hosted Mac;
- tests the **shipped release candidate**, i.e. the notarized build from the draft release, exactly as users get it. There is no automation XPC and no DEBUG hook (M3);
- drives it only through interfaces that exist in the shipped product:
  - `scutil --nc list/start/stop/status "<name>"` for connect, disconnect and status (it works on any NE configuration by name). **`scutil --nc start` yields `options == nil`, so the extension treats it as on-demand and latched (§5.2, §7.2; draft 6.1):** a case that needs manual semantics (clearing a `.hard`/`.backoff` latch, consuming a stash) first clears the latch (a manual start through the app, a re-provision with a higher revision or `updateCredentials`) or starts via the app's automation path; the harness must not assume `scutil --nc start` clears a latch;
  - fixtures are imported once per machine through the shipped file-open path (`open -a LockPlus fixture.conf`) and confirmed in the UI. Each policy variant is a separate pre-imported profile (`wg-ks`, `wg-noks`, `ovpn-tcp-ks`, `wg-split-rp`, `wg-v4only-noks`, `wg-v4only-noks-block6`, …), so the harness never toggles policy;
  - root-level OS actions: `pkill -9 -f io.github.steiale.lockplus.mac.tunnel`, `pmset`, `networksetup`, `route`/test-router rules;
  - Sparkle through the shipped `rc` channel (§12.1) for LK-10;
- captures on the physical interfaces (`en0` Wi-Fi, `en7` USB Ethernet) with BPF;
- runs the whole suite once per `dataPlane` mode (`.utunFD`, `.packetFlow`; §7.3). *Draft 8:* the product has no `dataPlane` switch, so the `.packetFlow` pass needs a FaultInjection-only switch in the extension (to build) and is then a non-gating suite like the other FaultInjection runs; the gating pass on the shipped RC is `.utunFD`;
- reaches every test server **via the self-hosted Mac's primary interface**, because the extension cannot reach a server behind a non-primary interface such as the colima bridge (S6, §9.3). The servers are the test VPS or a server host on the primary LAN. The en0 → colima relay of §15.7 is **not** used here: traffic to the Mac's own address never crosses a physical NIC, so the capture would not see the transport.
- Fault injection (`FaultInjection` build, §15.2) is a separate, non-gating suite.
- **Pass criterion for every window:** zero packets on a physical interface except
  - to or from the VPN endpoint (IP:port, proto);
  - DHCP, ARP, ND, RA;
  - with `allowLAN`, link-local and connected-subnet traffic;
  - **(draft 9, S2, D9-19)** APNs (17.57.x.x:5223, `excludeAPNs`) including its DNS lookups while blocked; for ≤ 3.5 s after `.connected`, the tail of flows opened before the switch (Apple QUIC); a probe packet within 20 ms of a state switch (in flight, not a leak).
- **Harness rules from S2 (draft 9):** the flag cuts SSH, so a run executes **detached in the target** (root) and writes its results locally; capture on the target's own en0; one WireGuard peer per concurrently running client (a shared peer roams the endpoint and stalls both); never capture during a throughput run (tens of GB per hour). The S2 scripts (`native/spike/s2/`: `run.sh`, `analyze.py`, probes every ~0.35 s for ICMP, TCP 443 and UDP DNS) are the starting point.

| Case | Scenario | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| LK-01 | Connected baseline (WG UDP; OVPN UDP) | criterion holds for 60 s of `curl`/`dig`/`ping` load |
| LK-02 | `kill -9` the extension while connected (kill switch on) | **Outcome (§10.1.1, draft 9 from S2 E1):** no packet on a physical interface except to the VPN endpoint, **except within ≤ 4 s after NE reports the failure** (measured 2.45–2.86 s), and the tunnel is back without user action; status leaves `.connected` ≤ 8 s. Repeated with an on-demand profile: the measured open time is recorded (NE doesn't restart; draft 10: the running app restarts it after 1.5 s, §10.4; §20 risk 24). *Draft 10, E2E-1 (VMs, product 200001, WG, `Tools/e2e/guest/ks.sh`): open 1.70 s (26) and 1.68 s (27), GO* |
| LK-03 | Reconnect: the server drops (endpoint blackholed by test-router rule), 3 min | blocking continues during `reasserting` (L-KS-1) |
| LK-04 | Sleep/wake (`pmset sleepnow` + `pmset schedule wake`) | no packets before the tunnel is up; reconnects ≤ 30 s (L-RC-5). *Draft 10: **manual, on real hardware.** VZ guests don't sleep (E2E-1: `pmset sleepnow` is a no-op, powerd keeps PreventUserIdleSystemSleep)* |
| LK-05 | Wi-Fi → Ethernet → Wi-Fi switch (`networksetup -setnetworkserviceenabled`) | no leak; reasserting → connected ≤ 20 s (L-RC-1) |
| LK-06 | Fragments and large packets: `ping -s 4000` through the tunnel, 1 GB SMB copy, RDP session for 5 min (L-KS-4) | no stalls; throughput ≥ 70 % of baseline |
| LK-07 | OpenVPN over TCP: LK-01..06 repeated with a `proto tcp` profile | same |

| LK-09 | IPv6: a v4-only full tunnel on a dual-stack LAN, three profiles: kill switch **on** (`wg-ks`), **off** (`wg-v4only-noks`), and off with "Block IPv6 without the kill switch" (`wg-v4only-noks-block6`) | on: no v6 egress on the physical NIC (includeAllNetworks + blackhole); off + toggle: no v6 egress (blackhole); off without toggle: v6 egress to the LAN is **expected** and recorded, matching the Go app and the UI warning (§10.5) |

Traffic before the pause is allowed only within the S1-recorded captive exemption (§10.1) |
| LK-16 | **ServerIP (TunnelCrack, F-3):** while connected, a user-space `curl` (and `nc -u`) to the **connected server's IP** on a port other than the tunnel's, for a kill-switch WG profile, a kill-switch OVPN profile and a non-kill-switch profile | the packets appear **only inside the tunnel** (on utun), never on a physical interface; any packet to the server IP on `en0` other than the tunnel transport's own 5-tuple fails the case |
| LK-17 | **Profile switch (F-12):** connected to kill-switch profile A, switch to kill-switch profile B from the menu; repeat A (kill switch) → C (no kill switch) | the unprotected window between A's stop and B's start is measured and recorded (expected: under 2 s); no packets outside it; the A → C switch shows the confirmation of UI-CONCEPT §6.2 |

### 15.4 Fuzzing

**Draft 8 (Conflicts aw; PF 9): Xcode 27.1's `swiftc` rejects `-sanitize=fuzzer`.** The targets are written as `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` entry points and built by `Tools/fuzz/build.sh`, which probes the toolchain:
- **Standalone mode (Xcode 27.1, the CI default):** ASan + SanitizerCoverage and the bundled driver (`Tools/fuzz/driver/`), which replays the corpus and its regressions and then runs seeded mutations (`FUZZ_ITERATIONS`, 2000 in CI). LPModel and LPParsing are compiled as one module from copies under `$LP_BUILD_ROOT/fuzz/` (never `/tmp`; the package sources are not edited).
- **libFuzzer mode:** used automatically when a swift.org toolchain is selected (`TOOLCHAINS=…` or `LP_FUZZ_SWIFTC`). A nightly real-libFuzzer job is optional and only if added later. No Homebrew llvm dependency.

Targets as built: `fuzz_ovpn_tokenizer`, `fuzz_ovpn_import` (tokenizer → allowlist → normalizer; the normalizer output re-tokenizes to the same stream), `fuzz_wg_parser`, `fuzz_legacy_keychain`, and (draft 9.1) `fuzz_zip_import`: `App/Services/ProfileZip.swift` (2.0.2: `Packages/ProfileValidator/Sources/LPValidatorService/ArchiveReader.swift` + `LPModel/ZipModel.swift`, where the reader now lives) compiled against ZIPFoundation at the `pins.sh` pin (fetched into `$LP_BUILD_ROOT/fuzz/ZIPFoundation`, commit-checked, built as its own Swift 5 module with the same sanitizers); it runs the validator, the full reader and, for every archive the validator accepts, ZIPFoundation's full iteration and capped inflation, asserting the iteration count. Corpus: `Tools/fuzz/corpus/<ovpn|wg|keychain|zip>/`, with the Go vectors exported by `Tools/fuzz/govectors/`. Crashes become fixtures in `Tools/fuzz/corpus/regressions/` (the nested-`setenv opt` classification, §8.2, came from one). `fuzz_lpwire_decode` is covered by the LPWire decode-fuzz unit test over every request type (§15.1).

**Not built yet** (§18): `fuzz_engine_check` (2.0.2, optional in the plan: `OpenVPNEngineCheck.evaluate` under ASan; no ASan driver for the shim exists, and the parity golden test covers the move), `fuzz_ovpn3_options` (C++: `OpenVPN3Options` parse of arbitrary bytes under clang ASan; memory safety of openvpn3's parser), `fuzz_crv1_cookie`, and the 8 h nightly run on the self-hosted Mac (the M5 gate).

The Swift-vs-openvpn3 differential is **not fuzzed** in v2.0. The Linux build and the C++ differential harness are cut (§21). Coverage comes from the unit differential over the shared corpus (§15.1), plus the import pipeline's runtime check [6], which rejects any disagreement for real inputs.

### 15.5 Update tests (L-UPD-1)

- A macOS 26 and a macOS 27 VM (`LP-macOS-26`, `LP-macOS-27`; Virtualization.framework via UTM, on the dev Mac) or a spare Mac; the same two VMs serve the S9/S10 matrix (draft 7.1; draft 7 had a third, 15.1 VM). **Manual, checklist-driven** for v2.0; Tart and MDM-scripted approval are cut (§21). Upgrade paths are tested on clean VM snapshots, never only on the dev Mac (rebuild churn confuses Background Task Management and launchd).
- Each VM keeps a snapshot "N-1 installed, extension approved by hand, fixtures imported, `rc` channel on". Approval is done by hand once per VM image; later same-team replacements need no re-approval. UTM 5 snapshots Apple VMs at **disk level** only (taken shut down), and the approval may also live in the VM's auxiliary storage; check once per OS that restoring keeps `[activated enabled]`, otherwise use APFS clones (`utmctl clone`) instead (§15.7).
- From the snapshot: connect with the kill switch on, then "Check for Updates" picks up the RC from the `rc` channel (§12.1).
- Assert:
  - `systemextensionsctl list` shows N activated and enabled, with N-1 terminated;
  - the tunnel resumes;
  - profiles, credentials (connect without prompt) and history are intact;
  - no dialog other than Sparkle's (in particular, no §11.3 quit dialog during the install);
  - a running old app whose bundle was replaced does not hang on a rejected XPC call (`errSecCSStaticCodeChanged`, -67034; ref/security C17).
- Also (ref/sparkle C17):
  - the **"Install on Quit"** path: quit, relaunch manually → the §4.2 preflight quiesces, replaces and resumes;
  - **install failure** after preparation (make `/Applications/LockPlus.app` non-writable for a standard user) → nothing stays stopped (variant B) and the error is shown;
  - a downgrade attempt is refused automatically, and "Reinstall tunnel component" performs it on request (§4.6);
  - with the app **quit and the tunnel up**: install N over N-1 by `brew upgrade`, by `brew upgrade --greedy` (credentials not wiped, extension not deactivated: the cask has no `uninstall script:`), by `ditto`, and by Finder drag-replace (the system's removal prompt, then `.removedDuringUpdate`), then launch (§4.2);
  - no §11.3 dialog during Sparkle's install, `brew upgrade` or logout;
  - with a `stayConnected` profile and the auto profile both on-demand enabled: the update disables on-demand on both, and both are restored afterwards (N5);
  - a **pause active across an update**: the resume agent is re-registered for the new binary (§10.4) and still ends the pause;
  - a phased item is not offered to a background check before its group's time but is offered to "Check for Updates…";
  - **once before GA, a key-rotation drill** on a VM (ref/sparkle C16): (1) a zip signed with the **old** key carrying a new public key → accepted; (2) a zip signed **only** with the new key → refused; (3) a Developer ID-signed DMG whose `edSignature` uses the new key, old key unavailable → accepted; (4) the follow-up zip signed with the new key → accepted. The lost-key feed behaviour uses a test build with `SUSignedFeedFailureExpirationInterval = 300`.

### 15.6 Security test checklist (each release; Fable reviews the code, these verify behaviour)

- [ ] XPC (Release RC): an unsigned peer, a wrong-identifier peer, an Apple Development-signed copy of the app, and a **tampered copy of the real Release app** (one byte changed in a resource, re-launched) are each rejected before any handler runs; the client sees 4097/4099/4102 and the extension logs no accept or handler line. The app rejects a fake extension listener (a team-signed binary registering a lookalike name is impossible without root and our provisioning; tested in the `FaultInjection` build).
- [ ] Release binaries contain no `113635.100.6.2.1` (the Debug requirement clause) and no `debugInjectFault`/`wgDebugCloseDevice`/`LP_FAULT_INJECTION` symbols (invariant 11).
- [ ] On macOS 27, `APP_REQ`/`EXT_REQ` match our own Developer ID (G2) builds (`codesign --verify -R`), including the post-quantum signature if S9 shows our builds carry one (27.1's `codesign` produced only a classical one by default; §5.3).
- [ ] Profile ownership: a second macOS user cannot provision or remove another user's profile over XPC, and receives no profile-scoped events or snapshots (uid filtering, §5.2).
- [ ] Every forbidden directive is rejected at import **and** at provision, with the app bypassed by a test client.
- [ ] No secret strings in: the unified log (`log show --predicate 'subsystem BEGINSWITH "io.github.steiale.lockplus"' --info --debug` with private data enabled via a configuration profile on the test Mac), the diagnostics bundle (every file, including `.ips`, `routes.txt`, `dns.txt`, `ne-configs.json`), crash reports (forced crash in DEBUG), `defaults read`, NE prefs (`/Library/Preferences/com.apple.networkextension.plist`), window-restoration state (`Saved Application State`), and the pasteboard 60 s after copying a secret.
- [ ] The editor and "Show password" windows are excluded from a `screencapture -l<windowid>` capture (`sharingType = .none`); the editor is not restored after relaunch.
- [ ] Sealed payload files are unreadable without the DP key; deleting the key yields "profiles locked" UI, not a crash; a locked screen yields "Keychain unavailable", not "locked".
- [ ] Extension store (the S4 variant in use): System keychain items exist only for provisioned profiles and are gone after `wipeAllSecrets`; or fallback files are root:wheel 0600 in a root 0700 directory, unreadable to a non-admin user, and contain only AES-GCM ciphertext (no planted secret found by `strings`/`grep`). Admin readability is documented, not tested as a failure.
- [ ] Tampered `profiles/*.json` (policy flipped) → quarantined, and NE preferences unchanged (§3.4). The same for a **replayed** older metadata + `.sealed` pair saved before a policy change (N6).
- [ ] The GitHub repository and environment secrets contain no EdDSA key, Developer ID certificate, provisioning profile or notarization credential, and no workflow has a signing or notarization step (N1).
- [ ] Export writes 0600 with `O_NOFOLLOW` (a symlink at the destination is refused); `RevealGate` is required.
- [ ] Zip bomb, 501-entry zip, path-traversal names: all rejected within limits (2.0.2: in the validator service; an entry over 1 MiB is a row, over 64 MiB unpacked refuses the archive; QR import is gone).
- [ ] *2.0.2:* the validator service runs as the console user with entitlements exactly `{app-sandbox}`, no sandbox denials during import (`log show --predicate 'sender == "Sandbox"'`), and no profile evaluation in the extension's log at import or provision (E2E-8 V1, V4); `kill -9` of the service during a large zip read gives "couldn't be checked safely" and the next import works (V3).
- [ ] *2.0.2:* another local user's `scutil --nc start` and System Settings toggle of our manual profile are refused (225), and so is the owner's own toggle (D-1, Diagnostics line); an Auto-Connect profile is still startable (residual); NE's restart of a kill-switch session without on-demand after `kill -9` and after a network return is honoured (E2E-8 S1–S11).
- [ ] *2.0.2:* the previous notarized app fails the new `APP_REQ` with rc 3 (`verify.sh pre` with `LP_PREV_APP`, R1), and an app rebuilt below the floor gets no accept line from a dev extension (R3).
- [ ] *2.0.2:* opening a file never saves or provisions without the Confirm click; during the self-test the only destinations are the probe host's addresses and the DNS servers, with nothing on en0 under the kill switch (E2E-8 O1–O9, T6, T7).
- [ ] *2.0.2 round 2:* an idle app makes a bounded number of `loadAllFromPreferences` calls over 60 s after launch and across one connect/disconnect (E2E-8 M2: count the "unknown connection" reloads in the `managers` log; no loop); a forged `pendingResume` or Auto-Connect choice in settings.json starts nothing (M1); a `kill -9` of the extension right after an Auto-Connect change, with the app reconciling before NE's restart, is admitted (Codex r2 #2); Save Only of a connected kill-switch OpenVPN profile with the validator stopped, then reconcile and `kill -9`: NE's restart is admitted (Codex r2 #1).
- [ ] Sparkle: a tampered archive and a lower version are refused; a feed edited after signing is refused; an unsigned or wrongly signed feed is refused until `SUSignedFeedFailureExpirationInterval`, then offered only in safe mode (no notes, no critical flag); a delta with a bad signature falls back to the full archive (ref/sparkle C18).
- [ ] Extension binary links no AppKit, SwiftUI or Sparkle; no `get-task-allow` and no `com.apple.security.cs.*` in its entitlements.
- [ ] A WEB_AUTH server, an encrypted key without a passphrase, and a proxy-auth profile each produce a visible error ≤ 5 s (L-OVPN-4); no `IV_SSO` reaches the test server.
- [ ] LK-16 (ServerIP) and LK-OVPN-CERT pass.
